reports.auditor: The auditor included an emphasis of matter regarding a management dispute with the 30% associate Enerqual Technology. Due to this dispute, the company receives no financial information from the associate. The investment is kept at its cost of ₹3 lakh without impairment testing.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid non-executive promoter-director Anil Raje ₹66.3 lakh for technical consultancy and ₹18 lakh for head office rent. It paid ₹20.3 lakh for business consulting to Aartech Solonics UK Ltd, an entity under management influence. The managing director received ₹34.9 lakh and the CEO received ₹35.4 lakh. Aartech also lent ₹4.33 crore to its subsidiaries, comprising ₹2.53 crore to AIC-Aartech and ₹1.80 crore to Faradigm, and bought ₹2.30 crore of goods from Faradigm.
reports.contingent: The company reported contingent liabilities of ₹6.48 crore for bank guarantees.
reports.outlook: The annual report states that the new 15,000 square foot Faradigm Ultracapacitors plant will be ready by this financial year. Civil work is currently in progress on government land in the Narmadapuram power-equipment cluster.
reports.other: Research and development spending was ₹81.67 lakh in FY26, representing 2.29% of revenue. The company holds listed small-cap and SME shares as well as mutual funds, which leads to large swings in other income. The report also notes that the UK associate Epsilon Ten was fully impaired for ₹3.93 crore in the previous year.
flags: The auditor highlighted a management dispute with an associate company that prevents Aartech from receiving its financial information.
A large share of profit comes from volatile treasury gains on listed small-cap and SME shares rather than core operations.
The company routinely capitalizes its research and development expenses into assets.
Significant related-party payouts include ₹66.3 lakh in technical consultancy paid to a non-executive promoter-director.
The company reported negative operating cash flows of ₹1.5 crore in FY25 and ₹0.75 crore in FY26.

reports.auditor: The auditor noted tax receivables and contingent liabilities as its key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: The company made routine purchases from Aarti group firms in FY26. This included about ₹20 crore from Aarti Industries, ₹11 crore from Aarti Pharmalabs, and ₹10 crore from Aarti Life Science. It also paid a small amount of interest to key management personnel lenders. Directors received about ₹11 crore in pay. These dealings were not considered material.
reports.contingent: The company has disputed tax claims totaling about ₹159 crore. This includes income-tax demands in appeal of ₹92.4 crore. It also faces excise, customs, and GST demands of ₹58.3 crore, plus an extra ₹8.4 crore in a subsidiary. Bank guarantees and letters of credit stand at ₹171 crore. The company has capital commitments of about ₹19 crore.
reports.other: In FY26, India revenue was ₹1,569 crore and international revenue was ₹996 crore. Exports made up 38% of sales, mostly to regulated markets. A low 7.6% effective tax rate driven by tax refunds lifted the net profit. The Baddi oncology formulation plant received USFDA approval and launched its first product. Prakash M. Patil ended his tenure as Chairman, Managing Director, and CEO.
flags: Contingent liabilities for tax and duty disputes total about ₹159 crore, which is roughly 10% of the company's net worth.
The auditor flagged tax receivables and these contingent liabilities as a key audit matter.
The effective tax rate was unusually low at 7.6% due to tax refunds, which artificially inflated the net profit for FY26.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. They noted two key audit matters: revenue recognition regarding variable consideration, contract modifications, and capitalised contract fulfilment costs, as well as the valuation and existence of ₹1,732 crore of inventory held across multiple sites.
reports.relatedParties: The company donated ₹12 crore of its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funds to foundations linked to the promoters, such as the Aarti Foundation. Additionally, a ₹6.7 crore land advance to a stressed NBFC was written off.
reports.contingent: The company reported contingent claims of ₹110 crore. This consists of ₹52 crore in disputed taxes, ₹38 crore for excise and customs disputes, and ₹19 crore for GST claims. It also holds letters of credit, bank guarantees, and discounted bills totalling ₹493 crore.
reports.outlook: Management noted the fast-growing Energy business for fuel additives. The pipeline includes a backward-integration project requiring ₹200–250 crore in capex, set to be commissioned by September or October 2027. It is also running trials for a new ethylation downstream product, PEDA.
reports.other: The end-use product mix was led by the Energy segment at 43%, followed by Agrochemicals at 18%, Polymers and additives at 14%, Dyes and pigments at 11%, and Pharma at 10%. Profits were aided by an exceptional gain of ₹28.5 crore from interest on tax refunds. The company also disclosed ₹246 crore in supplier-finance liabilities.
flags: The auditor highlighted the existence and valuation of a massive ₹1,732 crore inventory spread across multiple sites as a key audit matter.
A ₹6.7 crore land advance previously given to a stressed NBFC was completely written off.
The company routed ₹12 crore of its mandatory CSR spending to promoter-linked foundations.
Reported profits were flattered by an exceptional item of ₹28.5 crore in interest on tax refunds.
The company relies heavily on letters of credit, bank guarantees, and discounted bills amounting to ₹493 crore.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion but included an emphasis of matter. A target-redemption forward contract was inadvertently left out of FY25 fair-value calculations, causing a ₹29.73 crore loss to be booked in FY26. Derivatives and the capitalisation of ₹404 crore in gross fixed assets were key audit matters. The auditor also modified the books-of-account statement because the database-level audit trail on the SaaS accounting system could not be verified.
reports.relatedParties: Ganesh Polychem became a joint venture, from which the company received a ₹15 crore advance at 8%. The company placed a ₹15 crore deposit with promoter-group Valiant Organics, alongside paying them ₹15.5 crore in license fees and ₹13 crore in reimbursements. It provided a ₹7.8 crore inter-corporate deposit to Aarti Ventures. Sales to Aarti Drugs were ₹41.9 crore. In FY25, it purchased ₹85.5 crore in solar equipment from promoter-linked Prozeal Green Energy.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small, consisting of ₹7.9 crore in bank guarantees. The company also has capital commitments of ₹28.9 crore. The auditor's report noted no pending litigation that would affect the financial statements.
reports.other: The annual report notes state that a total foreign exchange loss of ₹33 crore was recorded for FY26. There is also a disclosure gap, as the financial accounts present only a single 'Pharmaceuticals' segment with no detailed segment profit and loss breakdown.
flags: The auditor highlighted a control lapse regarding a derivative contract inadvertently excluded from FY25 calculations, resulting in a ₹29.73 crore loss in FY26.
The auditor modified the books-of-account statement because the database-level audit trail on the company's SaaS accounting system could not be verified.
The accounts contain a disclosure gap by reporting a single 'Pharmaceuticals' segment without segment profit and loss details.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The only key audit matter was the valuation of finished-goods inventory, specifically regarding overhead allocation. The auditor also noted that the audit trail operated throughout the year.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings were modest. Key management personnel received ₹17.5 crore in pay. The company also purchased ₹1.6 crore worth of raw materials from a firm related to key management.
reports.contingent: The company reported small contingent liabilities of ₹17.25 crore. This consisted of ₹17.0 crore for income tax disputes and ₹0.2 crore for GST.
reports.outlook: Management noted that the Gulf conflict and Strait of Hormuz closure raised feedstock and freight costs. The report states the company has a 50% to 90% global share in key intermediates and validated four more CDMO products during the year.
reports.other: Sales outside India were ₹1,021 crore out of ₹1,329 crore in total product sales. Capital commitments fell to ₹39 crore from ₹80 crore. The plants in Sachin and Ankleshwar passed Japan PMDA inspections without major observations. The company also highlighted its 90% backward integration and a 16 MW solar plant.
flags: Payments to micro and small suppliers beyond the legal due date rose to ₹75.3 crore from ₹56.6 crore the previous year, incurring ₹1.23 crore in interest.
The Gulf conflict and Strait of Hormuz closure increased feedstock and freight costs.

reports.auditor: There was no auditor qualification. The key audit matter was the impairment of indefinite-life intangibles, specifically the brands.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include service tax of ₹4.64 crore, income tax of ₹4.41 crore, GST of ₹0.55 crore, and guarantees of ₹1.23 crore. Additionally, a former co-packer sued ADF USA in 2022; the US court granted an injunction and money award of roughly USD 2.8 million in ADF USA's favour, but this has been appealed.
reports.other: At March 2025, 17 lakh promoter-family shares were pledged, including 16.5 lakh by Parul Thakkar and 0.5 lakh by Sumer Thakkar, though the FY26 status was not found in the notes read. The managing director's commission is up to 5% of consolidated profit before tax, payable partly by overseas subsidiaries.
flags: A former co-packer has appealed a USD 2.8 million court award granted to ADF USA, making recovery of the money uncertain.
As of March 2025, 17 lakh promoter-family shares were pledged, and the FY26 status was not confirmed in the notes read.
The managing director is entitled to a high commission of up to 5% of the consolidated profit before tax.

reports.auditor: Walker Chandiok gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters included revenue recognition for rebates and discounts, and the impairment of a ₹258 crore investment in and an ₹8 crore loan to subsidiary AIL Dixon. The auditor noted one exception: the audit-trail edit log was not enabled at the database level. Under CARO, they reported slight delays in paying statutory dues in a few cases.
reports.relatedParties: The company sold goods to and received electricity reimbursements from ARK Infosolution, a promoter-group company. It also paid rent to its promoters. Donations and corporate social responsibility (CSR) funds were routed through the promoter family's Seth Parmanand Khemka Charitable Trust. The group had a CSR obligation of ₹3.9 crore. Exact transaction figures are not provided because the note's layout was hard to read, but the amounts are small relative to sales.
reports.contingent: The company faces total customs demands of ₹39.4 crore. This includes a ₹30.9 crore order for imported 4G routers, which is appealed to CESTAT with ₹6 crore paid under protest. Other contingent liabilities include ₹35.0 crore in GST demands and ₹19.0 crore for income tax, of which ₹3.6 crore remains contested. The company also has outstanding bank guarantees of ₹21 crore and AEO customs bonds of ₹310 crore.
reports.outlook: The management discussion states the Indian video-surveillance market was around US$4.4 billion in 2025 and is expected to grow 16–17% annually. IP cameras are growing at about 25%. A new government cyber-security testing rule applied from April 2025 barred uncertified stock. This shut out Chinese brands and helped CP PLUS double its market share to 43.3%, as it had one of the largest certified product portfolios.
reports.other: The company reports as a single security and surveillance operating segment. Its own CP PLUS brand made up 86% of FY26 revenue, while the rest was mostly third-party traded products that are being run down. Outstanding capital commitments stood at ₹69 crore, with capital work-in-progress at ₹84 crore in March 2026. A dividend of ₹1.64 per share was proposed for FY26.
flags: The company is fighting multiple tax and duty demands, including ₹39.4 crore for customs, ₹35.0 crore for GST, and ₹19.0 crore for income tax.
The auditor flagged that the mandatory audit-trail edit log was not enabled at the database level.
The auditor reported slight delays in the payment of some statutory dues.
The auditor highlighted a potential impairment risk for a ₹258 crore investment in and an ₹8 crore loan to subsidiary AIL Dixon.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unmodified opinion for both the standalone and consolidated accounts. The timing of revenue recognition was the only key audit matter. The auditor also noted that an accounting audit trail was not enabled in earlier years.
reports.relatedParties: The company purchased ₹31.0 crore of goods and services from its holding company, J. B. Advani & Co., up from ₹28.6 crore in FY25. It also made ₹4.9 crore in sales to the holding company and paid it a dividend of ₹15.7 crore.
reports.contingent: The company faces a ₹36.4 crore penalty under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, which is pending in court and has not been provided for. Other disputed claims include income tax of ₹15.8 crore, excise of ₹9.4 crore, sales tax of ₹6.6 crore, and other items of ₹4.2 crore. Capital commitments stood at ₹10.4 crore.
reports.other: The core welding segment generated ₹1,078.7 crore in revenue and a profit of ₹164.3 crore before exceptional items. The flares and process equipment segment posted a ₹23.1 crore loss on ₹56.7 crore of revenue. Unallocable expenses were ₹23.3 crore. Capital expenditure for the year was ₹26.3 crore. The company also granted 29,500 stock options in September 2025.
flags: A ₹36.4 crore penalty from the Bureau of Indian Standards is being fought in court and has not been provided for in the accounts.
The flares and process equipment segment remains a drag, reporting a ₹23.1 crore loss before exceptional items.
The company faces multiple disputed tax claims, including ₹15.8 crore for income tax and ₹9.4 crore for excise.
The auditor pointed out that an audit trail feature was not enabled in earlier accounting years.
A secretarial audit flagged a minor delay in the circulation of board minutes.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion and listed revenue recognition as the only key audit matter. Other auditors checked subsidiaries and a joint venture that made up ₹268.6 crore, or about 38% of group revenue. One foreign subsidiary, which had ₹2.88 crore in revenue and ₹1.32 crore in profit, was unaudited and relied on management certification. Oddly, the consolidated audit report mistakenly reused wording from the standalone report.
reports.relatedParties: The standalone related-party note shows the company bought ₹58.4 crore worth of items from its subsidiary Advait Greenergy (AGPL). The company also paid ₹0.98 crore in dividends to the Managing Director. The annual report's AGM notice included approvals for future transactions with AGPL up to ₹700 crore, and raised the pay ceilings for the MD's daughter to ₹55 lakh and son-in-law to ₹75 lakh.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities rose to ₹362.8 crore from ₹211.8 crore the year before. This included ₹211.4 crore in bank guarantees, ₹104.9 crore in letters of credit and bills, a ₹20 crore corporate guarantee for a subsidiary, and ₹22.5 crore in surety bonds. There is also a disputed customs demand of ₹3.98 crore from 2020-21 under penalty sections, which the company has appealed.
reports.outlook: The Management Discussion and Analysis stated that the order book grew to ₹1,304 crore by March 2026, with 64% from the transmission business and 36% from renewable energy. Strangely, the MD&A called the recommended ₹2 per share dividend "maiden" even though dividends were paid previously, and it left the financial ratio table blank with a note saying it would be updated later.
reports.other: Segment notes showed the transmission business earned ₹79.0 crore in profit on ₹459.2 crore of revenue, while the new energy segment made a much lower ₹14.0 crore profit on ₹268.1 crore. Geographically, 98% of business was in India, with just ₹3.9 crore earned overseas. The headline net profit was reduced by a ₹3.0 crore loss share from the TG Advait joint venture to settle at ₹55.1 crore. The capital-management note listed total debt at ₹142.1 crore including guarantees.
flags: The consolidated audit report sloppily reused wording from the standalone report.
A foreign subsidiary being wound up was not formally audited and its numbers were only management-certified.
The company faces a disputed customs penalty demand of ₹3.98 crore.
The management discussion section was published with a completely blank financial ratios table.
The standalone company bought ₹58.4 crore from its subsidiary AGPL, making it difficult to tell if group-owned asset construction is being booked as revenue.

reports.auditor: The auditor, C N K & Associates, issued an unmodified opinion. They highlighted the capitalization of projects in progress as a key audit matter. Under CARO, the subsidiary Aegis Terminal (Pipavav) was flagged for incurring cash losses. The audit trail operated throughout the year.
reports.relatedParties: CMD Raj Chandaria's pay rose to ₹10 crore, up from ₹6.6 crore in FY25. Promoter entities Trans Asia Petroleum and Huron received final dividends of about ₹55.6 crore and ₹66.7 crore, plus interim payouts. Vopak received ₹27.9 crore in interest. The year-end closing payable to related parties was about ₹413 crore.
reports.contingent: The company reported GST and sales-tax demands of ₹98 crore, up from ₹77 crore previously. There is an ongoing air-pollution matter before the Supreme Court involving ₹142 crore, and a minor electricity dispute of ₹0.8 crore. Outstanding capital commitments stood at ₹1,379 crore as of March 2026.
reports.outlook: The annual report indicated that phase 1 of the JNPA liquids project, which includes approximately 100,000 kl of capacity, was targeted for completion in the first half of FY27.
reports.other: The Gas segment generated ₹7,689 crore in revenue and ₹1,127 to ₹1,131 crore in EBITDA, while the Liquids segment saw flat revenue of ₹644 crore and ₹472 crore in EBITDA. One Gas customer represented 22% of total revenue. Minority shareholders accounted for ₹208 crore of the ₹1,107 crore reported profit.
flags: The auditor flagged the subsidiary Aegis Terminal (Pipavav) under CARO for incurring cash losses.
A major air-pollution case involving ₹142 crore is pending against the company before the Supreme Court.
Disputed GST and sales-tax demands have increased to ₹98 crore.
Customer concentration worsened, with a single Gas segment customer accounting for 22% of total revenue.
Significant profits leak to minority interests, with ₹208 crore of the reported net profit belonging to outside shareholders.

reports.auditor: The standalone auditor's report highlighted a key audit matter regarding investments in subsidiaries, noting a cumulative impairment provision of ₹662.7 crore (70.6% of standalone assets). Additionally, the auditor remarked that the audit trail was not enabled at the application level for certain tables across significant processes between April 1 and October 9, 2025.
reports.relatedParties: The annual report notes that the company has given corporate guarantees for the loans of related entities.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include ₹2.0 crore for labour and ₹2.5 crore for income tax. A ₹78 crore tax demand from FY18 was set aside by the Karnataka High Court and remanded. Additionally, ₹4 crore of refunds were adjusted under protest, and corporate guarantees were given for loans of related entities.
reports.other: Note 36 of the annual report shows customer concentration in the aerospace segment. The top customer accounted for 22.9% of FY26 revenue, the second for 19.1%, the third for 5.9%, and the fourth for 10.2%.
flags: The standalone auditor's report flagged a ₹662.7 crore impairment provision on subsidiary investments, showing past value destruction.
The software audit trail was not enabled for certain significant processes between April and October 2025.
Customer concentration is high, with the top two customers generating 42% of total revenue.
The company is dealing with a remanded FY18 tax demand of ₹78 crore.

reports.auditor: The auditor, Suresh I Surana & Associates, issued an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters included revenue cut-off, capex capitalisation, and inventory valuation. The CARO report was clean, noting no defaults, bank stock statements that agreed with the books, operational audit-trail software, and no whistle-blower complaints.
reports.relatedParties: In FY26, transactions with director-controlled companies totaled ₹17.3 crore, and managerial pay was ₹6.7 crore. In FY25, the company purchased land for ₹10.9 crore and a building for ₹8.0 crore from related parties. The CARO report noted all transactions were approved under Sections 177 and 188.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small. They include approximately ₹15 crore in bank guarantees and a ₹4.3 crore GST show-cause notice regarding ineligible input credit on IPO expenses, which is currently under appeal.
reports.outlook: Management plans to invest ₹100 crore for a new R&D building with 120 fume hoods and 8 technical labs, expected to be ready by Q2 FY28. The company also plans to spend ₹250 crore for Magnum Phase 2, which will add 4 new production blocks in FY28. Management warned that customer concentration is expected to rise further.
reports.other: Aether operates one reported segment with three business models: contract manufacturing (₹523 crore), large-scale manufacturing (₹489 crore), and contract research (₹105 crore). FY26 revenue was ₹920 crore from India and ₹240 crore from exports. Product concentration improved, with the top 5 products falling to 31.0% of revenue and the top 10 customers dropping to 40.3%.
flags: The largest customer's share of revenue increased to 18.98% in FY26, and management expects this concentration to rise further.
The company has a history of related-party asset purchases, having bought land for ₹10.9 crore and a building for ₹8.0 crore from related parties in FY25.

reports.auditor: Walker Chandiok (Grant Thornton India) issued a clean opinion for the group. The auditor flagged revenue and receivables as key audit matters. The component auditor, EY, also highlighted capitalised intangibles as a key audit matter due to large development costs.
reports.relatedParties: The company has small related-party transactions with Affle Holdings, AGPL, and AXPL. A major transaction is a ₹1,100 crore warrant issue (about 7.4 million warrants at ₹1,487 each) going to the promoter entity, Affle Holdings.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small. The largest item is an income tax demand of ₹6.5 crore for the 2017-18 assessment year. The company also has capital commitments of ₹28.7 crore.
reports.other: A 24.07% stake in Bobble AI, valued at ₹135.8 crore, has been classified as 'held for sale' for over two years. No impairment has been booked despite Bobble entering insolvency. Additionally, the company capitalised ₹165 crore in intangible assets and added ₹174 crore to intangibles under development.
flags: A ₹135.8 crore stake in Bobble AI remains unimpaired on the books despite the company facing insolvency.
Significant development costs are capitalised rather than expensed, which flatters the operating profit margins compared to peers.
Working-capital days jumped sharply from 25 to 82 days in FY26.
Operating cash flow to net profit conversion dropped to roughly 41% in the latest quarter.
Gross margins have declined by about 250 basis points from their peak, pointing to pressure on spreads.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The report highlighted revenue recognition, specifically regarding rebates and discounts, as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: Dealings with the promoter group Hindware included receiving ₹21.6 crore in rent and making ₹23.4 crore in sales. The company paid nil for management services to Hindware in FY26, down from ₹19.6 crore in FY25. Pay for key management personnel jumped 57% to ₹27.4 crore.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities stood at about ₹100 crore. These were mostly tax-related, including ₹50 crore for entry-tax demands. Capital commitments saw a massive jump, rising to ₹292 crore by March 2026 compared to just ₹35 crore the previous year.
reports.outlook: The management discussion noted that container glass utilisation was around 95%, while specialty glass was about 75%. A ₹47 crore debottlenecking project was commissioned by March 2026 to increase capacity. The board's report confirmed the company lost its bid to buy rival HNG after the Supreme Court rejected its resolution plan.
reports.other: The company reported two segments for FY26: Packaging products at ₹2,644 crore and Investment property at ₹21.6 crore. Customer concentration is notable, with just two clients making up 27.3% of FY26 revenue. The secretarial report disclosed a ₹5 lakh SEBI penalty for a listing violation, which the company appealed.
flags: Key management pay jumped 57% to ₹27.4 crore in a year where revenue growth was sluggish.
Capital commitments skyrocketed to ₹292 crore from ₹35 crore, signaling heavy upcoming cash needs.
The company relies heavily on a few buyers, with just two customers bringing in 27.3% of annual revenue.
The company faced a ₹5 lakh SEBI penalty for a listing rules violation.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion but listed key audit matters that highlight control gaps. The company lacks policies to classify slow-moving or obsolete inventory, implement a scrap policy, or consolidate foreign subsidiaries. Fixed-asset tagging is incomplete, and loans and advances are carried without confirmations. A ₹1.3 crore receivable from a bankrupt international customer was written off. Overseas subsidiaries were audited by other auditors.
reports.relatedParties: The company sold goods to promoter-owned US companies under the same management worth roughly ₹44 crore in FY25 (27% of revenue) and ~₹11 crore in FY26. It pays ~₹4 crore a year for services to promoter-owned Aimtron Technologies Pvt Ltd. Additionally, the standalone business lent ₹16.8 crore to Aimtron Electronics LLC for a US deal and ₹7.8 crore to Aimtron Mechatronics.
reports.contingent: The company faces an income-tax demand of ₹7.9 crore (10% paid) and a GST demand of ₹13 crore. These total ₹20.9 crore, which is roughly 45% of the FY26 net profit. It also received an income-tax transfer-pricing notice for its FY24 international transactions. The company has an EPCG export obligation of ₹187.3 crore that must be met by FY28.
flags: The auditor noted basic control gaps, such as missing policies for obsolete inventory and carrying unconfirmed loans and advances.
A significant portion of past revenue came from related-party trading with promoter-owned US companies.
The company faces tax and GST demands of ₹20.9 crore, equal to roughly 45% of its FY26 net profit.
The company received an income-tax transfer-pricing notice regarding its FY24 international transactions.
Fixed-asset tagging is incomplete, and a ₹1.3 crore receivable from a bankrupt international customer had to be written off.

reports.auditor: The auditor, Varadarajan & Co, gave a clean opinion with no qualifications or emphasis of matter. The accounts use Indian GAAP rather than Ind AS. The CARO report notes disputed tax and compliance penalties. The secretarial auditor noted delayed statutory filings and late related-party disclosures to the BSE, which resulted in a fine.
reports.relatedParties: Promoters D. Venkatesan and D. Manikandan were each paid ₹75 lakh along with rent, and the family received about ₹0.4 cr in rent. The company has a web of promoter-linked entities with advances, including ₹1.21 cr outstanding from Apex Material Sciences. Promoter advances of ₹2.6 cr and ₹6.0 cr from FY25 were repaid in FY26.
reports.contingent: The company is appealing RoC Chennai penalties totalling about ₹0.9 cr (amounts of ₹17.3 lakh, ₹26.0 lakh, ₹27.1 lakh, and ₹19.6 lakh) for CSR non-compliance between FY20 and FY23. There is also a disputed GST demand of ₹20.0 lakh.
reports.other: Trade receivables stood at ₹214.0 cr at the end of March 2026. Intangible assets of ₹8.4 cr appeared on the balance sheet for the first time. Out of ₹13.7 cr allocated for machinery in the IPO, only ₹2.9 cr was spent by March 2026, leaving ₹10.8 cr unspent because Chinese suppliers required end-user certificates.
flags: RoC penalties of about ₹0.9 cr for CSR non-compliance and a ₹20.0 lakh GST demand are being disputed.
The secretarial auditor flagged delayed statutory filings and late related-party disclosures that led to a fine.
Trade receivables were high, reaching ₹214.0 cr at the end of March 2026 against annual revenue of ₹319.6 cr.
Advances were made to a web of promoter-linked concerns, including ₹1.21 cr outstanding from Apex Material Sciences.
Intangible assets of ₹8.4 cr appeared on the balance sheet for the first time.

reports.auditor: The auditor's report includes an emphasis of matter regarding an income tax search at the company's premises in August 2025. The company received a notice for the block period from 1 April 2019 to 17 November 2025 and filed a block return on 6 April 2026. The financial impact is not ascertainable. The auditor also highlighted a key audit matter on revenue recognition concerning US chargebacks and rebates.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are negligible, amounting to about ₹8 crore on a standalone basis.
flags: The auditor issued an emphasis of matter due to an ongoing income tax search where the final financial impact is not ascertainable.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion with no emphasis of matter. The key audit matter was revenue recognition under Ind AS 115.
reports.relatedParties: The company reported no material related-party transactions that needed an AOC-2 filing.
reports.contingent: The company provided corporate guarantees for group SPVs totaling about ₹446 crore. This includes ₹157.5 crore for Ajmera Luxe, ₹125 crore for Ajmera Bora, ₹88 crore for Shree Yogi Realcon, and ₹75 crore for Ajmera Housing Bangalore. There are also income-tax demands of roughly ₹11.7 crore, mainly ₹9.2 crore for AY 2023-24. Additionally, a CSR shortfall was deposited into an unspent account.
flags: The company carries sizable contingent liabilities of about ₹446 crore from corporate guarantees given for group SPVs.
There are unresolved income-tax demands totaling roughly ₹11.7 crore.

reports.auditor: The auditors, Walker Chandiok, included an emphasis of matter in both the standalone and consolidated reports. This relates to a January 2025 income tax search and subsequent show-cause notices, with the financial impact still pending conclusion. Three subsidiary auditors also noted this. Additionally, the auditors reported a ₹0.45 crore fraud by subsidiary employees through inflated IT procurement. The company took disciplinary action and filed an insurance claim.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities totalled ₹99 crore. This includes ₹76.6 crore for income tax, mostly from a contested ₹73.4 crore pre-acquisition demand on Parabolic Drugs. It also includes ₹10.4 crore for indirect taxes and a ₹12.2 crore drug-pricing recovery claim by the NPPA. Additionally, the company had capital commitments of ₹80 crore at March 2026.
reports.outlook: Management highlights an export build-up, including a European CDMO contract to supply €35 million a year from FY28 to 2032. The company also secured a Zambia government supply contract for $25 million a year in FY27 and FY28 from India. A new local Zambian plant costing $45 million, where Akums will hold a 51% stake, is planned for FY29-30. A new injectable plant is currently operating at early teens utilisation.
reports.other: The company operates a 50.6 billion-unit capacity across various forms and holds 1,035 DCGI product approvals. R&D spending exceeded ₹100 crore over three years. Contract liabilities jumped to ₹1,076 crore at March 2026 from ₹65 crore the previous year, mainly due to a €100 million upfront prepayment for a European contract. A secretarial report noted the board composition breached SEBI rules from February to June 2025 after an independent director departed.
flags: An Income Tax search in January 2025 resulted in block assessment show-cause notices with an unquantified financial impact.
Auditors flagged a ₹0.45 crore misappropriation fraud by subsidiary employees through fictitious IT procurement.
The board composition breached SEBI compliance rules for several months after an independent director resigned.
Contingent liabilities total ₹99 crore, primarily driven by a ₹73.4 crore contested tax demand linked to Parabolic Drugs.
Reported cash balances are heavily inflated by ₹1,076 crore in contract liabilities, meaning much of the cash is actually a customer advance.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters were revenue variable consideration and income-tax and indirect-tax litigation. Under CARO, the auditor noted one whistle-blower complaint was under investigation at the report date. Additionally, the audit trail was not kept for some privileged-user changes, and database logs lacked pre-change values.
reports.relatedParties: The company sold its powder coatings business for ₹2,073 crore and its research centre for ₹70 crore to an AkzoNobel subsidiary. It also bought Dulux and related decorative intellectual property from AkzoNobel for ₹1,152 crore. The company continues to pay royalties to AkzoNobel entities to license international industrial brands.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include ₹47 crore in tax disputes. This consists of ₹26.5 crore for income tax, ₹10.2 crore for excise and customs, ₹7.6 crore for sales tax, and ₹2.7 crore for GST. There are also additional claims amounting to ₹6.7 crore.
reports.outlook: Management stated they will be seriously investing in capital expenditure for capacity expansion and localization. This includes adding more capacity at the Bengaluru industrial plant, though no specific investment amounts or timelines were disclosed. Capital expenditure for FY26 was relatively low at ₹47 crore.
reports.other: Exceptional items showed a ₹1,892.5 crore profit from selling the powder coatings business and research centre. The board reported a special interim dividend of ₹156 per share and a final dividend of ₹50 per share. The company also holds a 99.99% stake in the ICI India Research & Technology Centre subsidiary.
flags: One whistle-blower complaint was under investigation at the time of the report.
The audit trail was not maintained for some privileged-user system changes.
Database logs lacked pre-change values according to the auditor's report.
The company faces contingent liabilities of ₹47 crore in tax disputes and ₹6.7 crore in other claims.

reports.auditor: The auditor, KKC & Associates, gave an unmodified opinion and reported no audit-trail exceptions. The only key audit matter highlighted was the existence and valuation of the company's ₹2,511 crore inventory.
reports.relatedParties: Key management personnel, mostly the Amin family, received ₹61 crore in remuneration, representing about 9% of profit. The company made ₹63 crore in purchases from Shreno Publications, and paid ₹31.5 crore for services and ₹12.4 crore in rent to promoter-group company Alembic Ltd.
reports.contingent: Group contingent liabilities are a modest ₹100 crore, including ₹38.6 crore in guarantees and letters of credit, a ₹20.9 crore indirect-tax dispute, and a rooftop-solar dispute. Standalone guarantees are ₹348 crore, mostly for subsidiaries. The company also has capital commitments of ₹191.5 crore.
reports.other: Total FY26 revenue was ₹7,345 crore, with R&D expenses consuming ₹712 crore. The company reported net working capital of ₹1,812 crore and total borrowings of ₹1,430 crore. A dividend of ₹12 per share was declared. Nirayu Pvt Ltd is the controlling company.
flags: One customer accounted for a high 12% of total FY26 revenue at ₹853 crore.
Key management personnel remuneration was ₹61 crore, which consumed roughly 9% of the net profit.
The auditor highlighted a massive ₹2,511 crore inventory balance as a key audit matter.
The company took an ₹18.4 crore exceptional write-down on its Sikkim plant which is being exited.
An exceptional charge of ₹48.6 crore was recorded for labour-code gratuity provisions.

reports.auditor: The auditor, Kirtane & Pandit LLP, gave an unqualified opinion. They included key audit matters regarding the capitalization of plant and contingent liabilities.
reports.relatedParties: Alicon bought ₹36.2 cr of plant and equipment from promoter group company Atlas Castalloy, representing about a quarter of its FY26 capex. It also paid Atlas ₹4.0 cr in rent, ₹6.6 cr for purchases, and ₹6.3 cr for expenses. The board report stated these transactions were at arm's length.
reports.contingent: The company reported corporate guarantees of ₹54.6 cr, up from ₹46.2 cr, which are likely for its European subsidiary. It also has ₹9.4 cr in customs interest on unmet export obligations, ₹9.7 cr in bank guarantees, and ₹2.5 cr in court cases.
reports.other: Alicon has a single reportable segment for aluminium castings. Standalone exports fell by about 33% to ₹124 cr. The European subsidiary's pre-tax profit dropped from ₹10.4 cr to ₹0.74 cr on revenue of ₹122 cr. Exceptional items of ₹7.6 cr included a ₹5.0 cr labour-code gratuity and a ₹2.6 cr past sales-commission claim. Key management pay was ₹22.2 cr.
flags: Key management pay was ₹22.2 cr, which is very high relative to the consolidated net profit of ₹34.4 cr.
The company bought ₹36.2 cr of equipment from a promoter group company, making up about a quarter of its annual capex.
Standalone exports dropped roughly 33% year-on-year to ₹124 cr.
The European subsidiary saw its revenue drop 34% and its pre-tax profit nearly wiped out to ₹0.74 cr.
The company has ₹9.4 cr in contingent liabilities for customs interest on unmet export obligations.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The only key audit matter was revenue recognition regarding variable consideration.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid ₹15.6 crore in CSR funds to the Nirma Education and Research Foundation, a promoter trust. Key management personnel received ₹7.2 crore in pay. The company also made small sales of ₹0.6 crore to Aculife, part of the Nirma group.
reports.contingent: The company has a small contingent liability of ₹4.8 crore for an excise dispute on amiodarone at CESTAT. It also had capital commitments of ₹106 crore at the end of March 2026, up from ₹33 crore.
reports.other: The company operates as one reportable segment. Its former parent, GPL, remains the largest customer, providing ₹742 crore or 29% of revenue in FY26. Total revenue included ₹1,164 crore from India and ₹1,388 crore from outside India. A final dividend of ₹5 per share was declared. A flash fire at the Dahej plant caused a ₹20 crore loss.
flags: Former parent company GPL is the largest customer, making up 29% of FY26 revenue, indicating high customer concentration.
The company directed ₹15.6 crore in CSR funds to a trust linked to its promoter.
A flash fire at the Dahej plant resulted in a ₹20 crore loss during the year.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unmodified opinion. The only key audit matter noted in the report was litigation.
reports.relatedParties: The company stated that related-party transactions were in the ordinary course of business and conducted at arm's length.
reports.contingent: The company reported contingent liabilities of ₹36.8 crore covering tax, excise, and customs disputes.
reports.outlook: Management's discussion highlighted a new specialty chemical project at Dahej designed to substitute imports. The company increased its ACN market share as Chinese imports dropped. However, management warned of ongoing Chinese competition in ACN and customers' products, noting that price cuts could erode anti-dumping duty benefits. The report also mentioned a temporary force majeure shutdown of ammonia supply in March 2026 caused by LNG shortages.
reports.other: The company operates plants in Patalganga, Kurkumbh, and Dahej. FY26 exports were ₹319 crore, down from ₹343 crore in FY25, forming 22.7% of turnover with direct US exposure around 1%. Promoter family pay was high relative to profit at roughly ₹26 crore, representing about 14% of net profit. This included ₹13.6 crore for Executive Chairman Yogesh Kothari, and ₹6.1 crore each for Suneet Kothari and Kirat Patel.
flags: Promoter family pay is high, taking up approximately 14% of net profit (~₹26 crore).
Management warned that Chinese competition and price cuts could wipe out the benefits of the anti-dumping duty on ACN.
A force majeure event briefly stopped the supply of key raw material ammonia in March 2026 due to LNG shortages.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave a clean opinion. The key audit matter noted was the timing of revenue recognition based on export shipping terms.
reports.relatedParties: Three promoter-directors received ₹5.9 crore in pay, and relatives on the payroll received ₹1.4 crore. This totals about ₹7.3 crore in family pay against a net profit of ₹35.6 crore. The company also paid ₹0.5 crore in rent to a family firm.
reports.contingent: The company reported nil contingent liabilities, noting that a ₹0.6 crore customs claim was closed.
reports.other: The segment note reveals extreme customer concentration, with the largest customer, IKEA, buying ₹346.6 crore in FY26 to make up about 57% of total revenue. Borrowings stood at ₹86 crore in March 2026. Additionally, ₹90.4 crore of IPO money earmarked for machinery and a warehouse remains unspent in fixed deposits.
flags: About 57% of total revenue comes from a single customer, IKEA.
Promoter and family compensation of ₹7.3 crore is high compared to the net profit of ₹35.6 crore.
Around ₹90.4 crore of IPO funds meant for machinery and capital expenditure remains unspent in fixed deposits.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unmodified opinion with no emphasis of matter. Revenue recognition and the allowance for trade receivables were highlighted as a key audit matter.
reports.contingent: As at 31 March 2026, the group had committed to buy ₹2,170 cr of cloud infrastructure services, a massive increase from ₹21.8 cr a year earlier. Contingent liabilities include income-tax claims of ₹22.1 cr. This involves transfer-pricing adjustments of ₹77.2 cr with a tax impact of about ₹20 cr sheltered by losses, and a ₹2.1 cr TDS demand. The company also faces GST demands of ₹11.0 cr, up from ₹5.6 cr.
reports.outlook: The management discussion and analysis warns of risks regarding the company's exposure to certain large customers and the North American market.
reports.other: The Americas supplied ₹1,096 cr or 72.8% of total revenue. A single customer brought in ₹260 cr, representing 17.3% of revenue, up from ₹132.6 cr the prior year. Fixed assets are just ₹94 cr. The board's report mentions an extinguished ESOP liability, and the annual report confirms there are no pledges. It also notes the purchase of Argoid Analytics in November 2024.
flags: A single customer accounted for 17.3% of total revenue at ₹260 cr, nearly doubling its contribution from the previous year.
The company has a massive new take-or-pay-style commitment to buy ₹2,170 cr of cloud infrastructure, creating a fixed-cost risk if volumes fall.
The business relies heavily on the Americas, which generates 72.8% of its revenue.
The company faces contingent tax disputes, including ₹22.1 cr in income-tax claims and ₹11.0 cr in GST demands.

reports.auditor: The audit by Price Waterhouse Chartered Accountants LLP and K.S. Rao & Co was unmodified. Key audit matters included the ₹434 crore warranty provision and revenue cut-offs. Under CARO, the auditors noted that title deeds for some land, including 18.94 acres worth ₹77.8 crore and 15.66 acres of leasehold land, are still registered to Mangal Industries rather than the company. A subsidiary also reported cash losses of ₹19.6 crore.
reports.relatedParties: Standalone dealings with promoter-group firms totalled about ₹890 crore for the year. The company bought ₹381 crore of plastic components and ₹55 crore of assets from Mangal Industries. It spent ₹213 crore on plant construction and assets, plus ₹132 crore on services, from Amara Raja Infra. It also bought ₹110 crore in goods from Amara Raja Electronics. Additionally, buying Mangal's plastics business generated ₹428 crore in goodwill.
reports.contingent: Standalone contingent liabilities rose to about ₹370 crore from ₹250 crore. This included "other claims" jumping from ₹9 crore to ₹100 crore, and a ₹10.5 crore APGPCL power claim in arbitration involving a lien on the company's investment. Capital commitments included ₹299 crore for standalone contracts and a committed ₹495.5 crore investment for leased land at a Cheyyar recycling site.
reports.other: The annual report's consolidated segment note broke down the ₹13,814 crore total revenue. The core lead-acid segment posted revenue of ₹13,005 crore and a profit of ₹1,270 crore. The new energy segment grew revenue to ₹809 crore but posted a widening loss of ₹135 crore, while its assets doubled to ₹1,844 crore.
flags: Standalone related-party transactions with promoter-group entities were high, totalling approximately ₹890 crore for components, assets, and services.
Title deeds for some land and leaseholds, including a ₹77.8 crore parcel, are still registered to Mangal Industries instead of the company.
The new energy business remains unprofitable, reporting a widened loss of ₹135 crore for the year.
Standalone contingent liabilities increased to approximately ₹370 crore, driven by a sharp rise in "other claims" up to ₹100 crore.
The auditor's CARO annexure noted that a subsidiary company reported cash losses of ₹19.6 crore.

reports.auditor: S.R. Batliboi & Co (EY) issued a qualified opinion on the FY26 consolidated accounts. The qualification was because the accounts included unaudited figures for one subsidiary and the step-down joint venture Shivaliks Mercantile, which recognised an ₹81.9 crore share of loss. The auditor also flagged audit-trail gaps, noting the holding company and six subsidiaries lacked database-level logging on their Microsoft D365 systems, while two step-down subsidiaries had incomplete logs.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were modest, consisting of ₹80 crore for income tax, ₹14 crore for GST, and a corporate guarantee of ₹2.9 crore.
reports.other: The annual report showed FY26 revenue of ₹12,186 crore and a reported PAT of ₹226 crore. Profit was impacted by a ₹112 crore impairment loss on the Shivaliks joint venture. The Board's report noted the electronics division's scale, with Amber's stake in IL JIN diluted to roughly 60% after issuing ₹1,750 crore in CCPS to private equity investors. The report also detailed recent acquisitions, including raising its stake in Ascent to 98.5% and buying the remaining 50% of Amber Resojet for ₹1.74 crore.
flags: The auditor qualified the FY26 accounts due to the inclusion of unaudited figures for one subsidiary and a joint venture.
The auditor identified audit-trail gaps, with the holding company and several subsidiaries lacking database-level logging.
The company took a ₹112 crore write-off in FY26 for the Shivaliks joint venture, which was then sold for approximately ₹1.1 lakh.
Recurring exceptional items heavily impact profitability, causing reported earnings to remain significantly below management's adjusted figures.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion but included an emphasis of matter. Two years after a business transfer, title deeds for all immovable properties, a ₹2.92 crore loan, a property loan, fixed deposits, a ₹66 lakh bank guarantee, and 12 of 15 vehicles remain in the promoter's old proprietorship name. The company also holds a 50% share in a partnership owning a property with incomplete paperwork. Under CARO, the auditor noted irregular advance income tax deposits and ₹14.6 crore lent to a subsidiary without a repayment schedule.
reports.relatedParties: The company had a ₹4.9 crore short-term advance outstanding to Anondita Healthcare, a promoter-family partnership firm. It gave a ₹2.2 crore corporate guarantee for that associate concern's car loan. It rented a factory from a promoter company for ₹1.33 crore a year. The managing director lent and was repaid about ₹4.5 crore during the year. An IDFC loan is also jointly owed with the partnership firm and the subsidiary.
reports.contingent: The annual report notes one civil case filed against the company for ₹77 lakh. There are four criminal and three civil cases filed by the company. A long dispute with Swear Healthcare regarding glove-machine designs is pending in the Supreme Court.
reports.outlook: In his letter, the managing director noted that capacity was expanded to 869 million condoms a year. Four extra production lines, adding roughly 250 million pieces of capacity, are currently under trial and expected to be ready by January 2027.
reports.other: The annual report identifies only one business segment, as exports were under 10% of revenue. The company's own Cobra brand is owned by an 89.03%-held subsidiary. At March 2026, borrowings were ₹34 crore and cash was ₹10 crore. The board saw turnover during the year, with a whole-time director, the company secretary, and a promoter all leaving in financial year 2026.
flags: Two years after a business transfer, key property title deeds, bank loans, and vehicles remain in the name of the promoter's old proprietorship.
The auditor noted that ₹14.6 crore was lent to a subsidiary without any fixed repayment schedule.
The company was not regular in depositing advance income tax.
The core Cobra brand is held in an 89.03% owned subsidiary rather than the parent company.
The board saw significant turnover during the year, losing a whole-time director, the company secretary, and a promoter.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The only key audit matter noted was regarding IT systems and controls. The report also confirmed that the audit trail operated throughout the year.
reports.relatedParties: The company has an outstanding loan of ₹7.8 crore and provided a ₹7.5 crore corporate guarantee to Anthem Biopharma Pvt Ltd, a promoter-group firm with common directors. It also pays ₹0.3 crore for lease rent. The auditor found these terms were not prejudicial and repayments were regular. Three founder-directors received roughly ₹6.6 crore each, and relatives were on the payroll for small amounts.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include tax and GST disputes of roughly ₹10 to ₹40 crore, though the exact total was hard to read due to the report's layout. Capital commitments rose significantly from ₹154 crore to ₹450 crore.
reports.outlook: The management discussion highlights the construction of a new 30-acre greenfield site called Unit 4, which broke ground in 2025. This expansion will add 365 KL of custom synthesis capacity and 100 KL of fermentation capacity. It will also include a dedicated plant for food and nutraceuticals.
reports.other: The company operates in two segments: CRDMO brought in ₹1,773 crore, and Specialty Ingredients brought in ₹352 crore. Geographically, exports form 85% of revenue, with Europe contributing ₹1,145 crore, the USA ₹580 crore, and India ₹316 crore. The NeoAnthem subsidiary, Unit 3, remained loss-making for the year.
flags: The top three customers pose a high concentration risk by accounting for 56.7% of total revenue.
The NeoAnthem subsidiary remained loss-making and holds ₹195 crore in intercompany loans.
The company's initial public offering was entirely an offer for sale by existing investors for ₹3,395 crore.
Poor formatting in the report makes the exact total of contingent tax and GST disputes difficult to verify.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The only key audit matter noted in the report was the revenue cut-off.
reports.contingent: Anupam disclosed an off-balance-sheet guarantee for a US$120 million facility, disclosed as ₹1,136 crore, taken by Batam S.à r.l., a 15%-owned entity. Standalone corporate guarantees rose to a ₹432 crore contingent liability. Total guarantees surged compared to just ₹75 crore a year earlier. The company also pledged its shares in Doriath and Batam and gave a non-disposal undertaking over its Tanfac shares.
reports.outlook: Management stated that Japan and the US grew as customer markets. They noted the multi-year capital expenditure cycle is finished, with ₹315 crore spent in FY26. Management expects the standalone asset base of ₹2,500 to ₹2,600 crore can support ₹3,500 crore in revenue. The report cited risks including agricultural market cyclicality, Chinese price competition in agrochemical intermediates, and foreign exchange exposure from high exports.
reports.other: Fixed assets jumped to ₹3,713 crore in FY26. This included goodwill of ₹540 crore related to the Jayhawk acquisition.
flags: The company carries a massive ₹1,136 crore off-balance-sheet guarantee for a 15%-owned entity to fund its Jayhawk acquisition.
Total corporate guarantees jumped sharply from ₹75 crore to a ₹432 crore standalone liability plus the ₹1,136 crore facility.
Anupam has pledged its shares in subsidiaries and given a non-disposal undertaking over its Tanfac shares.
The buyout right tied to this acquisition funding structure means an eventual cash call or shareholder dilution.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unmodified opinion with no CARO qualifications. Key audit matters involved revenue cut-off and the capitalisation of property, plant, and equipment and capital work-in-progress, which includes interest capitalisation.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings were described as routine. Pay for key management personnel was ₹40.1 crore in FY26, up from ₹32.5 crore in FY25, representing about 4% of profit after tax. The company made ₹6.5 crore in purchases from associates. Promoter-family trusts and a university or foundation are also listed as related parties.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small, consisting of tens of crores for tax, labour, and other claims. The company also has capital commitments of ₹465 crore, up from ₹316 crore in FY25.
reports.other: The management discussion detailed FY26 segment results. Conductors revenue grew 32.7% to ₹12,712 crore with EBITDA of ₹1,040 crore. Cables revenue rose 25.8% to ₹6,220 crore with EBITDA of ₹633 crore, overtaking oils to become the second-largest segment. Oils revenue grew 5.6% to ₹5,373 crore with EBITDA of ₹376 crore. The company spent ₹740 crore on capex in FY26. Fixed-asset turnover was 10.2 times, down slightly from 11.1 times in FY25. The report also noted 19 UL approvals.
flags: The company reported an exceptional loss of ₹33 crore in FY26.
An old arbitration case was moved from a contingent liability into a provision based on the auditors' advice.

reports.auditor: Manubhai & Shah LLP issued an unqualified opinion with no emphasis of matter. The report included one routine key audit matter regarding revenue recognition. The CARO section noted disputed tax dues pending before the CIT(A), High Court, and Supreme Court.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings are minimal. They include ₹4.6 lakh in sales to promoter-linked Choksey Chemicals, ₹15 lakh in consultancy fees to Apco Enterprises LLP, and ₹10 lakh for rent. Key management personnel remuneration stood at ₹5.4 crore.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small at roughly ₹14 crore, or 2% of net worth. This includes ₹9.32 crore in income tax disputes over R&D and transfer pricing, ₹2.30 crore for GST, ₹1.42 crore for customs, and ₹1.13 crore for service tax. Capital commitments stood at just ₹1.57 crore at the end of March 2026.
reports.outlook: The Chairman's letter outlines plans for two group-captive renewable power projects expected to fulfill 60% to 70% of the company's power requirements. Additionally, the annual report's risk table cautions that nitrile latex remains in a global oversupply cycle.
reports.other: Reported segments are purely geographic, with FY26 India sales at ₹974.2 crore and exports at ₹452.6 crore; no single customer accounts for 10% of revenue. One-off expenses included ₹4.78 crore for new labour codes, ₹3.23 crore for policy changes, ₹2.61 crore for a long-term incentive plan, a ₹3.73 crore turbine impairment, and ₹1.97 crore in extra depreciation. Apcotex is also noted as India's sole maker of NBR, nitrile latex, and HSR.
flags: The company booked an undisclosed ₹8.0 crore provision for pending litigation, which management will not detail because it is sub judice.
The auditor's CARO report flags disputed tax dues currently pending at the CIT(A), High Court, and Supreme Court.
The company experienced a CFO turnover, with Sachin Karwa leaving in May 2025 and Vivek Thakur taking over in July 2025.
The annual report's risk table warns that nitrile latex remains stuck in a global oversupply cycle.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unqualified opinion with no qualifications. The valuation of finished-goods inventory was noted as the key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: The company reported no material related-party transactions other than the pay for key managerial personnel.
reports.contingent: The company has small disputed dues. These consist of ₹1.96 crore for GST input credits and ₹0.14 crore for customs.
reports.other: The promoter holding in the company stands at 72.62%. None of these promoter shares are pledged.

reports.auditor: The auditor flagged key audit matters including judgement on capitalising ₹75.1 crore in costs, obsolescence risk on ₹760 crore of inventory, related-party transactions, and the open purchase-price allocation for ₹145.2 crore of goodwill on IDL. The CARO report noted inadequate documentation for subsidiary loans and stated the company raised share capital to meet subsidiary obligations.
reports.relatedParties: The standalone company gave ₹297.7 crore in loans to subsidiaries in FY26. Outstanding loans total ₹315.6 crore, mainly to IDL (₹187.6 crore) and ADIPL (₹124.3 crore). These are repayable on demand at 9.9% interest with no stipulated repayment terms. A promoter-linked entity, Apollo Food & Beverages, took and repaid a ₹4.5 crore advance.
reports.contingent: Contingent claims jumped significantly to ₹63.6 crore from ₹3.2 crore the prior year. Bank guarantees and counter-guarantees stood at ₹48.3 crore.
reports.outlook: The management discussion notes that phase 1 production has started at the new 3.5 lakh square foot Unit 3 facility at Hardware Park-II. Full operations are expected before March 2027.
reports.other: The company reported all ₹904 crore in revenue under one segment for domestic electronic components, without disclosing the explosives business split. No customer exceeded 10% of revenue, and exports were nil. The secretarial audit revealed an ₹88,500 NSE penalty for late audit reports, ROC compounding for late cost-audit filing, and a CSR spending shortfall (₹0.75 crore spent versus a ₹1.05 crore obligation).
flags: The standalone entity gave on-demand subsidiary loans reaching ₹315.6 crore, which lacked stipulated repayment terms and had inadequate documentation.
The auditor noted that the company raised share capital specifically to meet the obligations of its subsidiaries.
Standalone inventory reached ₹760 crore, comprising a third of total assets, and was flagged by the auditor for obsolescence risk.
Contingent claims surged to ₹63.6 crore from just ₹3.2 crore in the previous year.
The company faced compliance issues, including an NSE penalty for late audit report submission and a shortfall in mandatory CSR spending.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion with no qualifications. Key audit matters included ₹822 crore for sales-incentive and warranty accruals, Reifencom's ₹277 crore goodwill and ₹189 crore indefinite intangibles, and Netherlands asset impairment. The auditor noted a lack of a real-time audit trail for privileged database edits.
reports.relatedParties: In FY26, the company purchased about ₹685 crore of traded goods from promoter-group firms Classic Industries & Exports and Vilas Polymer. It also paid lease rent to PTL Enterprises, a promoter-group lessor of the Kalamassery plant, alongside other entities.
reports.contingent: A ₹425.5 crore CCI penalty for a truck-tyre price cartel is pending Supreme Court appeal and not provided for. Other contingent liabilities include ₹515 crore for sales tax, ₹221 crore for income tax, ₹16 crore for claims, and ₹10 crore each for excise/customs/GST and litigation. Capital commitments stand at ₹1,774 crore.
reports.other: FY26 exceptional items were ₹1,034 crore, almost entirely for the Enschede plant closure and restructuring, plus ₹26 crore for labour-code costs. Vice-Chairman and MD Neeraj Kanwar received ₹78.4 crore in pay, up 96% and 541 times the median employee, while also drawing pay from a UK subsidiary. APMEA and Europe segment revenues were ₹20,206 crore and ₹8,856 crore, respectively.
flags: A ₹425.5 crore competition penalty for a price cartel case is pending and not provided for in the accounts.
The auditor noted a lack of a real-time audit trail for privileged database edits.
Reifencom's low margins pose an impairment risk to its ₹277 crore goodwill and ₹189 crore indefinite intangibles.
Vice-Chairman and MD Neeraj Kanwar's pay jumped 96% to ₹78.4 crore, which is 541 times the median employee pay.
The company booked ₹1,034 crore in exceptional items in FY26, largely due to closing and restructuring the Enschede plant.

reports.auditor: The auditor, PKF Sridhar & Santhanam, gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters included checking revenue cut-offs for long-transit exports and verifying bulk salt inventory using third-party surveys. In the CARO report, the auditor flagged that the factory land lease deed is not current and that the database-level audit trail was not enabled.
reports.relatedParties: Promoter-linked Goodearth Maritime provided jetty services, shipment management, and barge transport, costing about ₹25.8 crore in FY26 compared to ₹23.5 crore previously. Related party Jakhau Salt Company reimburses jetty expenses. The company also gave ₹319 crore in loans to subsidiary Neun Infra to fund the SiCSem project. Promoter P. Ranjit was paid ₹9.0 crore, down from ₹20.2 crore in FY25.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities fell to ₹192 crore in FY26 from ₹237 crore in FY25. reports.outlook: Management stated that Phase 1 of the brine-field expansion is mostly complete. The company also signed a memorandum of understanding with the Gujarat government for a captive 7 million tonnes per annum salt jetty. The report noted that finished salt inventory built up by ₹13 crore in the fourth quarter.
reports.other: The company acquired subsidiary Idealis Mudchemie through the bankruptcy court for ₹76.9 crore. During FY26, the company sold 13,263 tonnes of bromine, 4.2 million tonnes of industrial salt, and 644 tonnes of sulphate of potash. The standalone current ratio fell to 1.41 from 4.50 due to higher borrowing and lower mutual-fund balances.
flags: The factory land lease for the Hajipir site expired in July 2018 and is still pending renewal eight years later.
The income tax department sent a High Pitched Scrutiny Assessment communication following a search of the company.
The auditor flagged that the accounting software's audit trail was not enabled at the database level.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unmodified opinion with no emphasis of matter. Revenue recognition and inventory carrying value were highlighted as key audit matters.
reports.relatedParties: The company reported no AOC-2 related-party transactions.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were tiny, consisting only of a GST Tran-1 credit dispute amounting to ₹2.5 crore.
reports.other: The operating model uses a mix of outright land, joint developments, and joint ventures, along with HDFC Capital platform funding via optionally convertible debentures in three Bengaluru projects. The company only books revenue upon project completion when it receives an occupancy certificate or building-use permission.
flags: Reported revenue numbers are lumpy because they are only recognized upon project completion.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion with no emphasis of matter. The key audit matters were revenue recognition and the net realisable value of inventory, which stands at ₹ 2,701 crore.
reports.relatedParties: The company had routine dealings with its subsidiaries, joint ventures, and promoter entities including OPG Realtors, Karma Hospitality, and Woodstory. No pledges were found.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include ₹ 19.2 crore for GST and service tax, ₹ 1.4 crore for income tax, and ₹ 4.8 crore in corporate guarantees. A small mining penalty of ₹ 1.58 lakh paid to the Rajasthan mines department was disclosed in the business responsibility and sustainability report.
flags: A consumer complaint over an old delivered project has been converted into a class action lawsuit.
The Rajasthan government is attempting to acquire 15 hectares of the company's land at Milakpur.
The company faces unresolved contingent liabilities, including ₹ 19.2 crore for GST and service tax disputes.

reports.auditor: The auditor included an emphasis of matter regarding a CBI chargesheet filed in a Bihar special court. The chargesheet arraigns the company over a bribery FIR involving NHAI officials for alleged non-completion, deviation in executed work, and minor quality irregularities between April 2021 and August 2022.
reports.contingent: Standalone contingent liabilities at March 2026 included about ₹223 crore in disputed taxes. This comprised ₹77.8 crore for income tax from a 2016 search, ₹95.6 crore for sales tax, and ₹49.9 crore for GST. There were also ₹179 crore in funding commitments to group companies.
reports.other: Outstanding dues to MSMEs rose to ₹161 crore from ₹114 crore.
flags: The auditor issued an emphasis of matter regarding a CBI chargesheet against the company over a bribery FIR involving NHAI officials.
The company faces contingent tax liabilities of about ₹223 crore, including an income tax dispute from a 2016 search.

reports.auditor: Walker Chandiok & Co LLP gave an unmodified opinion. They noted a key audit matter on revenue recognition regarding volume and scheme discounts, as well as material-price accruals. The Corporate Governance section stated that independent director Arun Duggal resigned on 13 August 2025, but no reason was found in the read sections of the report.
flags: The auditor noted that the audit trail was not enabled at the database level for the accounting software.
The company faces an Enforcement Directorate FEMA inquiry seeking details on past imports, exports, and foreign investments.
Independent director Arun Duggal resigned in August 2025, and no reason was found in the annual report.
Promoters recently sold shares in the open market, and further supply of shares is possible to meet legal requirements.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unmodified opinion. However, they included a remark noting that an audit trail was not maintained for direct database changes. reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include corporate guarantees of ₹43 crore provided for its subsidiary, Astra Defence Technologies, and ₹80 crore for the ARC joint venture. reports.other: The company operates within a single reportable segment, generating a standalone FY26 revenue of ₹1,156 crore. R&D spending totaled ₹57.8 crore (about 5% of sales), split into ₹55.7 crore of revenue expenditure and ₹2.0 crore in capital. The corporate governance report noted an issue of preferential warrants totaling ₹174 crore, of which 25% (₹43.5 crore) has been received and utilized.
flags: The auditor explicitly remarked that an audit trail was not maintained for direct database changes.
Trade receivables stand at a heavy ₹708 crore, which necessitated a ₹14.8 crore expected-credit-loss provision.
Customer concentration is high, with just three customers accounting for 53% (₹610.5 crore) of total revenue.
The company carries significant off-balance-sheet risks, including ₹123 crore in corporate guarantees for its subsidiary and JV, plus a disputed tax penalty.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unqualified opinion. Key audit matters included revenue cut-off, provisions and contingencies, and the movement of ₹182.91 crore from capital work in progress to fixed assets. The CARO report noted that inventory in quarterly bank statements was ₹44.5 crore to ₹68.1 crore higher than in the company's books each quarter. Creditor balances also differed by up to ₹40 crore.
reports.relatedParties: The company had dealings with a promoter-influenced entity, Amod Stampings.
