Additionally, a promoter LLP named Atlanta UHV Transformers provided a free corporate guarantee of ₹1,320 crore on the company's SBI consortium limits.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities totaled ₹36.6 crore at the end of FY26, up from ₹15.1 crore the previous year. This included ₹33.5 crore for bills discounted but not yet due, plus small tax amounts and legal claims. The company also had ₹42.2 crore in capital commitments at March 2026.
reports.other: The annual report recorded consolidated goodwill of about ₹24.4 crore related to the acquisition of Atlanta Trafo.
flags: Quarterly statements given to banks showed inventory ₹44.5 crore to ₹68.1 crore higher than the company's books, alongside creditor discrepancies of up to ₹40 crore.
The company buys a substantial amount of core material from a promoter-influenced related party, with purchases from Amod Stampings reaching ₹114.6 crore in FY26.
The company relies on a promoter LLP for a ₹1,320 crore free corporate guarantee to support its bank limits.

reports.auditor: The auditor's report highlighted revenue recognition on fixed-price contracts by percentage of completion as a key audit matter, noting it is heavily dependent on judgement. A secretarial audit also found delayed AGM voting results, a late board-meeting notice, late shareholder approval for an independent director, and contra-trades by a designated person.
reports.contingent: The notes show small contingent liabilities of ₹15 crore for tax and legal matters.
reports.outlook: The management discussion and analysis outlines plans to build 'software 2.0' AI-native versions of every product. This includes tabular foundation models called Orion, transit back-office software, and a new security stack. The MD&A also showed long-term loans and advances jumping to ₹129 crore from ₹50 crore.
reports.other: Software services generated ₹933 crore, while equipment and product licences brought in ₹478 crore. The segment result for equipment and licences rose to ₹210 crore from ₹116 crore. Margins improved to about 44% from 29% because the company now owns the full transit stack. The parent company had 2,281 permanent employees. There was also a discontinued operations loss of ₹3.2 crore.
flags: The auditor flagged revenue recognition on fixed-price contracts as a judgement-heavy key audit matter.
A secretarial audit noted fines of ₹11,800 per exchange for delayed AGM voting results and a late board-meeting notice.
The secretarial audit also found contra-trades by a designated person whose profits had to be disgorged.
Long-term loans and advances jumped sharply to ₹129 crore from ₹50 crore.
The annual report recorded a discontinued operations loss of ₹3.2 crore.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. They included an emphasis of matter regarding a subsidiary merger that had no financial impact. The auditor also highlighted the capitalization and impairment of internally developed intangibles, such as software, as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: During FY26, the company borrowed and repaid ₹16 crore from the promoter company. It also sold IT services to promoter entities. There is an outstanding investment of ₹18.9 crore and a loan of ₹7.2 crore to Integrow Asset Management, a related party.
reports.outlook: The report notes that a ₹112 crore building sale will fund the company's AI build-out. It also highlights that the company fully prepaid its ₹56 crore lease-rental-discounting debt in May and June 2026, leaving it free of bank debt.
reports.other: The annual report shows that the company's rental segment was still loss-making for FY26.
flags: The rental segment remained loss-making for FY26.
The auditor raised a key audit matter over the capitalization and impairment of internally developed software.
The company had a one-day delay in filing half-yearly related-party disclosures and required a BSE waiver.
The company carries an outstanding investment of ₹18.9 crore and a ₹7.2 crore loan to a related party, Integrow Asset Management.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unqualified opinion. The only key audit matter was obsolescence provisioning for inventories, which stood at ₹214 crore at March 2026. The CARO report confirms the company is standalone with no subsidiaries.
reports.relatedParties: Sales to related party Meritor HVS (India) Ltd fell from about ₹1,669 crore in FY25 to a small amount in FY26. However, technical and service fees paid to MHVSIL jumped to ₹97.5 crore from ₹10.7 crore. Co-promoter Bharat Forge supplied raw materials and ₹18.5 crore in outside processing.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are very small, consisting of ₹1.5 crore in indirect-tax disputes and ₹0.02 crore for income tax. Outstanding capital commitments at March 2026 were ₹42.7 crore, up from ₹32.0 crore a year earlier.
reports.outlook: The management discussion states that capacity utilisation was about 90% in FY26, and new capacity should be operational by Q3 FY27. The launch of a new bus axle has slipped because it is being redesigned for future pass-by-noise norms. The MD&A lists a limited presence in EV-specific segments as a weakness.
reports.other: The employee-benefit note details a one-off ₹12 crore exceptional charge taken for gratuity and leave liability under the new Labour Codes. The related-party note also records that CFO Ranganathan S left the company on 21 November 2025.
flags: Technical and service fees paid to related party MHVSIL surged to ₹97.5 crore, eating up more than half of the company's net profit.
Co-promoter Bharat Forge now owns a competing axle business and also acts as a supplier, raising the risk of conflicts of interest.
CFO Ranganathan S resigned in November 2025, leaving the company with interim finance leadership.
The management discussion explicitly lists a limited presence in electric vehicle segments as a weakness.

reports.auditor: The auditor, Varma & Varma, gave an unmodified opinion. The audit trail operated all year. The only key audit matter noted was revenue recognition.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings were limited to the pay for key management personnel and a ₹0.5 crore consultancy fee paid to a relative's firm.
reports.contingent: The company had only about ₹2 crore in contingent liabilities. These related to tax and provident fund claims.
reports.other: The largest customer accounted for ₹190.6 crore, which was 11.9% of the revenue for FY26. In FY25, this customer brought in ₹121.4 crore, or 11.1%. Additionally, co-promoter Bhaskar Srinivasan sold a 5.71% stake and left the board in February 2026.
flags: Co-promoter Bhaskar Srinivasan and his family trusts sold a 5.71% stake in a ₹303 crore block deal and he left the board in February 2026.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. They noted one Key Audit Matter regarding the valuation of trade receivables, which are mostly government dues and have no provision made against them.
reports.relatedParties: The Chairman and Managing Director provided an unsecured loan of ₹12 crore to the company during FY26, earning ₹48.6 lakh in interest. The company paid a commission on profits to promoter-directors. It also gave ₹1.21 crore for CSR and ₹0.61 crore in donations to the Lakshmee Foundation, a hospital in Vijayawada. Additionally, the company paid rent and marketing service fees to Wiki Kids Pvt Ltd, a promoter-linked entity.
reports.contingent: The company reported bank guarantees of ₹60.8 crore at the end of March 2026, up from ₹39.4 crore previously. This rise was driven by advances taken against 100% guarantees.
reports.outlook: Management stated that the company has an order book of approximately ₹720 crore, which will be executed across FY27 and FY28. A new 9-acre facility for satellite ground stations is being built at Kondaparva village near Vijayawada, which is expected to become operational by the third quarter of FY27.
reports.other: The company operates as a single 'Electronics & Communication' segment with exports making up just 6.48% of FY26 turnover. Its medical devices subsidiary, Imeds Global Pvt Ltd, posted a ₹7.5 crore loss on ₹1.6 crore in revenue. During FY26, Avantel invested ₹10.1 crore in equity and ₹3 crore in convertible debentures into Imeds. The company also proposed issuing up to 45 lakh shares through ESOPs.
flags: The Chief Financial Officer is the Chairman's wife, indicating a lack of independence from the promoter family.
The company continues to fund its loss-making medical subsidiary, Imeds Global, which has now accumulated ₹18.3 crore in total losses.
The consolidated tax rate is unusually high at 39% because the subsidiary's heavy losses do not receive any tax credit.
The company frequently engages in related-party transactions, including an unsecured loan from the Chairman and donations to a promoter-linked hospital foundation.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unqualified opinion with no emphasis of matter. Key audit matters included revenue recognition, the valuation of financial instruments, and inventory.
reports.relatedParties: Thai Union Group owns 24.21% of the company and provides technical, financial, and marketing collaboration. Avanti pays ₹7.9 crore a year in royalties to Thai Union Feed Mill. Sales to Thai Union entities fell from ₹334.8 crore to ₹12.8 crore in FY26. However, sales to unnamed entities where key management has significant influence rose from almost zero to ₹420.2 crore.
reports.contingent: The company faces a disputed GST demand of ₹2.63 crore in tax and a ₹2.64 crore penalty regarding royalty payments, which is under appeal. It also has ₹3.65 crore in other standalone disputed demands.
reports.outlook: Management noted ongoing business risks from weather events like El Niño and diseases. As part of its current projects, the company is building a new 7,000-tonne shrimp processing plant at Krishnapuram.
reports.other: CMD A. Indra Kumar was paid ₹52.1 crore in FY26, up from ₹46.8 crore the previous year. Total pay for all whole-time directors reached ₹90.9 crore, representing about 10% of profit before tax. Pay above SEBI limits needs a special resolution each time. Additionally, the associate company Patikari Power lost ₹4.16 crore.
flags: Total pay for whole-time directors reached ₹90.9 crore, or about 10% of profit before tax, requiring a special resolution for exceeding SEBI limits.
There is a related-party disclosure gap, as sales to unnamed entities influenced by key management spiked to ₹420.2 crore.
A GST tax demand of ₹2.63 crore and a ₹2.64 crore penalty on royalties are currently under appeal.
The associate company Patikari Power reported a loss of ₹4.16 crore for the year.
The business faces ongoing risks from weather events like El Niño and diseases.

reports.auditor: S.R. Batliboi gave an unmodified opinion but noted several CARO points. They flagged serious delays in depositing ₹59.25 lakh in provident funds, fresh loans given to subsidiaries to repay overdue loans, and missing audit trails for one software. Eleven subsidiaries were audited by other firms, who also flagged CARO clauses. A ₹150.5 crore goodwill balance was listed as a key audit matter, and ₹7.98 crore of goodwill was impaired.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid ₹6.00 crore in legal and professional charges to Aerospace Resource Needs LLP, an entity linked to a director. It leased its DAL facility from associate Aero Electronics, providing a ₹2.8 crore deposit and ₹5.75 crore investment. Advances were made to director-linked Microcon Machine Tech (₹0.31 crore) and BNC Motors (₹0.49 crore). The chairman's travel expenses were ₹1.27 crore.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities included ₹34.6 crore in tax claims and ₹73.4 crore in bank guarantees. There is a ₹9.6 crore service-tax dispute at the Supreme Court and a ₹14.1 crore GST dispute at the Madras High Court. Capital commitments jumped sharply to ₹73.4 crore from ₹0.8 crore.
reports.outlook: Management detailed a major portfolio reset, selling its heavy engineering, auto, energy, and aerospace engineering services to Akkodis. They highlighted significant facility expansion plans, including an indicative ₹600 crore framework for a Missile Atmanirbhar Complex. Management noted that FY26 missed their internal targets of ₹215 crore EBITDA and ₹110 crore net profit because ₹142 crore of revenue, including land-systems and strategic electronics, was pushed out into the next year.
reports.other: The standalone continuing operations of the listed parent lost ₹83 crore before tax in FY26. Operating cash flow for the year was negative ₹1 crore, and free cash flow was negative ₹135 crore. Total net debt including leases reached ₹370 crore. The defence segment achieved a 21.9% margin on ₹378 crore of revenue, driven by sole-source design positions. The report also noted high leadership churn, with three CEO or chair changes since 2024.
flags: The standalone listed parent, stripped of the businesses being sold, lost ₹83 crore before tax in FY26.
The auditor flagged serious delays in depositing provident funds and the issuance of fresh loans to subsidiaries just to repay overdue ones.
Operating cash flow turned negative to minus ₹1 crore, pulling free cash flow down to negative ₹135 crore.
Capital commitments surged to ₹73.4 crore, while net debt including leases increased to ₹370 crore.
There has been significant leadership churn, with three CEO or chairman changes since 2024, alongside a money-losing German subsidiary.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The key audit matter was revenue cut-off. The auditor noted under CARO that the audit trail was not enabled at the database level for one accounting software, meaning direct data changes were not logged. Title deeds for property worth ₹27.2 crore are pledged with banks.
reports.relatedParties: The company has two 51% joint ventures with call and put options. Azad must buy Leo Primecomp's 49% stake in Azad Prime at the higher of fair value or ₹22.6 crore on trigger events, and has paid a ₹5.4 crore non-refundable advance. It also gave a ₹23.3 crore refundable advance to the Azad VTC partner. Azad provided ₹19.6 crore in intercorporate loans to the two subsidiaries at a 10% interest rate.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include a ₹21.9 crore customs duty demand related to EPCG and advance-authorisation export obligations, where discharge certificates are pending despite obligations being largely met. There are direct tax demands of ₹2.0 crore and GST demands of ₹0.2 crore. The company gave a ₹5.1 crore corporate guarantee for its subsidiary, Azad VTC. Capital commitments are ₹118 crore.
reports.other: The company has two small 51% subsidiaries. Azad VTC handles coatings, and Azad Prime is a joint venture with Leo Primecomp. Their FY26 turnovers were small at ₹10.4 crore and ₹8.3 crore, respectively. The Azad Prime subsidiary had negative reserves at March 2026.
flags: The auditor reported that an audit trail was not enabled at the database level for one accounting software, so direct data changes were not logged.
Azad has unusual buyout commitments and advances tied to its tiny joint ventures, including a requirement to buy a partner's stake for at least ₹22.6 crore.
The Azad Prime subsidiary had negative reserves as of March 2026.
There is a ₹21.9 crore customs duty demand because discharge certificates on export obligations remain pending.

reports.auditor: The auditor, Chopra Vimal & Co., gave a clean, unqualified report. The single key audit matter involved estimates of trade discounts and rebates. The report also noted that the SAP audit trail ran all year and was properly preserved.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid a royalty of ₹11.0cr to the promoter company Bajaj Resources, up from ₹9.5cr in FY25. It also paid ₹27.3cr to promoter entities against residential flats with no explanation given. Other dealings included ₹1.1cr in rent to promoter entities, ₹1.5cr in professional fees to a director, and ₹3.5cr in CSR spending through the Kamalnayan Jamnalal Bajaj Foundation.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small, consisting entirely of ₹9.9cr in indirect-tax claims.
reports.outlook: The management discussion states that capacity is not a constraint, as manufacturing relies on a mix of own and third-party units. It highlights that the hair oil category is mature and direct-to-consumer brands are lowering entry barriers. Management also notes that battling for growth outside its core brand is extremely competitive against very large competitors.
reports.other: Loss-making subsidiaries included Uptown Properties (₹0.25cr loss, holding ₹43cr of group goodwill), Bajaj Bangladesh (₹3.4cr loss on ₹15.0cr revenue), and recently acquired VPCL (₹0.39cr loss on ₹51.2cr revenue). The company spent ₹186.6cr to buy back 64.3 lakh shares at ₹290 each, and recommended no dividend for FY26. Naveen Pandey took over as the new MD on 1 July 2025.
flags: The company paid an unexplained ₹27.3cr to promoter entities against residential flats.
A royalty of ₹11.0cr, roughly 1% of sales, is paid to the promoter company Bajaj Resources.
The MD&A sloppily quotes India's hair-oil market at USD 152 million, which contradicts management's claim elsewhere of a 2 billion dollar market.
The core hair oil category is mature, and management notes that direct-to-consumer brands are lowering entry barriers.
The company faces extremely competitive battles against extremely large competitors to grow its non-core portfolio.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters focused on the timing of revenue recognition for distributor sales, inventory ageing provisions, and a ₹190 crore goodwill impairment for Starlite and Nirlep. The report also highlighted an inventory provision of ₹48 crore against a standalone stock of ₹534 crore.

This includes ₹185 crore in GST and sales tax disputes, a ₹28.9 crore E-waste dispute, ₹20 crore in claims, and ₹7.3 crore for income tax. The company also holds ₹10 crore in bank guarantees for its demerged EPC business. Open capital commitments fell to ₹2.9 crore, but future brand instalments require ₹49 crore by March 2027 and ₹43.4 crore by March 2028.

It also highlighted the company is No. 1 in mixer-grinders and No. 2 in water heaters. The Chairman's letter stated a ₹3 per share dividend was maintained despite the annual loss.

flags: The balance sheet contains hidden leverage through ₹1,508 crore of factoring and vendor-finance liabilities.
Contingent liabilities stand at roughly ₹253 crore, driven by a growing ₹185 crore in GST and sales tax disputes.
The company booked ₹91 crore in exceptional charges, heavily driven by goodwill and asset impairments.
Revenue discounts paid to distributors increased to ₹424 crore during the year.

reports.auditor: The auditor's opinion was unmodified. The only key audit matter noted in the report was revenue recognition.
reports.relatedParties: The company recorded sales of ₹51 crore to SVS Sourcings Pvt Ltd, an enterprise where key management has significant influence. It also had ₹11.8 crore in sales and ₹5.7 crore in purchases with MVL Medisynth. The company paid office rents to promoter entities and provided a ₹30 crore loan to its subsidiary Balaji Speciality Chemicals Ltd (BSCL).
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are relatively small at roughly ₹12 to ₹14 crore. This includes ₹5 to ₹7 crore for income tax, which covers disallowed interest on loans to subsidiaries and hotel capital expenditure. It also includes ₹3.1 crore for customs and ₹3.8 crore for GST disputes.
reports.other: The company owns 55% of its subsidiary BSCL. Exports accounted for 14.3% of consolidated revenue in FY26, spanning over 50 countries, with Europe taking 36.8% of these exports. Consolidated borrowings were ₹133 crore. A project bank loan for BSCL is backed by a personal guarantee from the promoters and a pledge of the promoters' shares in BSCL up to 1.5 times the loan amount.
flags: The subsidiary's bank loan is backed by a pledge of the promoters' shares in BSCL up to 1.5 times the loan amount and a personal guarantee.
The company engages in significant related-party trading, including ₹51 crore in sales to an enterprise where key management has significant influence.

reports.auditor: Prateek Gupta & Company gave an unmodified opinion. They noted one key audit matter regarding the recognition of supplier discounts, which are material to the cost of goods sold and net profitability. A subsidiary with ₹1,363 crore in revenue was audited by a different firm.
reports.relatedParties: The company sold about ₹194 crore to promoter-group firms and bought about ₹195 crore from them, plus ₹70 crore for job work and ₹19 crore for fixed assets. Receivables from related parties rose to ₹84.8 crore from ₹31.1 crore, with Bansal Enterprises Inc owing ₹38.5 crore on ₹59.5 crore of sales. A subsidiary guaranteed about ₹100 crore in bank loans for promoter company Bansal Aradhya Steel.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include ₹0.95 crore for GST and an EPCG export obligation of ₹215 crore. A subsidiary had pre-insolvency tax demands, including a ₹17.2 crore penalty, which the Delhi High Court orally set aside on April 22, 2026, awaiting a written order.
reports.outlook: Management targets reaching a 10% market share in two to three years and expects a double-digit EBITDA margin in the medium term. Total capacity is planned to reach about 8.9 lakh tonnes in the coming years.
reports.other: The company reports a single segment, with standalone exports at ₹369 crore in FY26. Return on equity was 11.9% (16.9% in FY25). An independent director resigned in August 2026. The board recommended no dividend. A fire at the Dadri plant caused an estimated ₹1.5 crore inventory loss without physical verification, and depreciation on the damaged machines was not charged.
flags: A subsidiary has guaranteed about ₹100 crore of bank loans for a promoter-group company, Bansal Aradhya Steel.
Receivables from related parties jumped to ₹84.8 crore, with one promoter company owing ₹38.5 crore against just ₹59.5 crore of sales.
The auditor flagged the recognition of supplier discounts as a key audit matter material to cost of goods sold and net profitability.
A fire at the Dadri plant caused an estimated ₹1.5 crore inventory loss that was recorded without physical verification.
The company did not charge depreciation on the machines damaged by the fire while the insurance claim remained unsettled.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unqualified opinion on the financial statements. They also included a Key Audit Matter (KAM) regarding ongoing litigations.
reports.relatedParties: The company reported material related-party purchases and sales. These deals included ₹3,687 crore with BASF Hong Kong and ₹1,029 crore with BASF SE. All these transactions were declared to be at arm's length.
reports.contingent: The company disclosed total contingent liabilities of ₹236 crore. Against these potential claims, it has only made provisions of ₹27 crore.
reports.other: The Board's report shows that exports were ₹348 crore, making up just 2.3% of the total turnover. Additionally, about 65% of input materials by value are sourced within India, meaning roughly a third is imported.
flags: The auditor highlighted ongoing litigations as a Key Audit Matter.
The company faces contingent liabilities of ₹236 crore, but has only provisioned ₹27 crore against them.
There are massive related-party transactions, including ₹3,687 crore with BASF Hong Kong and ₹1,029 crore with BASF SE.

reports.auditor: The auditor, L U Krishnan & Co., noted under an Other Matter that the accounts for Basilic Fly Studio Canada were unaudited and furnished by management. This subsidiary accounted for ₹67 crore in revenue and ₹10.1 crore in profit, which is about a fifth of group profit. Additionally, the UK subsidiaries, contributing ₹287 crore in revenue and ₹7.2 crore in profit, were audited by other auditors.
reports.relatedParties: The standalone accounts show related-party loans with a whole-time director.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were reported as nil.
reports.other: The notes on borrowings show total borrowings of ₹106 crore at March 2026. This includes an HDFC term loan of about ₹19 crore, which is secured by fixed deposits and a pledge of shares. It also includes a UK government-backed Coutts loan of about ₹11 crore and leases.
flags: The Canadian subsidiary's accounts, making up about a fifth of group profit, are unaudited and were just provided by management.
The standalone accounts contain related-party loans with a whole-time director.
A portion of the company's borrowings is secured by a pledge of shares.

reports.auditor: The auditor's opinion is unqualified. The key audit matter noted in the report is revenue recognition across the company's many stores.
reports.relatedParties: Payments to the Bata group are rising. In FY26, the company paid technical collaboration fees to Global Footwear Services of ₹73.6 crore, up 31% from ₹56.1 crore. It also paid brand royalty to Bata Brands of ₹11.6 crore and service fees of ₹6.5 crore. Total group payments were about ₹92 crore, roughly 2.6% of sales, despite falling profits.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small, standing at ₹19.0 crore for FY26 compared to ₹23.8 crore in FY25.
reports.outlook: Management notes competition from global and direct-to-consumer brands at the premium end, and from unorganised players for products below ₹1,000. Manufacturing is being shrunk rather than expanded, with voluntary retirement schemes in place. However, management intends for India to become a sourcing and export hub for the broader Bata group.
reports.other: Bata has a single reportable segment. Exceptional and one-off items in FY26 totaled ₹71.4 crore, comprising ₹42.4 crore for a voluntary retirement scheme, ₹6.7 crore for labour-code gratuity, and a ₹22.4 crore non-cash forex loss. FY26 capital expenditure was only ₹55.4 crore, funded internally without bank borrowings. A dividend of ₹9 per share was proposed, totaling ₹115.7 crore.
flags: Payments to the Bata group are rising and reached about ₹92 crore in FY26, taking up roughly 2.6% of sales while profits fell.
A dollar-denominated Hush Puppies minimum royalty liability caused a ₹22.4 crore non-cash foreign exchange loss due to rupee weakness.
The company has experienced four years of flat revenue while depreciation and group fees rose, causing profit before tax to drop significantly.
The MD & CEO and the Chief Strategy Officer are leaving the company, introducing strategy-reset risk right before a major product relaunch.
ICRA downgraded the company to 'Issuer Not Cooperating' and later withdrew the rating entirely, marking a lapse in disclosure.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unqualified opinion. The key audit matter noted was revenue recognition, specifically concerning year-end price variations.
reports.relatedParties: The annual report lists about 50 promoter-linked entities with heavy trading volumes. In FY26, purchases from Badve Autocomps were roughly ₹477 crore and sales were ₹314 crore. Purchases from Eximiius Autocomps were about ₹344 crore and sales were ₹162 crore. Dealings with Shreepriya Auto included ₹63 crore in purchases, ₹68 crore in sales, and ₹9 crore in rent.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small at roughly ₹21.9 crore, mainly comprising ₹12.1 crore in unpaid indirect taxes. Guarantees include a corporate guarantee for a promoter company loan of ₹41.3 crore and ₹32.0 crore of land pledged for another promoter loan of ₹214 crore. The company also provided massive guarantees for subsidiary loans, including a US$30 million standby letter of credit and a US$68.75 million guarantee for the Dubai trading arm, plus a £13.86 million guarantee for a UK loan.
reports.other: The management discussion notes a UAE trading arm that trades steel and other metals. This business generated ₹1,774 crore in FY26, making up 18.7% of total revenue, but it is low-margin and dilutes consolidated margins. Additionally, the board's report showed the company secretary resigned on 7 June 2026, and the H-One merger scheme was withdrawn and refiled.
flags: The company engages in heavy related-party trading with around 50 promoter-linked entities, involving hundreds of crores in sales and purchases.
The company has provided corporate guarantees and pledged land for loans taken by promoter-owned companies.
Large guarantees were extended for trading and foreign subsidiaries, including a US$68.75 million guarantee for the Dubai arm.
The low-margin UAE trading business dilutes the company's overall consolidated profit margins.
Governance saw some churn with the company secretary resigning in June 2026 and a merger scheme being withdrawn and refiled.

reports.auditor: The consolidated auditor's report provided an unmodified opinion. The analyst noted that there were no key audit matters or emphasis of matter paragraphs found.
reports.relatedParties: The company pays building rent to a promoter company, B.T. Associates. Promoters Rahul Batra and Varun Batra each received a salary of approximately ₹1.51 crore. Additionally, the company made purchases of about ₹26 crore from its subsidiary, Adley Formulations.
reports.contingent: The company reported small contingent liabilities, which consist of consolidated bank guarantees totaling ₹2.3 crore.
reports.other: The directors' report states promoter ownership fell from 64.6% to 59.1% due to debenture conversions and a share swap, with no share sales or pledges disclosed. The company acquired 66.09% of Nivian Lifesciences for ₹69.4 crore, paying ₹20.8 crore in cash and issuing 2,83,668 new shares at ₹1,712.49. Notes also reveal ₹25.9 crore was spent on land for an R&D plan that was subsequently dropped, and the land will be sold.
flags: CRISIL flagged an information availability risk, stating it lacked adequate information from the company to complete its rating review.
The company allocated ₹25.9 crore for land for a corporate office and R&D plan that it then abandoned.
Working capital is stretching, with the cash conversion cycle worsening to 100 days in FY26 compared to 53 days in FY22.
The company posted negative free cash flow for two consecutive years, with outflows of ₹16 crore in FY26 and ₹1 crore in FY25.
The table detailing related-party transactions in the annual report was partly unreadable.

reports.auditor: The auditor raised no qualification or emphasis of matter. However, the auditor listed the impairment of investments and loans to subsidiaries, as well as the fair valuation of investments, as key audit matters. It was also noted that some property title deeds are still in the old company name, Shivdeep Industries.
reports.relatedParties: The company has a history of merging promoter entities, such as Hanuman Agrofood and Vindhyawasini Sales, into the listed company. Additionally, the Bikaji Mega Food Park was divested in May 2025.
reports.contingent: Contingent items are small, including ₹0.62 crore for income-tax matters and a ₹0.36 crore stamp-duty demand. There is also about ₹10.8 crore in deferred duties on bakery machinery under the MOOWR scheme. The company had capital commitments of ₹124 crore at March 2026.
reports.outlook: Management states there is no need for large greenfield capacity since current utilisation is only at about 48%. Instead, the company is targeting higher capacity utilisation by FY29.
reports.other: Several subsidiaries reported losses for FY26. Petunt Food Processors lost ₹5.4 crore and has a negative net worth. Bikaji Foods USA lost ₹4.7 crore, Ariba Foods lost ₹2.7 crore, Bikaji Foods Retail lost ₹2.1 crore, and Bikaji Bakes lost ₹0.6 crore. The report also recorded the death of founder-chairman Shiv Ratan Agarwal in April 2026.
flags: Several subsidiaries are losing money, and Petunt Food Processors has a negative net worth.
The auditor highlighted the impairment of investments and loans to subsidiaries as a key audit matter.
Some property title deeds are still held in the company's old name, Shivdeep Industries.
The company's founder-chairman Shiv Ratan Agarwal passed away in April 2026.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion with no emphasis of matter. The report included a key audit matter on revenue recognition, specifically concerning the percentage-of-completion method on fixed-price contracts and unbilled revenue estimates. The auditor also checked the ageing of unbilled revenue.
reports.relatedParties: Standalone notes show receivables and unbilled amounts from subsidiaries acting as agents reached ₹565 crore, up from zero the prior year. This reflects an intra-group contracting change. These transactions were eliminated in consolidation and stated to be at arm's length.
reports.contingent: Standalone contingent liabilities rose to ₹184 crore from ₹120 crore. This includes ₹105.5 crore in income-tax matters like transfer-pricing and 10A disputes, up from ₹41.1 crore. It also includes ₹68.1 crore for GST and service tax, featuring a ₹47 crore Supreme Court case, and ₹6.5 crore in bank guarantees.
reports.other: The annual report showed total deal wins of $658 million for the year. The company recorded an effective tax rate of 34.4% due to a one-time US federal tax provision and took a ₹40.7 crore exceptional charge for the Labour Code. A note on credit risk highlighted that consolidated unbilled revenue rose to ₹312 crore from ₹189 crore, and receivables increased to ₹901 crore from ₹791 crore.
flags: Standalone contingent liabilities rose to ₹184 crore, driven by a sharp increase in income-tax and transfer-pricing disputes to ₹105.5 crore.
Consolidated unbilled revenue jumped 65% to ₹312 crore, alongside a rise in receivables to ₹901 crore.
Standalone receivables from subsidiaries acting as agents spiked to ₹565 crore from zero the year before, an intra-group contracting change worth watching.
The year included a ₹40.7 crore exceptional charge related to the Labour Code.

reports.auditor: Auditor MSKA & Associates gave an unmodified opinion but included an emphasis of matter. This highlighted delays beyond FEMA timelines covering ₹29.37 crore of import payments, ₹6.73 crore of export proceeds, and ₹3.02 crore of other receipts. Condonation applications are pending, and no penalty has been provided.
reports.relatedParties: Essar group entities buy small amounts of services, around ₹1 to ₹9 crore each, including ₹9.0 crore from Essar Projects in FY26. Dues include ₹6.8 crore from Essar Constructions and ₹6.6 crore from EPC Constructions.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small, consisting of about ₹25 crore in disputed tax, GST, and vendor claims.
reports.outlook: The Board's report states a plan to acquire about $200 to $250 million of revenue a year, which will be funded by internal cash and some debt.
reports.other: Exceptional charges for FY26 were ₹63 crore, including ₹47.3 crore for severance at the US unit BBX Inc., a ₹10.1 crore legal settlement, and ₹5.6 crore for Labour Code matters. The notes show a ₹354 crore receivable against the securitisation of trade receivables. Promoters and non-promoters invested through a preferential warrant issue at ₹417. The dividend payout is about 8%, and the company's credit rating is CRISIL BBB+/A2.
flags: The auditor flagged delays beyond FEMA timelines for import, export, and other receipts, with no penalty provided yet.
The company records recurring expenses as exceptional items every year, including a ₹63 crore charge in FY26 for severance and settlements.
Trade receivables are partly sold or securitised (₹354 crore), meaning reported debtor days understate the true credit given to customers.
Small but persistent related-party dues remain outstanding from Essar group entities.

reports.auditor: The main auditor gave an unmodified opinion and reported no key audit matters. However, an emphasis of matter noted a 2018 Punjab government contract termination that left subsidiary BLS E-Solutions with no revenue. The auditor also found a control gap, as the audit trail edit log was not enabled at the database level. Finally, the main auditor relied on other auditors for 21 subsidiaries, which hold ₹3,523 crore in total assets and ₹1,595 crore in revenue.
reports.relatedParties: The company sold services to related BLS-branded entities where the group has significant influence. This includes a notable jump in sales to a Kuwait entity to about ₹88 crore in FY26, up from ₹33 crore. It also sold to entities in Russia, Argentina, Brazil, and Qatar, and gave small loans to entities in Spain, Chile, Argentina, and Brazil. Additionally, rent was paid to promoter family members, including Diwakar Aggarwal and relatives.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include income-tax demands of ₹10.4 crore, plus a ₹9.6 crore demand for assessment year 2024-25 that is currently under rectification. There are also bank guarantees of ₹2.7 crore and other claims of ₹1.7 crore. Separately, capital commitments stood at ₹31 crore at the end of March 2026.
reports.outlook: The annual report outlines project plans by stating the UIDAI work order is valued at ₹2,055 crore. It also mentions a separate ₹100 crore Aadhaar enrolment order for Bihar.
reports.other: Segment results in the report show the Visa business generated ₹1,840 crore in revenue and ₹738 crore in EBITDA in FY26. The Digital segment earned ₹1,158 crore in revenue and ₹81 crore in EBITDA. The notes also reveal that standalone deposits of about ₹11 crore, along with further amounts in subsidiaries, are pledged against bank guarantees.
flags: The audit trail edit log was not enabled at the database level, which is a real control gap.
The main auditor relied on other auditors for 21 subsidiaries making up ₹3,523 crore of assets and ₹1,595 crore of revenue.
An emphasis of matter highlights a past contract termination in Punjab that left a subsidiary with no revenue, showing government contract risks.
Related-party sales to a Kuwait entity spiked to ₹88 crore from ₹33 crore, which warrants questioning.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The report highlighted revenue recognition and cut-off as a key audit matter, because the company books revenue only when goods arrive at their destination.
reports.relatedParties: The notes show director pay of ₹5.0 crore for Shiven Arora and ₹3.6 crore for Akshay Arora. Promoter-controlled entities from the Blue Circle group are listed as related parties, but the analyst found no large trading flows with them.
reports.contingent: The company has an income-tax dispute with a demand of ₹193 crore for disallowed depreciation on goodwill. It has provided ₹128.7 crore and paid ₹16.5 crore under protest, carrying ₹64.6 crore of interest as a contingent liability. The notes also show capital commitments of ₹69 crore.
reports.outlook: The annual report highlights capacity expansion plans, including a ₹250 crore backward-integration block at the Mahad plant. It also notes greenfield expansion at Vizag, where 102.48 acres of land were purchased for ₹43.5 crore.
reports.other: Customer concentration is extreme, with two clients making up 40.6% and 30.5% of product sales and 84% of receivables. Major geographical markets included Norway (₹383 crore), France (₹335 crore), India (₹95 crore), and the rest of the world (₹129 crore). The company finished the year debt-free with ₹400 crore in liquid assets, and a recent stock issue lowered the promoter stake from 79.81% to 73.15%.
flags: Two customers account for about 71% of product sales and 84% of receivables.
The company faces a ₹193 crore income-tax demand over disallowed depreciation on goodwill, with ₹64.6 crore in interest held as a contingent liability.
Because revenue is booked on arrival, transit delays create a timing risk that can swing quarterly results by ₹20 crore to ₹30 crore.

reports.auditor: The auditor is Deloitte. They gave an unmodified opinion with no emphasis of matter. Their key audit matter focused on cost estimates for fixed-price contracts.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities stood at ₹179 crore at the end of March 2026, down from ₹202 crore the prior year. This was mostly made up of ₹140 crore for income tax and ₹26 crore for GST. The company also reported uncertain tax positions of ₹16.5 crore. Capital commitments were ₹191 crore.
reports.outlook: Management expects the ₹3,500 crore data-centre MEP market to more than double in three years. They forecast industry room AC volumes to grow from 15 million to 30 million units by FY30, though industry margins are drifting down. The company aims for a 15% value share in room ACs. Product plans focus on cost reduction, including indigenising VRF cassette units at the Sri City plant.
reports.other: The company has plants in Himachal, Dadra, Wada, Ahmedabad, and Sri City. The Sri City plant has a capacity of 10.5 lakh split-AC units. In the ₹5,500 crore commercial AC market, Blue Star holds dominant shares of 53% in ducted systems and 48% in scroll chillers. The service network spans over 2,100 service centres, 4,000 channel partners, and 8,800 commercial refrigeration stores. Depreciation is climbing due to the new capacity.
flags: Contingent liabilities stood at ₹179 crore, largely due to disputed income tax and GST claims.
Management warned that room AC industry margins are drifting down over the long term.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The key audit matter was revenue recognition, specifically regarding discounts, rebates, and cut-offs.
reports.relatedParties: The company buys some glassware made at Borosil Scientific's Bharuch plant at roughly cost plus 5%. This accounts for under 10% of sales and was approved by shareholders. Other related party dealings involve shared services and reimbursements with Borosil Renewables and Kheruka family entities.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are negligible. They include an entry tax of ₹0.18 crore, income tax of ₹0.48 crore, and a workers' welfare cess of ₹0.15 crore. There are also bank guarantees of ₹1.1 crore.
reports.other: Promoter Shreevar Kheruka stepped down as MD and CEO, but his remuneration cap of up to ₹10 crore a year was approved. The financial notes also show an inventory write-down of ₹1.45 crore for the year.
flags: A remuneration cap of up to ₹10 crore a year was approved for the promoter after he stepped down as MD and CEO.
The annual report notes an inventory write-down of ₹1.45 crore.
The company relies on a related party, Borosil Scientific, for some of its glassware sourcing.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unmodified opinion. The only key audit matter noted was regarding revenue cut-off and the timing of the transfer of control. This was relevant because of a ₹32 crore timing effect in the fourth quarter.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid a new royalty of ₹1.4 crore to its group company, Borosil Limited, in FY26. It also paid ₹2.3 crore in expense reimbursements to the same company.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were small. They included about ₹14 crore in disputed taxes, ₹54.3 crore in bank guarantees, and ₹12.2 crore in supplier letters of credit. A previous tax demand of ₹19.5 crore for the 2016-17 assessment year was quashed by the Bombay High Court.
flags: The auditor highlighted a key audit matter concerning revenue cut-off and the transfer of control, tied to a ₹32 crore timing effect in Q4 sales.

reports.auditor: The auditor included an emphasis of matter regarding an income tax survey in December 2025, where management made an ad-hoc provision. They also noted a ₹92.2 crore property-tax demand and an arbitration over a ₹8.6 crore deposit. Key audit matters covered revenue recognition, recoverability of investment property, recoverability of ₹11,401 crore in inventory, and ₹578 crore in joint-development deposits.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings were small, and nothing material was seen. This included rent and services with Mysore Holdings for ₹0.36 crore in revenue.
reports.contingent: As of March 2026, contingent liabilities included new GST claims of ₹54.8 crore, service tax claims of ₹42.3 crore, sales tax and VAT of ₹14.9 crore, and bank guarantees of ₹46.8 crore.
reports.other: The board recommended a final dividend of ₹2 per share for FY26, creating a ₹48.9 crore outflow, and a 1:3 bonus issue in May 2026. Promoters pledged only 1.15 lakh shares, or 0.08%. The company saw two CFO changes in 18 months, with Jayant Manmadkar resigning in October 2025 and Yogesh Patel joining on February 2, 2026. Small loss-making subsidiaries included Tetrarch Developers (losing ₹10 crore) and Vibrancy Real Estates (losing ₹5.7 crore).
flags: The income tax department conducted a survey at group premises in December 2025, resulting in an ad-hoc provision.
The company experienced two chief financial officer changes in an 18-month period.
The hospitality subsidiary faces a disputed property-tax demand of ₹92.2 crore.
The company has unprovided contingent liabilities for GST claims of ₹54.8 crore and service tax of ₹42.3 crore.

reports.auditor: The consolidated opinion is clean with no key audit matters. However, 14 foreign and 2 Indian subsidiaries were audited by other auditors. These units represent ₹1,182.7 crore of assets and ₹1,168.7 crore of revenue, forming the majority of the group. On a standalone basis, the parent's exposure to subsidiaries is 34% of total assets, which was flagged as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: Key managerial personnel (KMP) pay was ₹10.7 crore in FY26, up from ₹9.6 crore in FY25. Sales to a KMP-linked entity, Hardware Renaissance Inc, were ₹1.36 crore, but the receivable balance was ₹2.03 crore. The company also invested ₹4.9 crore in Clean Max Sundarban for renewable power.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include ₹34.5 crore for income tax, up from ₹10.2 crore. There is a ₹17.1 crore National Green Tribunal environmental compensation claim for Tarapur, which the Supreme Court stayed after a 30% deposit. Other claims include excise and taxes of ₹19.7 crore, GST/VAT of about ₹3.6 crore, and bank guarantees of ₹5.3 crore. Capital commitments were ₹4.4 crore.
reports.outlook: Management notes that no big capital expenditure is planned. Future growth is expected to come from better use of existing plants. The vanillin and aroma plants currently run at utilization levels below 30%. The Americas remain the primary geographic focus for revenue.
reports.other: Continuing operations reported a loss after tax of ₹31.5 crore, and operating EBITDA was ₹106.9 crore. Exceptional items totaled ₹25.5 crore, including a ₹11.5 crore loan and interest provision, ₹7.6 crore for fire losses, and ₹4.1 crore in Vinpai deal costs. Vinpai was acquired for ₹147.3 crore via a share swap and convertible bonds. India Ratings downgraded the company's bank loans to BBB-.
flags: The annual report states the company will seek waivers for financial covenants covering net worth, liabilities, and debt ratios.
Management pay increased to ₹10.7 crore in a year where continuing operations recorded a loss.
The receivable of ₹2.03 crore from related-party Hardware Renaissance Inc exceeds the entire year's sales of ₹1.36 crore to that entity.
Contingent liabilities for income tax more than tripled to ₹34.5 crore.
The majority of the group's assets and revenue across 16 subsidiaries were audited by other auditors, rather than the principal firm.

reports.auditor: BSR & Co gave a clean opinion but added a modification regarding the audit trail. The new accounting software lacked a SOC report. Because of this, the auditor could not confirm if the database edit log was enabled or check for tampering between April and December 2025. They stated the audit trail was not preserved as required. Revenue recognition for ₹1,758.8 crore in goods sold was highlighted as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: Related party dealings were modest. The company paid about ₹1 crore a year in rent to Kabeer Textiles, an entity influenced by key management personnel. It also paid salaries to relatives. Short-term pay for key management personnel was ₹13.97 crore, up from ₹12.58 crore the previous year.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small, including ₹3.14 crore for GST. The CARO annexure also notes disputed GST dues of about ₹3 crore from 2017 to 2025 at the first appellate stage. An older ₹52.57 crore income tax demand listed the previous year is no longer shown. The company had capital commitments of only ₹5.8 crore at the end of March 2026.
reports.outlook: Management noted that industry demand has been slower to broaden. They plan to consolidate the unit economics of the current retail network before resuming exclusive brand outlet expansion. The report named competition from global brands and direct-to-consumer start-ups in the ₹1,500 to ₹3,000 price band as key risks, along with the threat of counterfeit products.
reports.other: The company operates a single reported segment for footwear. In FY26, it sold 26.0 million pairs at an average selling price of ₹683, with women's products accounting for about 15.8% of revenue. The company manufactures 37.2% of its shoe uppers and 49.6% of its soles in-house, sourcing about 90% of raw materials domestically. Brand awareness rose to 98% and consideration to 66%.
flags: The auditor modified the report because the accounting software lacked an edit log, preventing them from ruling out data tampering for most of the year.
The annual report stated plans to pause store expansion to consolidate unit economics, which conflicts with later management guidance to open up to 100 stores.
The company faces disputed GST dues of about ₹3 crore spanning 2017 to 2025.
Management warned in the report that overall industry demand has been slow to broaden.
The company highlighted risks from counterfeits, global brands, and direct-to-consumer start-ups in its target price bands.

reports.auditor: The auditor identified key audit matters regarding the capitalisation of ₹36.6 crore for internal software development, goodwill impairment testing for a ₹310 crore balance, and the purchase-price allocation for Kognitiv. The auditor also reported that it could not confirm a database-level audit trail at a third-party accounting software provider.
reports.other: By customer location, revenue included ₹408 crore from the USA, ₹113 crore from the UK, and ₹213 crore from other regions. The Kognitiv acquisition cost ₹147 crore net of a ₹25 crore churn indemnity. Capitalised software development was ₹36.6 crore, capex was ₹39.4 crore, and depreciation and amortisation was ₹75 crore. Cash and equivalents stood at ₹483 crore, including ₹323 crore in unutilised IPO proceeds, with borrowings of ₹45 crore. The Singapore-based promoter holding company owned 49.70% of the shares.
flags: The auditor could not confirm a database-level audit trail at a third-party accounting software provider.
The auditor marked the capitalisation of ₹36.6 crore in internal software development as a key audit matter, noting this cost bypasses immediate EBITDA deductions.
A substantial ₹310 crore goodwill balance was flagged as a key audit matter requiring impairment testing.

reports.auditor: The group auditor, Brahmayya & Co, gave an unmodified opinion but noted inventory valuation as a key audit matter. They did not audit five subsidiaries and eight step-down subsidiaries, which account for ₹3,463 crore of assets, ₹2,038 crore of revenue, and ₹303 crore of profit. One step-down subsidiary's accounts were entirely unaudited. Additionally, the auditor noted that the audit-trail edit log was not enabled at the database level for payroll and ledger software.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid about ₹3.7 crore for rent and consultancy to promoter-linked Ashvich companies. It also purchased ₹2.2 crore of solar power from its associate, Sunsole. The Guatemala subsidiary is 69% owned.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are very small. They include ₹0.6 crore for tax, ₹10 crore in letters of credit, and ₹6.7 crore in guarantees.
reports.other: The annual report notes detail two main business segments. The first is emerging markets (Rest of the World) selling branded and plain generics, and the second is the US/regulated markets segment selling sterile injectables and eye drops.
flags: Over 90% of the group's revenue and ₹3,463 crore of its assets were audited by other, mostly overseas, auditors rather than the main group auditor.
One step-down subsidiary's financial accounts were left completely unaudited.
The required audit-trail edit log was not enabled at the database level for the company's payroll and ledger software.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion but included an emphasis of matter. The accounts for Awuko and Foskor were prepared on a non-going-concern basis. This led to ₹134.6 crore in exceptional write-offs, including ₹118.6 crore for Awuko and ₹16.0 crore for Foskor. The auditor also flagged VAW Russia as a key audit matter because its carrying value is ₹1,190.8 crore, representing 22.5% of group assets.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small, totalling under 3% of net worth. These include disputed taxes of ₹47.2 crore, electricity board claims of ₹3.9 crore, and other claims of ₹67.7 crore. The company also reported outstanding capital commitments of ₹63.6 crore as of March 2026.
reports.other: Segment profit before tax was ₹256 crore for Ceramics, ₹97 crore for Abrasives, and ₹91 crore for Electrominerals. Ceramics generates more than half the segment profit despite being only 24% of sales. The report notes that backward integration through mines, fusion, and captive hydel power provides a cost advantage. Exceptional charges of ₹134.6 crore were recorded for Awuko and Foskor. Additionally, ₹297 crore of cash is trapped at the VAW Russia subsidiary due to repatriation restrictions.
flags: The auditor drew an emphasis of matter because the Awuko and Foskor accounts were prepared on a non-going-concern basis, causing ₹134.6 crore in exceptional write-offs.
VAW Russia is a key audit matter as it makes up 22.5% of group assets (₹1,190.8 crore) and operates under international sanctions.
A significant ₹297 crore of cash is trapped at the Russian subsidiary and is not available to the rest of the group due to repatriation restrictions.

reports.auditor: The auditor, Deloitte Haskins & Sells, highlighted direct-tax litigation as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: The company sold ₹774 crore in goods to parent group firm Carraro Drive Tech Italia, which is about 34% of its revenue. It also made payments to the group including ₹85 crore for purchases, ₹27.7 crore for corporate service charges, ₹20.0 crore for professional fees, and ₹9.9 crore for royalty.
reports.contingent: The company has contingent liabilities of ₹210 crore for income-tax disputes, equal to about 37% of its net worth. It also had capital commitments of ₹13.3 crore as of March 2026.
reports.other: Customer concentration increased, with major customers accounting for 48.9% of revenue compared to 43.0% in FY25.
flags: Income-tax disputes total ₹210 crore, representing about 37% of the company's net worth.
The auditor marked direct-tax litigation as a key audit matter.
The company is heavily dependent on its parent group, which accounts for 34% of its sales.
Payments to the parent group for royalty, services, and professional fees equalled around 44% of net profit.
Major customers account for nearly half of total revenue at 48.9%.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. A key audit matter was the impairment of investments in subsidiaries, which have a carrying value of ₹29.9 crore. The company also made small impairments in FY26 on its Turkish appliance venture and Carysil Ceramictech.
reports.relatedParties: The CMD's daughter, Rhea Parekh, is employed as VP of International Marketing, and a pay rise was proposed for her at the AGM. Promoter entity Acrycol Minerals acts as a supplier. Other transactions were tiny, like ₹0.01 crore to Café Chico. New guarantees for subsidiaries were small at ₹1.5 crore.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were negligible at just ₹0.23 crore.
reports.other: FY26 volumes were 7.82 lakh quartz sinks, 1.67 lakh steel sinks, 71,000 appliances, and 36,000 faucets. The US subsidiary, United Granite, reported US$9.7 million in revenue and ₹11.4 crore in EBITDA, turning around from a loss two years prior. UK subsidiary revenues dropped as the local market contracted. A ₹3 per share dividend was proposed.
flags: The auditor flagged the impairment of investments in subsidiaries, carrying a value of ₹29.9 crore, as a key audit matter.
The company had to record small impairments on its Turkish appliance venture and Carysil Ceramictech in FY26.
The UK surfaces business is shrinking, with local subsidiaries reporting lower revenue as the market contracted.

reports.auditor: The auditor's report is clean with no qualification or emphasis of matter. Revenue recognition was the only key audit matter noted.
reports.contingent: The standalone company has income-tax disputes of ₹38.8 crore, of which ₹28.8 crore has been paid under protest. There are also bank guarantees amounting to ₹19.3 crore.
reports.other: The company reached a capacity of roughly 77,000 tonnes a year across India and Vietnam. The large spending phase ended in FY26 after the Vietnam and Indian expansions became operational, which caused capital work-in-progress to fall sharply from ₹450 crore in FY25 to ₹3 crore in FY26.
flags: The standalone business faces contingent liabilities including ₹38.8 crore in income-tax disputes and ₹19.3 crore in bank guarantees.
The parent company's production capacity has been flat for over 10 years, with all new capacity sitting entirely in subsidiaries.

reports.auditor: The auditor's report included a key audit matter regarding revenue. This covered receivables and contract assets, with a focus on estimates for fixed-price and multi-element contracts. No audit qualifications were seen.
reports.relatedParties: The company is family-run by Chairman Rakesh Verma and whole-time director Rashmi Verma. Their son, Rohan Verma, was appointed as Joint MD starting July 1, 2026, with a salary of ₹1.5 crore a year. The report also notes a small related-party lease with Rashmi Verma for up to ₹8.4 lakh.
reports.contingent: The company faces a new GST demand of ₹8.05 crore regarding input tax credits for FY26. It is contesting the claim and has made no provision for it. The company also holds bank guarantees of ₹35.5 crore, up from ₹29.3 crore in FY25, which are backed by fixed deposits.
reports.outlook: The management discussion reported an open order book of ₹1,754.4 crore at March 2026, which includes fixed-price contracts of ₹492.2 crore. Management outlined a capital allocation of about ₹120 crore for organic growth. This is aimed at capitalising rented IoT devices, funding government working capital, and creating intellectual property.
reports.other: In FY26, Map-led revenue was ₹315.5 crore with an EBITDA margin of 47.4%. IoT-led revenue grew 35% to ₹158.6 crore with a 16% margin. The company deployed 1.8 lakh new IoT devices. Small ₹2 crore investments were made in IwayPlus and Prashanth Advanced Survey LLP. International revenue and joint venture losses were not material.
flags: The auditor highlighted revenue recognition, specifically estimates on fixed-price and multi-element contracts, as a key audit matter.
The company is contesting a new ₹8.05 crore GST demand on input tax credits and has not made a provision for it.
The reported ₹1,754.4 crore open order book includes an 18% GST component.

reports.auditor: B S R & Co. gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters included revenue recognition and the purchase-price allocation for Camso, which involved a consideration of ₹236.5 crore for intangibles and no goodwill.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid a licence fee of about ₹26 crore to RPG Enterprises in FY26, up from ₹24 crore in FY25. Promoters H.V. Goenka and Anant Goenka received ₹5.0 crore and ₹4.75 crore respectively as non-executive director commissions. This accounted for ₹9.75 crore of the total ₹10.9 crore non-executive director commissions. A voluntary Deloitte review of related-party processes found no gaps.
reports.contingent: Consolidated contingent liabilities were approximately ₹275 crore in March 2026, up from ₹263 crore, with indirect taxes being the largest at about ₹164 crore. A ₹252.16 crore Competition Commission cartel penalty is not provided for. Capital commitments stood at ₹1,785 crore, rising from ₹706 crore. There is also a US$44 million deferred payment for the Camso brand due three years after acquisition.
reports.outlook: The management discussion stated that capacity utilisation was over 80%. The company produced 4.5 crore tyres in FY26, up from 3.96 crore in FY25. Expansion plans include increasing Chennai passenger car and utility vehicle capacity from 95 lakh to 130 lakh tyres a year by FY28, and Nagpur two-wheeler capacity from 80,000 to 100,000 tyres a day.
reports.other: CEAT operates in a single reportable segment, which is tyres. No single foreign country accounts for more than 10% of its revenue. At March 2026, the parent company had a loan of ₹759 crore (about US$80 million at 8% interest) to CEAT OHT Lanka, and the Sri Lankan rupee exposure cannot be hedged.
flags: A Competition Commission cartel penalty of ₹252.16 crore is pending in the Supreme Court and has not been provided for.
A second Competition Commission case found CEAT and its agent cartelised a 2013 state-transport tender, with a hearing still pending.
A ₹759 crore parent loan to CEAT OHT Lanka carries an unhedged currency exposure to the Sri Lankan rupee.
The annual report's table layout for contingent liabilities was garbled, meaning the reported ₹275 crore total is only an approximation.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave a qualified opinion on standalone internal financial controls for FY26. An ₹8.985 crore bogus purchase fraud by employees colluding with vendors was discovered, and some remediating controls remained untested at the report date. Additionally, the subsidiary auditor included an emphasis of matter noting that the Ludhiana–Rupnagar Greenfield Highway accounts were prepared on a non-going-concern basis after NHAI terminated its concession.
flags: The auditor issued a qualified opinion on standalone internal financial controls following an ₹8.985 crore employee-vendor fraud.
Some remediating internal controls related to the fraud remained untested at the time of the audit report.
The Ludhiana–Rupnagar Greenfield Highway subsidiary had its concession terminated by NHAI and is no longer a going concern.
The company uploaded its annual report as a scanned image PDF, which hinders readability and disclosure accessibility.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave no qualification or emphasis of matter. However, the auditor's report lists the computation of unbilled revenue as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: The company approved a material related-party transaction of up to ₹50 crore among Ceinsys, Allygram, and Grammer AG. Meghe-group entities and relatives also appear in the related-party list, which includes guarantees given to banks.
reports.contingent: The company had no capital commitments at the end of March 2026. Bank guarantees stood at ₹81 crore.
reports.other: The company had 1,104 employees. Two major customers accounted for ₹315 crore, making up 48% of FY26 revenue. The US subsidiary, Technology Associates Inc., reported a turnover of ₹26.1 crore and a loss of ₹22.0 crore. The 70% owned joint venture Allygram posted a ₹46.2 crore turnover and a ₹17.0 crore profit. The board varied the objects of previously raised capital to allow for joint ventures.
flags: Six senior leaders, including the CFO, Vice-Chairman, and CEO-designate, resigned between September 2025 and June 2026.
Customer concentration is severe, with just two clients generating 48% of FY26 revenue.
Unbilled revenue jumped to ₹319 crore (48% of income), which the auditor highlighted as a key audit matter.
The acquired US subsidiary, Technology Associates Inc., recorded a loss of ₹22.0 crore for the year.
The board varied the objects of the raised capital to permit joint ventures after acquisition funds sat idle.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unqualified or clean opinion. The report highlighted one key audit matter, which was verifying the existence of inventory across the company's many different locations.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings were mostly with wholly owned subsidiaries. This included ₹607 crore in purchases during FY26 at the standalone level. These transactions are eliminated in the consolidated accounts, and no large dealings with promoter entities were found.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities included disputed GST and sales tax claims of ₹33.1 crore, up from ₹2.2 crore. There was also a ₹3.7 crore civil claim regarding weights and measures, and an income tax dispute of ₹1.8 crore. The company had capital commitments of ₹45 crore at the end of March 2026.
reports.other: The accounts list a single reportable segment called Consumer Products. FY26 exports were ₹159 crore, down 10%. Notes detail the Wim Plast merger effective May 2026, issuing 46.5 lakh and 16.8 lakh new Cello shares to minority holders. The balance sheet showed a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.01, ₹126 crore in cash, and about ₹535 crore in current investments. The Chairman's letter highlighted the 2025 re-acquisition of the Cello stationery trademark.
flags: Disputed GST and sales tax claims increased significantly to ₹33.1 crore from just ₹2.2 crore.
The auditor flagged the verification of inventory existence across multiple sites as a key audit matter.
Inventory levels rose to ₹833 crore compared to ₹700 crore the previous year.
Annual exports fell by 10% to ₹159 crore.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion and found no emphasis of matter. Key audit matters focused on the estimation of contract revenue, costs, and claims, along with the recoverability of receivables and contract assets.
reports.relatedParties: The annual report lists revenue from approximately 25 Adani group entities as related-party transactions. The exact total amount of these transactions was not calculated in the file.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities totalled about ₹880 crore at March 2026. This included ₹686 crore in claims not acknowledged as debt, ₹105 crore for indirect tax, ₹50 crore for property tax, and ₹38 crore for income tax.
reports.other: The company reports only a single segment, which is Engineering and Construction. The main inputs for its projects are steel, cement, fuel and diesel, bitumen, labour, and subcontractors.
flags: Contingent liabilities stand at about ₹880 crore, representing a substantial 37% of the company's net worth.
The report shows revenue from around 25 Adani group entities, underscoring high group concentration.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Inventory obsolescence for the ₹457 crore balance was highlighted as a key audit matter. A CARO remark noted that audit-trail logging was not enabled for privileged-access changes. It also stated that the lease deed for the KIADB land expired in December 2023, and the title transfer is still pending.
reports.relatedParties: The company plans to build a new plant on land owned by a promoter group private company, though the lease terms are not yet disclosed. Centum Industries Pvt Ltd, a promoter entity, is also listed as a related party stemming from a 2016 slump-sale.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small. They include disputed income tax claims of ₹4.6 crore and disputed indirect tax of ₹9.4 crore.
reports.other: The company booked ₹203 crore in standalone exceptional charges, including a ₹153.8 crore provision on its Centum UK investment and a ₹39.5 crore receivables write-off for its Canadian subsidiary. The company had ₹60 crore of unused QIP funds remaining at the end of March 2026. Promoters hold 46.8% of shares with zero pledges.
flags: Two clients accounted for ₹424 crore or 44% of FY26 standalone revenue, with the top five making up over 65%.
The auditor raised a key audit matter over inventory obsolescence risks for the large ₹457 crore inventory balance.
The company took massive ₹203 crore exceptional write-offs for its UK and Canadian subsidiaries.
The KIADB land lease deed expired in December 2023 and the formal title transfer is still pending.
The auditor noted that audit-trail logging was not enabled for privileged-access system changes.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unmodified opinion, highlighting revenue cut-off as a key audit matter. While the holding company's CARO report was clean, about ten small subsidiary companies were flagged for cash losses. Furthermore, one subsidiary received a qualified report regarding bank stock statements, disputed dues, and an auditor resignation.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings were minor during the year. These included small purchases of under ₹1 crore from Star Cement and Century Led, as well as donations to the Century Charitable Trust.
reports.contingent: The company reported capital commitments of ₹130 crore as of March 2026, up from ₹88 crore a year earlier. Contingent liabilities increased, involving income-tax claims of ₹32 crore (up from ₹0.2 crore) and excise and service tax claims of ₹10.5 crore.
flags: Income-tax claims against the company rose significantly to ₹32 crore from just ₹0.2 crore the previous year.
The auditor flagged about ten small subsidiary companies for incurring cash losses.
One subsidiary received an audit qualification concerning bank stock statements, disputed dues, and an auditor resignation.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion with no emphasis of matter. Key audit matters included expected credit losses on ₹274 crore of receivables, which carry a ₹15.4 crore provision. Revenue presentation net of discounts, incentives, and rebates was also flagged as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: Key managerial personnel remuneration was ₹20.4 crore in FY26, up from ₹19.0 crore in FY25, representing about 10% of profit after tax. The company paid ₹1.3 crore in rent to Madhusudan Industries, a promoter entity. Promoters held a 54.4% stake with no pledges seen.
reports.contingent: Claims not acknowledged as debt jumped to ₹29.1 crore in March 2026 from ₹2.2 crore. This is primarily a ₹28.7 crore income-tax demand for FY2019-20 at CIT (Appeals). GST disputes added about ₹2.6 crore. The company also had ₹7.6 crore in letters of credit and guarantees, and ₹2.1 crore in capital commitments.
reports.outlook: The management discussion cited industry estimates projecting the Indian sanitaryware market to reach about $1.34 billion by 2030. It noted that organised players currently make up roughly 60% of the domestic market.
reports.other: Company-reported FY26 metrics showed declines, with EBITDA margin at 15.3% (down from 17.9% in FY25), ROCE at 17.8% (down from 21.4%), and ROE at 14.5% (down from 18.3%). FY26 capex for buildings and plant was ₹21.95 crore, resulting in a gross block of ₹616 crore. Borrowings consisted solely of lease liabilities. The sale of two LLPs generated a ₹5.5 crore profit booked in other income.
flags: Claims not acknowledged as debt spiked to ₹29.1 crore, largely due to a ₹28.7 crore income-tax demand for FY2019-20.
Key managerial personnel remuneration was high at ₹20.4 crore, absorbing roughly 10% of the profit after tax.
The auditor highlighted expected credit losses on receivables, requiring a ₹15.4 crore provision.
Return ratios and margins deteriorated in FY26, with ROCE falling to 17.8% and EBITDA margins dropping to 15.3%.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Revenue cut-off was highlighted as a key audit matter, and the audit trail was maintained.
reports.relatedParties: The company bought ₹26.0 cr of goods in FY26 (₹26.6 cr in FY25) from Finor Piplaj Chemicals, an entity influenced by the Shah family. This was roughly 15% of material costs, with ₹3.4 cr payable at year-end. It also bought ₹2.9 cr from, sold ₹1.3 cr to, and received ₹40 lakh rent from sister listed company Chembond Material Technologies. The pricing basis was not disclosed. Pay was ₹2.0 cr for the CMD and ₹1.5 cr for the water-subsidiary ED.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were small at ₹0.54 cr. This consisted of ₹0.43 cr for GST and ₹0.11 cr for income tax.
reports.outlook: The management discussion noted the company is asset-light with inherently flexible plant capacity. No new plant is planned. The FY26 capital expenditure of roughly ₹21 cr was primarily for demerger asset re-tagging and office renovation.
reports.other: Revenue from India was ₹317 cr and overseas was ₹8.8 cr. Other expenses included a ₹4.4 cr write-back of the expected-credit-loss provision, which was about 10% of profit before tax. The cash-flow statement showed weak conversion, with operating cash flow of only ₹8 cr against ₹35 cr in net profit. Receivable ageing showed ₹114 cr net, with only ₹7.6 cr not yet due, ₹99 cr up to 6 months overdue, and ₹6.7 cr fully provided.
flags: The company bought ₹26.0 cr in materials from a promoter-linked entity without disclosing the pricing basis.
Cash flow from operations was extremely weak at just ₹8 cr compared to a net profit of ₹35 cr.
FY26 profit quality was lowered by a ₹4.4 cr expected-credit-loss provision write-back.
Receivables are heavily stretched, with ₹99 cr up to six months overdue and only ₹7.6 cr not yet due.

reports.auditor: The auditor highlighted onerous contracts and the net realizable value write-down of inventory as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: The company pledged its shareholding in the group company TCI Sanmar to that company's lenders. It also provided a corporate guarantee of ₹332 crore to SIPCOT for a soft loan to its subsidiary CCVL, with ₹77 crore drawn so far.
reports.contingent: Standalone contingent liabilities included ₹55 crore for direct tax, ₹22 crore for indirect tax, and ₹16 crore for other items. The company also had standalone capital commitments of ₹302 crore.
reports.outlook: Management noted that Indian demand for paste PVC is roughly 1.92 lakh tonnes and is growing at 7 to 8 percent annually. They highlighted trade policy risks, pointing out that a quality control order on PVC was rescinded in November 2025.
reports.other: The company reported a standalone net loss of ₹1,003 crore for FY26 after taking a huge ₹898 crore impairment on its investment in subsidiary CCVL, cutting its book value from ₹1,556 crore to ₹658 crore. A single customer accounted for ₹291.6 crore, or about 13 percent of standalone revenue. Managing Director Ramkumar Shankar left on 31 March 2026.
flags: The auditor made onerous contracts and inventory write-downs a key audit matter.
The company booked a massive ₹898 crore impairment on its CCVL subsidiary, leading to a standalone net loss of ₹1,003 crore.
Shares in group company TCI Sanmar have been pledged to support that entity's lenders, posing a cross-group exposure risk.
Managing Director Ramkumar Shankar exited the company at the exact close of the financial year on 31 March 2026.
Management flagged trade policy risks after a quality control order on PVC was rescinded in November 2025.

reports.auditor: The auditor provided an unmodified opinion. They included a Key Audit Matter regarding revenue recognition, which specifically highlighted significant related-party transactions and the need to test that they were conducted at arm's length.
reports.relatedParties: Mahindra & Mahindra is the largest customer, generating ₹1,893 crore in CY2025 sales, making up 20% of consolidated and 30% of India revenue. The company is seeking approval for up to ₹2,300 crore a year in M&M sales. European subsidiaries also participate in a cash pool with the Spanish parent. In CY2025, they borrowed €139.3 million and lent €25.2 million to the parent, and are asking shareholders to approve up to €504 million a year for these flows.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities totaled about ₹147 crore at the end of December 2025, representing around 2% of net worth. These consisted of ₹52.7 crore for power surcharges, ₹32.5 crore for water charges, ₹22.4 crore for income tax, ₹15.6 crore for stamp duty and cess, ₹13.8 crore for excise, and ₹4.5 crore for new customer claims. Capital commitments stood at ₹107.5 crore, up from ₹81 crore the previous year.
flags: The auditor flagged revenue recognition as a Key Audit Matter due to the high volume of significant related-party transactions.
The company depends heavily on related party Mahindra & Mahindra, which accounted for roughly 20% of consolidated revenue.
Shareholders are being asked to approve massive cash-pooling flows with the Spanish parent company of up to €504 million annually.
The company faces roughly ₹147 crore in contingent liabilities involving multiple disputes over power, water, and taxes.

reports.auditor: B S R & Co. gave an unmodified opinion but noted key audit matters on percentage-of-completion revenue of ₹386 crore and impairment of ₹16,729 crore for plant and capital work-in-progress. They flagged that an audit trail was not enabled at the database level for the holding company and 32 subsidiaries until 27 March 2026. CARO remarks highlighted issues with title deeds and late statutory dues, including ₹24 crore and ₹73 crore of FY26 advance tax paid 6 to 9 months late. Twelve subsidiaries had cash losses.
reports.relatedParties: There were about 35 material related-party resolutions with subsidiaries at the July AGM covering intra-group EPC, loans, and guarantees. A September corrigendum changed the tenure of related-party transaction approvals. Transactions with Brookfield entities were small and mostly for rent and rooftop power.
reports.contingent: Contingent items include tax claims of around ₹98 crore, bank guarantees of ₹1,037 crore, and capital commitments amounting to ₹831 crore. There are also put options to buy back the 26% equity stakes held by clients at fair value.
reports.other: At the end of March 2026, founders Kuldeep Jain and KEMPINC LLP had pledged 11,597,866 shares to 360 ONE Prime for KEMPINC borrowings. This represents about 9.9% of the company, roughly half of the founder group's holding.
flags: An audit trail was not enabled at the database level for the holding company and 32 subsidiaries until 27 March 2026.
Advance tax payments of ₹24 crore and ₹73 crore were paid six to nine months late.
The auditor noted that 12 subsidiaries reported cash losses.
The founders have pledged about 9.9% of the company's shares for borrowings.
The company faces contingent tax claims of approximately ₹98 crore.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The only key audit matter mentioned was revenue recognition and cut-off.
reports.contingent: The company reported contingent liabilities of just ₹15 crore.
reports.outlook: Management highlighted new growth from hindered amine light stabilisers (HALS) produced by its wholly owned subsidiary. A new hydroquinone and catechol plant with a 10,000-tonne capacity was commissioned in December 2025, offering a revenue potential of ₹260 crore to ₹300 crore at full use.
