The subsidiary also benefits from a concessional tax rate and an SGST refund scheme.
reports.other: In FY26, standalone sales came from performance chemicals (72%), pharma and agro (19%), and FMCG (9%). Exports made up 61% to 67% of consolidated revenue. The company also secured REACH registration for the EU. Managing Director Siddharth Sikchi received ₹6.2 crore and Ashok Boob received ₹4.0 crore. This pay dropped 27% to 57% after the promoters gave up most of a bonus worth about ₹11 crore.
flags: A single customer accounted for 13.3% of standalone revenue (₹106 crore) in FY26, up from 10.8% in the previous year.

reports.auditor: The statutory auditors, Walker Chandiok, reported a suspected fraud to the Audit Committee following a whistle-blower complaint. The company claimed it investigated and found no material financial impact, but the amount was undisclosed. Auditors noted the SAP database lacked an enabled audit trail and could not comment on the third-party-hosted SAP Rise system. Impairment of investments in subsidiaries was a key audit matter.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were modest at ₹53 crore for tax and other matters. Consolidated capital commitments stood at only ₹39 crore as of March 2026.
reports.outlook: Management stated that FY26 revenue was hurt by destocking in two large commercial molecules, leading to about ₹260 crore in lost revenue. Disruption at the Nacharam formulation site cost another ₹61 crore. The company plans a capital expenditure of around ₹300 crore for FY27.
reports.other: The company recorded ₹1,284 crore in consolidated goodwill. For recent acquisitions, it paid ₹258 crore for a 67.5% stake in Sapala and booked a ₹226 crore liability to buy the rest. It also bought 56% of NJ Bio for ₹548 crore. At year-end, net cash was ₹152.7 crore, with operating cash flow of ₹368 crore and free cash flow of ₹173 crore.
flags: Statutory auditors reported a suspected fraud to the Audit Committee under Section 143(12) based on a whistle-blower complaint.
The SAP system audit trail was not enabled at the database level, and auditors could not verify the third-party-hosted system.
The US FDA issued a Warning Letter for the Nacharam formulations site in January 2026.
The company recorded a one-off inventory provision of ₹19.5 crore and a customer settlement of ₹12.6 crore.
Consolidated goodwill is high at ₹1,284 crore, with subsidiary impairment marked as a key audit matter.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unmodified opinion. The timing of revenue recognition (cut-off) was highlighted as the key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: Transactions included family remuneration and rent paid to Sudhir, Ankur, and Megha Vaid. The company also made a ₹0.66 crore investment in Celliimune Biotech and provided small loans to its subsidiary Stellon Biotech.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were small at ₹3.9 crore, relating to excise and income tax disputes.
reports.other: The company claims a leading global share in immunosuppressant APIs. Customer concentration has decreased, with the top 10 customers accounting for 37.6% of revenue in FY26, down from 48.2% in FY21. Total receivables stood at ₹465 crore at the end of March 2026.
flags: Out of ₹465 crore in total receivables, about ₹68 crore was overdue by more than six months and roughly ₹40 crore by more than a year.
The auditor flagged revenue-recognition cut-off as a key audit matter.

reports.auditor: The statutory auditor, Seth & Associates, issued an unmodified audit opinion. However, because the company is listed on the SME exchange, the accounts do not include key-audit-matter reporting. The auditor was paid a total fee of only ₹4.18 lakh for the year for the entire group.
reports.relatedParties: The company reported FY26 sales of ₹10.2 cr to associates and common-control entities, up from ₹0.6 cr the prior year. It also made purchases of ₹3.2 cr, investments of ₹18.4 cr, and earned interest income of ₹0.6 cr from them. The company has a net borrowing of roughly ₹6.3 cr from key management personnel. Outstanding receivables include ₹13.4 cr from private companies where a director is a member or director, and ₹0.85 cr from firms where a director is a partner.
reports.contingent: The company provided guarantees to banks and third parties amounting to ₹20.9 cr. It also has claims not acknowledged as debts totaling ₹0.15 cr.
reports.other: The annual report notes that fixed assets increased to ₹43 cr from ₹23 cr. A goodwill of roughly ₹12.9 cr was added following the Fusion business combination. Total trade receivables reached ₹121.3 cr, representing more than half of the company's FY26 revenue. The corporate governance report shows the company raised funds through a ₹50.1 cr preferential cash issue, share-swap issues, and a bonus share issue. The joint managing director also serves as the chief financial officer.
flags: Operating cash flow was deeply negative at −₹55 cr in FY26, resulting in a 375-day cash cycle where profits are not converting to cash.
Trade receivables spiked to ₹121.3 cr, which makes up more than half of the company's total revenue for the year.
Sales to related parties jumped 16x alongside ₹14.25 cr in receivables owed by companies linked to the directors.
The joint managing director simultaneously holds the position of chief financial officer, presenting a potential governance conflict.
The statutory auditor was paid an unusually low fee of just ₹4.18 lakh for the entire group.

reports.auditor: Deloitte Haskins & Sells issued an unmodified opinion with no key audit matters on the standalone accounts. The audit trail operated correctly with no tampering noted.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings were small. Key management personnel received about ₹10.4 crore in pay. The company paid about ₹2.4 crore in rent to promoter relatives and made a few crore in purchases from its associate La Chandra Pharmalab.
reports.contingent: The company reported only ₹2.0 crore in contingent liabilities, which related entirely to tax matters.
reports.other: The company reported being the fastest-growing among India's top 30 drug companies. FY26 domestic sales were led by women's health (27.5%), cardio-diabetes (25.4%), and pain (11.4%). The company owns 79 brands and noted a track record of growing acquired brands. It holds a 31.15% stake in associate La Chandra Pharmalab. Research and development spending increased to ₹25.1 crore from ₹11.8 crore.
flags: The recent IPO was a pure offer-for-sale, meaning the company received no new money.
FY26 profit included a one-time ₹19.1 crore charge for new labour codes.

reports.auditor: The auditor highlighted a key audit matter regarding significant outstanding advances to a related party for buying raw materials and capital assets. Under CARO, the auditor noted that quarterly stock statements given to banks differed from the company's books by up to ₹6 crore each quarter. They also found audit-trail gaps for fixed assets, inventory, and cost records, and reported that subsidiary NSEPPL's software lacked an audit trail.
reports.relatedParties: The company deals with Prilika Enterprises, a promoter entity holding about 10%. Prilika sold the springs business to Cosmic via a business transfer agreement, with ₹9.75 crore paid in FY25, ₹9.75 crore advanced for another unit, and ₹9.75 crore yet to be executed. Prilika also rents out premises and performs job work for the company. There was a ₹10.3 crore trade payable owed to Prilika as of March 2025.
reports.contingent: The annual report notes a ₹10.3 crore claim from Cosmic Ferro Alloys currently in arbitration, stemming from a January 2022 business transfer agreement. The company has also provided a ₹49 crore corporate guarantee for its subsidiary, NSEPPL.
reports.other: The management discussion notes the group operates as a single business segment. The directors' report states that ₹100 crore from a March 2025 preferential issue is kept in fixed deposits, while ₹74 crore was spent on capex and subsidiaries. A subsidiary paid ₹20 crore to Sagacious Capital to participate in acquiring new units through insolvency. Term loans are about ₹35 crore, and working-capital lines are roughly ₹80 crore. Trade receivables doubled to ₹205 crore.
flags: The auditor raised a key audit matter over significant year-end advances given to a related party.
Quarterly stock statements submitted to banks did not match the accounting books, differing by up to ₹6 crore each quarter.
The auditor found missing audit trails for fixed assets, inventory, and costs, while a subsidiary's software completely lacked an audit trail.
The company faces an ongoing arbitration dispute over a ₹10.3 crore claim from Cosmic Ferro Alloys.
Trade receivables doubled to ₹205 crore, which includes ₹5.5 crore that is over three years old.

reports.auditor: The standalone auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters included derivative valuation and the recognition of state incentive income, which required judgement on eligibility and timing. Under CARO, the auditor noted that stock statements submitted to banks differed from the company books due to unreported advances from subsidiaries and provisional figures, though there were no defaults.
reports.relatedParties: A ₹10 crore loan given to the chairman in FY25 was repaid during the year. A ₹0.47 crore loan to CEO Pankaj Poddar was also repaid in FY26. Additionally, CSR funds were directed to promoter-linked charities, including ₹2.8 crore to the Sitaram Jaipuria Foundation and ₹3.3 crore to the Cosmo Foundation.
reports.contingent: Consolidated contingent liabilities include ₹101 crore in bank guarantees to third parties (up from ₹61 crore), excise and service-tax disputes of ₹48.6 crore, income tax demands of ₹9.1 crore, and other claims of ₹7.2 crore. Unexecuted capital commitments fell to ₹43 crore at March 2026 from ₹123 crore.
reports.outlook: Management notes total BOPP capacity reached 2,77,000 tonnes a year after a new line started in June 2025, alongside capacities for BOPET, CPP, coated, metallised, and other specialty films. Exports reached ₹1,592 crore to over 100 countries. Looking ahead, the company plans to commission an 18,000-tonne coating line in FY27 and targets ₹200 crore in revenue for Cosmo Consumer by FY30.
reports.other: The company held ₹420 crore in cash and liquid investments at year-end. The Zigly pet care business acquired two veterinary hospitals in Mumbai and Bengaluru. Total short-term pay for key management reached ₹52.7 crore, up from ₹30.7 crore in FY25. The company only discloses two reporting segments in the report: packaging and specialty chemicals.
flags: Chairman Ashok Jaipuria received ₹24.4 crore in remuneration, which is 387 times the median employee salary.
Total short-term pay for key management was ₹52.7 crore, consuming roughly a third of the entire ₹156 crore consolidated net profit.
Stock statements provided to banks did not match the company's books due to unreported subsidiary advances and provisional figures.
The annual report lacks disclosure on film volumes, revealing information for only two broad segments.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. A Key Audit Matter was accounting for property, plant, and equipment, focusing on useful lives and impairment. An audit trail is in place. Under CARO, disputed income tax, GST, and service tax dues are noted as small, with the largest being an income tax dispute of about ₹19 crore.
reports.relatedParties: The report notes no related-party issues other than family pay. The Chairman and Managing Director's pay rose 112% in FY26 to about ₹11.9 crore, comprising a ₹6.05 crore salary and ₹5.86 crore commission. This is 169 times the median employee pay. His son, the whole-time director, was paid about ₹4.0 crore, an increase of 108%.
reports.contingent: Capital commitments not provided for were ₹785 crore, up from ₹491 crore the previous year. The company had bills discounted of ₹157 crore at the end of March 2026, rising from ₹86 crore previously. There are also small disputed tax dues, led by an income tax claim of about ₹19 crore.
reports.other: The Directors' Report states that subsidiaries DR Axion and Sunbeam Lightweighting are being merged, which is expected by the end of FY27. In FY26, DR Axion had a turnover of ₹1,619 crore. Sunbeam had a turnover of ₹1,397 crore but reported a loss of ₹40 crore. The acquired German subsidiary recorded a turnover of ₹346 crore and a profit of ₹16.7 crore.
flags: The Chairman's pay rose 112% to ₹11.9 crore, representing 169 times the median employee salary.
The whole-time director's pay increased by 108% to about ₹4.0 crore.
Subsidiary Sunbeam Lightweighting reported a loss of ₹40 crore for the year.
Capital commitments not provided for jumped to ₹785 crore from ₹491 crore.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion and noted under CARO that the audit trail operated throughout the year with no tampering. Key audit matters included the Butterfly impairment and impairment testing for ₹779 crore of goodwill from the 2015 demerger.
reports.contingent: Standalone contingent liabilities included income tax of ₹143.9 crore, GST/VAT of ₹222.6 crore, excise and customs of ₹11.3 crore, and third-party claims of ₹32.8 crore. EPR e-waste liabilities were ₹83.8 crore due to a legal challenge over floor prices. Capital commitments were ₹11.4 crore, and previous guarantees of ₹249 crore for Butterfly ended.
reports.other: Consolidated profit before tax and exceptional items was ₹677 crore, with lighting revenue at about ₹1,083 crore. The company booked ₹754.9 crore in standalone exceptional items, consisting of a ₹716 crore impairment on Butterfly investments and trademarks, ₹20.4 crore for Vadodara plant restructuring, and ₹18.5 crore for the new Labour Code. The company is net cash positive and debt-free after repaying its final NCD tranche.
flags: The company took a massive ₹716 crore exceptional write-off to impair its investment and trademarks in Butterfly.
The auditor flagged the Butterfly write-off and testing for ₹779 crore of historical goodwill as key audit matters.
The company faces significant contingent tax liabilities, including ₹222.6 crore for GST/VAT and ₹143.9 crore for income tax.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion and stated that the audit trail operated all year. Key audit matters included the valuation of goodwill and investments, fixed-price revenue recognition, receivables, and inventories.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were ₹82 crore. This mainly consisted of a ₹55 crore service tax claim and a ₹15 crore GST claim.
reports.other: The company factors some of its receivables without recourse. The report also showed no pledge of promoter shares.
flags: Goodwill stood at ₹1,972 crore at the end of March 2026 before recent acquisitions, which was flagged as a key audit matter.

reports.auditor: S.R. Batliboi & Associates (EY) gave an unmodified opinion and noted the audit trail operated all year. They tested the ₹71.8 crore goodwill on the Altek acquisition as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: The notes detail a ₹44 crore advance to Cyient Israel on the balance sheet. They also log key management personnel changes, noting the CEO, CFO, and two independent directors resigned in 2025, and the new CEO joined from the parent company, Cyient.
reports.contingent: The company disclosed no contingent liabilities as of March 2026. It reported capital commitments of ₹7.8 crore.
reports.other: The management discussion noted profit was flattered by a ₹19.6 crore non-taxable earn-out reversal because the acquired Altek unit missed targets. Normalised profit was ₹56.3 crore, falling 24%, with normalised EBITDA at ₹130.2 crore or 10.3%. The report also highlighted high customer concentration. Customers each contributing over 10% of revenue together accounted for ₹702.8 crore, or 55.7% of FY26 revenue, compared to ₹1,051.7 crore, or 69.2%, in FY25.
flags: High management turnover occurred in 2025, with the CEO, CFO, and two independent directors resigning.
Reported profit was inflated by a ₹19.6 crore earn-out reversal because the Altek acquisition missed its targets.
Revenue is highly concentrated, with major customers accounting for 55.7% of total FY26 revenue.
The balance sheet carries a ₹44 crore advance to Cyient Israel, which exposes the company to regional risks.

reports.auditor: Deloitte Haskins & Sells issued an unmodified opinion. Revenue recognition regarding control transfer and cut-off was named a key audit matter. The auditor noted an audit-trail gap in a third-party payroll software that was not enabled on 1–2 April 2025, and they were unable to comment on it for January to March 2026.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings are clean with no material transactions. Promoters S. Rangarajan and Rekha Rangarajan hold 22.8% and 19.0% respectively, with the total promoter holding flat at 42.41% for three years. Key management personnel pay was ₹4.3 crore.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are tiny at ₹6.9 crore for income, sales, and service taxes. There are about ₹5 crore in disputed dues that have not been deposited. Capital commitments stand at ₹36.6 crore. The company has given sizeable bank guarantees of ₹677.7 crore, backed by lien-marked deposits.
reports.outlook: Management notes the company is building nine floors of new factory space at its Chennai campus. They highlighted investments of over ₹135 crore in new products. Depreciation has risen as earlier capitalized product development costs are now being amortized.
reports.other: The company operates one reportable segment for defence electronics. Geographically, India accounted for ₹863 crore, while exports fell to ₹61.8 crore. Other income dropped to ₹25 crore as QIP cash was spent, though ₹37.65 crore remained unspent at March 2026. The cash conversion cycle was reported at 365 days.
flags: Bank guarantees given stand at ₹677.7 crore, which is sizeable compared to the net worth of ₹1,736 crore.
The auditor flagged an audit-trail gap in a third-party payroll software and could not comment on it for January to March 2026.
Exports shrank from 15% of revenue in FY25 to just 6.7% in FY26.
The company wrote off ₹2.9 crore in liquidated damages in FY26, showing occasional delivery penalties.

reports.auditor: The auditor's report highlighted key audit matters regarding the company's fixed-price revenue and percentage-of-completion accounting, driven by rising unbilled revenue. The auditor also flagged the significant goodwill balance of ₹611 crore as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: The promoter family holds a 66.33% stake and manages both the parent company and its subsidiaries. Sameer Kanodia serves as the CEO of both Lumina and TNQ. The annual report stated that all related-party dealings were conducted in the ordinary course of business, with none being material.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small, consisting of ₹11.0 crore for disputed income tax and ₹0.6 crore for GST. The company also reported outstanding bank guarantees of ₹54.0 crore. Capital commitments stood at ₹13.6 crore at the end of March 2026.
reports.outlook: The annual report outlines very light capital expenditure plans, mostly focused on upgrading older office buildings, as growth capital is primarily directed toward acquisitions. The report also notes that currency exposure is hedged using forward contracts.
reports.other: The company has eight of its own products that generate some intellectual property-led revenue, though the exact revenue breakdown is not disclosed. Additionally, borrowings include a ₹150 crore acquisition loan that is secured by asset charges and a pledge of TNQ shares.
flags: The auditor raised a key audit matter over fixed-price revenue accounting due to rising unbilled revenue.
The auditor flagged the significant ₹611 crore goodwill balance as a key audit matter.
The company pledged its shares in TNQ to secure a ₹150 crore acquisition loan.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an Emphasis of Matter for several unprovisioned disputes. These include a ₹54.9 crore electricity tax case pending in the Supreme Court, a ₹12.4 crore customs dispute with a ₹26 crore fine, and a November 2023 tax search that reduced MAT credit by ₹28.9 crore. They also highlighted a state government order to repossess 793 acres of plant land. Key audit matters included provisions, contingent liabilities, and deferred tax.
reports.relatedParties: Key management and their relatives received ₹20.4 crore in pay for FY26. Three managing directors received an additional ₹6.6 crore in commission. Saatvik Jain, the President and a relative of a managing director, received a ₹10 crore performance bonus. Altogether, the promoter family and key managers took home nearly ₹37 crore, compared to a total net profit of ₹48 crore.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities totaled ₹193.6 crore in FY26. This includes ₹93.7 crore for lease rent, cess, electricity, and water, of which ₹31.8 crore relates to river-water charges under an agreement that expired in 1995. Other disputed claims include ₹40.3 crore for customs, ₹30 crore for income tax, ₹12.3 crore for excise and GST, and ₹10.8 crore for sales tax. Capital commitments stood at ₹36.6 crore.
reports.outlook: The annual report notes that basic chemical plants are running at essentially full capacity, leaving no room for volume growth except in the newly expanded CPVC segment. Management has ruled out expanding basic chemical volumes or investing in backward integration for raw materials like VCM, stating that the plant's capacity is too small to justify it.
reports.other: Basic Chemicals generated ₹1,538 crore or 71% of revenue, but made only ₹0.4 crore in segment profit with low margins of 2.4% to 3.5%. Specialty Chemicals generated ₹592 crore, but made ₹131.8 crore in profit, contributing 80% of total earnings with margins around 30%. A share-neutral merger of promoter holding companies into DCW took effect in February 2026.
flags: The auditor highlighted an unprovisioned ₹54.9 crore electricity tax dispute and a ₹12.4 crore customs claim with a ₹26 crore fine.
A November 2023 income-tax search led to orders cutting the company's available MAT credit by ₹28.9 crore, along with penalty notices.
The state government ordered the repossession of 793 acres of land at the Sahupuram plant because assignment deeds were never executed.
Contingent liabilities are high at ₹193.6 crore, which includes a ₹31.8 crore claim for river-water charges from an agreement that expired in 1995.
The promoter family and key managers were paid nearly ₹37 crore, including a ₹10 crore bonus to a promoter relative, which is very high against a ₹48 crore net profit.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unmodified opinion on the financial statements. They identified revenue recognition and the valuation of inventory, which stood at ₹392 crore at the end of March 2026, as key audit matters.
reports.relatedParties: The company reported related-party purchases of roughly ₹13.4 crore in FY26 from Kkalpana Industries (India) Ltd, the group company from which DDev was demerged in 2022. While a royalty of ₹4.6 crore was paid to Kkalpana in FY25, this was nil in FY26. Additionally, the company pays rent to its promoter entity, Bbigplas Poly.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were relatively small, consisting of income tax demands of about ₹2.2 crore and other demands of ₹9.2 crore. The company also disclosed bank guarantees of ₹24 crore and capital commitments amounting to ₹75 crore.
reports.outlook: The report highlights the development of a water-tree-retardant XLPE product, an import substitute that was tested at a German lab. It notes that achieving certification for the next voltage level (220 kV) will require three to four years of field performance.
reports.other: The annual report stated a capacity utilisation of 75% for the year. It showed FY26 exports totalled ₹718 crore, going to over 55 countries primarily in MENA and Europe. The report also confirmed the company is net-debt-free. The governance section noted that the promoter holds 74.99% of shares, and two independent directors also serve on Kkalpana's board.
flags: The auditor highlighted the significant inventory balance of ₹392 crore as a key audit matter.
The free float is limited, as the promoter holds the regulatory maximum of 74.99% of the shares.
Two independent directors also sit on the board of related-party Kkalpana Industries, from which the company was demerged.

reports.auditor: S.R. Batliboi & Co. LLP gave a qualified opinion for the second year in a row. The auditors could not assess the impairment of ₹47.6 crore of assets at Malwa Power after its power-purchase agreement expired in April 2025. They also included an emphasis of matter regarding a retrospective downward tariff cut by PSPCL on the Abohar biomass plant. This dispute is in court, and no provision has been made.
reports.contingent: The standalone notes show income tax, GST, and customs demands that appear to be in the tens of crores, though exact totals are unclear from the layout. The company also has standard export obligations of ₹202 crore under duty-free import licenses that must be fulfilled.
flags: The auditor issued a qualified opinion because they could not assess impairment on ₹47.6 crore of assets at the Malwa Power subsidiary.
An emphasis of matter was flagged regarding a retrospective tariff cut by PSPCL, which is in dispute with no financial provisions made.
The company faces contingent liabilities for tax, GST, and customs demands in the tens of crores.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unqualified opinion. They flagged two key audit matters: the company's contingent liabilities, and the mining subsidiary DMSL raising ₹800 crore in compulsory convertible debentures.
reports.relatedParties: The promoter entity SCM Commercial holds ₹151 crore in 8% optionally convertible debentures and ₹300 crore in DMSL compulsory convertible debentures. Subsidiary MAL committed up to ₹75 crore to an alternative investment fund (SOA Fund Series I) managed by SCM Commercial. A ₹21 crore deposit is receivable from the chairman.
reports.contingent: Consolidated contingent liabilities were ₹779 crore at March 2026. The largest items were GST input-credit disputes of ₹283 crore, supplier claims of ₹212 crore, and sales-tax/VAT disputes of ₹157 crore. Disclosed separately are a ₹357 crore GAIL gas-pricing claim pending in the Supreme Court and a ₹96 crore income-tax penalty under appeal.
reports.outlook: The annual report targets commissioning of the Gopalpur and Dahej expansion plants during H2 FY27. Post-expansion, ammonium nitrate capacity will reach about 1.0 MTPA, making it the third largest pure-play producer globally, and weak nitric acid capacity will reach about 1.2 MTPA.
reports.other: The Chemicals segment reported revenue of ₹5,304 crore and a result of ₹1,147 crore. The Fertilisers segment posted revenue of ₹6,166 crore and a result of ₹420 crore, with low-margin traded fertiliser sales more than doubling to ₹1,760 crore. The Australian Platinum Blasting arm is now 100% owned, and Char Dham Chemicals was bought for ₹121 crore. DMSL has pledged 30 to 51% of PCL shares to project lenders.
flags: Subsidiary MAL committed up to ₹75 crore of group money to an investment fund managed by the promoter entity SCM Commercial.
Major capacity expansions have slipped again, with the annual report quietly delaying commissioning to H2 FY27.
The company faces a ₹357 crore GAIL gas-pricing claim in the Supreme Court and a ₹96 crore income-tax penalty under appeal.
Routine contingent liabilities remain high at ₹779 crore, largely due to GST, sales-tax, and supplier disputes.
The mining subsidiary DMSL has pledged 30 to 51% of PCL shares to project lenders.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. There were no key audit matters reported.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are negligible at ₹0.5 crore. The company has capital commitments of ₹686 crore.
reports.outlook: Management highlighted plans to introduce new products like MIBK, acetophenone, and fluorinated chemicals such as BTF. A major ₹11,500 crore mega-project is underway to build an integrated polycarbonate plant. The company also noted that China's new rules on hazardous nitration capacity act as a positive tailwind.
reports.other: In FY26, the Phenolics segment earned ₹5,401 crore in revenue and ₹695 crore in EBIT. The Advanced Intermediates segment had ₹2,553 crore in revenue and ₹107 crore in EBIT, pulled down by start-up losses at Deepak Chem Tech. The company holds over 50% of the Indian phenol and acetone market.
flags: Return on capital employed dropped sharply from 44% in FY22 to just 11% in FY26.
The Advanced Intermediates segment had weak margins of 4% in FY26, dragged down by start-up losses at the Deepak Chem Tech subsidiary.
The company has ₹1,828 crore tied up in capital work-in-progress that is not yet earning any return.

reports.auditor: Deloitte Haskins & Sells gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters included Ecom Express purchase-price allocation (₹1,042 crore goodwill) and goodwill impairment testing. Under CARO, the auditor noted title deeds of properties acquired from FedEx in 2021 are not transferred, unpaid professional tax of ₹0.8 crore, and disputed dues. Subsidiaries Delhivery Freight Services and Ecom Express were flagged for cash losses. One subsidiary did not maintain an audit trail for April–October 2025.
reports.relatedParties: The company purchased about ₹25 crore of sortation equipment from its 40.92% owned associate Falcon Autotech, down from about ₹63 crore in FY25. Key management personnel received remuneration of ₹18.3 crore, up from ₹9.3 crore in FY25. Employee loans of ₹140.7 crore were granted during the year with ₹3.4 crore outstanding, and key managers repaid ₹47.7 crore of loans.
reports.contingent: The consolidated contingent-liability note shows disputed income tax of ₹38.3 crore and GST of ₹0.7 crore. The analyst notes a gap with the auditor's CARO report, which lists much higher disputed GST of about ₹108 crore and income tax of about ₹69 crore plus ₹40 crore not deposited. Capital commitments were ₹137 crore at March 2026.
reports.other: The company reports one segment for logistics services but discloses service lines. The largest customer concentrated 19.23% of net sales in FY26, up from 17.71% in FY25. The core business still loses money after tax before ₹340 crore of treasury income, with statutory net profit at ₹153 crore. Ecom Express was acquired for ₹1,369 crore, resulting in ₹1,042 crore of goodwill. No bank term loans were taken during the year.
flags: The core business continues to lose money after tax at the statutory level before treasury income is added.
The largest customer concentration rose to 19.23% of net sales in FY26.
Auditors flagged subsidiaries Delhivery Freight Services and Ecom Express for cash losses, and one subsidiary lacked an audit trail for April–October 2025.
Title deeds for properties acquired from FedEx in 2021 have not yet been transferred.
The CARO report lists disputed GST and income tax dues much higher than those disclosed in the contingent liabilities note.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The key audit matters identified in the report were revenue timing and IT controls.
reports.relatedParties: Managing Director Prashant Garg received ₹2.4 crore in pay. His spouse, Neelu Garg, received ₹0.55 crore, with an AGM resolution raising this to ₹66.2 lakh and allowing up to 20% annual increases until FY31. The company paid ₹0.44 crore in rent to promoter Chitra Garg and made ₹5.1 crore in sales to its associate LSN.
reports.contingent: The company has very small contingent liabilities, consisting only of a ₹0.72 crore GST appeal.
reports.outlook: Management notes the addition of 18 new hardfacing torches at the Nimji plant, increasing overlay capacity by 16,848 square metres per year to over 70,000 square metres per year. A new strip-slitting line for flux-cored wire also went live. The MD&A warns of competition from cheap Chinese electrodes, wires, and wear plates in commoditised segments.
reports.other: The company reports as a single operating segment, so it does not disclose segment margins. It made a ₹2.15 crore strategic investment for about a 10% stake in Tejorup Sunmay Systems. The report also notes subsidiaries in Singapore, Turkey, and the UAE, along with associates LSN Diffusion and Mecdiff.
flags: The MD&A warns of competition from cheap Chinese electrodes, wires, and wear plates in commoditised segments.
The company invested ₹2.15 crore in a defence start-up that is currently pre-revenue.

reports.auditor: The auditor's report contains no qualifications or adverse remarks. A CARO point confirms that IPO funds were applied for their stated purposes.
reports.relatedParties: Form AOC-2 disclosed that MD J. Madhusudhan Varma was paid ₹32 lakh for professional services between April and July 2025, before his formal appointment terms. The company uses Indian GAAP AS-18 for its related-party notes.
reports.outlook: The MD&A notes that a new subsidiary, Abhedhya Systems, was established in May 2026 for RF and microwave subsystems, with revenue expected from FY28. It also highlights Project Udaan, funded by ₹51.74 cr from the IPO, which had a capital work-in-progress of ₹4.45 cr at March 2026.
reports.other: The AGM notice details large family pay packages: MD J. Madhusudhan Varma receives ₹1.44 cr plus 1.5% of net profit, the CEO and one director each receive ₹60 lakh plus 3%, and another director gets ₹48 lakh plus 0.5%. The MD&A reports post-IPO net worth at ₹108.1 cr, cash at ₹34.2 cr, and borrowings down to ~₹4.1 cr. The annual report also notes MoUs with Sperry and Eirad.
flags: The board approved fixed pay for the founding family totaling ~₹3.1 crore—roughly 30% of FY26 net profit—plus 8% of profits.
The MD was paid ₹32 lakh for professional services in the months prior to his formal appointment terms.

reports.auditor: Deloitte Haskins & Sells gave an unmodified opinion. Revenue recognition on effort- and unit-based contracts and unbilled revenue was a key audit matter. The auditor noted that the audit trail (edit log) was not enabled for payroll and procurement software, as well as one accounting package, between April and December 2025.
reports.relatedParties: Pass-through invoicing with Quess for un-novated contracts was not treated as a related-party transaction.
reports.contingent: Standalone contingent liabilities were ₹12.9 crore. This includes ₹8.7 crore for provident fund on allowances under a Bombay High Court stay, ₹2.9 crore for PF damages and interest, and ₹1.4 crore for Pune professional tax. Unexecuted standalone capital contracts rose sharply to ₹81.5 crore from ₹12.8 crore. A corporate guarantee of ₹118.8 crore for MFXchange expired during the year.
reports.other: The annual report claimed the company's dependence on top clients was falling. The report's annual general meeting notice also recorded that former CEO Gurmeet Chahal resigned effective 31 May 2026, and Sameer Ahluwalia took over on 1 June 2026.
flags: The auditor noted that audit trails were not enabled for payroll, procurement, and an accounting software package for nine months of the year.
The company faces ₹11.6 crore in contingent liabilities over disputed provident fund allowances, damages, and interest.
Top-10 client concentration rose, directly contradicting the annual report's claim that client dependence was falling.
The annual general meeting notice confirmed the CEO resigned just 12 days after giving an upbeat earnings call.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. No emphasis of matter was found in the extracts reviewed.
reports.contingent: As of March 2026, standalone bank guarantees stood at ~₹1,214 crore and corporate guarantees for subsidiaries at ~₹846 crore. The company faced claims of ~₹71 crore and GST disputes of ~₹3 crore. It also had a capital commitment of ~₹2,612 crore to invest in subsidiaries.
reports.other: In FY26, 16.23 million warrants issued to non-promoter entities were converted into shares. This raised the equity capital from ₹146 crore to ₹162 crore. The promoter stake dropped from 70.15% to 63.14%. No share pledges were found.
flags: The promoter stake was diluted from 70.15% to 63.14% following the conversion of warrants by non-promoter entities.
The company has a large capital commitment of ~₹2,612 crore to invest in its subsidiaries.
Corporate guarantees given for subsidiaries amount to a substantial ~₹846 crore.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an emphasis of matter on the standalone results. Goodwill of ₹1,326.86 crore from a past merger is being amortised over 99 years under a court scheme instead of using standard impairment rules. Without this, assets would be ₹745.90 crore higher. The company also breached a financial covenant on ₹84.44 crore of NCDs, with some waivers pending. Covenants on another ₹48.92 crore of NCDs and a ₹63.67 crore term loan were modified. Key audit matters included goodwill, subsidiary investment impairment, and uncertain tax positions.
reports.relatedParties: The company relies on a promoter-group external commercial borrowing (ECB) of up to CHF 200 million. This unsecured, 10-year loan charges 4% interest with a two-year moratorium, and is funded by personal assets and guarantees to repay Indian debt. Global MD Arpit Vyas drew no remuneration during the year.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include disputed income tax of ₹374.95 crore, of which ₹46 crore was paid under protest. The company also faces excise and GST claims of about ₹31 crore, and has provided ₹14 crore in guarantees for former subsidiaries or joint ventures. Capital commitments for property, plant, and equipment rose to ₹385 crore, plus ₹44 crore for intangibles.
reports.other: The annual report noted that past regulatory issues with the EDQM at the Bavla site crushed the historical operating margins for the India business.
flags: The auditor emphasized a standalone covenant breach on NCDs worth ₹84.44 crore, with waivers still pending.
Goodwill of ₹1,326.86 crore is being amortised over 99 years rather than standard impairment, keeping reported assets ₹745.90 crore higher than they would be otherwise.
The auditor highlighted potential impairment risks concerning ₹4,798 crore in consolidated goodwill and ₹2,828 crore in subsidiary investments.
The company faces a massive ₹374.95 crore in disputed income tax claims.
The firm is heavily dependent on a pending, unsecured promoter-group loan of up to CHF 200 million to repay its Indian debt.

reports.auditor: B.K. Khare & Co. gave an unmodified opinion. The key audit matter was revenue recognition regarding volume discounts. The CARO report noted a slight delay in a few cases of depositing statutory dues and a disputed GST amount. The audit trail operated successfully all year.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid ₹4.5 cr for machine and development charges to promoter-linked Divgi Transmission Systems & Technologies Pvt Ltd, up from ₹3.3 cr in FY25. It also paid ₹0.5 cr in rent to a promoter holding company and bought IT services from KMP-influenced Quixotic Studios. The Managing Director's pay is 31.7 times the median employee salary.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small at ₹3.9 cr, which includes ₹2.4 cr for stamp duty and ₹1.0 cr for claims. Capital commitments increased to ₹50.5 cr at the end of March 2026, up from ₹25.8 cr the prior year.
reports.outlook: The management discussion contains very long, promotional commentary about the future, with the Managing Director using phrases like 'historic crossroads' and 'afterburner thrust'. However, the large 'potential' numbers management discusses are not firm commitments.
reports.other: The company has 278 permanent employees across four plants, a gross block of ₹421.6 cr, and spent ₹11.8 cr on R&D in FY26. Working capital improved, with net days falling to 68 from 96 and receivable turnover rising to 5.24x. Of the ₹169.7 cr raised in the March 2023 IPO for machinery, only ₹77.9 cr was spent, and ₹72.7 cr remains unspent in bank deposits three years later.
flags: Out of the IPO proceeds raised for machinery in March 2023, ₹72.7 cr remains unspent after three years, depressing returns and questioning capital planning.
Related-party transactions are growing, including ₹4.5 cr paid for machine and development charges to a promoter-linked company.
The Managing Director's pay is elevated at 31.7 times the median employee salary.
Management uses highly promotional language in its commentary, but the large 'potential' revenue numbers it shares are not firm targets.
The auditor flagged slight delays in a few cases of statutory dues and a disputed GST amount.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters covered revenue timing and trade-receivable credit-loss judgements. The CARO report was clean on statutory dues, defaults, and stock statements. It did note a GST input-credit dispute of ₹1.57 crore where the Rajasthan High Court rejected the company's writ in January 2025.
reports.relatedParties: Managing Director Ashish Mangal was paid ₹5.35 crore, equal to about 6% of net profit. Promoter loans were rotated, with ₹13.3 crore taken and ₹12.9 crore repaid. The company recorded an ₹11 crore property purchase from promoter entity Shiv Kripa Pipes in FY25. Sales of ₹1.96 crore were made to the chairman's Mangal Electrical Industries. A previous ₹344.75 crore corporate guarantee from promoter firm Indokrates was withdrawn.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities reached ₹207.5 crore, rising from ₹172.1 crore the prior year. This primarily included ₹174.4 crore in bank guarantees and ₹25.1 crore in discounted LC bills. Additionally, there are income-tax demands of ₹2.65 crore and indirect-tax demands of ₹1.94 crore. Collateral for a related party's loan fell to nil. The company also holds a remaining capital commitment of ₹11.19 crore.
reports.other: FY26 total sales were ₹1,197.8 crore. Product sales included HT/HV cables at ₹755.9 crore, LT/LV cables at ₹346.6 crore, and conductors at ₹72.4 crore. Private buyers accounted for ₹956.3 crore, the government for ₹160.0 crore, and exports for ₹81.6 crore. Solar cables grew over 100% to reach 18-19% of revenue. Promoters hold 68.18% with no disclosed pledges. Unsecured promoter loans were ₹2.2 crore at 9%. The company has 1,073 permanent staff.
flags: Contingent liabilities are substantial at ₹207.5 crore, largely driven by bank guarantees and discounted bills.
The company faces a GST input-credit dispute of ₹1.57 crore for which the Rajasthan High Court has rejected its writ.
Promoter loans were rotated during the year, and an ₹11 crore property was previously bought from a promoter entity.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The only key audit matter raised was regarding revenue recognition.
reports.relatedParties: L&T, which owns an 18.45% stake, acts as an investor, partner, supplier, and customer. E2E uses L&T data-centre space, L&T uses E2E cloud services, and an agreement covers monetising L&T-built GPUs. At March 2026, E2E had ₹3.7 crore of unbilled revenue due from L&T.
reports.contingent: The company reported no contingent liabilities.
reports.outlook: Management argues that sovereign, open-weight deployments favour an Indian AI factory over API-only models. The company set up a wholly-owned subsidiary, SovCloud Technologies, for large GPU clusters and to enable funding arrangements. Capital commitments at March 2026 were ₹19 crore.
reports.other: Borrowings at March 2026 included ₹80.0 crore in long-term debt, ₹23.2 crore in short-term debt, and ₹55.9 crore in leases, against equity of about ₹1,685 crore. Unused funds from 2024 preferential issues stood at ₹50.2 crore and ₹77.1 crore. Headcount was just 207.
flags: L&T serves as an 18.45% shareholder while simultaneously acting as a key supplier, partner, and customer.
Promoter holding has fallen significantly from 59.71% to 39.45% due to equity dilution.
Debt is rising rapidly, with a new subsidiary established specifically to enable further funding arrangements.
Profitability relies on a six-year useful life for computer equipment, despite new chips arriving much faster.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters highlighted in the report included related-party transactions and receivables impairment for expected credit losses.
reports.relatedParties: The company engaged in sales, purchases, and service transactions with several promoter-group companies. These related parties include Power Build, Emtici Engineering, Eimco Elecon, Elecon Hydraulics, and Akaaish Mechatronics.
reports.contingent: The company reported contingent liabilities for excise and service-tax disputes amounting to ₹49.3 crore, as well as GST disputes totaling ₹10.4 crore.
flags: The auditor highlighted related-party transactions with several promoter-group companies as a key audit matter.
Receivables impairment for expected credit loss was flagged as a key audit matter.
The company faces contingent liabilities of ₹49.3 crore for excise and service-tax disputes, plus ₹10.4 crore for GST disputes.

reports.auditor: Price Waterhouse Chartered Accountants LLP flagged the carrying value of ₹170 crore in subsidiary investments as a key audit matter. Cash-flow projections were required for one subsidiary to assess the investment and guarantees. The auditor also considered whistle-blower complaints in their CARO report.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are very small. They include ₹1.3 crore in tax disputes and a railway-bridge arbitration case where Elgi is the claimant.
reports.outlook: Management's five-year plan targets ₹6,615 crore in revenue by FY31, alongside an 18% EBITDA margin and a 35% ROCE. They expect the global market to grow roughly 3.5% annually to US$27 billion by 2030. Future operations include shifting shared services to India and launching a new vacuum-pump line, funded by anticipated annual cash accruals of ₹300 to ₹400 crore.
reports.other: FY26 segment revenue for compressors was ₹3,613 crore with a pre-tax profit of ₹548 crore, while the automotive arm posted ₹339 crore in revenue and ₹37 crore in profit. Capital commitments fell to ₹62 crore. Several subsidiaries lost money: Elgi Compressors Europe lost ₹22.2 crore, Michigan Air Solutions lost ₹6.8 crore, F.R. Pulford lost ₹2.6 crore, and Rotair lost ₹0.5 crore. Patton's and Michigan hold negative reserves of ₹72 crore and ₹29 crore, respectively.
flags: The auditor raised a key audit matter regarding the carrying value of ₹170 crore in subsidiary investments.
A regulatory enquiry under FEMA issued summons seeking data on past imports, exports, sales to subsidiaries, and overseas investments.
The company received whistle-blower complaints during the year, and some remained open at the end of March 2026.
The main European subsidiary lost ₹22.2 crore in FY26 and carries massive negative reserves of ₹386 crore.
Distribution subsidiaries in the US and Australia missed revenue targets, reported ongoing losses, and hold negative reserves.

reports.auditor: The auditor, MSKA & Associates, gave an unmodified opinion and named revenue recognition as a key audit matter. The CARO report noted that quarterly stock and receivable statements filed with banks differed from the books by roughly ₹1 to ₹1.4 crore per quarter. Title deeds for ₹28.5 crore of property were pledged with banks, and there were slight delays in some statutory dues. Also, a database audit trail was only enabled from 29 April 2025 and is not enabled for payroll software.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings are small. The company made ₹2.6 crore in purchases from Karakoram Healthcare LLP and paid office rent to promoter companies.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include tax disputes of ₹4.1 crore for service tax, excise, and GST, plus a ₹3.5 crore supplier claim in court. A ₹2.5 crore income-tax dispute was resolved in FY26. Promoters provided personal guarantees on loans of ₹149 crore. Unspent capital commitments stood at ₹48.3 crore.
reports.outlook: The annual report states plans to expand total production capacity from 1,370 tonnes per day in FY25 to 2,149 tonnes per day by the end of FY27.
reports.other: The company paid no dividend for FY26 to retain cash for capital expenditure. From its IPO, it repaid ₹210 crore in debt and used funds for projects, leaving ₹68.1 crore unspent. The balance sheet carries a highly unusual treasury book of roughly ₹397 crore parked in alternative investment funds, market-linked debentures, mutual funds, listed Swiggy shares, and unlisted IKF Finance shares, with ₹55.7 crore in further AIF commitments. Working capital improved, with debtor days dropping to 68.
flags: Quarterly stock and receivable statements filed with banks did not agree with the books, showing differences of roughly ₹1 to ₹1.4 crore per quarter.
An audit trail at the database level was only enabled from 29 April 2025, and no audit trail exists for the payroll software.
The auditor noted slight delays in the payment of some statutory dues.
A large portion of the company's cash is parked in alternative investment funds, unlisted shares, and Swiggy stock, exposing it to unusual treasury risks.
Title deeds for ₹28.5 crore of property are pledged with banks, and promoters have given personal guarantees on ₹149 crore of loans.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Revenue recognition was identified as a key audit matter, and an audit trail was maintained.
reports.contingent: Total contingent liabilities were ₹259 crore, down from ₹394 crore in FY25. This includes tax liabilities of ₹170 crore plus ₹89 crore in interest following a December 2020 income-tax search on Emcure, Zuventus, and Gennova, with appeals still ongoing. There is also an unquantified arbitration claim involving Cebis (Vayam).
reports.other: The company has its own chemistry for the iron franchise, Tenectase, and 11 to 12 chiral-pure compounds, and holds an 86% market share for its S-metoprolol molecule. Internationally, it has a first-generic position in liposomal amphotericin B in some markets.
flags: CEO Satish Mehta and former US unit Heritage were named in US generic price-fixing cases, with some settlements still being finalised.
The company faces a ₹259 crore contingent tax liability including interest due to a December 2020 income-tax search.
An unquantified arbitration claim related to Cebis (Vayam) remains pending.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion with no emphasis of matter. They noted a key audit matter regarding revenue recognition, specifically evaluating performance obligations over time versus point-in-time.
reports.contingent: The company faces a ₹128 crore claim plus interest from 3i Infotech alleging criminal conspiracy and wrongful share redemption, which it denies and has not provided for. A prior FY25 contingent liability of ₹17.8 crore for buying back unsold stock from partners was settled in FY26. Other contingent liabilities are small, including ₹3.2 crore for income tax and ₹0.15 crore for GST.
reports.outlook: The report highlights heavy capital spending covering product development, acquisitions, and data centres in the US, Europe, UAE, and India. It also points out risks regarding regulatory dependence, noting a past rule change that forced a stock buyback from partners.
reports.other: The company acquired 51% of Cryptas for €5 million in cash. The deal includes an earn-out based on 10x 2026 EBITDA and a put/call option on the remaining 49% between 2028 and 2030, which has a floor valuation of 1x revenue.
flags: 3i Infotech is claiming over ₹128 crore plus interest for alleged criminal conspiracy, a dispute that is not provided for in the accounts.
The Cryptas acquisition includes a put option with a floor of 1x revenue, which could force a large payout even if its earnings stay low.
The company has heavy capitalized spending on product development and data centres, contributing to negative free cash flow.
The business is highly dependent on regulations, as evidenced by a past rule change that forced the company to buy back unsold stock from partners.

reports.auditor: The FY26 auditor's report included an emphasis of matter on three serious revenue-recognition issues. First, a contractor's claim of ₹410 crore against EIL's counter-claim of ₹129 crore is pending in the Supreme Court over a 2016 termination. Second, ₹86 crore of FY25 revenue was recognised on an HRRL change order that remains unapproved and unsettled, with inadequate disclosure. Third, an Angola receivable of ₹59 crore from FY2016-17 was fully provided following earlier accounting criticism by the CAG.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings were mainly with joint ventures, including Ramagundam Fertilizers and Numaligarh Refinery, and PSU clients. The file notes that nothing unusual was found. The Government of India stake remains steady at 51.32% with no pledges.
reports.contingent: Standalone contingent liabilities at March 2026 totalled about ₹742 crore against a net worth of about ₹3,146 crore. This includes commercial claims of ₹198 crore and tax disputes of about ₹543 crore. The tax disputes involve Karnataka VAT claims of ₹424 crore, ₹53 crore, and ₹9 crore, which the note states are reimbursable by clients.
flags: The auditor flagged a ₹410 crore contractor claim against EIL pending in the Supreme Court.
The auditor highlighted ₹86 crore of FY25 revenue recognised on an unapproved HRRL change order with inadequate disclosure.
An Angola receivable of ₹59 crore from FY2016-17 was fully provided after previous CAG criticism.
The company faces total contingent liabilities of about ₹742 crore, including large tax disputes and commercial claims.

reports.auditor: Deloitte Haskins & Sells issued a qualified opinion on the standalone and consolidated accounts because a ₹19.61 crore receivable from one customer is disputed with no provision made. The auditor could not judge its recoverability, and the company has filed a criminal complaint. The auditor also reported a material weakness in internal financial controls over this disputed receivable, and noted that the database audit trail was not enabled.
reports.relatedParties: At March 2026, EPACK had outstanding loans to its group entities including ₹22.3 crore to its Hisense subsidiary EMTPL (down from a peak of ₹28 crore) and ₹23.8 crore to its EPAVO joint venture. The company also earned ₹3.7 crore in corporate guarantee income from EMTPL. The EPAVO joint venture saw its losses double in FY26.
reports.contingent: Guarantees given jumped from ₹26.2 crore to ₹176.7 crore, largely providing off-balance-sheet support for EMTPL's debt. There is an income-tax demand of ₹29.0 crore for AY2023-24 currently under appeal, but only ₹4.76 crore is shown as a contingent liability. Other contingent liabilities include ₹5.3 crore for income tax and ₹2.2 crore for GST.
reports.other: The company reported operations under a single segment. The single largest customer accounted for ₹566 crore in sales in FY26. In the management discussion, EPACK claimed to have the highest room air conditioner backward integration at one location in India. The Board's report noted secretarial audit qualifications for not filing a Statement of Deviation after changing IPO-proceeds usage, unreviewed risk policies, and missing entries in the insider-trading database.
flags: The auditor gave a qualified opinion because a disputed ₹19.61 crore receivable has no provision and its recoverability cannot be judged.
A material weakness was flagged in internal financial controls regarding disputed receivables, and the database audit trail was not enabled.
The secretarial audit flagged missing insider-trading database entries and the failure to file a Statement of Deviation for IPO proceeds.
An income-tax demand of ₹29.0 crore was received, but only ₹4.76 crore of it is recognized as a contingent liability.
Outstanding guarantees jumped sharply to ₹176.7 crore, mostly to back a subsidiary's borrowing.

reports.auditor: SRBC & Co (EY network) gave an unqualified opinion. They highlighted one key audit matter regarding revenue recognition and cut-off. Under CARO, the auditor noted that the accounting software's audit-trail (edit log) was not enabled for privileged or admin changes. Bank stock statements agreed with the books, and there were no defaults.
reports.relatedParties: In FY26, the company sold about ₹185 crore of goods to Meghmani group companies. This included ₹121.6 crore in sales to the listed group entity Meghmani Organics. The company also purchased renewable power from an associate. These transactions were stated as arm's length.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities total ₹84.7 crore, or about 4% of net worth. This includes ₹44.2 crore in commercial claims for alleged non-fulfilment of contracts. Tax disputes involve ₹16.6 crore for income tax on captive power, a ₹17.3 crore GST demand on ECB interest, ₹6.2 crore for customs, and ₹0.25 crore for service tax. Capital commitments stood at ₹54.6 crore, and there is an EPCG export obligation of ₹176 crore.
reports.outlook: Management aims to increase the Derivatives and Specialty share of revenue to over 70% by FY28, up from 52% in FY26. They also target 90-95% captive chlorine use by FY28. The Chairman noted FY26 volumes fell 4% due to an 8-yearly caustic plant maintenance, a long monsoon, and PVC anti-dumping uncertainty. The MD&A revealed the company took a mark-to-market loss on a foreign-currency loan as the rupee fell.
reports.other: The accounts show only one reportable segment. Exports halved from ₹169 crore to ₹77 crore, making up just 3% of FY26 revenue. The auditor's ratio note highlighted that receivables rose. The Directors' report proposed a dividend of ₹5 per share, totaling ₹21.6 crore for a 6.5% payout, with no buyback. The notes show CFO Sanjay Jain left in August 2025, replaced by Rakesh Agrawal in November 2025.
flags: The auditor noted that the accounting software's audit-trail log was not enabled for privileged or admin changes.
Contingent liabilities reached ₹84.7 crore, which includes ₹44.2 crore in commercial claims for alleged non-fulfilment of contract obligations.
The company suffered an undisclosed mark-to-market loss on a foreign-currency loan due to a drop in the rupee.
The EPCG export obligation has jumped to ₹176 crore, which must be fulfilled by February 2032.
The auditor's ratio note pointed out an increase in receivables, while total export revenue halved during the year.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Revenue recognition was the only key audit matter. Other auditors audited 15 foreign subsidiaries with ₹3,645 crore in revenue. One subsidiary and one associate were unaudited but immaterial. The CARO report was clean. Bank stock statements matched the books, and there was only a minor ₹2 lakh provident fund dispute from 2013-14.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small. They include disputed indirect tax of ₹39 crore, disputed direct tax of ₹25 crore, and bank guarantees of ₹7.7 crore. Outstanding capital commitments stood at ₹51 crore in March 2026.
reports.outlook: Management noted the new Thailand plant, commissioned in November 2025, is still in customer validation. The pending Indovida merger will create a combined revenue of about US$1 billion, with 75% generated from emerging markets. The report acknowledges customer concentration as a risk but does not quantify it.
reports.other: All regions saw FY26 revenue growth, but Europe's EBITDA fell 3.2% with a 14.5% margin. Exceptional items totaled ₹28 crore, including ₹15.6 crore for merger costs, ₹6.7 crore for a China factory closure, and ₹5.9 crore for a labour-code gratuity. Assets worth ₹1,368 crore are pledged as normal bank security. Hemant Bakshi replaced Anand Kripalu as MD and CEO.
flags: A change in control is occurring as Blackstone sells a 24.9% stake to Indorama, making minority shareholders dependent on a Thai conglomerate's capital allocation.
Europe operations continue to face operational challenges, with EBIT margins falling to 4.8%.
Capex is running ahead of depreciation, and depreciation is growing faster than EBITDA, which is dragging down overall EBIT margins.
Working capital requirements are increasing, with inventory days rising to 177 and free cash flow dropping 43% in FY26.
A factory in China was closed at a cost of ₹6.7 crore, continuing a trend of earlier closures tied to customer relocations.

reports.auditor: Walker Chandiok gave an unmodified opinion, noting revenue recognition as a key audit matter. The auditor flagged that a database-level audit trail was not enabled for the parent company and five subsidiaries. Additionally, six subsidiaries generating ₹545 crore in revenue were audited by other auditors.
reports.relatedParties: In FY25, Eris purchased a 19% stake in Swiss Parenterals directly from its own promoters for ₹237.5 crore. In FY26, it acquired the final 30% from the Swiss founder for ₹423 crore using new Eris shares. The company also lent ₹47 crore to its joint venture, Levim Lifetech.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include DPCO pricing notices of ₹20.9 crore, tax and GST claims of ₹17.0 crore, and other items of ₹13.7 crore. Unfulfilled export obligations stand at ₹97 crore, with ₹16.2 crore of duty at risk. Capital commitments are ₹191 crore, plus up to ₹100 crore in equity and ₹50 crore in funding committed to Levim.
reports.outlook: Management stated there will be no new acquisitions for now, as their priority is manufacturing. To prepare for active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) price increases of 70% to 80%, the company built up about nine months of raw material and packaging stock.
reports.other: The company's top 25 brands account for about 65% of branded sales, with 13 ranking in the top five of their segments and six generating over ₹100 crore each. Price control exposure is 17% of revenue. Eris also acquired Velbiom probiotics brands for ₹50 crore.
flags: The auditor noted that a database-level audit trail was not enabled for the parent company and five of its subsidiaries.
Eris bought a 19% stake in Swiss Parenterals from its own promoters for ₹237.5 crore.
The company faces DPCO pricing notices of ₹20.9 crore and tax or GST claims totaling ₹17.0 crore.
The company has an unfulfilled export obligation of ₹97 crore, risking ₹16.2 crore in duties.
Management had to tie up cash in nine months of inventory due to expected raw material price spikes of 70% to 80%.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The only key audit matter noted in the report was regarding revenue recognition.
reports.relatedParties: Shareholders approved related-party transactions with the ELITe joint venture for up to ₹1,463 crore in FY27. They also approved transactions of up to ₹380 crore each for personal guarantees on loans provided by the promoter, Arvind Singhania, and the holding company, Wilemina Finance Corporation.
reports.contingent: The company faces disputed tax claims of ₹11.9 crore for excise, customs, and service tax, along with ₹0.3 crore for income tax. Additionally, the parent company provides a letter of comfort and corporate guarantees for the loans of its subsidiary, Filmtech.
reports.outlook: Management targets commercial operations for the ELITe chemical recycling joint venture by calendar year 2028. At full utilization, this 70,000-tonne plant could earn about US$150 million in revenue with a 40% to 45% profit margin, supported by an anchor deal with Nike and partnerships with Taro Plast and Hyosung TNC.
reports.other: The company added a 20,000-tonne recycling extruder during the year. It raised ₹165.25 crore through warrants, though ₹9.75 crore remained unsubscribed. A dividend of ₹0.25 per share was declared, which the promoter waived. Furthermore, Arvind Singhania stepped down as CEO to become non-executive chairman, and his son was appointed as a whole-time director.
flags: The company faces unresolved tax disputes totaling ₹12.2 crore across excise, customs, service, and income taxes.
The company relies on personal guarantees from the promoter and the holding company for its loans, with approved transaction limits of up to ₹380 crore each.
Shareholders have approved very large related-party transaction limits for FY27, including up to ₹1,463 crore solely for the ELITe joint venture.
Out of a planned ₹175 crore warrant issue, ₹9.75 crore was left unsubscribed.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unqualified opinion. Impairment testing is noted as the key audit matter because the balance sheet holds ₹4,967 crore of goodwill and indefinite-life brand intangibles from a 2022 acquisition, representing 74% of total assets. A sustained growth miss could force a non-cash write-down.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party transactions are only with subsidiaries and are small. No fees paid to the parent entities, Advent or Lunolux, are seen in the note.
reports.contingent: The company has about ₹80 crore in contingent liabilities. This consists of disputed sales tax of ₹26.6 crore, GST of ₹21.8 crore, excise of ₹14.4 crore, income tax of ₹14.0 crore, and others.
reports.other: The company reports as a single segment. FY26 standalone revenue showed product sales of ₹2,064 crore (up 13.7%) and service sales of ₹630 crore (up 4.1%), making services about 23% of total revenue. AMC income received in advance (contract liabilities) increased from ₹150.9 crore to ₹204.6 crore, representing revenue to be booked in later years. Lunolux Ltd of Cyprus holds a 62.56% ownership stake.
flags: Goodwill and brand intangibles total ₹4,967 crore (74% of total assets), posing a risk of a non-cash write-down if the company misses growth targets.
Service revenue grew by only about 4% in FY26, significantly lagging behind the 14% growth seen in product sales.
The company faces contingent liabilities of approximately ₹80 crore relating to various disputed taxes.

reports.auditor: The auditor's report includes an emphasis of matter regarding a ₹171.55 crore penalty levied by the Competition Commission of India. Additionally, the CARO annexure noted that the company had not submitted its Q4 FY26 stock statement to banks by the time the audit report was signed.
reports.relatedParties: The related party transactions note shows the company paid a commission of ₹2.1 crore per year in both FY25 and FY26 to non-executive director Arjun Lamba.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include a ₹171.55 crore Competition Commission of India cartel penalty, which the NCLAT has stayed following a 10% deposit. The company also reported contingent indirect tax claims of ₹19.8 crore and other minor claims of ₹0.3 crore.
reports.outlook: Management notes the total dry-cell battery market is around ₹4,000 crore. The company maintains a massive reach of approximately 4.5 million retail touchpoints. On the capital expenditure front, Eveready is investing in a new alkaline battery plant in Jammu; capital work-in-progress for this facility stood at ₹176 crore at the end of March 2026. The company also permanently closed its Noida plant.
reports.other: FY26 revenue was broken down into batteries (₹972 crore), flashlights (₹179.7 crore), and lighting and electricals (₹340.9 crore). Net debt stood at ₹178 crore, while operating cash flow was ₹83 crore. Reported profits were boosted by a net exceptional gain of ₹48.6 crore—driven by a ₹105.2 crore land sale gain, partially offset by a ₹15 crore arbitration settlement and labour charges—and a deferred tax credit of ₹85.1 crore from old MAT credits.
flags: The auditor issued an emphasis of matter over a ₹171.55 crore CCI penalty for cartelisation.
The CARO report highlighted that the Q4 FY26 stock statement to banks was not submitted on time.
The company paid ₹15 crore to settle an arbitration over old legacy loans tied to the promoter group.
Eveready pays ₹2.1 crore annually in commission to a non-executive director.
Reported profits are significantly inflated by a one-off land sale gain and old deferred tax credits.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The report included a key audit matter regarding ₹7 crore of property, plant and equipment and ₹12.4 crore of capital work-in-progress. These assets have been idle for a considerable period due to demand contraction. The CARO section also highlighted a ₹351.3 crore GST dispute.
reports.relatedParties: The parent company provided a letter of financial support to its US subsidiary, CP Industries. This letter ensures the subsidiary can meet its day-to-day obligations up until 31 May 2026.
reports.contingent: The company reported a contingent liability for a GST, interest, and penalty demand of ₹351.3 crore covering FY2017-18 to FY2022-23. This dispute is pending before CESTAT Ahmedabad and has not been provided for in the accounts. The notes also mention a US environmental exposure as a contingency, though there are no known claims.
reports.outlook: The management discussion highlights that the company is India's largest manufacturer of high-pressure seamless steel gas cylinders. It confirms that the greenfield facility in Mundra has two operational lines. Management also noted that the new plant in Egypt has been commissioned.
reports.other: FY26 segment profits were ₹119 crore in India, ₹47 crore in the US, and ₹1.8 crore in the UAE, while other regions lost ₹2 crore. The Egypt joint venture is now 97% owned, and Hungary operations were divested. The FY26 net profit included a ₹30 crore deferred-tax asset at the US subsidiary and an exceptional ₹12.6 crore US employee-retention tax refund.
flags: A massive ₹351.3 crore GST and penalty dispute is pending, which is not provided for in the accounts.
The auditor flagged ₹19.4 crore in idle assets and capital work-in-progress due to shrinking product demand.
The FY26 net profit was inflated by a ₹30 crore deferred-tax asset and a ₹12.6 crore exceptional gain.
The parent company had to issue a letter of financial support so its US subsidiary could meet daily obligations.
The company faces a contingent environmental exposure risk in the United States.

reports.auditor: The auditor's opinion is unmodified, and CARO remarks are clean with statutory dues deposited and no loans on the pledge of securities. However, the auditor raised a key audit matter regarding the valuation of Silox India, an unlisted promoter-group company. It was valued by a management-appointed valuer using EV/EBITDA multiples, where a 10% change in the multiple changes the valuation by ₹27 crore.
reports.relatedParties: The company sold a 39.98% stake in its associate Mobitrash to promoter Ashwin C. Shroff in November 2025 at a ₹0.4 lakh gain, which was near book value. Excel also paid ₹1.65 crore in CSR funds to a Shroff-linked institute. Additionally, the company had FY26 transactions totaling ₹6.4 crore with Silox.
reports.contingent: The company reported a new ₹13.5 crore GST demand in FY26, which was nil the previous year. Additional contingent liabilities include ₹1.4 crore for customs, ₹0.4 crore for excise, and ₹0.3 crore for claims.
reports.outlook: The management discussion highlights that Excel uses multi-source yellow phosphorus from Kazakhstan and Vietnam as a real entry barrier against new Indian rivals, since India lacks domestic production and China restricts exports. The report also details a contract line with a five-year term for an Indian specialty chemicals company. This generates ₹35–40 crore in annual conversion revenue, with the customer supplying raw materials and funding most of the plant via a ₹25 crore trade advance.
reports.other: In FY26, the company reduced its segment reporting to a single Chemicals segment, no longer disclosing product-group profits. FY26 exports grew 27% to ₹223 crore, while domestic revenue grew 9% to ₹864 crore. Consolidated investments totaled ₹1,126 crore. Most of this cash pile is held in shares rather than cash, primarily group companies like Tanfac Industries at ₹383 crore and Silox India at ₹338 crore.
flags: The auditor flagged the valuation of unlisted promoter-group company Silox as a key audit matter, noting a 10% multiple change moves the value by ₹27 crore.
The promoter group sits on both sides of several transactions, including the sale of a Mobitrash stake and CSR payments to a Shroff-linked institute.
Segment reporting was reduced to a single Chemicals segment, removing visibility into product-group profitability.
Around ₹720 crore is tied up in Tanfac and Silox stakes, inflating equity, halving reported returns, and acting as illiquid holdings rather than cash.
A new ₹13.5 crore GST demand emerged as a contingent liability in FY26.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters included revenue recognition, ₹414 crore in trade receivables concentrated among government and large customers, and ₹95.9 crore in recoverable GST input credits, where the auditor relied on management's assessment. All eight overseas subsidiaries were audited by other auditors. The CARO report noted delays in a few cases for depositing PF, TDS, and GST.
reports.relatedParties: Exicom belongs to the HFCL group. During FY26, sales to HFCL were about ₹60 crore, a steep increase from roughly ₹3 crore in FY25. The company also received about ₹46 crore in advances from HFCL. Additionally, promoter Nextwave converted a ₹55 crore loan into rights shares during the year.
reports.contingent: At the end of March 2026, contingent liabilities included bank guarantees of ₹57.6 crore, letters of credit totaling ₹11.6 crore, and tax demands of about ₹2.7 crore.
reports.outlook: The board's report cited industry-wide pricing pressure in the domestic EV charging segment. The annual report outlined capital expenditure of ₹144.6 crore on a standalone basis and ₹239.3 crore consolidated, primarily for a new Hyderabad plant and Tritium development. This expansion is expected to increase AC-charger capacity from roughly 42,000 to 2,22,000 units a year.
reports.other: The annual report detailed exceptional items for FY26, which included ₹7.0 crore for a voluntary retirement scheme at the Solan plant and ₹0.9 crore for a labour-code gratuity. It also disclosed that 25,66,585 shares held by promoter Nextwave Communications are pledged as security to working-capital lenders.
flags: Promoter Nextwave Communications has pledged 25,66,585 Exicom shares as security for working-capital borrowings.
The auditor highlighted that ₹414 crore in trade receivables are concentrated among government and large customers.
The auditor reported delays in a few cases regarding the deposit of PF, TDS, and GST.
For ₹95.9 crore in recoverable GST input credits, the auditor relied entirely on management's assessment.
The board's report warned of industry-wide pricing pressure in the domestic EV charging segment.

reports.auditor: The auditor, B S R & Co., gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters highlighted in the report included warranty provisions and dealer loyalty-scheme incentives, as both areas require heavy management judgement.
reports.relatedParties: The auditor noted no red flags in related-party dealings, which mainly consisted of normal intra-group lead purchases. The Directors' Report states that subsidiary Chloride Metals supplies about 80% of the company's lead and lead-alloy needs.
reports.contingent: Standalone contingent liabilities included ₹66 crore in claims and ₹61 crore in guarantees. Tax demands for excise, service tax, and customs jumped to ₹57 crore from ₹5 crore. There is also an unquantifiable landlord claim in the Bombay High Court. Additionally, Exide provided a ₹3,000 crore corporate guarantee for subsidiary EESL's borrowings.
reports.other: The company does not report separate segments, operating entirely under a single storage batteries segment. Subsidiary financial data showed that EESL generated ₹158 crore in revenue but recorded a loss of ₹248 crore. Subsidiary Chloride Metals reported ₹6,036 crore in revenue with a small loss of ₹14 crore.
flags: Subsidiary EESL posted a substantial loss of ₹248 crore on just ₹158 crore of revenue.
Contingent tax demands for excise, service tax, and customs jumped sharply to ₹57 crore from ₹5 crore.
The company faces an unquantifiable landlord claim currently in the Bombay High Court.
Exide has given a large ₹3,000 crore corporate guarantee for EESL's borrowings.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unqualified opinion with no emphasis of matter. Revenue recognition for fixed-price contracts was listed as the key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: The company gets 35% of its revenue from Expleo Group companies. Overseas subsidiaries lent ₹97.5 crore to Expleo Services SASU (France) at 9.5% to 10% interest, and shareholders approved related-party loans up to ₹280 crore. The company also paid a new management fee of ₹24.1 crore to Expleo Services SASU entities in FY26, which was nil the previous year.
reports.contingent: The company has contingent liabilities of about ₹78.5 crore. These mainly consist of value-added tax (VAT) and income-tax disputes.
reports.outlook: The board's report notes a tiny capital expenditure, adding ₹3.1 crore to the gross block. A new aerospace and defence facility was inaugurated in Bengaluru with a much larger lab for test-bench assembly, while the Coimbatore centre was closed and merged into Chennai. The company also incorporated a new subsidiary in GIFT City and recommended a final dividend of ₹110 per share.
reports.other: Revenue from operations came 40% from Europe, 14% from the UK, and 14% from the US. Work is split 75% offshore and 25% onsite. The annual report states employee attrition was 25% in FY26, up slightly from 24% in the previous year.
flags: The company relies heavily on its parent group for 35% of its revenue.
Overseas subsidiaries have lent ₹97.5 crore to the parent company, with shareholder approval allowing up to ₹280 crore in group loans.
A new management fee of ₹24.1 crore was paid to parent entities in FY26, draining cash.
The annual report discloses an employee attrition rate of 25%, conflicting with the CEO's claim of 15% on the earnings call.
Constant-currency revenue fell by 0.4% in FY26, meaning all reported growth came from a weaker rupee.

reports.auditor: The KPMG-affiliated auditor issued an unmodified opinion. However, the auditor highlighted the timing of revenue recognition as a key audit matter, noting there is pressure on management to achieve performance targets.
reports.relatedParties: The annual report showed no material related-party transactions other than paying remuneration to management and issuing dividends to the promoters.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were very small, totalling just ₹0.6 crore. This included income-tax disputes, which fell from ₹0.28 crore to ₹0.11 crore during the year. Capital commitments dropped from ₹3.4 crore to ₹0.34 crore.
reports.other: The three main products made up 73.1% of FY26 value. Dimer acid contributed about ₹140 crore, linoleic acid about 30%, and isostearic acid ₹25.9 crore.
