The tocopherol and sterol plant remained completely idle. The Directors' report showed the company spent ₹34 crore to buy back 4.25 lakh shares at ₹800 each, raising the promoter holding. The CMD was paid ₹2.67 crore, which was 41.8 times the median employee salary.
flags: The auditor flagged the timing of revenue recognition as a key audit matter due to pressure to achieve performance targets.
The CMD's pay was ₹2.67 crore, consuming about 43% of the company's total net profit for the year.
The company spent ₹34 crore on a share buyback in a year with low profits, and the promoters did not tender their shares proportionately.
The research and development spending figure was left completely blank in the annual report.
The company's tocopherol and sterol plant sat completely idle with zero volumes produced in FY26.

reports.auditor: Kirtane & Pandit gave an unmodified opinion. Revenue recognition and related-party transactions were key audit matters; for the loan and receivables due from LinguaSol, the auditor relied on a personal guarantee from its promoters. Under CARO it noted slight delays in some statutory dues, small unpaid TDS interest from FY23, and ₹15.53cr of loans to the US subsidiary Fidelsoft Inc.
reports.relatedParties: Dealings with related parties, subsidiaries and others gave about 28% of the parent's FY26 revenue, and loans and receivables due from them were about 34% of its assets. Fidel Consulting KK bought ₹6.57cr of services, and CoolPro International was paid ₹1.37cr for professional services. The parent paid ₹6.82cr to promoter Sunil Kulkarni to buy Fidel Technologies KK, from which he also draws pay. LinguaSol owes a ₹2.71cr loan at 7% plus ₹0.83cr in receivables, to be cleared by FY30.
reports.contingent: None: the accounts show no contingent liabilities at March 2026 or March 2025.
reports.other: Statutory segment notes show 95% of FY26 consolidated revenue (₹97.5cr of ₹102.4cr) came from outside India. Group profit included ₹9.3cr from the parent, ₹2.0cr from IM Corp for one quarter, and ₹1.0cr from Techvine. The balance sheet recorded ₹18.6cr of goodwill on consolidation and ₹8.9cr in intangibles. The Indian parent had 222 permanent employees at March 2026.
flags: About 28% of the parent's FY26 revenue came from related parties, and related loans or receivables made up 34% of its assets.
LinguaSol owes a ₹2.71cr loan and ₹0.83cr in receivables with no provision made, relying entirely on a personal guarantee and expected turnaround.
The parent paid ₹6.82cr to the promoter to acquire Fidel Technologies KK, a subsidiary from which he also draws pay.
The secretarial audit noted compliance lapses, including a late FC-GPR filing, an NSE fine for incorrect voting result formats, and occasional disclosure delays.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. They highlighted two key audit matters. One was revenue recognition. The other was an insurance claim for a fire at the Tapukara plant, because estimating the recoverable amount required significant management judgment.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid a lease rent of ₹2.5 crore for the year to MD Rahul Jain and JMD Aanchal Jain. It paid a brand royalty of ₹0.5 crore to promoter-controlled Fiem Auto & Electrical Industries. The Italian subsidiary received ₹13.8 crore in design fees, and the Japan subsidiary received ₹2.1 crore for R&D. Key management personnel were paid ₹17.1 crore, which included ₹3.6 crore to the departed CEO. The company also gave ₹4.6 crore in CSR funds to the promoter-controlled Fiem Foundation.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities included ₹1.2 crore for GST disputes. A vendor discounting scheme contingent liability dropped sharply from ₹85.0 crore to ₹0.9 crore because the company stopped discounting bills for two major customers. Capital commitments stood at ₹41.6 crore at the end of March 2026, up from ₹7.1 crore a year earlier.
reports.outlook: The management discussion notes that a new electronics test lab was commissioned in Gurugram to develop light-control modules and hands-off-detection sensors. However, both of these products are currently only at the proof-of-concept stage and have not yet secured any orders.
reports.other: FY26 net sales were ₹2,790.65 crore, generating an EBITDA of ₹393.3 crore and a net profit of ₹253.9 crore. By product, lighting contributed ₹2,095 crore, mirrors ₹298 crore, and plastic parts ₹254 crore. The company declared a dividend of ₹40 per share, totaling ₹105.3 crore. Following a fire at the Tapukara plant, ₹48.7 crore of assets were booked as recoverable against an ₹82.3 crore claim. The company has no rated debt and no credit rating.
flags: The auditor flagged an insurance claim for a recent plant fire as a key audit matter due to the significant management judgment involved.
The company directed ₹4.6 crore of its corporate social responsibility funds to a promoter-controlled foundation.
Key management pay included a ₹3.6 crore payout to a CEO who recently departed.
The company pays brand royalties and lease rents to its promoters and their controlled entities.

reports.auditor: The principal auditor gave an unmodified opinion but did not audit 12 subsidiaries accounting for ₹434.8 crore in assets, ₹348.8 crore in revenue, and ₹36.1 crore in PAT. This means most of the US business was audited by others. The consolidated report listed no key audit matters despite a transformational acquisition.
reports.relatedParties: The AGM notice sought approval for up to ₹500 crore in related-party dealings for FY27 between FZE and CrudeChem, including ₹100 crore for goods and ₹400 crore for loans and advances. A separate proposal included a 5-year loan of up to ₹100 crore to CrudeChem. The company gave loans to CrudeChem of ₹13.1 crore in FY26. Executive directors Sanjay Tibrewala and Aarti Jhunjhunwala are also managers of the CrudeChem group companies.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were negligible, consisting of about ₹0.3 crore for tax and ₹3 crore in bank guarantees. The group also had capital commitments of only ₹4.5 crore as of March 2026.
reports.other: The annual report did not disclose the acquisition price or purchase-price allocation for CrudeChem. However, it noted CrudeChem had a FY26 turnover of ₹252 crore, a PAT of ₹35.9 crore, and a net worth of ₹38.1 crore on a full-year consolidated basis.
flags: The principal auditor did not audit 12 subsidiaries, meaning most of the newly acquired US business was audited by other firms.
The consolidated auditor's report listed no key audit matters despite a major acquisition.
The annual report did not disclose the acquisition price or the purchase-price allocation for CrudeChem.
Approval is sought for up to ₹400 crore in loans and advances to CrudeChem, a 53%-owned subsidiary with a net worth of only ₹38.1 crore.
Executive directors Sanjay Tibrewala and Aarti Jhunjhunwala simultaneously hold manager roles at the CrudeChem group companies.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion and noted that the audit trail operated throughout the year. The only key audit matter was the impairment of the joint venture, Finolex J-Power. The joint venture's net worth is substantially eroded, and the investment is carried at ₹110.9 crore after ₹208.6 crore of past impairment.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid dividends of ₹37.6 crore to Orbit Electricals and ₹17.8 crore to Finolex Industries. It received a ₹72.4 crore dividend from Finolex Industries. The company sold ₹53.5 crore of material to its joint venture, Finolex J-Power, and provides this joint venture with unconditional financial support and a ₹185.7 crore bank guarantee.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities totaled ₹178.7 crore. This included ₹66.2 crore for sales tax, ₹51.1 crore for income tax, ₹36.5 crore for GST (which rose from ₹8.2 crore), and ₹23.9 crore for excise duty. The company also has a ₹185.7 crore bank guarantee supporting its joint venture. Unexecuted capital commitments were ₹22.5 crore at year-end.
reports.other: Standalone business segments showed electrical cables with ₹5,490 crore revenue and ₹562.9 crore EBIT. Communication cables had ₹500.3 crore revenue and ₹13.9 crore EBIT. Copper rods generated ₹2,142.6 crore in mostly captive revenue with ₹3.2 crore EBIT, and others (FMEG) added ₹261.5 crore revenue with ₹4.7 crore EBIT. Unallocable income was ₹224 crore. The company owns 32.39% of Finolex Industries, which in turn owns 14.51% of the company.
flags: A promoter control dispute is ongoing, with the company appealing a civil court order regarding votes cast by major shareholders.
Seven non-executive directors served unusually short terms of weeks to months between March and November 2024.
The joint venture's net worth has been substantially eroded, forcing the company to provide unconditional financial support and large bank guarantees.
Cross-holdings with Finolex Industries complicate company control and inflate reported other income.
There were changes in the compliance officer role during the year.

reports.auditor: The audit opinion is unmodified. The auditor listed three key audit matters: the capitalisation of internally generated intangibles, fixed-price revenue based on percentage of completion, and goodwill impairment.
reports.contingent: The company had no capital commitments at the end of March 2026, dropping from ₹25 crore a year earlier. Contingent liabilities were small at ₹9.7 crore and consisted mainly of tax and GST appeals.
reports.other: In FY26, the Americas made up 67.3% of revenue, Europe and the UK were 19.9%, and APAC was 12.8%. The company recorded an exceptional item of ₹11 crore for new labour codes. Additionally, FY26 profit was boosted by a ₹53.4 crore deferred-tax asset recognised on the losses of foreign subsidiaries.
flags: The parent company and its directors paid ₹2.6 crore in FY26 to settle a show-cause prosecution notice for the late deposit of ₹40.5 crore in tax deducted at source.
FY26 profit was flattered by a ₹53.4 crore deferred-tax asset based on foreign subsidiaries' losses.
The auditor flagged the capitalisation of internally generated research and development intangibles as a key audit matter.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion and noted no disputed statutory dues. They highlighted revenue recognition and the capitalization of property and equipment as Key Audit Matters, citing the judgment needed to separate capital from revenue expenses. A secretarial audit flagged that unpaid dividends from FY2015-16 to FY2017-18 were not yet transferred to the investor protection fund.
reports.relatedParties: The company sold roughly ₹26 crore of goods to promoter-group UAE entities Innovus Healthcare LLC and Fredna FZE in FY26. It paid about ₹1.7 crore in rent to promoter company Fredna Enterprises and roughly ₹2.4 crore in interest on loans from director Fredun Medhora. The company also gave an unsecured, non-interest-bearing loan of about ₹5.6 crore to subsidiary Fredun Retail, which is repayable on demand with no formal terms.
reports.contingent: The annual report notes that the company's bank loans are backed by the personal guarantees of the promoters. The auditor reported that the company has no disputed statutory dues.
reports.outlook: In the management discussion, the company reported a full-year net profit of ₹33.2 crore, a 60% increase. Management highlighted a strategy of owning or co-owning product registrations, noting they currently have about 1,100 registered products and over 1,000 more in the pipeline.
reports.other: The directors' report states the company operates in just one reportable segment, which is pharmaceuticals. Working-capital loans carry interest rates between 9% and 11.5%. The report also details that subsidiary Fredun Retail acquired pet care brands for zero cash by issuing equity in the combined entity.
flags: The Managing Director also acts as the Chief Financial Officer, leaving the company without an independent finance head.
The company gave about ₹5.6 crore in unsecured, zero-interest loans to a subsidiary, repayable on demand without formal terms.
The company engaged in significant related-party sales of roughly ₹26 crore to promoter-group entities in the UAE.
The annual general meeting sought approval to lend to or guarantee loans for corporate bodies in which directors have an interest.
A secretarial audit noted that older unpaid dividends have not yet been transferred to the government's investor protection fund.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave no qualification or emphasis of matter. Key audit matters were the investments in foreign subsidiaries and inventory valuation and existence. The auditor also noted the main raw and packing materials are acetic acid, vinegar, chemicals, salt, fresh greens, gherkins, garlic and spices.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid rent to promoter family members Iqbal Ahmed (₹57 lakh) and Kouser Afshan (₹11.4 lakh). It provided ₹15.9 crore in inter-corporate loans to its Spanish subsidiaries. In FY25, it borrowed ₹11.2 crore from the CMD and bought ₹9.5 crore in capex from Concrete Builders. None are large relative to sales, but family ties are dense.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities total ₹32.5 crore. This consists of a ₹30 crore corporate guarantee to Conservas Selectas, a ₹2.5 crore GST demand raised in the name of the predecessor partnership (Freshara Picklz Exports), and a TDS demand of roughly ₹0.19 lakh.
reports.other: The standalone company invested ₹7.53 crore of equity for 100% of two Spanish subsidiaries bought out of bankruptcy. It also allotted 23.16 lakh warrants on 13 March 2026 at ₹168 each (totaling ₹38.9 crore), with the ₹9.5 crore received so far going into the Spanish deal.
flags: The 328-day cash conversion cycle and ₹180 crore of debt, heading for a ₹400 crore borrowing limit, are key issues.
The company gave a ₹30 crore corporate guarantee for bank loans to a bankrupt Spanish business earning low margins.
The auditor highlighted inventory valuation and existence as a key audit matter, which is concerning given the 282 inventory days.
A ₹2.5 crore GST demand was raised in the name of the predecessor partnership.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The report included Key Audit Matters regarding revenue timing, tax provisions, and gratuity. It also noted that railway retention money of ₹26.7 lakh sits in receivables.
reports.relatedParties: Dealings with promoter-linked associate concerns totaled roughly ₹48 cr. This included sales of ₹13.4 cr to Frontier Alloy Steels. The company paid ₹10.8 cr for job work and ₹4.9 cr for components to Vishpa Rail Equipments, plus rent. It also had ~₹13.4 cr of purchases and ~₹5.1 cr of sales with NWFP Equipments and P.C. Packagers.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were tiny. They consisted of bank guarantees for ₹0.34 cr and letters of credit for ₹3.27 cr.
reports.outlook: Management stated a target of reaching ₹1,000 cr in revenue in the next 5 years. The report noted this growth will require introducing new products.
reports.other: FY26 revenue was ₹322.06 cr, EBITDA was ₹86.31 cr, and net profit was ₹61.31 cr. Company ROCE was 43.6%. The installed spring capacity is 9,900 MT. Management claims a 40% market share in coil springs. Exports were practically nil, with foreign-currency earnings of just ₹0.71 lakh for air-spring samples. Payable days collapsed to 33 from 94.
flags: Related-party dealings with promoter-linked associate concerns totaled roughly ₹48 cr, which is about 15% of revenue.
Five Bhatia family directors took about ₹7.2 cr in pay, amounting to approximately 12% of the year's profit.
The company holds ₹38.6 cr in mutual funds and ₹6.1 cr in listed equities, an unusual treasury structure for an engineering company.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unqualified opinion. Revenue was highlighted as a key audit matter because of price variations passed on to customers. The auditor also noted that the audit trail feature was not enabled in one software system.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are modest. They include ₹4.3 crore for direct tax and ₹7.2 crore for indirect tax, which involves ₹4.4 crore in GST TRAN-1 disputes. There are also claims of ₹24.7 crore and an old tax case regarding management fees paid to a group company.
reports.other: The company recorded an exceptional charge of ₹13.3 crore in FY26 related to the labour code. The report also highlights that a 30-year partnership with HL Mando and various technology licences give the company access to technology it could not build alone.
flags: The auditor reported that the required audit trail was not enabled in one of the software systems.
The company has an unresolved old tax case concerning management fees paid to a group company.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unmodified opinion. The only key audit matter highlighted was related to property, plant and equipment and capital expenditure.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings were small. Directors received ₹3.2 crore in pay. The promoter's son is employed by the company as a Vice President.
reports.contingent: Nord-Lock AB sued the company over Gallock washers with a ₹2 crore claim shown, but plaintiffs reserved the right to claim more. Other contingent items include disputed income tax of ₹3.3 crore, bank guarantees of ₹1.0 crore, and letters of credit of ₹5.5 crore. Capital commitments stood at ₹12.9 crore.
reports.other: The business is reported as one single segment. FY26 exports were ₹111.5 crore out of ₹314.3 crore total revenue. One customer made up 16.0% of sales, down from 23.6% in FY25. Current assets reported to banks differed from the books by up to ₹7.2 crore a quarter, which was reconciled. A Shanghai subsidiary posted a ₹0.07 crore loss.
flags: Nord-Lock AB is suing the company over a patent, and the plaintiffs reserved the right to claim damages on all infringing sales after the trial.
The company faces a disputed income tax liability of ₹3.3 crore.
Current assets reported to banks differed from the book value by up to ₹7.2 crore a quarter due to valuation differences.
A single customer accounted for 16.0% of the company's total revenue in FY26.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified, clean opinion with no emphasis of matter. The only key audit matter was checking the fair value of ₹107 crore in preference shares held in a subsidiary.
reports.relatedParties: The annual report states that related-party transactions were carried out in the ordinary course of business. No specific names or amounts are provided.
reports.contingent: The company provided a ₹445.7 crore performance guarantee to a customer on behalf of its Mexico subsidiary. There are also small tax disputes involving ₹28.7 crore for customs, ₹3.9 crore for excise and service tax, ₹3.9 crore for sales tax and GST, and ₹1.4 crore for income tax.
reports.outlook: Management's long-term Strategy 2030 aims to double volumes, grow operating profit by 2.5 times, and keep returns on capital above 22%. They target an operating profit of ₹25,000 per tonne, expected mostly in the later years of FY29 to FY30, with specialty products staying at 35% to 40% of the mix.
reports.other: The company reports only one business segment, with FY26 revenue of ₹2,202 crore from India and ₹3,025 crore from overseas. The year included an exceptional charge of ₹30.9 crore for new labour codes. The company also spent ₹37 crore on research and development and holds 111 patents.
flags: The company faces a large contingent liability of ₹445.7 crore for a performance guarantee, which equals roughly 16% of its standalone net worth.
There is customer concentration risk, as a single unnamed customer provides more than 10% of total revenue.
Income from a multi-year project in Mexico is kept confidential and not quantified in the financial notes.
The annual report does not disclose figures for total production capacity or capacity utilisation.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave no qualification. The key audit matter was the estimation of trade discounts.
reports.relatedParties: The company is promoted by the Mimani family through Srivaru Agro Pvt Ltd. At March 2025, it had lent ₹26.3 crore to holding company Srivaru Agro and Back Bone Sales Pvt Ltd, plus ₹12.6 crore in accrued interest. All of this was recovered in FY26. The company paid ₹1.68 crore in rent to a promoter company, Purnaa Real Estate (OPC), and paid rent to the MD and his father. MD pay was ₹3 crore, and total key management pay was ₹3.24 crore.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities included income-tax demands under appeal of ₹7.45 crore and GST demands of ₹4.31 crore. There was also ₹3.01 crore for saved EPCG duty.
reports.outlook: The commissioning of the IPO-funded Darjeeling plant has slipped to towards the end of the 2027-2028 financial year. Management cited supply-chain and geopolitical reasons for this delay.
reports.other: By March 2026, IPO funds were used to repay ₹60 crore of debt, spend ₹2.46 crore on the Darjeeling plant, and use ₹7.7 crore for general corporate purposes. An unutilised ₹49.5 crore sits in fixed deposits. The ESOP trust bought 5.245 lakh shares on the market for ₹10 crore.
flags: Only ₹2.46 crore of the ₹45 crore allocated for the new Darjeeling plant was spent by March 2026, and its launch has been delayed by about two years.
The company is sitting on ₹49.5 crore of idle, unutilised IPO funds in fixed deposits.
The company had lent large sums to promoter entities before the IPO, showing poor past governance, although these were fully repaid in FY26.

reports.auditor: The auditor identified related-party loans as a key audit matter. They highlighted uncertainty over whether ₹385 crore in related-party advances will be recovered. These are part of ₹957 crore in total loans and advances, which represent 33.86% of group assets.
reports.relatedParties: The company has lent ₹385 crore to related parties. The annual report also asked for shareholder approval for up to ₹200 crore in material transactions with MD Shekhar G. Patel for FY27, covering property purchases and other dealings. A similar resolution was proposed for his son, Amanvir Patel.
reports.contingent: The notes show long-running income tax disputes for AY2007-08 and AY2008-09 pending in the Supreme Court and Gujarat High Court. The exact amounts are not fully quantified. A separate tax demand of ₹1.55 crore for AY2015-16 was already recovered by the tax department.
reports.other: MD and CEO Shekhar G. Patel holds a 34.97% stake in the company. In total, the promoters hold 73.06%.
flags: The auditor highlighted uncertainty over the recovery of ₹385 crore lent to related parties.
Loans and advances make up a dangerously high 33.86% of total assets.
The company sought approval for up to ₹200 crore in property and other deals with the promoter and his son.
The company faces long-running, unquantified tax disputes in the Supreme Court and High Court.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion and noted no emphasis of matter. The key audit matter was revenue recognition on long-term fixed-price contracts, specifically the estimates of the cost to complete them.
reports.relatedParties: The company gave a ₹450 crore inter-corporate deposit to LM Wind Power Blades (India) Pvt Ltd, which is the GE Vernova group's cash-pool entity. This loan is repayable on demand and earns interest between 5.49% and 6.35%.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities total about ₹458 crore, which is large compared to the net worth of roughly ₹580 crore. This includes ₹203.7 crore for sales tax, ₹13.3 crore for GST, ₹110.6 crore for income tax, and ₹130.1 crore for other unacknowledged claims.
reports.other: The company has a 50% joint venture named NTPC-GE Power Services. For FY26, this venture reported revenue of ₹766 crore, a profit before tax of ₹43 crore, and an order book of ₹2,183 crore. The company's current sales come from services for coal-fired power plants, including core maintenance, upgrades, and completing legacy boiler projects.
flags: About half of the company's liquidity, amounting to ₹450 crore, is lent on demand to a related GE Vernova group entity.
Contingent liabilities of about ₹458 crore are unusually large relative to the company's net worth of roughly ₹580 crore.

reports.auditor: The auditor included an emphasis of matter in both the standalone and consolidated reports regarding a February 2026 notice from the PMLA Court in Patna for a pre-cognizance hearing on an Enforcement Directorate complaint. The auditor also highlighted revenue, receivables, and contract assets on AMISP contracts as a key audit matter, because allocating these across supply, installation, and operations requires management judgment.
reports.relatedParties: The company has significant exposure to the Gemstar platform, a joint venture where GIC holds 74% and Genus holds a 26% stake. Genus acts as the exclusive supplier to this platform. Related-party loans and advances, largely directed to the Gemstar platform, surged from about ₹75 crore to ₹528 crore during FY26.
reports.contingent: According to note 35 of the annual report, the company has contingent liabilities consisting of ₹119.9 crore in bank guarantees and approximately ₹19.5 crore related to tax disputes.
reports.other: The annual report is where the February 2026 PMLA court notice regarding the Enforcement Directorate case first surfaced, as it had not been updated during the previous earnings calls.
flags: The auditor issued an emphasis of matter concerning a court notice over an Enforcement Directorate and PMLA complaint.
Revenue and contract asset accounting on AMISP projects was flagged as a key audit matter due to the judgment involved.
Related-party loans and advances, primarily to the Gemstar joint venture, spiked significantly to ₹528 crore.
The company faces contingent liabilities of ₹19.5 crore from tax disputes.

reports.auditor: S.R. Batliboi (EY) gave an unqualified opinion with a single key audit matter regarding revenue cut-off. In the consolidated report, they noted that the audit trail was not enabled for direct database changes.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings are limited to the pay of key management personnel and directors.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include about ₹47 crore for income tax (down from ₹107 crore in FY25), ₹123 crore for excise, customs, and service tax, and ₹3.5 crore for other claims. The company also has uncertain tax positions related to 80-IA and transfer pricing.
reports.outlook: The management discussion notes that global demand grows slowly at about 2.25% to 2.5% a year. Global supply has seen 7 million tonnes of new natural soda ash capacity added in Inner Mongolia, alongside some plant closures in the US, UK, and Poland. The company faces structurally lower cash costs from these foreign producers but maintains a 26% share of Indian demand.
reports.other: Revenue from outside India was ₹114 crore (3.7%), with no customer exceeding 10% of revenue. Following the 2023 textiles demerger, the company has only one reportable business plus salt. Environmental and forest clearances for the Kutch greenfield project have been challenged by local residents before the National Green Tribunal.
flags: Environmental and forest clearances for the Kutch greenfield project are currently being challenged before the National Green Tribunal by local residents.
The auditor noted that the audit trail was not enabled for direct database changes in the consolidated report.
The company faces contingent liabilities of ₹123 crore for indirect taxes and has uncertain tax positions regarding 80-IA and transfer pricing.
The company had previously written off ₹53.6 crore in loans given to its old employee share trust.

reports.auditor: The FY26 audit report contained no emphasis of matter.
reports.other: In FY26, the company reported revenue of ₹1,533 crore, EBITDA of ₹313 crore, and a net profit of ₹201 crore. It listed its IPO during the year, raising ₹400 crore in fresh capital and ₹64.26 crore from a promoter offer-for-sale. Promoters Gopal Kabra and Mehul Shah hold a 79.2% stake. Following the IPO, the company ended the year with a net cash surplus of ₹240.6 crore.
flags: Growth depends heavily on the delayed launch of the PM-KUSUM 2.0 government scheme.
The current order book of ₹541 crore is too thin to support the management's target of doubling revenue.
The company faces high customer and geographic concentration risk due to its reliance on Maharashtra state schemes.
Receivables are stretched, with debtor days standing at 140 due to government subsidy programs.
The stock trades below its ₹153 IPO price, and promoters sold ₹64 crore during the listing.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters included year-end revenue cut-off and Cenexi goodwill impairment. Seven subsidiaries, which accounted for ₹2,006 crore in revenue, were audited by other auditors.
reports.relatedParties: The company has related-party dealings with Fosun companies. It makes sales to Fosun Pharma USA of roughly ₹240 crore a year, with a receivable of about ₹68 crore at March 2026. It also purchases raw materials from Fosun Wanbang and Chongqing Carelife.
reports.contingent: The company faces an unquantified dispute at Cenexi Laboratories Thissen in Belgium with a partner over 2016 and 2021 cooperation agreements, which management cannot reliably estimate. Other contingent liabilities are small, including tax claims of about ₹10 crore.
reports.outlook: The chairman's letter outlines a ₹2,000 crore capital expenditure programme over five years for the base business. This covers new lines for vials, ophthalmics, blow-fill-seal, liposomes, and CDMO. For FY26, base business revenue grew 11% to ₹4,561 crore, while Cenexi revenue reached €182 million with EBITDA improving to near breakeven.
reports.other: The company operates a B2B model doing contract manufacturing and profit-sharing. Customer concentration is moderate, with one customer accounting for 13.5% of revenue at ₹870 crore. Cenexi goodwill rose to ₹294 crore due to euro translation, with no impairment, though its discount rate increased to 12.6%. For FY26, ROCE was 11.7% and RoNW was 10.5%.
flags: The promoter is a Chinese state-linked group, which poses risks if US BIOSECURE-type rules are widened.
There is an unquantified dispute with a partner at Cenexi Laboratories Thissen that the company cannot reliably estimate.
Seven subsidiaries generating ₹2,006 crore in revenue were audited by other auditors.
A single customer accounted for 13.5% of total revenue, or ₹870 crore, in FY26.

reports.auditor: The auditor, S R B C & Co LLP, noted key audit matters for revenue recognition on long contracts, business-combination accounting, and impairment testing for ₹229.6 crore of goodwill. In the audit trail, they reported that a database-level log was not evidenced for the parent company's ERP system.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small. They consist of indirect tax and income tax disputes totalling roughly ₹12 crore.
reports.outlook: The management discussion highlighted an opening FY27 order backlog of ₹2,194 crore, up 34% from the prior year. Total order intake grew 20% to ₹3,714 crore. Non-traditional industries such as defence, nuclear, oil and gas, and semiconductors accounted for 43% of the FY26 order intake.
reports.other: Geographical revenue included ₹976 crore from India and ₹2,548 crore from overseas. The standalone Indian business posted revenue of ₹1,034 crore and EBITDA of ₹135 crore. Consolidated capital expenditure of ₹97 crore was lower than the depreciation of ₹158 crore. Shares of subsidiaries are pledged against acquisition debt of GMM International, though there are no promoter share pledges.
flags: The auditor noted that a database-level audit log was not evidenced for the parent company's ERP system.
Shares of subsidiaries are pledged against the borrowings of GMM International.
Consolidated capital expenditure in FY26 was lower than the annual depreciation.

reports.auditor: The auditor included an emphasis of matter regarding a Department of Telecommunications licence-fee demand of ₹21,370 crore. The auditor also flagged Key Audit Matters concerning urea subsidy recognition, an inventory of stores and spares worth ₹527 crore, and tax or legal litigation.
reports.relatedParties: The annual report notes that the promoters, Gujarat State Investments and GSFC, hold a 41.3% stake in the company. The notes on loans also classify a ₹2,431 crore deposit parked with a state-owned body corporate as unsecured.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities total ₹359 crore, comprising contract claims of ₹230 crore, excise and GST of ₹105 crore, and income tax of ₹24 crore. Capital commitments stand at ₹1,508 crore. The company faces a ₹21,370 crore licence-fee demand from the Department of Telecommunications, but it has not shown this as a contingent liability.
reports.other: Most Bharuch plants operated well above rated capacity in FY26, including ammonia at 148%, urea at 131%, and acetic acid at 155%. In contrast, the TDI-II plant at Dahej ran at 77% capacity over 276 days due to equipment, maintenance, and gas constraints. Sales are largely domestic, with only ₹12 crore in export incentives. Additionally, a 2012 demerger of a VSAT and ISP business worth ₹6 crore remains unsettled because the licence transfer was never approved.
flags: The company faces a massive ₹21,370 crore telecom licence-fee demand that is neither provided for nor disclosed as a contingent liability.
A substantial ₹2,431 crore deposit parked with a state entity is classified as unsecured in the annual report.
The TDI-II plant at Dahej suffered from reliability issues, running at only 77% utilization due to equipment, maintenance, and gas constraints.
A 2012 demerger of the VSAT and ISP business remains unsettled because the required licence transfer was never approved by regulators.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave a clean opinion with no qualifications or emphasis of matter. The report noted revenue recognition for crop protection and goodwill impairment as key audit matters.
reports.relatedParties: The company does pet-food contract manufacturing for Godrej Consumer Products, which brought in about ₹9.5 crore in profit during the fourth quarter. It also provided a surety bond for a related party.
reports.contingent: The company has about ₹131 crore in claims not acknowledged as debt. These include disputed excise, customs, GST, and income tax claims.
reports.other: During the year, the company spent ₹708.6 crore to buy 36.79% of Creamline Dairy, plus ₹8.9 crore for another 0.46%, taking its ownership to 99.78%. It also put ₹199 crore into Astec LifeSciences' rights issue, raising its stake to 67.03%.
flags: The company faces about ₹131 crore in unacknowledged claims for various taxes and duties.
A surety bond was provided on behalf of a related party.

reports.auditor: The auditor included an emphasis of matter regarding the December 2024 fire at the Rajkot plant and the related insurance accounting, noting that ₹37.46 crore was received in FY26. The key audit matter was the estimation of discounts and rebates.
reports.contingent: The company has roughly ₹69 crore in undeposited, disputed GST dues following a GST audit at its Rajkot branch for the years FY17 to FY22. This equals about 14% of its net worth.
reports.other: According to the secretarial audit, Managing Director Bipinbhai Hadvani pledged an additional 47 lakh shares to Tata Capital. This increases his total encumbrance to 1.05 crore shares, representing 8.42% of the company's equity.
flags: The company faces approximately ₹69 crore in disputed, undeposited GST dues from FY17 to FY22, representing roughly 14% of its net worth.
The Managing Director has pledged more shares, bringing his total encumbered stake to 8.42% of the company's equity.

reports.auditor: The FY26 audit had no emphasis of matter.
reports.other: Accounting for the acquisition of Alcon Builders & Engineers recognised customer-relationship intangibles of ₹87.5 crore and goodwill of ₹30.2 crore. A scheme of amalgamation of Alcon and Jogbani Highway into the company is currently under the NCLT process.
flags: The Alcon acquisition added ₹30.2 crore in goodwill and ₹87.5 crore in intangibles to the balance sheet, and the formal merger is still pending NCLT approval.

reports.auditor: The auditor included an emphasis of matter regarding a 2022 CBI case. In this incident, three employees were arrested along with NHAI officials in Guwahati under the Prevention of Corruption Act. The matter is currently stayed by the Gauhati High Court.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities mostly consisted of bank guarantees, which stood at ₹2,449 cr at March 2026. The company also had tax and other claims amounting to ₹110 cr. This included GST on HAM annuities of ₹61 cr at its special purpose vehicles.
reports.other: The annual report notes an income-tax search that took place on 9 October 2025. This search was conducted at the company's offices and the homes of its promoters and the CFO, though no tax demand had been made yet.
flags: The auditor drew attention to a 2022 CBI corruption case involving the arrest of three company employees.
An income-tax search was conducted in October 2025 at the company's offices and the homes of its promoters and CFO.
The company faces ₹110 cr in tax and other claims, including a GST dispute on HAM annuities.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unmodified opinion. The only key audit matter noted was regarding US revenue recognition, chargebacks, and rebate accruals. Additionally, one tiny subsidiary was audited by a different firm.
reports.relatedParties: The company purchased ₹47.2 cr of packaging from Product Armor Packaging, a promoter-influenced entity, up from ₹41.5 cr in FY25. It also paid ₹7.6 cr in rent to the Chigurupati Family Trust, an increase from ₹2.0 cr the previous year. The Chairman and Managing Director received ₹28.4 cr in pay, which is roughly 5% of the net profit. Three other family members were paid ₹2.8 cr each.
reports.contingent: Outstanding capital commitments stood at ₹318 cr at the end of March 2026. Contingent liabilities for tax disputes were tiny at just ₹0.9 cr. Additionally, RMRx LLC is suing Granules Consumer Health for breach of contract in New Jersey, with depositions currently under way, though the financial size of the lawsuit is not disclosed.
reports.other: The company operates and reports as a single business segment. Exports accounted for 96% of FY26 revenue, bringing in ₹5,144 cr out of the ₹5,366 cr total. No single customer represented 10% of revenue. The company raised ₹666 cr in equity during FY26, which included a ₹366 cr upfront payment for promoter warrants. Borrowings at the end of the year included ₹174 cr in lease liabilities.
flags: The annual report notes that the Gagillapur FDA warning letter negatively impacted revenue through a production slowdown, higher consultancy fees, and increased air-freight costs.
RMRx LLC is suing the consumer health subsidiary for breach of contract, with the size of the claim not disclosed.
The company engaged in related-party deals, including paying ₹47.2 cr for packaging to a promoter-influenced entity and ₹7.6 cr in rent to a family trust.
The Chairman and Managing Director's pay was ₹28.4 cr, which takes up roughly 5% of the company's total net profit.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. A key audit matter was the impairment of subsidiary investments, where indicators were identified but no impairment was booked. Under CARO, the auditor noted that an audit trail was not kept for changes by certain privileged users and was not enabled at the database level.
reports.contingent: Consolidated contingent liabilities included ₹129.4 crore for customs, largely from an appealed ₹56.4 crore demand (plus interest and penalties) that treated 2018–2021 e-scooter part imports as complete knock-down kits. Other disputed sums were ₹44 crore for sales tax, ₹33.7 crore for claims, ₹26 crore for excise, ₹14.5 crore for wages, and ₹6.1 crore for income tax.
reports.outlook: Management highlighted the structural risk of a shrinking market for diesel three-wheelers, noting diesel now makes up only about 20% of the L5 segment as electric vehicle share rises. It also flagged policy risks, noting that the L5 electric three-wheeler subsidy ran out in December 2025.
reports.other: The electric mobility unit (GEML) saw its standalone loss widen to ₹272.8 crore in FY26. Other loss-making units included MLR Auto (₹26.9 crore) and Bestway (₹8.3 crore). Exceptional items totaled ₹35.3 crore, which included a ₹16 crore write-off for a failed e-powertrain project, a ₹15.8 crore labour-code provision, and a ₹3.6 crore fee for land-use breaches. The notes also detailed past write-offs and repayments regarding FAME-II subsidy breaches.
flags: The auditor found that the required audit trail was not maintained for changes by certain privileged users and was not enabled at the database level.
The company is fighting a major customs demand of ₹56.4 crore plus interest and penalties over how it imported e-scooter parts.
Losses at the main electric vehicle subsidiary widened significantly to ₹272.8 crore during the year.
The company booked exceptional expenses for a failed e-powertrain project and for breaching land-use rules.
Management warned that its core diesel three-wheeler market is shrinking as electric vehicles gain share, even as key electric subsidies run out.

reports.auditor: S S Kothari Mehta & Co. LLP gave an unmodified opinion. Revenue recognition on standalone sales of ₹2,376 crore and preserving the audit trail were key audit matters. There were no CARO qualifications for any group companies.
reports.relatedParties: Dealings involved the Mittal family group. The company purchased ₹74.1 crore of goods from Greenpanel Industries in FY26, compared to ₹72.7 crore in FY25. Commission of roughly ₹5.8 crore was paid to Seema Realcon, where a director is the whole-time director's brother. The MD and CEO received pay of about ₹9.9 crore, up from ₹8.3 crore.
reports.contingent: Consolidated indirect-tax disputes jumped to ₹70.3 crore at March 2026, up from just ₹2.8 crore a year earlier. The parent company's share is only ₹7.0 crore, leaving about ₹63 crore unexplained in subsidiaries. Direct-tax disputes stood at ₹5.7 crore. The company also had letters of credit for ₹39.8 crore and capital commitments of ₹17 crore.
reports.other: Segment results on an EBIT basis for FY26 showed a ₹476 crore profit for laminates, a ₹28.7 crore loss for plywood, and an ₹86.0 crore loss for panels. The chipboard segment held ₹829 crore in assets but earned an EBIT loss of ₹86 crore for the year.
flags: Consolidated indirect-tax disputes jumped unexpectedly to ₹70.3 crore, leaving roughly ₹63 crore unexplained within subsidiary companies.
Higher interest and depreciation costs from new plants caused FY26 net profit to fall 60% below FY24 levels, despite 32% higher revenue.
Return on capital employed is a weak 8%, weighed down by a high net debt of ₹934 crore.
Management pushed back the plywood segment's break-even target from the full year to just the final quarter of FY27.
The company restated its previous quarter's laminate volumes and realisations in a presentation without clear explanation.

reports.auditor: The standalone auditor's report gave a clean opinion. The only key audit matter was estimating discounts and rebates in revenue, which is relevant because discounting is now aggressive.
reports.relatedParties: The company reported small sales of ₹5.6 crore to Greenlam group firms in FY26. It also paid rent to a promoter firm.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities included small indirect-tax disputes of ₹10.4 crore. The company also has an outstanding EPCG export obligation of ₹154 crore, down from ₹306 crore a year earlier. Failing to meet this obligation means repaying the duty saved along with interest.
reports.other: The management discussion stated that MDF made up 91.2% of FY26 revenue, while plywood accounted for under 10%. Receivable days increased from 11 in FY25 to 21 in FY26, and the cash cycle was 38 days. The notes also recorded a CFO change in June 2025 and a new sales head in March 2025.
flags: The Income Tax Department searched the company's registered office, plants, and the promoter's home in early 2026, with the financial impact not yet determined.
GST intelligence searched offices and the Rudrapur plant in July 2025, leading to a voluntary payment of ₹4.8 crore for ineligible input-tax credit along with interest and penalty.
An outstanding EPCG export obligation of ₹154 crore carries the risk of having to repay saved duty with interest if the company fails to meet it.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion and listed revenue recognition as a key audit matter. The CARO report flagged cash losses at the joint venture and delays in depositing statutory dues by the parent company and its subsidiaries.
reports.relatedParties: Family-linked companies Greenlam and Greenpanel are listed as related parties. The company has small approved trades with them, including sales to Greenlam of up to ₹10 crore.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include ₹26.9 crore for indirect taxes and ₹2.8 crore for consumer cases. The company provided ₹554.6 crore in guarantees for its subsidiaries and joint venture. It also has a ₹115 crore commitment for a proposed investment. An income-tax search occurred in early 2026 without any demand order yet.
reports.outlook: The management discussion notes that the MDF industry had a capacity of 5.1 million CBM against a demand of 3.7 million CBM in FY26. It highlights the risk that debt is rising into an MDF industry that still has 28% spare capacity.
reports.other: The company recorded an exceptional write-off of ₹15.2 crore in FY26 for GMEL, Dubai, which included a ₹9.5 crore guarantee, a ₹2.7 crore investment, and ₹3.0 crore in advances. The stake in GMEL was reduced from 49% to 19% and the entity was renamed Greenwud Panel.
flags: Income-tax authorities searched the company's premises in early 2026.
The auditor reported cash losses at the joint venture and delays in depositing statutory dues.
The company recorded a ₹15.2 crore exceptional write-off for its Dubai entity, continuing a trend of international write-offs.
Management noted the risk of taking on debt to expand into an MDF industry that still has 28% spare capacity.

reports.auditor: The auditor, Rajendra & Co., gave an unqualified opinion. They included a key audit matter regarding contingent liabilities that stem from uncertain tax positions.
reports.relatedParties: Dealings were mostly with subsidiaries. The company had an outstanding loan of ₹8.5 crore to a subsidiary, made ₹9.9 crore in purchases from GCSL, and put ₹5 crore equity into GCSL. Key management personnel received ₹5.2 crore in pay, and ₹0.68 crore was paid as professional fees to the management's side.
reports.contingent: Standalone contingent items at March 2026 included GST of ₹6.65 crore, income tax of ₹3.14 crore, and sales tax of ₹0.71 crore. There were also excise and service tax claims of ₹0.20 crore, and other claims of ₹1.68 crore. The company provided bank guarantees of ₹8.37 crore and a ₹6.53 crore guarantee for subsidiary loans.
reports.outlook: Management noted that Indian reclaim rubber consumption grew 7% in CY2025, with a 15% growth in tyre applications. The company is reassessing the operating model for its polyolefins subsidiary. The report highlights risks from non-compliant recyclers and a demand-supply imbalance for extended producer responsibility (EPR) certificates.
reports.other: Standalone reclaim rubber net revenue was ₹464.4 crore with a segment result of ₹53.9 crore. The 'Others' segment had ₹61.7 crore in revenue and a ₹1.8 crore result. Unallocated costs were −₹26.3 crore. Consolidated equity fell to ₹178.4 crore despite a profit, heavily impacted by a ₹13.3 crore pre-tax loss on a euro loan cash-flow hedge. The polymer composites business was shut down due to US tariffs.
flags: Key management personnel pay of ₹5.2 crore was unusually high compared to the standalone profit of just ₹8.9 crore.
The Directors' report carelessly claimed profit took a 5% hit, when standalone profit actually fell 76%.
The auditor highlighted uncertain tax positions as a key audit matter.
The polymer composites business was shut down in Q3 FY26 because of US tariffs.
The company faces risks from non-compliant recyclers and an imbalance in the EPR certificate market.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Revenue recognition regarding rebates, returns, and timing was flagged as a key audit matter. The auditor also noted that an audit trail was maintained in the SAP system.
reports.relatedParties: The company pays annual rent of ₹4.2 crore to promoter company Gufic Private Ltd and ₹0.48 crore to Gufic Chem. It keeps a ₹3.5 crore security deposit with Gufic Private. Gufic Private also owns the Navsari land used as loan security and provides a corporate guarantee of up to ₹36.4 crore.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include ₹2.1 crore in sales tax and excise disputes. There are also ₹9.6 crore in letters of credit and guarantees.
reports.other: The promoters hold a 72.50% stake in the company. There are no shares pledged by the promoters.
flags: The Navsari plant land used as loan security is owned by a promoter company, tying a key asset to related parties.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The report noted no key audit matters and confirmed that the required audit trail was properly maintained.
reports.relatedParties: The company guaranteed ₹498 crore of debt for promoter-group company Inox Renewable Solutions, an increase from ₹422 crore. It also reported outstanding balances due of ₹94 crore from Inox Renewable Solutions and ₹43 crore from Inox Wind.
reports.contingent: Total consolidated contingent liabilities rose to ₹698 crore from ₹614 crore the previous year. This includes ₹200 crore in tax disputes, such as transfer-pricing additions on foreign subsidiary sales and corporate guarantees. It also faces an ₹80 crore customs demand regarding advance-licence conditions. No provisions were made for these disputes.
reports.outlook: Management highlights its backward integration into materials like fluorspar as a core cost advantage. It is targeting end markets such as semiconductors, batteries, data centres, green hydrogen, and automotive. Management notes that incoming PFAS regulations in Europe and the United States remain a long-term risk for the fluoropolymers business.
reports.other: The chemicals segment posted revenue of ₹5,030 crore and an EBITDA of ₹1,371 crore, a 27% margin. Meanwhile, the electric vehicle products subsidiary is loss-making, bringing in ₹33 crore in revenue but an EBITDA loss of ₹80 crore. The standalone debt-to-equity ratio improved to 0.22 from 0.31.
flags: The company guarantees ₹498 crore of debt for promoter-group entity Inox Renewable Solutions.
Contingent liabilities have grown to ₹698 crore and include large unprovisioned tax and customs disputes.
The new electric vehicle materials segment is generating widening losses, posting a negative EBITDA of ₹80 crore on minimal revenue.
Proposed PFAS chemical regulations in Western markets pose a long-term threat to the fluoropolymers business.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. They noted fixed-price revenue based on percentage-of-completion as a key audit matter.
reports.contingent: The company reported small contingent liabilities. These include ₹5.2 crore for income tax and ₹8.7 crore for GST.
reports.other: The company owns a campus in Electronic City, funded by a 10-year term loan maturing in 2032. Borrowings were ₹1,494 crore at March 2026, largely consisting of overdrafts secured by liens on the company's own fixed deposits. Goodwill stood at ₹777 crore with no impairment recorded. Recent acquisitions shifted the geographic revenue mix more toward India and the Middle East.
flags: Gross cash and gross debt are both inflated by borrowing against the company's own fixed deposits, which carries a material interest cost.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion but noted an exception regarding the audit trail. They reported that the edit log is not enabled at the database level for the company's accounting software.
reports.contingent: Standalone contingent liabilities include letters of credit, corporate guarantees, and standby letters of credit totaling ₹377 crore, an increase from ₹246 crore. These are mainly for subsidiary borrowings. The company also has export obligations of ₹34 crore and small tax claims.
reports.other: The annual report confirms that all proceeds from the company's initial public offering have been fully used.
flags: The auditor warned that the accounting software does not have an edit log enabled at the database level.
Contingent guarantees and letters of credit increased to ₹377 crore to support subsidiary borrowings.

reports.auditor: The auditors gave an unmodified opinion. They highlighted one key audit matter regarding Kavach revenue recognition. The company books this revenue on a percentage-of-completion basis using estimated costs to complete, and auditors flagged these estimates as complex.
reports.relatedParties: Shareholders were asked to approve up to ₹700 crore a year in transactions with subsidiaries, the Cochin Shipyard joint venture, and associate companies. These associates include Tonbo Imaging, Naval Systems & Technologies, and Xalten Systems, where promoter-family director Kavita Prasad Aluru sits.
reports.contingent: Outstanding bank guarantees stood at ₹303.4 crore. The company carries a Kavach warranty provision of ₹92.75 crore for the defect-liability period. Capital commitments were ₹46.9 crore. Tax and legal claims are small, including ₹24.7 crore for excise, ₹6.3 crore for sales tax, and ₹5.4 crore for an arbitration.
reports.outlook: Management expects Kavach to remain about 50% of sales in FY27, with strong sales continuing into FY28 before a potential decline from FY29 onwards. They target total sales over ₹5,000 crore by FY30. Electric truck pilot sales are delayed to July 2027 to redesign motors without rare-earth magnets. Army and artillery fuze approvals are expected in 2027. Ongoing expansions include doubling PLT battery capacity, Ni-Cd batteries, and an electronic fuze plant. Telecom batteries face excess capacity and price pressure.
reports.other: All FY26 revenue growth came from Kavach-led Electronics, which posted ₹1,626 crore. Batteries contributed ₹1,416 crore and Defence ₹212 crore. Exports totaled about ₹528 crore. The company formed a new joint venture with Cochin Shipyard for marine electric drive trains. Surplus cash will fund R&D, dividends, private equity, and direct start-up stakes. There is no plan to appoint a single CEO for succession; instead, nine semi-independent units will be run. Standalone net profit was ₹796.8 crore.
flags: About 50% of FY26 sales came from one product (Kavach) and one customer (Indian Railways).
Management expects Kavach sales and profits to face competition and potentially decline starting in FY29.
Auditors flagged the complex estimates used by management to recognize Kavach revenue on a percentage-of-completion basis.
Strategy and capital allocation rely heavily on the founder-chairman, creating key-person risk.
Electric truck pilot sales have been delayed by nine months due to rare-earth magnet supply issues requiring a motor redesign.

reports.auditor: B S R & Co. (KPMG network) gave an unmodified opinion. The key audit matter was impairment of goodwill (₹388cr) and other non-financial assets. The audit trail (edit log) was not enabled for privileged and database-level changes at the parent and four subsidiaries, and not at all at four other group companies. Under CARO, title deeds of two properties in Bengaluru and Vijayawada (₹49.5cr gross) are still in the names of merged companies. Eleven subsidiaries and seven step-down subsidiaries (₹875cr of assets) were audited by other firms.
reports.relatedParties: HCG paid ₹58.1cr in cash to buy back 16.2 lakh vested options at the change of control, including ₹17.1cr to former CEO Meghraj Gore and ₹2.0cr to the former CFO; this was charged to equity, so it never reached profit. CVC's parent separately paid ₹48.3cr of bonuses directly to HCG employees on 30 May 2025. The founder and chairman, Dr B.S. Ajaikumar, received ₹2.57cr of medical consultancy charges and ₹2.0cr of professional fees after becoming non-executive, plus ₹1.0cr of salary for April–May. After the year, the Milann fertility business was sold to Inviga Healthcare Fund I, which he controls, for an enterprise value of ₹63.2cr.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were ₹103cr (₹69cr a year earlier), of which ₹76.1cr is customs duty under EPCG export-promotion licences (₹52.2cr). An ₹8.3cr misclassification demand carries a 100% penalty and personal penalties on employees, and there is a ₹10.4cr GST demand on FDG, the PET-scan tracer, plus old VAT, sales-tax and excise disputes. Undiscounted lease commitments are ₹1,453cr, ₹150cr of it due within a year.
reports.outlook: Management says about 400 beds already built but not in use can be opened over three to four years. Mature hospitals (over ₹10cr of revenue a month) earn a 26% margin and 27% return on capital, against 5% and −22% for the six smallest, so filling the newer ones is the main lever.
reports.other: FY26 revenue was ₹2,538cr: West ₹1,133cr, South ₹995cr, East ₹283cr, Kenya ₹74cr (2.9%) and Milann ₹60cr. Doctors are paid largely as consultants (₹549cr, 21.6% of revenue). Owners' profit was ₹13.8cr after ₹44.6cr of exceptional items (₹31.9cr Milann goodwill write-down, ₹12.7cr labour-code gratuity). Lease liabilities were ₹825cr, with ₹85.9cr of lease interest and ₹84.5cr of right-of-use depreciation below operating profit. The report's own return on capital ratio was 6.63%, against the 14% pre-Ind AS figure management quotes. KKR (Hector Asia) owns 54.27% and the founder 9.30%.
flags: The Milann fertility business was sold to a fund controlled by the chairman, at about one times sales after a ₹31.9cr write-down.
₹58cr was paid in cash to buy back staff options at the change of control (₹17.1cr to the former CEO), charged to equity so it never touched profit.
Contingent customs-duty claims under EPCG licences rose to ₹76cr from ₹52cr, one carrying a 100% penalty and personal penalties on employees.
The audit trail was not enabled for privileged changes at the parent and four subsidiaries, and not at all at four other group companies.
The report's own return on capital was 6.63%, far below the 14% management quotes.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The only key audit matter noted in the report was regarding provisions and contingent liabilities.
reports.relatedParties: By the end of FY26, the company had put ₹180 crore in equity and ₹400 crore in optionally convertible debentures into TACC. It also guaranteed ₹1,230 crore of TACC's SBI loan facilities.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities totalled about ₹110 crore. This included ₹81 crore for income tax, which increased from ₹72 crore. The company also has a ₹1,230 crore corporate guarantee given to SBI for TACC.
reports.other: The company reported two segments for FY26. The graphite segment had a result of ₹270 crore, up from ₹217 crore in FY25. The power segment reported ₹15 crore. Total standalone revenue was ₹2,569 crore. India accounted for ₹847 crore or 33% of sales, while the USA accounted for ₹440 crore or 17%. No single customer made up more than 10% of sales.
flags: The annual report shows the US made up 17% of FY26 revenue, contradicting management's claim on a call that it was under 10%.
The company faces contingent liabilities for income tax disputes totalling ₹81 crore.
The company has extended a large ₹1,230 crore corporate guarantee for TACC.

reports.auditor: The auditor's opinion and the CARO statutory checklist report are clean.
reports.relatedParties: The company purchased ₹64 crore in goods from promoter-group Exicom in FY26, up from ₹11 crore in FY25. The managing director's pay increased to ₹12.07 crore from ₹7.50 crore. Anant Nahata, a relative of key management, is MD and CEO of Exicom and will hold 6.5% of the defence subsidiary HASPL.
reports.contingent: The company has ₹764 crore in bank guarantees and ₹358 crore in letters of credit. It also provided a ₹265 crore guarantee for its subsidiary HTL.
reports.other: The business operates in four segments: Telecom Products, Defence, Turnkey Contracts, and Others. FY26 telecom revenue was ₹2,931 crore with a 26.1% margin, while the turnkey segment posted a ₹113 crore loss. Exports reached ₹2,047 crore. One customer generated ₹646 crore of sales, and Reliance Jio made up 13–14%. The company holds ₹206 crore in short-term loans from other companies costing 12–15%. Most bank loans include personal and promoter guarantees, plus a 23.9% pledge of subsidiary HTL.
flags: Purchases from promoter-group company Exicom jumped sharply to ₹64 crore from ₹11 crore the previous year.
There is no regular chairman on the company's board of directors.
A single customer accounted for ₹646 crore, representing over 10% of total FY26 sales.
Most bank loans require the managing director's personal guarantee and a promoter guarantee, alongside a pledge of 23.9% of subsidiary HTL.
The company pays high interest rates of 12–15% on ₹206 crore of short-term loans from other companies.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The only key audit matter highlighted was revenue recognition, specifically concerning discounts and price adjustments.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small, consisting of about ₹32 crore for tax and other matters. There is also an EPCG export obligation of ₹10 crore.
reports.outlook: The company plans to export about 50,000 tonnes of coal tar pitch from its new capacity by FY28. To support this growth, it has added new liquid-pitch export terminals at Haldia and Mangalore.
reports.other: Carbon materials & chemicals earned ₹828 crore on ₹4,367 crore revenue; Power made ₹19 crore, and Others ₹274 crore. Exports reached ₹1,358 crore across 61 countries, with no single customer exceeding 10% of revenue. The company reported a ₹64 crore foreign-exchange loss. Capital work-in-progress was ₹372 crore, with fixed-asset additions of about ₹450 crore. Around ₹511 crore in bank deposits are pledged against credit facilities.
flags: The company has a large, opaque exposure of about ₹935 crore in low-yield NCDs of a non-group company (DBRL) to fund a tyre revival.
Management claims there will be no incremental debt, yet borrowings more than doubled from ₹313 crore to ₹770 crore in FY26.
Working capital is stretching, with the cash conversion cycle lengthening from 73 days to 103 days over two years.
Cash generation is weak, as FY26 operating cash flow was only 64% of EBITDA and free cash flow was a negative ₹63 crore.
Earnings quality is impacted because 17% of FY26 pre-tax profit came from volatile other income and fair-value gains on unlisted investments.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion with no emphasis of matter. The key audit matter was the timing of revenue recognition.
reports.relatedParties: The company trades with a promoter-group entity, Elventive Tech Pvt Ltd, which also holds preferential warrants. In the second half of FY26, Hirect bought ₹11.9 crore and sold ₹6.8 crore with this entity. It also bought ₹16.7 crore from Force Motion Technology LLP, another entity influenced by key management personnel.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small, consisting of ₹1.0 crore for GST, ₹11.4 crore for bank guarantees, and ₹5.8 crore for letters of credit. The company also has capital commitments of ₹10.3 crore.
reports.other: A 1:1 bonus issue doubled the share count. The company declared a dividend of ₹1.40 per share. The Board's Report notes new subsidiaries including Coincade Studios, Hirect Global Holdings, and Hirect FZ-LLC. A ₹100 crore preferential issue to Tata Small Cap Fund was noted as an event after the balance sheet. Promoter-group entity Elventive Tech Pvt Ltd received 2 lakh warrants at ₹1,368.22, with 25% received but unused at year-end. The company has 190 to 200 engineers and 42 to 50 products in development.
flags: The company has related-party dealings and issued warrants to a promoter-group entity named Elventive Tech Pvt Ltd, which shares a brand name with the French subsidiary and requires clear disclosure.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave no qualification or emphasis of matter. Revenue recognition was noted as the key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: The promoter holding company, Vanity Case India Pvt Ltd, was amalgamated into the company, with 46,458,145 new shares allotted to its shareholders. The Nashik manufacturing unit of Avalon Cosmetics Pvt Ltd, an entity under common control, was also demerged into the company in exchange for 1,680,939 shares. Previous FY25 figures were restated for these group mergers.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small. They include an income-tax demand of ₹2.78 crore, bank guarantees of ₹1.91 crore, and letters of credit of ₹0.87 crore.
reports.other: The company operates 42 factories across 12 states and holds US FDA and Russian approvals for its Baddi site. While it does not name its customers, its history of taking over brand-owner plants shows links to Hindustan Unilever, Reckitt, and PepsiCo.
flags: The company absorbed its promoter holding company and another commonly controlled entity in a related-party restructuring.
Prior year financial figures for FY25 had to be restated to account for these group mergers.

reports.auditor: The consolidated report includes a material uncertainty related to going concern for the discontinued subsidiary Evok Homes, which has a negative net worth of ₹5.6 crore and had its ₹8.4 crore investment fully written off. Under Other Matters, the auditor noted that two companies were consolidated using management-certified unaudited figures.
reports.relatedParties: The company provided a ₹25 crore corporate guarantee for loans taken by Hintastica.
reports.contingent: Standalone contingent liabilities total around ₹28–30 crore for tax demands and claims. Within this, claims not acknowledged by the company jumped to roughly ₹23.5 crore. The company also maintains a ₹25 crore corporate guarantee for Hintastica's loans, which is down from ₹69.5 crore a year earlier.
reports.other: The company recorded several exceptional items in FY26. It took a ₹44 crore charge for exiting fans, coolers, purifiers, and furniture fittings, which covered asset write-offs, bad debts, and stock. It also booked a ₹39 crore standalone write-down on its Hintastica investment, representing about ₹34–35 crore of goodwill at the group level, alongside a ₹0.7 crore labour-code cost.
flags: The auditor raised a material uncertainty regarding the going concern status of subsidiary Evok Homes.
Two companies were consolidated based solely on management-certified unaudited figures.
Standalone claims not acknowledged by the company jumped to approximately ₹23.5 crore.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The audit highlighted related-party transactions and defined-benefit obligations for labour-code changes as key audit matters. Other auditors audited two foreign and three step-down subsidiaries, which accounted for ₹438 crore in revenue and ₹408 crore in assets. Three foreign step-down units, including Omeras entities, were prepared under local GAAP and reviewed by local auditors.
reports.relatedParties: Key management personnel (KMP) were paid ₹12.8 crore, which was about 23% of the year's net profit. The company took ₹11.1 crore in unsecured loans from KMP and repaid ₹26.9 crore, paying ₹0.7 crore in interest. A ₹1 crore capital advance was given to KMP. Additionally, the company made ₹7.8 crore in sales to entities where directors have an interest, leaving a ₹3.0 crore receivable balance.
reports.contingent: The company has small contingent liabilities consisting of approximately ₹0.7 crore for a disputed service tax claim.
reports.other: The annual report notes that the listed entity Kinam Enterprise, a heat exchanger business that was 70% owned by the company, amalgamated into HLE Glascoat in August 2025.
flags: The auditor flagged related-party transactions as a key audit matter.
Key management personnel remuneration of ₹12.8 crore consumed approximately 23% of the year's net profit.
The company issued a ₹1 crore capital advance to key management personnel.
The company engaged in ₹7.8 crore of sales to entities in which its directors have an interest.
Significant foreign subsidiaries generating ₹438 crore in revenue were audited by other auditors or only reviewed under local GAAP.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters included revenue recognition for discounts and return provisions, and testing goodwill and brand impairment. The auditor noted an audit-trail lapse: one price-master application ran all year without an edit log, and three systems, including distribution and point of sale, failed to log changes made by privileged users.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party transactions consisted of dealings with subsidiaries and pay for key management personnel. The annual report noted nothing unusual in these transactions.
reports.contingent: The company has a major dispute with a former Dubai distributor, RSM General Trading, which claimed AED 45 million (₹100 crore). An Indian arbitration ruling recently found Honasa's termination valid and awarded it AED 7.25 million (₹19 crore), though a Dubai court hearing was pending. Total claims against the company not acknowledged as debts stand at ₹34 crore, up from ₹28 crore last year. Capital commitments are ₹1 crore.
reports.outlook: Management notes that consumer switching costs in beauty and personal care are low. To defend its market share, the company plans to rely on its speed of launching new products, content creation, and search share. The company will also continue its asset-light model, relying on outsourced manufacturing while directing capital toward brand building and advertising.
reports.other: The company operates in a single beauty and personal care segment, dominated by India, and does not disclose revenue splits by segment or brand. In FY26, 68% of revenue came from online channels and 32% from offline. The board's report noted like-for-like revenue of ₹2,479 crore, a 71.2% gross margin, and ₹200 crore in net profit. IPO funds were primarily used for advertising (₹182 crore), general acquisitions (₹122 crore), and brand outlets.
flags: The auditor flagged a lapse in IT controls, noting that one price-master application lacked an edit log all year and three other systems did not record privileged-user changes.
The company is fighting a massive ₹100 crore legal claim from a former Dubai distributor.
Total claims against the company not acknowledged as debts increased to ₹34 crore in FY26 from ₹28 crore the prior year.
Management warned that consumer switching costs are low, meaning customers can easily defect to rival beauty brands.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The only key audit matter noted in the report was tax litigations.
reports.relatedParties: The company purchased ₹3.6 crore in services from promoter firm HPL India Ltd and recorded a deferred receivable of ₹4.7 crore from it. Key management personnel pay was ₹7.2 crore. The company also redeemed ₹21 crore in 10% cumulative redeemable preference shares held by promoters.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are very small, totaling well under ₹10 crore. They consist entirely of various tax, excise, VAT, and GST demands.
reports.other: Metering segment revenue fell 4.6% to ₹1,026 crore, while the consumer and industrial segment grew 25.6% to ₹785 crore. The company closed two lighting-project joint ventures in March 2026 and inaugurated a dedicated panel-meter and water-meter plant in Gurugram. The accounts showed a small exceptional charge of roughly ₹5 crore, and the company declared a dividend of ₹1 per share.
flags: The FY26 accounts show no receipt of a ₹129.6 crore trademark settlement paid by Havells to the promoter group.
Trade receivables at the end of March 2026 included about ₹29 crore that is over three years old and ₹8 crore flagged as credit-impaired.

reports.auditor: The auditor's report noted revenue cut-off as its only key audit matter. Under the CARO section, the auditor pointed out that title deeds for some land in Silvassa and Daman are still held in former company names like Huhtamaki PPL Ltd.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid its parent, Huhtamaki Oyj, ₹105.3 cr in CY25 for software, IT, and centralised services, which is up from ₹80.5 cr in CY24. No trademark royalty was paid, but ₹99.1 cr was owed to the parent at the end of CY25. The parent also received ₹10.2 cr in dividends. Additionally, the company owes an ECB debt to fellow subsidiary Huhtamaki Finance Co. V B.V., with the due date moved to June 2027.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small. The largest is an excise duty appeal of about ₹9 cr, plus a few other tax disputes of a few crore each. Capital commitments dropped to ₹15.5 cr at the end of CY25 with no growth projects in the pipeline. The company has an export obligation of ₹295 cr against duty-free imported machines; ₹153 cr of this is completed, but a discharge certificate is awaited.
reports.outlook: Management noted that revenue has been shrinking for three years because the company dropped low-margin business. Capex for CY25 was ₹55.8 cr, focused entirely on capacity optimisation, efficiency improvements, and maintenance. The board also approved an undisclosed capex plan for a Bengaluru plot to meet a 50% land-use condition.
reports.other: The company has only one reportable segment for packaging and does not disclose product, volume, or capacity splits. Management refused to share capacity utilisation details, citing competition. Three parent nominee directors left during the year. A property in Daman was held for sale, and label operations were consolidated.
flags: Payments to the parent company for software and centralised services are large and rising, reaching ₹105.3 cr in CY25.
Three parent nominee directors resigned from the board during 2025-26.
Title deeds for some land properties are still held in former company names rather than the current entity.
Management declines to disclose capacity utilisation or volume splits to investors, citing competition.
The company has no growth projects in the pipeline, with capital commitments falling to just ₹15.5 cr.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion that does not contain any qualification. The report highlights revenue recognition on customised solutions as the only key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: The company reported sales of ₹2.3 crore to promoter-influenced firms, such as Frizics Transport Refrigeration. It also paid rent and vehicle hire charges to relatives of key management, and held ₹0.2 crore in loans from key managers. The file notes these transaction amounts are small.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities consist entirely of bank guarantees. These amounted to ₹4.3 crore and ₹24.7 crore across the two years shown in the report.
reports.other: The directors' report shows that the company's wholly owned subsidiary, Bharat Refrigerations, generated ₹48 crore in revenue for FY26. Another subsidiary, Icebest, in which it holds a 60% stake, generated about ₹3 crore in revenue.

reports.auditor: The auditor provided an unmodified opinion but highlighted two Key Audit Matters. First, they flagged the capitalization of product under development due to the risk that costs are capitalized without meeting proper criteria. Second, they flagged revenue recognition, noting the risk that revenue might be booked early to meet expectations.
reports.contingent: The notes detail delivery-delay penalties, known as liquidated damages. The company deducted ₹3.8 crore from its FY25 revenue for these penalties and carried a provision of ₹3.9 crore for liquidated damages as of March 2026.
reports.outlook: The Directors' report notes that securing US federal and defence sales depends on a pending "Blue sUAS" certification. Furthermore, the annual report outlines a completion schedule for ₹56.8 crore worth of intangible projects currently in "time and cost over-run," targeting completion within a year.
reports.other: The company reports as a single segment, providing no audited split between defence and civil revenue. Its US subsidiary posted a loss of ₹9.5 crore on just ₹0.19 crore of revenue in FY26. The company heavily capitalizes development costs; it added ₹81.6 crore to "product under development" in FY26. The total balance for these uncompleted products reached ₹109.5 crore by March 2026, with ₹13 crore of this amount being more than two years old.
flags: Capitalized research and development spending of ₹81.6 crore flatters the earnings, as the actual operating profit was only ₹6 crore.
The auditor raised concerns over potential early revenue recognition and improper capitalization of development costs as Key Audit Matters.
The US subsidiary is burning cash, losing ₹9.5 crore on negligible revenue while awaiting required certifications.
Supply chain pressures for electronic parts and cameras have caused delivery delays, forcing the company to carry a ₹3.9 crore provision for penalties.

reports.auditor: Price Waterhouse & Co Chartered Accountants LLP gave an unmodified opinion. They noted a database-level audit trail was enabled only from 18 May 2025. The auditor highlighted the impairment test of a ₹97 crore investment in associate IFB Refrigeration as a key audit matter, noting it required a significant level of management's judgement.
reports.relatedParties: The company bought ₹235.7 crore of goods from associate IFB Refrigeration, up 67% from ₹141.1 crore in FY25. It bought ₹145.3 crore of services from promoter-group company IFB Appliances Ltd, up from ₹120.4 crore. Sales included ₹80.5 crore to IFB Automotive Pvt Ltd and ₹13.6 crore to Travel Systems Ltd. Advances to the associate rose to ₹61.8 crore from ₹32.5 crore. Key management personnel pay was ₹53.9 crore.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were ₹36.6 crore, comprising ₹12.3 crore for GST, ₹5.5 crore for excise, ₹5.8 crore for income tax, and a ₹10.2 crore share of the associate's liabilities. No provision was made for higher e-waste EPR floor prices being contested in court. Capital commitments were ₹56.7 crore at March 2026, up from ₹13.1 crore a year earlier.
reports.other: FY26 segment revenues were ₹4,461 crore for Home Appliances (FY25 ₹4,060 crore) and ₹1,007 crore for Engineering (FY25 ₹900 crore). Motors added ₹66 crore and Steel ₹185 crore, bringing total revenue to ₹5,619 crore. Gross product sales of ₹7,105 crore included ₹1,733 crore of traded products. This gross figure was reduced by ₹1,778 crore (25%) for trade schemes and discounts to reach ₹5,327 crore net. Engineering MD P H Narayanan left on 31 March 2026.
