flags: Related-party purchases are large, including ₹235.7 crore from associate IFB Refrigeration and ₹145.3 crore in services from promoter-group company IFB Appliances Ltd.
Advances to the associate company increased to ₹61.8 crore.
The auditor flagged the ₹97 crore investment in the associate as a key audit matter due to the significant management judgment required for its impairment test.
The database-level audit trail was only enabled from 18 May 2025.
Trade schemes and discounts consumed ₹1,778 crore, representing 25% of gross product sales.

reports.auditor: The statutory audit opinion is unmodified. However, the auditor included an emphasis of matter on two issues. First, a 2016 amalgamation used a purchase method creating ₹267 crore in goodwill that Ind AS would not have allowed, though it is now fully amortised. Second, an ₹8.3 crore income-tax appeal is pending in the Calcutta High Court. Additionally, the corporate governance certificate is qualified because shareholder approval for a director's appointment was four days late.
reports.relatedParties: The Directors' report states there were no material related-party transactions during the year.
reports.contingent: The company faces contingent income-tax disputes of ₹11.2 crore. Additionally, goodwill-depreciation claims for assessment years 2018 through 2021 have been disallowed or reopened, which carries a potential tax impact of about ₹40 crore. There is also a pending Section 10AA tax appeal for ₹8.3 crore. Standalone capital commitments were ₹35 crore at the end of March 2026, up from ₹6 crore a year earlier.
reports.other: The annual report breaks down external sales by location. India generated about ₹1,102 crore, making up 58% of sales. Europe accounted for roughly ₹429 crore or 23%, while the Americas brought in around ₹338 crore or 18%. Sales in the rest of Asia were small. The Directors' report also confirms that no promoter shares are pledged.
flags: The corporate governance certificate is qualified because shareholder approval for a director's appointment missed the deadline by four days.
The auditor highlighted an ongoing ₹8.3 crore Section 10AA income-tax appeal pending in court.
The company faces a potential tax hit of around ₹40 crore from disallowed and reopened goodwill-depreciation claims.
There are additional unresolved income-tax disputes totaling ₹11.2 crore.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion and confirmed that the audit trail was maintained. They highlighted key audit matters regarding revenue cut-off and the carrying value of the company's investment in its UAE subsidiary.
reports.relatedParties: The company made sales of ₹49.9 crore to promoter-controlled Mysore Petro Chemicals and Bluesky Petrochem, up from ₹25.4 crore in FY25. It also bought ₹14.5 crore of property and equipment from them in FY25. There is a reporting contradiction: the business responsibility report claims related-party purchases were 55.16% of all purchases, but the financial notes state zero purchases.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities total about ₹100 crore. This includes ₹42.7 crore for income tax, ₹40.3 crore for a disputed Maharashtra electricity duty, ₹14.2 crore for excise, ₹3.0 crore for service tax, and ₹0.3 crore for GST. Additionally, rupee term loans of ₹146.9 crore carry personal guarantees from two directors, which binds the estate of one director who recently died.
reports.outlook: Management forecasts domestic demand for phthalic anhydride to grow from 0.56 million tonnes in 2025 to 0.72 million tonnes by 2031, a 6.5% growth rate. The management discussion also noted the return on capital employed dropped to 1.21% and debt-service cover fell to 0.73.
reports.other: The company operates a single reportable segment for phthalic anhydride and its derivatives. Exports provided 10.33% of turnover at ₹199 crore. Consolidated profits were dragged down by a ₹20.9 crore loss in the UAE subsidiary. The standalone business booked a ₹28 crore forex and fair-value loss on a Euro loan. Capital commitments stood at ₹65.6 crore. Treasury surplus is invested in credit-risk instruments like InvITs and corporate debentures.
flags: The UAE subsidiary lost ₹20.9 crore on unexplained investments without having commenced regular operations, which the auditor flagged as a key audit matter.
There is a major disclosure error regarding related-party purchases, with one section of the report claiming they are 55.16% of total purchases and the notes claiming zero.
The company faces roughly ₹100 crore in contingent tax and duty claims, equal to about 5% to 6% of its market value.
Treasury funds are exposed to credit risk through investments in real estate debentures and NBFC bonds rather than standard bank deposits.
The estate of a deceased director remains bound by a personal guarantee covering ₹146.9 crore of the company's term loans until lenders release it.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion with no key audit matters. However, they included a modified remark regarding the company's compliance with audit-trail or edit-log rules under Rule 11(g).
reports.relatedParties: Several promoter-linked firms trade with the group through purchases, rent, and sales. These include Raina Metal Tech, Life Tek Solutions, Singh Engineering, Singh Enterprises, Safe Solutions, IKIO Led Lighting LLC, and Bright Future USA. In FY26, sales included ₹1.2 crore to Krishna Computech and ₹1.0 crore to Bright Future USA. Promoters also lent money to the group during the year, though specific amounts were unclear.
reports.contingent: The company has small contingent liabilities. These include a customs and indirect-tax demand of ₹1.3 crore, an income tax demand of ₹1.4 crore, and a corporate guarantee of ₹9.0 crore. Capital commitments stood at ₹21.9 crore at the end of March 2026.
reports.other: Exports were ₹116 crore in FY26, making up 19.5% of total revenue. Customer concentration is high, with one customer contributing ₹146 crore. Subsidiary IKIO Solutions relies on major customers for over 93% of its revenue, while Royalux Lighting gets over 38% from two customers. The deadline to use ₹39 crore in unspent IPO funds was extended to FY27. Acquisitions included 88% of Gravus Tech and Royalux General Trading LLC.
flags: The auditor issued a modified remark concerning compliance with audit-trail edit-log requirements.
A single customer accounted for about a quarter of group revenue at ₹146 crore in FY26.
Subsidiary IKIO Solutions depends heavily on major customers for over 93% of its revenue.
The company has left ₹39 crore of its IPO funds unspent three years after listing, forcing a deadline extension.
The group engages in related-party trades and borrowed money from its promoters during the year.

reports.auditor: Price Waterhouse Chartered Accountants LLP gave an unmodified opinion. The key audit matter was revenue net of discounts and rebates, which relies on judgemental accruals. The auditor flagged an audit-trail exception, noting that edit logs were not kept for changes made by certain privileged users or for direct database changes.
reports.relatedParties: Managing Director Hemant Jalan received ₹3.6 crore in pay. The company paid ₹2.14 crore in Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funds to the Payal Jalan Charitable Trust, which is controlled by the promoters. This was an increase from ₹1.71 crore in FY25. There were also minor dealings with subsidiary Apple Chemie and Halogen Chemicals, an associate controlled by key management personnel.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities increased to ₹29.2 crore from ₹23.3 crore the previous year. This includes ₹27.4 crore for GST disputes, notably a ₹19.26 crore demand with interest and penalties regarding IPO-related expenses, which is under appeal. Other items include ₹1.6 crore for income-tax matters and ₹0.2 crore for a Kerala building tax dispute. Indigo also guarantees ₹18 crore of bank facilities for its subsidiary Apple Chemie.
reports.outlook: Management noted that a new 90,000 KL plant in Jodhpur will increase water-based paint capacity by 52%, from 1,72,000 KL to 2,62,000 KL per year. While this capacity is far ahead of current demand, the company stated the primary benefits will be reduced freight costs and improved delivery lead times for North, East, and Central India, rather than immediate volume gains.
reports.other: The corporate overview stated that a new 12,000 KL solvent plant in Jodhpur has been operational since early 2026.
flags: The auditor flagged that edit logs were not maintained for direct database changes or edits by certain privileged users.
The company faces a ₹19.26 crore GST demand, including interest and penalties, related to IPO expenses.
Corporate social responsibility payments of ₹2.14 crore were routed to a charitable trust controlled by the promoters.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion with no loan defaults reported. However, they included an Emphasis of Matter regarding a material uncertainty about the going-concern status of subsidiary FPP Holding LLC. The report also noted Key Audit Matters for ₹44 crore in capitalised R&D development costs and a ₹24.4 crore sales-return provision.
reports.contingent: Consolidated contingent liabilities include ₹32.6 crore for GST, ₹6.6 crore for excise and service tax, and ₹4.8 crore for income tax. The company also listed ₹12.8 crore in bank guarantees and an FMRAI wage case that has been pending since 2012.
reports.other: The promoters (Kare/Panandikar family) hold a 58.9% stake with no shares pledged. Subsidiary FPP Holding LLC reported a loss of ₹23.7 crore for the year. The company also booked a ₹10 crore bad-debt provision, which included a bankrupt customer.
flags: The auditor warned of a material uncertainty regarding the going concern of subsidiary FPP Holding LLC, which has a negative net worth of ₹42.3 crore.
Capitalised R&D costs of ₹44 crore flatter the reported financial results in a loss-making year.
Trade payables stretched significantly, surging 48% to ₹309 crore, with overdue payments to MSME suppliers reaching ₹90 crore.

reports.auditor: The standalone auditor's report contained no qualifications or emphasis of matter. However, the auditor did highlight the impairment testing of investments in subsidiaries—specifically InfoBeans Inc. in the US and Eternus/InfoBeans CloudTech—as a key audit matter.
reports.other: Consolidated notes show the top 5 clients account for roughly 40% of revenue and the top 10 make up 57%, with no single client exceeding 10%. About 94% of clients return each year. The board's report noted employee turnover rose to 14% in FY26, up from 12% in FY25. The report also recorded a buyback of 2,15,520 shares at ₹464 and a 3:1 bonus issue.
flags: Three customers accounted for about 66% of total receivables at the end of March 2026.
The auditor flagged the impairment testing of investments in subsidiaries as a key audit matter.

reports.auditor: Statutory auditor CND & Associates gave an unmodified opinion with no emphasis of matter and no key audit matters reported. Under CARO, the auditor noted ₹4.21 crore of loans or advances given to another entity.
reports.relatedParties: Promoters lent money to the company, leaving ₹3.41 crore from the MD and ₹0.57 crore from the CFO outstanding at March 2026. The company purchased goods and fixed assets from directors' proprietorships, Prasad Innovations and Prasad Engineering Works. Filings also cover up to ₹6 crore to Keerthi Enterprises (a relative's firm) for factory construction, up to ₹50 crore with Swastik, and a ₹30 lakh yearly professional fee to the promoters' daughter.
reports.outlook: Management notes that Scope Metals acts as its exclusive agent in Israel, securing a ₹15 crore single order in May 2026 with consistent repeat deliveries. The company also plans to set up a DRDO-backed 100 kg vacuum-melting inert-gas atomiser in the next year or so. Funded by an ₹8.73 crore DRDO sanctioned outlay, this will have a capacity of 200–250 tonnes for clean powders.
reports.other: For FY26, segment revenues were ₹40.6 crore for powders and ₹13.3 crore for tungsten heavy alloys, with exports making up 18% (₹9.8 crore). Four of the seven board members belong to one family. The accounting policy allows capitalising borrowing costs on qualifying assets, but the FY26 cash flow shows the ₹0.85 crore interest paid exactly matched the P&L finance cost, disclosing no capitalised amount. Segment profits were not maintained before FY26.
flags: Two FY26 accounting write-backs for unbilled revenue and unvalidated capitalised development totaled ₹4.88 crore, making up about 9% of the year's sales.
The auditor flagged ₹4.21 crore of loans or advances given to another entity under CARO reporting.
The company engages in extensive related-party transactions, including promoter loans, purchases from directors' firms, and factory construction by a relative's proprietorship.
Four of the seven board directors belong to a single family.
Segment profit records were not maintained before FY26, obscuring the historical profitability of its separate divisions.

reports.auditor: BSR & Co. gave an unmodified opinion with a key audit matter on revenue recognition. The auditor included a remark stating they were unable to comment on whether the audit trail was enabled at the database layer of the company's two accounting packages.
reports.relatedParties: The company had small dealings, such as packing material and minor sales, with promoter-relative entities including Azine Healthcare, Pharmatech Healthcare, Nugenic Pharma, and Shubh Packaging. There are outstanding loans to subsidiary Univentis of ₹49.9 crore, down from ₹107.1 crore in the prior year. Additionally, directors Manoj and Vinay Lohariwala provided personal guarantees for bank borrowings.
reports.contingent: The company disclosed no contingent liabilities. A GST show-cause notice for ₹15.8 crore regarding excess input tax credit refunds from May 2020 to March 2024 was dropped on 14 April 2026.
reports.other: Standalone revenue included a ₹19.1 crore GST-linked incentive, and other income included ₹6.9 crore from government-grant amortisation. Government-grant receivables rose to ₹55.4 crore from ₹26.1 crore. The company also paid its first dividend to promoters. The financial notes report only a single operating segment and do not provide revenue splits for the Jammu plant or for domestic versus export businesses.
flags: A rising share of profit comes from government incentives, with ₹55.4 crore sitting as a receivable, making collection timing and scheme continuity important.
The auditor was unable to confirm whether the audit trail was enabled at the database layer of the accounting packages.
The annual report lacks basic disclosure on revenue splits, such as domestic versus exports or specific business unit performance, reporting only a single operating segment.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. They noted one key audit matter regarding revenue recognition for long-term design-build contracts. The company uses the percentage-of-completion method, and auditors flagged the cost-to-complete estimates as judgemental.
reports.relatedParties: The company made sales to promoter-group company INOX Air Products of ₹145.0 crore in FY26, down slightly from ₹151.6 crore in FY25, accounting for about 9% of revenue. There were also smaller purchases from INOX Air Products and Bombay Fluid System Components, and rent paid to INOX Chemicals LLP.
reports.contingent: The company faces a tax reassessment notice over a ₹52 crore deduction claimed for money paid on behalf of a former US subsidiary, though it has interim relief from the High Court. Other contingent liabilities include ₹245 crore in bank and corporate guarantees, ₹3.1 crore in disputed service tax, and ₹1.1 crore in income tax. Capital commitments stood at ₹15.8 crore.
reports.other: The company reports only one segment, cryogenic equipment, in its accounts and does not calculate segment-wise EBITDA. Capital expenditure was ₹47.4 crore in FY26 and ₹127.4 crore in FY25. The company also booked an exceptional expense of US$0.94 million (₹8.5 crore) after an arbitral tribunal found it breached a non-compete agreement.
flags: Auditors highlighted cost-to-complete estimates for long-term project contracts as a judgemental key audit matter.
An arbitral tribunal ordered the company to pay US$0.94 million (₹8.5 crore) for breaching a 10-year US non-compete agreement.
The company received a tax reassessment notice regarding a ₹52 crore deduction claimed for money paid on behalf of its old US subsidiary.

reports.auditor: The auditor included an emphasis of matter regarding funds invested in six SPVs for SECI wind projects. These projects had expired completion dates, rejected extensions, ₹55.8 crore in invoked bank guarantees, and pending appeals. The auditor also highlighted ₹114.8 crore of services rendered but not yet billed. Key audit matters involved revenue recognition, litigation, and impairment of receivables, which are mainly from state-owned enterprises.
reports.relatedParties: The company gave a corporate guarantee of ₹180.5 crore for a bank loan of Inox Clean Energy. Group company GFL guarantees ₹498 crore of Inox Wind's borrowings. The company also expensed ₹13.5 crore for doubtful inter-corporate deposits owed by related parties.
reports.contingent: The company faces contingent liabilities of ₹95.9 crore for contractor claims. It also faces customer claims of ₹121.5 crore, which are limited to outstanding balances.
flags: The auditor flagged investments in six SPVs where deadlines expired, extensions were rejected, and ₹55.8 crore in bank guarantees were invoked.
The auditor noted ₹114.8 crore of operations and maintenance services that were rendered but not yet billed.
The company faces contingent liabilities including ₹95.9 crore in contractor claims and ₹121.5 crore in customer claims.
The company provided a ₹180.5 crore corporate guarantee for a bank loan of related party Inox Clean Energy.
The company expensed ₹13.5 crore for doubtful inter-corporate deposits owed by related parties.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion and confirmed the audit trail operated all year. They highlighted two key audit matters. The first is revenue recognition on license and implementation contracts, which involves multiple performance obligations and percentage-of-completion accounting. The second is the capitalisation of product development.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include tax proceedings, but the amounts are not material. The company has ₹13 crore in bank guarantees, which are fully cash-backed. Capital commitments stood at ₹12 crore at the end of March 2026.
reports.outlook: Management notes in the report that North America is now one of the company's most important growth markets.
reports.other: The promoter holding stands at 29.6% and is slowly declining. The company did not disclose any pledged shares.
flags: The auditor flagged revenue recognition and the capitalisation of product development as key audit matters because both require accounting judgments that allow profit to be moved between periods.

reports.auditor: Price Waterhouse gave a clean opinion. The auditor noted two key audit matters: the goodwill impairment test on the AQuity cash-generating unit, and revenue recognition.
reports.contingent: The company faces small tax and transfer-pricing disputes of ₹4.9 crore. It also received a FY22 transfer-pricing demand of ₹16.1 crore after the year-end. AQuity India has EPFO provident-fund demands, which carry a ₹12.6 crore provision. A contingent consideration of about ₹41.7 crore from past business combinations is still on the books.
reports.outlook: The management discussion notes a healthcare sector and geographic concentration risk, as the entire business is located in the US. It also highlights that net debt fell from ₹563 crore in March 2025 to ₹252 crore in March 2026.
reports.other: The company reports a single segment with 100% US exposure. The existing term loan is secured by a lender pledge of 100% of the shares in the US subsidiary, IKS Inc. The report also notes the TruBridge acquisition had an enterprise value of up to $565 million.
flags: The entire business is concentrated in the US healthcare sector, posing a significant geographic and sector risk.
A post-year-end transfer-pricing demand of ₹16.1 crore and other tax disputes of ₹4.9 crore are outstanding.
AQuity India faces EPFO provident-fund demands that required a ₹12.6 crore provision.
The auditor highlighted the AQuity unit's goodwill impairment test and revenue recognition as key audit matters.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters included revenue cut-off and the valuation of ₹371 crore in inventory. Under CARO, the auditor noted no undisputed dues in arrears and no disputed statutory dues pending.
reports.relatedParties: FY26 purchases from promoter-linked entities totaled ₹131.9 crore, up 31% from ₹100.7 crore. This included ₹69.4 crore from Mayadevi Polycot, ₹40.0 crore from NCVI Enterprises, and ₹22.5 crore from NM Merchantiles. These were stated as arm's length transactions. NCVI also provided a ₹27.65 crore surety on customs bonds.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were small at ₹5.7 crore. This includes a ₹2.06 crore customs order for duty and penalties alleging incorrect ASEAN-India FTA certificates of origin, which the company is appealing. Outstanding capital commitments stood at ₹69 crore at March 2026.
reports.other: The company operates two segments, pharmaceuticals and chemicals, from a single integrated site at Barnala, Punjab. The management discussion noted API capacity of 30,726 MTPA and chemicals capacity of 1,82,400 MTPA. The promoter group raised its holding with no preferential share issue during the year.
flags: Managerial remuneration of ₹21.75 crore is high, representing about 16% of the company's FY26 net profit.
Purchases from promoter-linked entities rose 31% to ₹131.9 crore, involving the same entities that are buying the company's shares on the open market.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters included inventory valuation, impairment of plant assets (which total ₹4,942 crore, or 40% of assets), and impairment of investments and loans to subsidiaries. The CARO report highlighted ₹54.06 crore in unpaid loans and interest to associate Krebs Biochemicals, with some unpaid for over 730 days. The auditor also noted the audit trail for direct database changes was kept for only three days due to system limits.
reports.relatedParties: The company has an associate, Krebs Biochemicals. Ipca provided loans to Krebs, of which ₹54.06 crore in loans and interest remained unpaid. Additionally, Ipca pledged a ₹11 crore deposit for a bank loan taken by Krebs.
reports.contingent: The company reported small contingent liabilities totalling ₹249 crore.
reports.other: Consolidated revenue was ₹9,646 crore, split between India at ₹4,387 crore and outside India at ₹5,260 crore (including ₹2,140 crore from the US). The company took a ₹118.9 crore impairment on its exposure to Krebs. Exceptional items included an EU fine for Niche Generics of €19.55 million (₹204 crore). Unichem closed its Ireland plant and sold its Jogeshwari land for ₹279 crore, booking a ₹17.65 crore gain.
flags: The auditor noted that ₹54.06 crore of loans and interest to associate Krebs Biochemicals were unpaid, with some amounts overdue for more than 730 days.
Ipca impaired ₹118.9 crore of its exposure to Krebs Biochemicals during the year.
The company booked a ₹204 crore exceptional expense to pay an EU fine for Niche Generics.
The IT audit trail for direct database changes was only maintained for three days because of system limitations.

reports.auditor: SCV & Co. LLP gave an unmodified consolidated opinion but included an emphasis of matter. The subsidiary auditor flagged a material uncertainty on going concern for Bioeq Energy Holdings, which had a capital deficiency of ₹443 crore and depends on parent support. A Singapore subsidiary also relies on parent support. Key audit matters included revenue recognition for industrial-project contracts.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include claims not acknowledged as debt of ₹80.9 crore, up from ₹58.1 crore the prior year. The company also reported export-obligation bonds of ₹720 crore and customs bonds or guarantees of ₹48 crore. Capital commitments stood at ₹89.5 crore, compared to ₹69.5 crore previously.
reports.other: The Puri family promoters own 62.43% of the company and have not pledged any of their shares.
flags: The subsidiary's auditor flagged a material uncertainty on going concern for Bioeq Energy Holdings due to a ₹443 crore capital deficiency.
Claims not acknowledged as debt rose to ₹80.9 crore from ₹58.1 crore the previous year.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave a qualified opinion because foreign subsidiaries—accounting for ₹229.7 crore of turnover (81% of group revenue) and ₹200 crore of net worth—were not audited by any auditor, only certified by management. The report included an emphasis of matter regarding ongoing inquiries from Indian regulatory authorities with uncertain outcomes. It also flagged receivables over six months and unconfirmed balances as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: The company is run by a family board consisting of Managing Director Sanjay Soni, his mother Shashi Soni (Chairperson), and his wife Kiran Soni (Chief Financial Officer). Their pay is modest, ranging from ₹3 lakh to ₹4 lakh a month.
reports.contingent: The company is facing transfer-pricing and income-tax disputes totaling around ₹17.7 crore for the assessment years 2009-10 to 2017-18, with some cases pending at the Karnataka High Court.
reports.other: The management discussion noted a cost shift, as FY26 employee costs fell from ₹112 crore to ₹109 crore while consultancy charges jumped from ₹30 crore to ₹80 crore. The company aggressively capitalizes development costs, holding ₹276 crore in intangible assets (mainly technical know-how). It added about ₹23 crore in FY26 against just ₹14.5 crore in amortization. Domestic revenue for FY26 was ₹19.4 crore.
flags: The auditor issued a qualified opinion because foreign subsidiaries generating 81% of group revenue (₹229.7 crore) are entirely unaudited.
An emphasis of matter was raised due to ongoing, uncertain inquiries from Indian regulatory authorities.
There are unresolved transfer-pricing and income-tax disputes amounting to ₹17.7 crore.
The auditor highlighted overdue receivables exceeding six months and unconfirmed balances as a key audit matter.
The company aggressively capitalizes software development costs, which flatters operating profit while free cash flow remains consistently near zero.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The only Key Audit Matter raised was regarding revenue recognition.
reports.relatedParties: The company is controlled by Infinity Holdings, a Mauritius-based private equity fund, along with Aresko entities. The promoter group holds a 69.1% stake following a buyback in which the promoters did not participate.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities for FY26 totaled about ₹22 crore, rising from ₹16 crore the previous year. This included ₹10.2 crore for customs duty, ₹5.8 crore for VAT, a new ₹4.8 crore income tax claim, and ₹1.6 crore for GST.
reports.outlook: Management flagged an ongoing transition in its C&FA distribution network in the risk section. The report also warned of structural industry risks stemming from National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM) price controls and government initiatives pushing for generic prescriptions.
reports.other: The company operates an entirely asset-light model, relying completely on third-party contract manufacturers. Its distribution reach includes over 1,000 medical reps and 1,200 distributors across 4,000 towns, with about 92% of its portfolio outside price controls. Managing Director Manish Gupta received FY26 pay of ₹3.54 crore, which included ESOP perquisites, and he was allotted 1,55,000 shares upon exercise.
flags: The company is controlled by a private equity fund, meaning a future stake sale could alter management or strategy.
A C&FA distribution transition is underway, posing potential risks to channel inventory.
Contingent liabilities grew to roughly ₹22 crore, featuring a new ₹4.8 crore income tax dispute.
An entirely outsourced manufacturing model means product quality depends completely on third-party contract manufacturers.
The business faces structural risks from potential expansions in NLEM price controls and government generic-prescription pushes.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Inventory valuation was a key audit matter because overheads are allocated manually in Excel. The auditor noted that two subsidiaries with ₹43 crore revenue were audited by other auditors, while two subsidiaries with ₹16.5 crore revenue were unaudited and management-certified.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small. They include tax demands of about ₹3.8 crore, bank guarantees for the company's own performance of approximately ₹93 crore, and a ₹0.5 crore corporate guarantee for the Jash Invent joint venture.
reports.other: Standalone domestic revenue grew 18% to ₹318 crore, but exports fell 28% to ₹176 crore due to US tariffs and the Middle East war. Several subsidiaries struggled: Rodney Hunt's profit fell 56% to US$1.28 million, and Waterfront posted a £0.31 million loss. Additionally, standalone inventory of ₹195 crore included a ₹7.8 crore write-down to its net realisable value.
flags: Inventory overheads are allocated manually in Excel, which the auditor highlighted as a key audit matter.
Two subsidiaries with ₹16.5 crore in revenue were unaudited and relied on management certification.
The Waterfront subsidiary was loss-making for the year, while Rodney Hunt's profit dropped by 56%.
The company took a ₹7.8 crore write-down on its standalone inventory to reflect its net realisable value.

reports.auditor: The auditor, Vinod Singhal & Co. LLP, gave an unmodified, clean opinion. There were no key audit matters reported because the company is an SME. The CARO report was clean regarding dues, loans, and deposits.
reports.relatedParties: The Managing Director received a pay of ₹21.6 lakh. He gave the company an unsecured loan of ₹10.8 crore by March 2026 (with ₹9.2 crore taken in FY26), up from ₹1.3 crore the previous year, earning ₹0.37 crore in interest. He also sold 7.6 lakh shares for about ₹11.6 crore in the IPO offer-for-sale. A pre-IPO placement occurred at roughly ₹116.5 per share in April 2025.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were reported as nil, even though the company has margin deposits for bank guarantees related to an EPC project.
reports.other: The IPO included an ₹84.4 crore fresh issue, and a pre-IPO placement raised ₹5.2 crore. Cash and bank balances were only ₹0.54 crore at March 2026, falling from ₹3.86 crore the year before. There is an apparent disclosure error in the notes: trade-payable ageing shows ₹22.4 crore as disputed MSME dues, but the specific MSME note states only ₹8.25 lakh is owed.
flags: Cash and bank balances fell to just ₹0.54 crore at the end of March 2026.
Contingent liabilities are reported as nil despite the existence of bank-guarantee margin deposits.
There is a contradictory disclosure where ₹22.4 crore is listed as disputed MSME dues, while another note claims only ₹8.25 lakh is owed.
The Managing Director sold about ₹11.6 crore worth of shares in the IPO while simultaneously lending ₹10.8 crore back to the company at interest.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave a clean opinion with no qualifications in the CARO report. Key audit matters focused on revenue cut-off and inventory valuation, specifically noting commodity hedging and FIFO methods. The key audit matters also noted that the group uses commodity derivatives to hedge zinc and pays dross suppliers in about five days.
reports.relatedParties: Key management personnel pay in FY26 included ₹1.61 crore for Anirudh, ₹1.67 crore for Suresh, ₹1.48 crore for Anuj, and ₹0.37 crore for Aakriti Jhunjhunwala. The company paid rent and fit-out costs to promoter entities: ₹0.75 crore to Crystal Towers, ₹0.89 crore to BDJ Impex, and ₹0.16 crore to Vision Projects. Material related-party approval was sought for transactions with BDJ Oxides, an intra-group entity with a 5.87% minority stake.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small, totaling ₹1.15 crore in FY26 compared to ₹2.72 crore in FY25. This includes ₹0.97 crore for customs and ₹0.18 crore for entry tax. Capital commitments stood at ₹8.6 crore at March 2026, rising from ₹1.5 crore a year earlier.
reports.other: Customers exceeding 10% of revenue bought ₹494.1 crore (51% of revenue) in FY26, compared to ₹465.3 crore (55%) in FY25. Export revenue was ₹109.4 crore (11%) in FY26, up from ₹67.2 crore (8%) in FY25. Out of the ₹165 crore fresh IPO issue, ₹116.2 crore was used. However, ₹33.1 crore remained unused in bank deposits, including ₹16.9 crore (of ₹60 crore) for BDJ Oxides' working capital, ₹12 crore for JG's working capital, and ₹4.3 crore for an R&D centre.
flags: Customers exceeding 10% of sales accounted for a highly concentrated 51% of total revenue in FY26.
Two years after listing, ₹33.1 crore of the IPO money remains unused in bank deposits.
The company has a heavy working-capital burden because it pays its dross suppliers almost immediately in about five days.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion but added an emphasis-of-matter note because FY25 figures were restated. This restatement occurred because Cavendish Industries merged into JK Tyre effective 22 Dec 2025, with an appointed date of 1 Apr 2025. The key audit matter was revenue recognition, specifically concerning discounts and rebates.
reports.relatedParties: The company recorded about ₹402 crore in tyre sales to its associate Valiant Pacific LLC. Total sales to associates were roughly ₹524 crore. The company also noted trust contributions and dividends received from promoter-group company J.K. Fenner. The board stated there were no material related-party transactions.
reports.contingent: The company has an unprovided CCI penalty of ₹309.95 crore from a 2011–12 tyre cartel case, plus a personal penalty on Director Arun Bajoria, which is appealed at the Supreme Court. Standalone contingent liabilities were ₹309.94 crore (down from ₹384.75 crore). This includes ₹161 crore for excise, customs, and GST, ₹27 crore for income tax, ₹5 crore for service tax, and ₹116 crore in other claims.
reports.other: CMD Dr Raghupati Singhania earned ₹43.6 crore (₹13.6 crore fixed, ₹30 crore commission) and MD Anshuman Singhania earned ₹39.0 crore (₹9.0 crore fixed, ₹30 crore commission). Their combined ₹83 crore pay is 11% of the ₹748 crore standalone FY26 PAT. Director Arun Bajoria earned ₹5.3 crore. Capital work-in-progress was ₹1,100 crore by March 2026, up from ₹418 crore. Installed capacity exceeds 38 million tyres. No promoter shares were pledged.
flags: The CMD and MD received a combined pay of about ₹83 crore, consuming roughly 11% of the standalone FY26 profit of ₹748 crore.
The company faces an unprovided ₹309.95 crore CCI penalty for a 2011–12 tyre cartel case that is currently appealed at the Supreme Court.
Standalone contingent liabilities stand at ₹309.94 crore, mainly from disputed excise, customs, GST, and other tax claims.
The auditor included an emphasis of matter due to the restatement of FY25 financial figures following a corporate merger.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Revenue recognition, including contract assets under the judgement-heavy input method, was named a key audit matter. The Chemdist joint venture's CARO report was adverse on four clauses: stock statements to banks mismatched with books, delayed statutory dues, short-term funds used for long-term purposes, and cash losses.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings included ₹247.9 crore in sales of goods to promoter JNK Global's India project office for the BPCL Bina project. There were also material related-party transactions involving the JNK Chemdist joint venture and the founders' separate business, Chemdist Process Solutions.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were negligible, showing only a ₹0.3 crore tax claim. However, JNK India provided a ₹25 crore corporate guarantee for the Chemdist joint venture's bank lines, jointly with the founders.
reports.other: Consolidated segment results showed combustion equipment revenue of ₹759.7 crore with a ₹139.2 crore profit, and process equipment revenue of ₹58.8 crore with a ₹2.5 crore profit. The company formed a 51% joint venture, JNK Chemdist, which bought a business and IP for ₹41.6 crore, creating ₹1.7 crore in goodwill. Out of ₹264.6 crore in IPO funds earmarked for working capital, ₹264.4 crore was utilized by March 2026. The company declared a dividend of ₹0.30 per share.
flags: The Chemdist joint venture received an adverse CARO report citing mismatched stock statements, delayed statutory dues, cash losses, and short-term funds used for long-term purposes.
A significant 32.38% of shareholder votes were cast against material related-party transactions involving the Chemdist joint venture.
Revenue concentration is high, with 30% of FY26 revenue tied to a single related-party customer.
The auditor flagged revenue recognition under the input method as a judgement-heavy key audit matter.

reports.auditor: The auditor highlighted revenue recognition for long-term projects as a key audit matter. This involved ₹300 crore of CY25 revenue calculated using the input method and included the assessment of liquidated damages. The auditor also reported that the SAP audit trail was not enabled at the database level.
reports.relatedParties: The company pays its parent a brand fee of 0.6% of net sales, plus a referral and technical royalty of 1% to 3% on contract slabs. In CY25, these payments were ₹1.8 crore and ₹2.7 crore.
reports.contingent: The company faces service-tax demands from 2010 to 2017 totaling ₹236 crore, which includes penalties and interest. This is under appeal at CESTAT with about ₹4.3 crore pre-deposited. Additionally, after the year-end, an unnamed customer filed an arbitration notice claiming liquidated damages, extra costs, and lost profit for an allegedly underperforming mill. Management relies on a provision made in an earlier year for this claim.
reports.other: The annual report notes that the company operates as a single reported segment.
flags: Contingent tax liabilities of ₹236 crore are larger than the company's standalone net worth of ₹209 crore.
An unnamed customer has served an arbitration notice claiming damages and lost profits for an allegedly underperforming mill.
The company pays brand fees and royalties to its parent, skewing related-party economics in the parent's favor.
The auditor flagged that the SAP accounting audit trail was not enabled at the database level.

reports.auditor: Auditor B S R & Co. LLP gave an unmodified opinion. Revenue recognition was a key audit matter, and the audit trail operated successfully. The CARO report noted pending tax disputes of about ₹37.5 crore for FY20 to FY23 over disallowed royalty and expenses.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid ₹47.8 crore in royalty to its parent, JTEKT Japan, in FY26. Shareholders are being asked to approve up to ₹550 crore a year in transactions with the parent company, covering royalties, development costs, components, and capital goods.
reports.contingent: The company had capital commitments of ₹204.7 crore at the end of March 2026, up from ₹155.5 crore the previous year. There are pending tax disputes of ₹37.5 crore. Additionally, the parent company guarantees ₹59.8 crore of the company's bank debt.
reports.other: Management stated the return on capital employed was 7.87% and return on equity was 7.4% to 7.8%. Bank borrowings increased from ₹153 crore to ₹337 crore to help fund capital expenditures of ₹444 crore. Promoters fully participated in a rights issue, leaving over ₹0.6 crore unspent at year-end.
flags: Royalty payments to the parent company are heavy and rising, reaching ₹47.8 crore in FY26, which equals 62% of the previous year's net profit.
The company is asking shareholders to approve up to ₹550 crore a year for transactions with its Japanese parent.
There are pending tax disputes totaling ₹37.5 crore for FY20 to FY23 regarding disallowed royalty and expenses.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion and reported no frauds, while the secretarial audit was clean. Revenue recognition was named as a key audit matter. The auditor noted that a database-level audit trail was only enabled from January or March 2025. They also provided no assurance on a third-party-hosted revenue system.
reports.relatedParties: The company has Bhartia-group links and shares common directors with Jubilant Pharmova. CARO confirms these transactions comply with Sections 177 and 188. However, the company is still updating its documentation for transfer-pricing-specified transactions.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities totalled ₹454 crore, up from ₹352 crore a year earlier, representing about 15% of net worth. This includes ₹176 crore for income tax, mainly related to transfer pricing. State excise claims rose to ₹167 crore from ₹72 crore. The total also includes customs of ₹33 crore, central excise of ₹30 crore, and other items of ₹32 crore.
reports.outlook: The annual report's risk section notes that some businesses, such as choline, benefit from EU and US anti-dumping duties on China. The removal of this trade protection would hurt the company.
reports.other: The directors' report shows the company acquired 100% of Remidex Pharma, effective 30 March 2026, adding a premixes and formulations plant in Bengaluru for human nutrition. The BRSR shows that exports made up 44.3% of FY26 turnover.
flags: Contingent liabilities rose to ₹454 crore, representing about 15% of net worth, driven heavily by tax and excise claims.
The auditor gave no assurance on a third-party-hosted revenue system and noted database audit trails were only enabled late in the year.
The company is still updating its documentation for transfer-pricing-specified related-party transactions.
Removal of EU and US anti-dumping duties on China would hurt businesses like choline.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued unmodified opinions with no fraud reports and a maintained audit trail. There were no key audit matters on the standalone report. For the consolidated report, testing the impairment of ₹2,826 crore in goodwill and ₹1,079 crore of intangibles under development (pipeline products) was highlighted as a key audit matter.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities total roughly ₹419 crore. This mostly consists of ₹368 crore for income tax and ₹35 crore for GST disputes. Other lawsuits and investigations exist but are not quantified.
reports.outlook: Management targets ₹13,500 crore in revenue by 2030, with 23–25% EBITDA margins, zero net debt, and high-teens returns on capital. CDMO, API, and Generics revenue are expected to double, while Discovery revenue should triple. Expansion plans include a CAD 145 million Montreal Line 5 project, supported by CAD 48.8 million in government aid, with revenue expected from FY29. The company is also building six PET manufacturing sites in the US.
reports.other: FY26 segment revenue and EBITDA were: Radiopharmaceuticals ₹1,178 crore (41% margin); Radiopharmacy ₹2,512 crore (~1% margin); CDMO Sterile Injectables ₹1,755 crore (₹314 crore EBITDA); Allergy Immunotherapy ₹785 crore (35% margin); Drug Discovery ₹654 crore (₹151 crore EBITDA); and Generics ₹774 crore (₹83 crore EBITDA). The company reported ₹1,122 crore in capital commitments for property, plant, and equipment as of March 2026.
flags: The FDA issued a Warning Letter for the Montreal facility in May 2026 following nine Form 483 observations, forcing the site to run lean.
The auditor highlighted the impairment testing of ₹3,905 crore in goodwill and pipeline intangibles as a key audit matter.
The company faces unprovided contingent liabilities of roughly ₹419 crore, largely from tax disputes.
High-margin SPECT supply is vulnerable because it depends on the troubled Montreal site until products can move to third-party manufacturers.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion with no emphasis of matter. The key audit matter was revenue recognition. Under CARO, the auditor noted that no loans were raised on the pledge of subsidiary shares.
reports.relatedParties: In FY25, the company bought capital goods worth ₹45.3 crore from Log9 Material Scientific, an entity where the company or its key managers have significant influence. There were also small consultancy and advance dealings with Karisma Goods, which is linked to key management personnel.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities for tax and excise disputes stood at ₹54.4 crore, remaining unchanged from the previous year. The company also had ₹1,506 crore in unspent capital commitments as of March 2026, up from ₹705 crore.
reports.outlook: The annual report notes plans for an Odisha greenfield forged wheel plant with an investment of about ₹3,000 crore. The plant will have a capacity of 1 lakh wheelsets and 20,000 loose wheels a year.
reports.other: Subsidiary JTRWF made a net profit of ₹56.6 crore, while Stone India recorded a ₹36.3 crore turnover and a ₹29.7 crore loss before tax. The management discussion noted return on net worth fell from 17.2% to 6.4%, and interest cover dropped from 8.6x to 5.0x, though debt-to-equity stayed low at 0.16. Additionally, ₹43.64 crore of QIP funds sat idle for over two years.
flags: Return on net worth fell sharply from 17.2% to 6.4%, and interest cover dropped from 8.6x to 5.0x.
Over ₹43 crore of QIP funds meant for a foundry have sat idle for two years, and the board is seeking a second change to use it for general purposes.
The company bought ₹45.3 crore of capital goods from a related party where management has significant influence.
Unspent capital commitments more than doubled to ₹1,506 crore.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion with no emphasis of matter. The only key audit matter noted was revenue recognition. The auditor's CARO report mentioned that two properties worth ₹6.9 crore still await title transfer from an old acquisition.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings were small. They included pay for key management, commissions of ₹5.1 crore payable at March 2026 (up from ₹0.6 crore), along with dividends and rent paid to promoter-linked entities. There were no loans or guarantees given to related parties.
reports.contingent: The company disclosed about ₹10 crore in contingent liabilities. However, the auditor noted roughly ₹71 crore in tax demands under appeal, including ₹43 crore for excise and ₹27 crore for sales tax or VAT, suggesting the rest is either provided for or considered remote. Capital commitments stood at ₹3.4 crore.
reports.outlook: The management discussion highlighted its market leadership, with Ujala remaining the number one fabric whitener for four decades, and Exo and Maxo coils ranking second in their categories. Modern trade, e-commerce, and quick commerce channels grew by 26% during the year. The company spent ₹67 crore on capital expenditure in FY26 for capacity expansion, upgrades, and automation.
reports.other: Promoter shareholding remained flat at 62.9%, with no shares pledged. The company wrote off ₹24.5 crore in bad debts during FY26. Additionally, ₹100.4 crore of goodwill from the 2011 Henkel India acquisition remains on the books, tested as a single unit without impairment as of March 2026.
flags: The auditor noted that two properties worth ₹6.9 crore still await title transfer from an older acquisition.
There are roughly ₹71 crore in tax demands under appeal, despite only ₹10 crore being shown as contingent liabilities.
The company wrote off ₹24.5 crore in bad debts, which is notable given its generally low receivables.
The ₹100.4 crore goodwill from the 2011 Henkel acquisition is tested as one unit, but the loss of the Pril brand weakens it.

reports.auditor: The standalone auditor, Choksi & Co., gave an unqualified opinion but included an emphasis of matter. They flagged a material uncertainty over the going-concern status of the French subsidiary, Jyoti SAS. Its net worth is eroded by recurring losses at Huron. It also faces a French judicial investigation and has machines under customs control. Despite this, Jyoti India has not impaired its ₹341.6 crore investment and ₹160.1 crore in loans and advances to the subsidiary.
reports.contingent: The report lists disputed taxes of about ₹25 crore. Bank guarantees and letters of credit amount to approximately ₹441 crore. Capital commitments stand at ₹56 crore.
reports.outlook: The Management Discussion and Analysis notes that FY26 consolidated growth was 15%, but would have been about 19% without a ₹67 crore reversal of Huron revenue. It also mentions the 10,000-machine Rajkot expansion budgeted at about ₹450 crore, with FY26 consolidated capital expenditure at ₹323 crore.
reports.other: Exports made up only 5.2% of the company's standalone turnover of ₹1,949 crore in FY26. The report's notes also confirm an ongoing French judicial investigation, which has resulted in the interim seizure of €3.02 million in funds and two residential properties belonging to Jyoti SAS.
flags: The auditor flagged a material uncertainty over the going-concern status of the French subsidiary due to eroded net worth and recurring losses.
Management has not impaired its ₹341.6 crore investment and ₹160.1 crore in loans to the struggling French unit.
The French subsidiary is facing a judicial investigation that includes the interim seizure of €3.02 million in funds and two residential properties.

reports.auditor: The consolidated audit opinion is unmodified. Revenue recognition and rebates were highlighted as a key audit matter. The auditor noted an exception because the accounting software's audit trail was not enabled at the database level. Additionally, a subsidiary's CARO report is qualified under clause xi(a) due to fraud.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small, consisting of tax and duty claims, and a standby letter of credit for the Nepal joint venture loan, each under ₹30 crore. The company also has capital commitments of ₹130 crore.
reports.other: The FY26 profit jump was driven by cost cuts, dealer unification, and closing the loss-making plywood arm. The Tiles segment reported ₹4,280 crore in revenue with a ₹651 crore result. The Others segment made ₹550 crore in revenue with a ₹44 crore result. Exceptional items of ₹44 crore included a ₹19.8 crore embezzlement, a ₹4.8 crore loan impairment, and labour-code charges.
flags: The CFO of a step-down subsidiary siphoned about ₹20 crore through forged authorisations.
A subsidiary's CARO report received a qualified opinion due to this fraud.
The company's accounting software did not have the audit trail enabled at the database level.
Exceptional items totaled ₹44 crore, which included a ₹19.8 crore embezzlement loss and a ₹4.8 crore loan impairment.
The bathware business remains loss-making or operates at low margins.

reports.auditor: The auditor highlighted three key audit matters. First, Valex Ventures missed its post-acquisition performance projections, yet no impairment was booked. Second, the loss-making CPP film division was marked as discontinued, requiring restated comparatives. Third, ₹7.03 crore in export incentives was not recognized. The auditor also raised a CARO point regarding the related-party acquisition of Valex Ventures.
reports.relatedParties: The company bought a 76% stake in UK-based Valex Ventures from its own Chairman and Managing Director, Manoj Agarwal. The ₹8.02 crore purchase price was paid by issuing him 3.34 lakh new shares at a price above book value. Additionally, the company's term loans are personally guaranteed by the Chairman and Deputy Managing Director.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small. They include ₹7.9 crore in bank counter-guarantees and ₹0.2 crore in DGFT undertakings. The company also noted a contingent asset of ₹7.03 crore for export-incentive licences, which were not booked because the import duty on polypropylene was temporarily suspended.
reports.outlook: The Board's report outlines a new non-woven project located in the old CPP division building. Two needle-punch lines are planned, with machines arriving from June 2026. The company targets an internal rate of return of 15% to 20% and a return on capital employed above 20% for this project, expecting it to require 30 to 40 days of working capital.
reports.other: The company fully exited its loss-making CPP film division, classifying it as a discontinued operation. Over the year, the company issued equity, including 7.52 lakh shares from warrant conversions in May 2025, and another 10.12 lakh warrants priced at ₹130 each in August 2025.
flags: The company purchased a 76% stake in Valex Ventures directly from its Chairman using new shares priced above book value.
The auditor flagged that Valex Ventures missed its acquisition projections, yet no impairment loss was recorded on the investment.
Management has described the revenue and profit of the newly acquired Valex Ventures as timid.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unmodified opinion. The key audit matter highlighted in the report was the estimation of variable consideration, specifically relating to rebates and discounts.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid a royalty of ₹32.7 crore (0.4% of sales) and small technical fees to its parent company, Kansai Japan. The parent company also received ₹227 crore in dividends. Sales to fellow Kansai subsidiaries were modest at about ₹7 crore.
reports.contingent: The company reported tax disputes of roughly ₹45 crore, primarily consisting of excise, service tax, and GST credits totaling ₹44.8 crore. It also provided a corporate guarantee for a bank loan taken by its Bangladesh subsidiary. Capital commitments stood at ₹92.8 crore at the end of March 2026. A Supreme Court issue regarding provident funds was judged to be immaterial.
reports.outlook: The management discussion and analysis noted that the company is a leader in automotive coatings and gained market share in FY26. Moving forward, it is growing its presence in alloy wheels, underbody coatings, seam sealers, and electric vehicle (EV) applications.
reports.other: FY26 featured exceptional standalone losses, including a ₹44.7 crore Wage Code gratuity, a ₹10.2 crore warehouse fire loss in Ghaziabad, and ₹5.8 crore in impairments. The Bangladesh subsidiary posted a ₹27.6 crore loss on falling revenue, while the Nerofix unit lost ₹7.6 crore and is being merged into the company. A 60% stake in Sri Lanka was sold for about ₹5 lakh. The year also saw management churn, with a new MD, a new CFO, and the exit of a Japanese whole-time director.
flags: The Bangladesh subsidiary reported a ₹27.6 crore loss as its revenue dropped sharply from ₹143 crore to ₹91 crore.
The construction chemicals subsidiary, Nerofix, reported a loss of ₹7.6 crore.
The company faced exceptional standalone losses of ₹44.7 crore for a Wage Code gratuity, ₹10.2 crore for a warehouse fire, and ₹5.8 crore in impairments.
The company has unresolved tax disputes totaling ₹44.8 crore related to excise, service tax, and GST credits.
There was notable management churn with a new MD and CFO taking over, alongside the departure of a Japanese whole-time director.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave no qualifications or emphasis of matter. The key audit matter was the estimate of sales returns, discounts, and schemes. This is material because unsold seed comes back from dealers.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities stood at ₹225.7 crore at March 2026. This included ₹129.0 crore for tax and ₹96.6 crore for legal claims. Legal claims jumped from ₹19.7 crore previously, which was not explained in the read notes. There are also pending block tax assessments for FY12 to FY18 following a search.
reports.other: Subsidiaries such as Aditya Agritech and Genomix Agri Genetics sell 'me-too' hybrids under other brands. These subsidiaries compete directly with the parent company. The company also consolidates an employee trust.
flags: Legal claims within contingent liabilities jumped without explanation from ₹19.7 crore to ₹96.6 crore.
The tax department is disputing the company's tax-exempt agricultural income claims, which threatens both historical and future tax rates.
Sister-brand subsidiaries sell competing hybrids, creating direct competition with the parent company.
The company consolidates an employee trust in its financials.

reports.auditor: K.P. Rao & Co signed an unmodified opinion for the year. However, eight overseas subsidiaries were not audited, and three other subsidiaries with ₹31 crore in assets were also unaudited. The key audit matters were revenue recognition and IT controls within a highly customized ERP system. Walker Chandiok is proposed to take over as the new auditor from the September 2026 AGM.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings outside the group were small. The annual report notes that the company provided services worth about ₹5 crore to Kaynes Technology Inc. and Kemsys Inc.
reports.contingent: The company reported capital commitments jumping to ₹810 crore from ₹29 crore the prior year. Contingent liabilities included huge corporate guarantees to subsidiaries of ₹2,390 crore, bills discounted with banks of ₹455 crore, performance bank guarantees of ₹191 crore, customs bonds of ₹103 crore, and letters of credit of ₹69 crore. There is also a ₹6 crore NCLT claim against subsidiary Gridcrest.
reports.other: The report outlines three main business lines: core EMS, smart metering, and pre-revenue chip packaging and bare PCB units. Customer concentration is high, with a single client bringing in ₹844 crore, or 24% of total revenue. Exports accounted for ₹351 crore, or 9.7% of sales. The new pre-revenue subsidiaries are largely financed by liabilities, with Kaynes Semicon reporting ₹615 crore in assets against ₹626 crore in liabilities.
flags: Eight overseas subsidiaries and three other subsidiaries with ₹31 crore in assets were entirely unaudited.
Corporate guarantees to subsidiaries spiked massively to ₹2,390 crore.
Customer concentration grew significantly, with one customer generating 24% of total revenue.
The company carries ₹455 crore in bills discounted with banks as a contingent liability.
The new chip packaging and bare PCB subsidiaries are pre-revenue and funded heavily by liabilities.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave a clean report with no qualifications, reservations, adverse remarks, or emphasis of matter. Revenue recognition was highlighted as a key audit matter. The statutory auditor will change to Walker Chandiok for FY27 to FY31, as the previous term has ended.
reports.relatedParties: The group has a construction joint venture named Kapstone Constructions and an alternative investment fund called Kapstone Opportunities Fund. No material related-party transactions were flagged.
reports.contingent: As of March 2026, the company had standalone contingent liabilities of ₹84.4 crore for indirect tax, ₹23.4 crore for income tax, and ₹4.6 crore for other items.
flags: The company faces standalone contingent liabilities of ₹84.4 crore for indirect tax and ₹23.4 crore for income tax.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The only key audit matter was over-time revenue recognition, which requires judgement on cost estimates. Under CARO, the auditor flagged issues at subsidiaries: M.E. Energy had disputed statutory dues, while Monga Strayfield had delays in depositing statutory dues, disputed dues, and quarterly bank stock statements that did not match its books.
reports.relatedParties: Promoter company Firstview Trading provided a corporate guarantee to lenders for a 2% annual fee, costing ₹1 crore on ₹50 crore in FY26. A director also provided a personal guarantee of ₹120 crore. Williamson Magor charged ₹15 lakh in corporate charges, and legal fees were paid to Khaitan & Co. Subsidiary directors' firms traded with the group, generating ₹4.8 crore in purchases and ₹5.8 crore in sales.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were small, comprising roughly ₹1 crore in tax and employee claims. The company also provided a ₹25 crore corporate guarantee for a subsidiary's bank lines. Capital commitments stood at ₹10.2 crore at the end of March 2026, up from ₹3.3 crore a year earlier.
reports.outlook: The management discussion states the company is a custom process equipment maker serving over 20 sectors with more than 8,000 installations. Plans include capacity expansions at the Saravali facility and M.E. Energy Phase II.
reports.other: The company has only one reportable segment for engineering products. FY26 revenue from India was ₹353.5 crore, while revenue from outside India reached ₹270.4 crore, making up 43% of the total. Warrants were converted at ₹166 in FY26. The board saw changes, with a non-executive director resigning in March 2026, an independent director resigning in April 2026, and a company secretary change.
flags: The auditor highlighted over-time revenue recognition and cost estimates as a key audit matter.
Subsidiaries received negative CARO remarks for delayed and disputed statutory dues.
A subsidiary's quarterly stock statements submitted to banks did not match its books.
A promoter company charges a 2% annual fee to provide a corporate guarantee to lenders.
Two directors resigned from the board between March and April 2026.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion but included two emphasis of matter paragraphs. First, the ₹5,800 crore DyStar award was treated as a non-taxable capital receipt, meaning a future tax demand is possible. Second, they noted the write-off of trade receivables, loans, and deposits as exceptional items. Under CARO, the auditor noted loans of ₹198.7 crore to subsidiaries and associates, including ₹54.8 crore to associate Kiri Infrastructure, where a repayment schedule has not been stipulated.
reports.relatedParties: Sales to related parties made up 35% of total sales in FY26, up from just 0.09% the prior year. This mainly consisted of ₹181 crore in sales to the Lonsen Kiri joint venture. The company also made purchases from promoter-linked entities Metallonia Metals and Colorstar, and paid rent and interest to promoter-linked Saptak Buildcon.
reports.contingent: The contingent liabilities note shows a corporate guarantee of ₹1,446 crore backing a since-repaid Claronex loan. The company earned a ₹12.4 crore guarantee commission from Claronex in FY26. There are disputed taxes of ₹32 crore to ₹47 crore. Foreign-currency receivables and payables are outstanding beyond RBI settlement periods and must be regularised. Additionally, there are long-outstanding capital advances for equipment never received, where third-party confirmations are being sought to determine recoverability.
reports.outlook: The management discussion noted that pricing power is cyclical rather than structural. FY26 operating margins were negative because selling prices remained largely unchanged while input costs rose. The board decided to pay no dividend for FY26 to keep cash for upcoming projects and to maintain a working-capital margin of ₹1,500 crore to ₹2,000 crore.
reports.other: Standalone revenue rose 19% to ₹778 crore, but reported EBITDA was negative ₹35 crore for an operating margin of -18.2%. The company recorded an exceptional gain of ₹5,881 crore from the DyStar legal award, pushing net worth to ₹6,436 crore. The core business is a backward-integrated chain making dyes and intermediates. Notes reveal that some plant land is held in the name of the late chairman Pravin Kiri in a fiduciary capacity.
flags: The auditor warned that treating the ₹5,800 crore DyStar award as a non-taxable receipt could lead to a future tax demand.
The auditor highlighted the write-off of trade receivables, loans, and deposits as exceptional items.
Loans totaling ₹198.7 crore were given to subsidiaries and associates without any stipulated repayment schedule.
Long-outstanding capital advances were paid to suppliers for equipment never received, and their recoverability is unconfirmed.
Foreign-currency receivables and payables remain outstanding beyond RBI settlement periods and need to be regularised.

reports.auditor: The auditor identified revenue recognition on long-term contracts as a key audit matter, noting ₹68.6 crore of revenue was recognized over time. The CARO report states that the auditor considered whistle-blower complaints received by the company during the year. No audit qualifications were found.
reports.relatedParties: The company supports its loss-making foreign subsidiaries with guarantees. It provided a guarantee of €3.675 million to ICICI Bank for Rodelta. It also issued guarantees of US$5.5 million and THB 125 million for Kirloskar Brothers Thailand.
reports.contingent: Standalone contingent liabilities reached ₹159.9 crore by March 2026, up from ₹143.3 crore. This consists mainly of disputed taxes, including ₹103.4 crore for excise, service tax, and GST, ₹27.9 crore for income tax, and ₹16.1 crore for sales tax. Legal claims stand at ₹7.6 crore and labor claims at ₹4.9 crore.
reports.other: The annual report shows working capital worsened, with work-in-progress inventory rising from ₹180 crore to ₹241 crore and supplier advances increasing from ₹32 crore to ₹91 crore. Several subsidiaries reported losses for the year. This includes the KBIBV holding company (₹14.3 crore loss), Kolhapur Steel (₹9.9 crore loss, negative reserves ₹155 crore), Rodelta (₹4.9 crore loss, negative reserves ₹30 crore), and the Thailand unit (₹1.2 crore loss, negative reserves ₹18.6 crore).
flags: The auditor noted that they considered whistle-blower complaints received by the company during the year.
Multiple subsidiaries are reporting losses and carry large negative reserves, dragging down overall performance.
The company carries significant risk by guaranteeing loans of €3.675 million, US$5.5 million, and THB 125 million for these loss-making foreign units.
Contingent liabilities are substantial at ₹159.9 crore, largely due to disputed indirect and direct taxes.
Working capital metrics deteriorated in the report, with work-in-progress inventory jumping to ₹241 crore and supplier advances nearly tripling to ₹91 crore.

reports.auditor: The auditor, G. D. Apte & Co., gave an unmodified opinion with no emphasis of matter. Key audit matters included revenue recognition and ₹190 crore in goodwill. The auditor also flagged IT-controls risk for the Arka lending arm. The CARO report notes ₹106.8 crore of disputed income-tax demands not deposited, along with smaller sales-tax and GST items.
reports.relatedParties: The company's UAE subsidiary is purchasing Kirloskar Trading SA in South Africa. The annual report describes this target as a promoter group company. This involves a total injection of about ₹8 crore.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include ₹5.8 crore for income-tax demands and ₹52 crore in claims not acknowledged as debt. Capital commitments outstanding were ₹391 crore at the end of March 2026.
reports.outlook: Management aims for consolidated revenue of ₹16,000 crore by FY30. New emission rules for gensets and construction equipment require re-engineering and long customer approvals. The company relies on qualification-heavy niches like nuclear, Navy, and railway projects which have long approval cycles. A ₹700 crore Phase 1 capacity expansion will be operational by April 2027, alongside a ₹1,400 crore Phase 2 expansion for high-horsepower engines.
reports.other: The B2C fluid dynamics business was moved into a subsidiary in October 2025. The US subsidiary, Kirloskar Americas, made a loss of ₹19.9 crore on ₹69.8 crore turnover, and its liabilities exceed its assets. The standalone business recorded a ₹29.7 crore exceptional charge related to the labour code.
flags: The CARO report lists ₹106.8 crore in disputed income-tax demands, but contingent liabilities only disclose ₹5.8 crore, leaving an unexplained gap.
The US subsidiary is loss-making and its ₹132 crore in liabilities exceed its ₹82 crore in assets.
The auditor flagged IT-controls risk as a key audit matter for the Arka financial services arm.
A UAE subsidiary is buying a promoter group company in South Africa for approximately ₹8 crore.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion, noting year-end revenue cut-off as the key audit matter. Under CARO, there were no whistle-blower complaints and no major disputed statutory dues, noting only a minor ₹0.7 crore.
reports.contingent: The company has small contingent liabilities. These consist of claims worth ₹11.8 crore and customs disputes of ₹1.4 crore.
reports.outlook: The report outlines a ₹320 crore PLI commitment for Zephyros and related parts like motors and heat exchangers at the Saswad and Nashik plants. About ₹60 crore was spent by March 2026, with the rest planned over FY27 and FY28.
reports.other: Subsidiary Systems & Components lost ₹4.3 crore in FY26 on a ₹28.3 crore turnover, dropping reserves to ₹5.7 crore. The company booked a ₹14.0 crore exceptional labour-code charge in FY26, and fully written off its road-roller business following a ₹3.8 crore impairment in FY25. Promoter holding is 38.81% with no pledges. Aman Kirloskar took over as MD from K. Srinivasan.
flags: Subsidiary Systems & Components reported a loss of ₹4.3 crore in FY26, bringing its reserves down to ₹5.7 crore.
The company booked an exceptional labour-code charge of ₹14.0 crore in FY26.
The road-roller business was completely written off following a ₹3.8 crore impairment in FY25.
Promoter shareholding is relatively low at 38.81% and is drifting down slightly due to ESOP dilution.

reports.auditor: The auditor included an emphasis of matter regarding unpaid dues of ₹1,363.3 crore on Kaleswaram Package 4. The report noted that management considered these receivables as good for recovery.
reports.contingent: Standalone contingent claims at March 2026 were ₹646 crore, up from ₹464 crore the previous year. This includes ₹287.9 crore for income tax, about ₹176 crore for indirect taxes, and ₹182.2 crore for civil cases. It also includes corporate guarantees given for SPVs.
reports.outlook: The company is diversifying its business operations. Beyond its traditional focus on road EPC, HAM projects, irrigation, and urban water pipelines, it is now entering coal mining as a mine developer and operator, alongside new work in flyovers, railways, and metro projects.
flags: The auditor issued an emphasis of matter regarding ₹1,363.3 crore in concentrated, unpaid irrigation dues from Kaleswaram Package 4.
Contingent liabilities for civil cases spiked to ₹182.2 crore from just ₹0.26 crore a year earlier, with no explanation provided in the report.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion but noted key audit matters regarding revenue recognition, property, plant and equipment, and a sale-and-leaseback gain. The fixed-asset module of the new SAP system was not configured by the signing date, forcing reliance on management's manual workings. A CARO remark noted slight delays in depositing TDS, TCS, GST, PF, and ESIC, along with some small income-tax demands unpaid for over six months.
reports.relatedParties: FY26 group sales were ~₹617 crore: K.P. Energy ₹370.0 crore, KPI Green Energy ₹175.5 crore, Sun Drops ₹53.6 crore, and KPIG Energia ₹15.4 crore. KPI Green Energy supplied ₹215.8 crore of purchases (₹113 crore payable). Capital purchases included KPGenix at ₹41.3 crore and KPI Green Hydrogen at ₹12.8 crore. Promoter Dr Faruk Patel received a 2% royalty of ₹19.2 crore (FY25: ₹13.9 crore, unpaid: ₹7.7 crore). Advances included a ₹32.9 crore property advance to Faruk (₹19.1 crore given FY26), a ₹42.1 crore deposit to Quyosh, and receivables from Faaiz (₹1.3 crore) and Renewable Minds (₹1.4 crore).
reports.contingent: The company states there are no contingent liabilities. However, a ₹5.47 crore property advance from FY16–17 to Mukesh Engineering is currently in litigation at the Gujarat High Court. Additionally, interest on delayed MSME payments was not provided for.
reports.other: The company reports a single geographic segment, which is 100% domestic. The cash-flow statement indicates the company sold and leased back its major plant and machinery, generating roughly ₹150 crore in sale proceeds and converting owned machines into lease liabilities.
flags: The auditor noted the new SAP fixed-asset module was unconfigured at signing, forcing reliance on manual management workings.
Nearly half of FY26 revenue (~₹617 crore) came from related-party group companies, making margins dependent on internal transfer pricing.
The company pays a heavy 2% turnover royalty (₹19.2 crore in FY26) to the promoter for use of the "KP" brand.
Significant company funds are tied up with the promoter family, including a ₹32.9 crore property advance and a ₹42.1 crore deposit.
A major sale-and-leaseback of plant and machinery was executed, which effectively acts as off-balance-sheet financing.

reports.auditor: The auditor, BSR & Co., gave an opinion with no qualification or emphasis of matter. They listed accounting for business combinations and fixed-price revenue recognition as key audit matters.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small, consisting of bank guarantees of ₹15.9 crore, a customs bond of ₹2.3 crore, and minor tax appeals. The company provided corporate guarantees for subsidiaries of ₹54.5 crore (GmbH) and ₹28.4 crore (US holding), but no subsidiary borrowings were drawn.
reports.other: FY26 revenue was $724.8 million. Passenger cars made up 79.0% of revenue and commercial vehicles 18.1%. By geography, Europe was 48.0%, the US 27.4%, and Asia 24.6%. Profit fell 24% due to an exceptional charge of ₹59.7 crore for new Labour Codes (₹48.2 crore for gratuity, ₹11.5 crore for leave) and a ₹37.6 crore share of joint venture or associate losses. Co-founder and Chairman Ravi Pandit died and ceased being a director.
flags: Strategic top-25 clients accounted for a highly concentrated 86.6% of FY26 revenue.
Permanent-employee turnover was high at 26% in FY26.
FY26 profit was hit by a ₹59.7 crore exceptional charge and ₹37.6 crore in joint venture or associate losses.
Goodwill on consolidation swelled to ₹2,798 crore, representing 39% of total assets.
The auditor highlighted accounting for business combinations and fixed-price revenue recognition as key audit matters.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave a qualified opinion on both the standalone and consolidated financial statements. The Enforcement Directorate is investigating Joint Managing Director Anoop Kumar Gupta, KRBL, and its subsidiary KRBL DMCC under money-laundering laws over the AgustaWestland case. An independent firm found no conclusive evidence to ascertain the impact, but the auditor cannot comment on necessary adjustments until the investigation ends. Additionally, land at Dhuri worth ₹15.32 crore was attached.
reports.contingent: The standalone contingent liabilities include ₹50.67 crore for indirect taxes and ₹15.32 crore for the Enforcement Directorate matter. Other items stand at ₹40.39 crore, down from ₹252.51 crore the previous year, and direct tax claims are ₹1.12 crore.
reports.other: The promoters maintained a steady 60.17% holding with 0% of their shares pledged. The company experienced governance churn during the year, with two independent directors resigning in April and September 2025, alongside the resignation of the Company Secretary.
flags: The auditor issued a qualified opinion on the financial statements due to an ongoing Enforcement Directorate investigation.
The Enforcement Directorate has filed a criminal money-laundering complaint against KRBL, its subsidiary KRBL DMCC, and its Joint Managing Director.
Company land at Dhuri worth ₹15.32 crore was attached as part of the investigation.
The company saw governance churn with two independent directors and the Company Secretary resigning during the year.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion with no key audit matters reported. The report also noted that the audit trail operated successfully.
reports.relatedParties: The company bought two residential flats from Managing Director Ankur Shah for ₹43.6 lakh and ₹40.1 lakh. It made purchases and paid rent to promoter entities Krish Industries and White Gold Technologies. A previous loan of ₹4.75 crore to associate Waveoptix was converted into equity at ₹19,000 a share, and further loans were given. The MD's wife, Preyal Shah, was allotted 2.52 lakh shares.
reports.contingent: Outstanding bank guarantees were ₹31.7 crore, down from ₹47.3 crore the prior year. The company provided a ₹5 crore corporate guarantee for associate Waveoptix's bank loans. It also has a disputed liquidated-damages claim of ₹0.83 crore and capital commitments of ₹10.7 crore, net of ₹8.1 crore in advances.
reports.other: Defence is the sole reportable segment, as the dairy business is too small to report separately. Late-delivery charges and discounts reduced contracted revenue by ₹9.97 crore, up from ₹5.25 crore last year. Management saw sudden churn: whole-time director Sandeep Kadam passed away in March 2026, and CFO Piyush Patel left in April 2026.
flags: Late-delivery charges and discounts are rising, cutting contracted revenue by ₹9.97 crore.
The company purchased two residential flats from its own Managing Director for ₹43.6 lakh and ₹40.1 lakh.
A ₹4.75 crore loan to an associate was converted into shares at ₹19,000 each, and the company guarantees ₹5 crore of that associate's bank loans.
There was abrupt management churn, with the CFO resigning in April 2026 shortly after a whole-time director passed away.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. However, they highlighted two key audit matters for the standalone entity. The first was revenue recognition, driven by fast growth, new trading activity, and a high volume of sales to the subsidiary. The second was the carrying value of ₹399 crore in subsidiary loans and investments, which accounts for 70% of the standalone net worth.
reports.relatedParties: The auditor flagged a high volume of related-party transactions, specifically sales made to the company's subsidiary. Additionally, the standalone entity provided ₹48.3 crore in on-demand loans to subsidiaries and holds ₹350.7 crore invested in them.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities included ₹44.7 crore in letters of credit, ₹20.7 crore in bank guarantees, and ₹4.9 crore in indirect tax disputes. Export obligations under EPCG and advance authorizations surged to ₹29.4 crore from ₹8.1 crore a year earlier; duty will become payable if these are not met. The company also had capital commitments of ₹42.4 crore.
reports.outlook: The management discussion notes that legacy Plant I ran at 84% to 86% utilization in FY26. The new, wholly owned Plant II, which is six times larger, was inaugurated in March 2026 to make products like bus ACs and dry coolers.
