The company targets commercial HVAC clients like Daikin, Carrier, and Voltas, rather than room ACs. Management also reported that the debt-to-equity ratio rose from 0.07 to 0.33.
reports.other: Consolidated trading purchases jumped sharply to ₹34.2 crore during the year, up from just ₹3.4 crore previously.
flags: Standalone investments and on-demand loans to subsidiaries reached ₹399 crore, representing a massive 70% of standalone net worth.
The auditor flagged revenue recognition as a key risk due to new trading activity and high related-party sales to the subsidiary.
Export obligations jumped to ₹29.4 crore, threatening duty penalties if the company fails to meet them.
Trading purchases increased tenfold to ₹34.2 crore.

reports.auditor: The auditor confirmed compliance with laws for related-party transactions. The report included an emphasis of matter regarding a favourable Jharkhand High Court order that quashed an electricity duty, creating a ₹4.6 crore contingent asset rather than a liability. Under CARO, the auditor flagged that quarterly returns submitted to banks did not match the company books. For example, March 2026 receivables were ₹197.2 crore in the books versus ₹208.7 crore reported to banks, with similar mismatches in September 2025.
reports.relatedParties: The company reported ₹9.35 crore in sales during FY26 to Bull Auto Parts, a firm where a Kross director is the proprietor, down from ₹12.1 crore in FY25. There was ₹4.9 crore outstanding from this entity. The company also had small unsecured loans of about ₹1.7 crore from its promoters.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities totalled ₹39.7 crore. This consisted of ₹34.9 crore for bills discounted, ₹2.8 crore for excise and service tax, ₹1.7 crore for income tax, and ₹0.3 crore for GST. The company also reported capital commitments of ₹68.8 crore at the end of March 2026.
reports.other: The company operates under a single reporting segment, though the MD&A noted that trailer axles and suspensions made up 42.6% of FY26 revenue. Revenue from outside India was ₹20.2 crore, representing 3.0% of total sales. Total debt at the end of March 2026 was ₹53.7 crore, comprising ₹29.1 crore in long-term debt, ₹23.2 crore in short-term debt, and ₹1.4 crore in leases.
flags: The auditor noted that quarterly returns submitted to banks did not agree with the company's books, citing repeated mismatches in receivables over eight quarters.
Audited figures showed export revenues at 3.0% of total sales, which conflicted with management's claim of 4% on earnings calls.
The company carries a significant contingent liability of ₹34.9 crore tied to bills discounted with recourse, which could pressure cash flows if customers default.

reports.auditor: Price Waterhouse Chartered Accountants LLP gave an unmodified opinion. The report contained no emphasis of matter. The only key audit matter was the timing of revenue recognition on project contracts, specifically looking at point-in-time versus over-time recognition and the right to payment.
reports.relatedParties: The company routes 70% to 80% of its exports through KSB group companies. It pays trademark fees and technology licence royalties to its parent, KSB SE, which cost between ₹31 crore and ₹37 crore a year during CY24 and CY25. Transfer pricing is governed by an Advance Pricing Agreement, but its renewal for April 2023 to March 2028 was still awaiting approval at the end of December 2025.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities totalled ₹212 crore at the end of December 2025, rising from ₹192 crore the previous year. This included ₹130.7 crore in GST, excise, and service tax disputes over input credits and classifications. It also included ₹54.9 crore for income tax disputes and ₹26.4 crore for labour and other claims. Capital commitments stood at ₹39.6 crore.
reports.outlook: The opening message of the annual report noted that the company spent ₹115 crore in CY25 on capacity, modernisation, and digitisation. Management guided for ₹80 crore to ₹120 crore in yearly capital expenditure going forward to fund sustenance and growth.
reports.other: Segment notes showed that pumps generated ₹2,215 crore in revenue and ₹285 crore in profit during CY25. The valves segment recorded ₹481 crore in revenue and ₹70 crore in profit. The overall sales mix was 83% domestic and 17% exports.
flags: Contingent liabilities reached ₹212 crore by December 2025, which equals about 12% of the company's net worth.
Exports are highly dependent on the parent group, with 70% to 80% routed through KSB group companies.
A key transfer pricing agreement governing parent-company dealings was still awaiting government renewal approval at the end of 2025.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The key audit matters highlighted were revenue recognition and the capitalisation of large capex. The auditor also confirmed that the audit trail operated throughout the year.
reports.relatedParties: The company made small purchases of about ₹0.3 crore from promoter firms Kushal Electricals, Waterloo Motors, and KSH Distriparks. Remuneration for key management personnel was ₹13.5 crore for the year.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities consisted of ₹8.5 crore in bank guarantees. The company had capital commitments of ₹41.5 crore at the end of March 2026. There is also an EPCG export obligation of ₹201.8 crore to meet from April 2026; failing to do so would require paying ₹33.6 crore in saved duties plus interest.
reports.other: The company reports one single business segment of making magnet winding wires, with exports reaching ₹823 crore in FY26. From the IPO proceeds, ₹226 crore was used to repay debt, and ₹34.6 crore was spent on machinery and rooftop solar, with no deviation reported. Total borrowings stood at ₹316 crore at the end of March 2026.
flags: The CEO resigned on 31 March 2026, alongside other changes to the company secretary and board directors.
Pay for key management personnel was ₹13.5 crore, taking up about 12% of profit, which is high for the company's size.
Customer concentration is high, with the top 10 customers bringing in 51.15% of FY26 revenue.
The company faces a large ₹201.8 crore export obligation from April 2026, risking penalties if unmet.
A massive ₹1,117 crore of current and fixed assets are pledged to lenders.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an emphasis of matter on the Decision Point dispute, where sellers claim ₹220 crore compared to the ₹70 crore or less provided by the company. The auditor warned this might have an adverse effect on the group's functioning. The auditor also noted an audit-trail exception at Decision Point. Key audit matters included goodwill carrying value, revenue recognition, and a new ERP migration.
reports.contingent: There is a major unresolved dispute over the purchase of the remaining 20% of Decision Point. The sellers claim ₹220.3 crore, while the company estimates a maximum of ₹70.3 crore and has booked a ₹67.7 crore redemption liability. Other than this, contingent liabilities are tiny, amounting to just ₹0.05 crore for income tax.
reports.other: The company owns about 80 to 90% of Decision Point and holds a $3 million SAFE note in Healtheon AI. Promoters Venkat Viswanathan and Pramadwathi Jandhyala own 65.1% of the company, but no dividend has ever been paid despite large treasury investments.
flags: The auditor issued an emphasis of matter regarding the Decision Point purchase dispute, warning it could adversely affect the group's functioning.
Decision Point sellers are claiming ₹220.3 crore for the remaining 20% stake, drastically higher than the company's ₹70.3 crore estimate.
The auditor flagged an audit-trail exception at Decision Point's books.

reports.auditor: The auditor, Deloitte Haskins & Sells, gave an unmodified opinion. They highlighted one key audit matter regarding an impairment test on ₹491.6 crore of Lote fluorination assets due to declining performance. No impairment was booked, as it depends on management's growth forecasts.
reports.relatedParties: The annual report notes that related-party dealings are small.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include indirect-tax disputes of ₹70.7 crore (up from ₹40.4 crore in FY25) and bank guarantees of ₹77.1 crore. There is a customs case involving denatured-ethanol duty with ₹3.5 crore paid under protest. Title transfers for merged-entity properties remain pending.
reports.outlook: The management discussion highlighted the company's position as India's largest ethyl acetate maker and a top-three player globally outside China. It noted that its ketene and fluorination operations rely on specialized hazardous-process permits and skills. It also reported that butyl acetate production started at the Mahad site.
reports.other: The company changed its depreciation method from written-down-value to straight-line. Without this, standalone depreciation would have been ₹112.9 crore higher, resulting in a ₹20.3 crore pre-tax loss. Earnings also included a ₹40.7 crore one-time gain from a favourable electricity charge order. Exports were 32% of revenue, the USA accounted for about 10%, and the top 10 customers made up 20% to 27% of revenue.
flags: The company avoided a ₹20.3 crore standalone pre-tax loss only by changing its depreciation method to save ₹112.9 crore.
FY26 earnings were artificially boosted by a ₹40.7 crore one-time electricity charge gain, which the utility has appealed.
The auditor raised a key audit matter over ₹491.6 crore of fluorination assets due to declining performance, with no impairment booked yet.
Indirect-tax disputes increased to ₹70.7 crore, up from ₹40.4 crore in the previous year.
The company experienced management churn, noting the resignation of its CFO in April 2026.

reports.auditor: The auditor, S.R. Batliboi, gave an unmodified opinion. They highlighted goodwill impairment as a key audit matter. They also noted that the audit trail was not enabled for direct database-level changes in some of the company's software.
reports.contingent: The company disclosed no contingent liabilities. It reported capital commitments of ₹52 crore as of March 2026.
reports.other: Key managerial personnel pay rose to ₹42.0 crore in FY26 from ₹13.8 crore, mainly due to ₹32.7 crore in share-based pay. The company's associates are losing money, contributing a ₹11.2 crore share of loss for the year. It acquired 60% of Trenes.com and 54.66% of Brevistay (for ₹65.69 crore), holding rights to buy the rest. Additionally, ₹740.8 crore from a share issue to Prosus remained unused at year-end.
flags: The auditor warned that the required audit trail was not enabled for direct database-level changes in certain software.
Associate companies are losing money, resulting in a ₹11.2 crore share of loss for the year.
Compensation for key managers tripled to ₹42.0 crore, heavily driven by share-based pay.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. They noted a key audit matter regarding investments, specifically the sale of equity and debt instruments. There was no emphasis of matter.
reports.relatedParties: In FY26, the company purchased ₹162.8 crore in goods from group listed company Lakshmi Electrical Control Systems (LECS). It also had ₹9.3 crore in sales and ₹2.1 crore in services with LECS. Approval was sought for up to ₹450 crore in future dealings with LECS. A relative of the Chairman holds 7.6 lakh shares in LECS.
reports.contingent: Standalone contingent liabilities included ₹0.98 crore in claims not acknowledged as debt, ₹0.93 crore for excise, and ₹6.2 crore for GST. The company reported letters of credit worth ₹28.6 crore and guarantees of ₹26.9 crore. Capital commitments were ₹14.9 crore.
reports.other: Standalone FY26 segment revenue and profit were ₹1,801 crore and ₹9.8 crore for textile machinery, ₹1,205 crore and ₹97.2 crore for machine tools and foundry, and ₹207 crore and ₹28.7 crore for the advanced technology centre. Standalone exports totaled ₹344 crore. Promoters held a 30.80% stake with no disclosed pledges. The company also contributed 4.21 acres of surplus land for a joint development on a revenue-share basis.
flags: The core textile machinery division is deeply cyclical, earning just ₹9.8 crore in profit on ₹1,801 crore of revenue in FY26.
The company made large related-party purchases of ₹162.8 crore from LECS, a company in which a relative of the Chairman holds shares.
Overseas subsidiaries are operating at a loss, with the Dubai unit reporting a ₹32 crore loss in FY26.

reports.auditor: The auditor included an emphasis of matter regarding a ₹134.1 crore insurance claim asset in subsidiary Daawat Foods related to a fire in Bhopal. The insurer rejected the claim, but a district court ruled in favour of LT Foods in December 2023. The insurer's appeal is pending in the Madhya Pradesh High Court. Management stated that ₹136 crore is outstanding and ₹50 crore was received against a bank guarantee, with no income booked.
reports.relatedParties: The company engaged in large transactions with group entities, which included purchases from Raghunath Agro Industries and packaging services from Sara Flexi Pack LLP. Additionally, the company provided standalone guarantees totaling ₹617 crore for the working-capital loans of related parties, of which ₹253 crore was drawn.
reports.contingent: The company provided standalone guarantees amounting to ₹617 crore for related parties' working-capital loans, with ₹253 crore drawn. The company is also involved in an ongoing legal dispute in the Madhya Pradesh High Court over a repudiated ₹134.1 crore insurance claim.
reports.other: The report noted some loss-making units. The subsidiary Bonne Nature in Uganda reported negative reserves and a loss in FY26. Furthermore, new entities located in the Middle East and Arabia also recorded small losses.
flags: The auditor drew attention to a disputed ₹134.1 crore insurance claim asset whose outcome is binary and pending in the High Court.
The company extended large standalone guarantees of ₹617 crore for the working-capital loans of related parties.
The business relies on large related-party transactions for purchases and packaging with group entities.
The Uganda subsidiary Bonne Nature is operating with negative reserves and reported a loss for the year.

reports.auditor: Price Waterhouse Chartered Accountants LLP gave an unmodified opinion, with an emphasis of matter regarding the approved mergers of Lumax Ancillary and IAC India. Key audit matters included customer price-adjustment liabilities and ₹39.8 crore invested in three loss-making subsidiaries without any impairment taken. The auditor also noted a control gap, as core accounting software lacked a database-level audit trail and application-level logs for privileged users.
reports.relatedParties: The company has sizeable dealings with its promoter-controlled sister company, Lumax Industries. Shareholders approved material related-party transactions. The annual report notes FY26 transactions of roughly ₹379 crore, plus royalty payments of ₹4.0 crore and rent paid to both Lumax Industries and the chairman. There are also small loans given to key management personnel.
reports.contingent: The group had capital commitments of ₹96.6 crore in March 2026, up from ₹42.8 crore the prior year. Contingent liabilities totaled about ₹36 crore, consisting of ₹30.6 crore for income tax, ₹4.5 crore for GST, and ₹1.1 crore for legal disputes. A ₹7.8 crore bill-discounting decree was won on appeal in April 2025, and the deposit was refunded.
reports.other: The standalone notes in the annual report mention that deposits of ₹38.9 crore are pledged as security for a subsidiary's loan.
flags: The auditor flagged a control gap because core accounting software lacked a database-level audit trail and application-level logs for some privileged users.
No impairment was taken on ₹39.8 crore of investments in three subsidiaries whose accumulated losses leave their net worth below carrying value.
Deposits of ₹38.9 crore have been pledged as security for a subsidiary's loan.
The group faces contingent liabilities of about ₹36 crore, mainly for disputed income tax and GST claims.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The key audit matter was revenue recognition regarding price-variation accruals with customers, as estimating these cost recoveries at year-end is critical to the company's margins. The CARO report only noted small disputed customs dues.
reports.relatedParties: In FY26, the company paid ₹57.8 crore in royalties to Stanley, which is about 1.4% of revenue and roughly 34% of net profit. Purchases from the Stanley group were about ₹322 crore. Purchases from promoter-group companies Lumax Auto Technologies and Lumax Ancillary totalled ₹478 crore. Sales to Lumax Auto Technologies were ₹204 crore. Service charges paid to Lumax Management Services were ₹31.6 crore.
reports.contingent: Disputed customs demands include ~₹26.4 crore plus a ₹13.2 crore penalty over imported mould values, which is under appeal, and ₹26.9 crore over customs classification. There are disputed transfer-pricing additions of ₹26.7 crore for AY22 and ₹24.0 crore for AY23. The company also faces new GST notices and a ₹2.5 crore Sanand property tax claim. Capital commitments stood at ₹172.6 crore at the end of March 2026.
reports.outlook: Management targets increasing the LED share of revenue to 65–70%. The report states an EBITDA margin target of 12% within two years, reaching the early teens within two to three years. The value of lamps per passenger vehicle is expected to reach ₹22,000–25,000 in four to five years. The company also highlighted a single-source contract win for the Honda Activa and Shine models.
reports.other: The company owns 21.28% of SL Lumax, which had an FY26 turnover of ~₹2,900 crore and an EBITDA margin of ~14%. Passenger vehicles made up 65% of the sales mix. Net profit absorbed a ₹17.8 crore exceptional charge for new labour codes. The top three customers accounted for about 61% of revenue. No promoter share pledges were disclosed.
flags: Customer concentration is high, with the top three automakers generating roughly 61% of FY26 revenue.
Royalty payments to Stanley equalled 34% of net profit, and related-party purchases were very large relative to profits.
The management report claims capital spending was internally accrued and not debt-funded, but total borrowings actually rose.
The auditor flagged the estimation of price recoveries from customers as a key audit matter, underscoring a vulnerability in profit margins.
The company faces multiple large disputed tax demands, including customs and transfer-pricing claims.

reports.auditor: The auditor (S. C. Makhecha & Associates, fee ₹7 lakh) gave an unmodified opinion. They included an emphasis of matter regarding expired office leases in four cities pending renewal, and two modified leases where a ₹2.59 crore right-of-use asset and ₹2.40 crore lease liability were derecognised. Key audit matters were revenue recognition and contingent liabilities.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party trade is minimal, featuring ₹1.48 crore in sales to Modern Machine Tools. Notably, since 1 October 2025, the CMD (Rupesh Mehta) and a whole-time director (Nikesh Mehta) are paid via professional/management consultancy fees of ₹3 lakh and ₹2 lakh a month plus GST, rather than a salary.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities consist entirely of ₹11.6 crore for bank guarantees and letters of credit.
reports.outlook: The Management Discussion and Analysis states that a new 13-acre expansion will enable the company to sustain an annual growth rate of around 20%. Phase-1 of this site provides for an additional 1,000 to 1,500 machines.
reports.other: The company has no subsidiaries and does not report separate segments. Promoters hold 73.22% with no pledged shares. A note on bank stock statements (inventory and receivables) reported ₹145.6 crore at March 2026, showing a minor ₹0.6 crore discrepancy with the books.
flags: The annual report's MD&A projects around 20% annual growth, which is noticeably lower than the 30%+ guidance given by management in earnings calls.
The top promoters are paid through professional consultancy fees rather than a traditional executive salary structure.
The auditor flagged an emphasis of matter regarding expired office leases pending renewal.
There is a small ₹0.6 crore discrepancy between bank stock statements and the company's books.

reports.auditor: The auditor, S H B A & Co. LLP (formerly Bathiya & Associates), gave an unmodified opinion with no emphasis of matter. They flagged revenue recognition as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: The company buys from and pays several firms owned by relatives of directors and key managers (including Mamata Airwings, Srikaram Digital Marketing, and Shree Maruti Travels). Individual line items ranged from ₹0.1 cr to ₹2.6 cr, with the largest expense line at ~₹2.2 cr. Total director remuneration and commission was ~₹5.4 cr. Sales to the US subsidiary were ₹19 cr.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are negligible, consisting of ₹0.32 cr for tax and ₹0.12 cr for guarantees.
reports.other: India accounted for 37% of revenue. Geographic revenue included India at ₹83.3 cr, the USA at ₹56.5 cr, Canada at ₹3.8 cr, and Mexico at ₹2.3 cr. The US subsidiary, Mamata Enterprises Inc., reported a turnover of ₹63.0 cr, profit before tax of ₹4.5 cr, and net profit of ₹3.8 cr. Growth spending included sales hires for the US and packaging businesses.
flags: Director remuneration of ₹5.4 cr consumed roughly one-third of the company's net profit for the year.
The company engages in multiple related-party transactions with firms owned by relatives of its directors and key personnel.
Revenue from the core North American market (USA, Canada, and Mexico) fell sharply, highlighting severe geographic concentration risk.

reports.auditor: The auditor provided a clean opinion on the consolidated statements. There were no qualifications, emphasis of matter remarks, or key audit matters reported.
reports.relatedParties: The company buys materials from Manorama Africa Limited in Ghana, which is 100% owned by Vice-Chairperson Vinita Saraf. These purchases amounted to ₹191.8 crore in FY26 and ₹229.7 crore in FY25, representing roughly 20-25% of all raw-material purchases for FY26. A ₹200 crore omnibus approval for FY27 purchases is being sought at the AGM.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are very small. They consist of general claims of ₹0.81 crore, a GST demand of ₹0.19 crore, and an income tax claim of ₹0.35 crore.
reports.other: Promoter compensation rose sharply during the year. Pay for Ashish Saraf increased to ₹2.85 crore from ₹1.80 crore in FY25, while pay for Vinita Saraf increased to ₹1.55 crore from ₹0.97 crore. Additionally, the report indicated that imported seeds and butters account for about 50-60% of the company's raw materials.
flags: The company sources 20-25% of its raw materials through a related-party entity fully owned by the Vice-Chairperson.
Promoter compensation rose sharply during the financial year.

reports.auditor: M S K A & Associates LLP gave an unmodified opinion and listed revenue recognition as a key audit matter. The firm did not audit 12 subsidiaries that generate ₹2,817 crore or roughly 95% of group revenue; these relied on other auditors. They also noted a database-level audit trail was not enabled for one accounting software.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid managerial remuneration of ₹13.3 crore to Mark Saldanha and ₹7.7 crore to Sandra Saldanha, totaling about 5% of profits. It also paid ₹1.07 crore in rent to Mark Saldanha and granted ESOPs to the CFO and a director.
reports.contingent: The company reported no contingent liabilities and no loans taken against pledged shares. There were capital commitments of ₹53.9 crore at the end of March 2026.
reports.outlook: The management discussion notes that inventory was deliberately built up in FY25 and FY26 to protect the business against tariff and war risks. The report also highlights risks from being a price-taker in commodity medicines and having heavy concentration in pain therapy.
reports.other: Total FY26 revenue was ₹2,951 crore. This included ₹1,533 crore from North America, ₹1,015 crore from the UK and Europe, ₹303 crore from Australia and New Zealand, and ₹99 crore from the rest of the world. Two major customers accounted for ₹679 crore, making up 23% of total revenue.
flags: The primary auditor did not audit 12 subsidiaries that account for 95% of the group's total revenue.
A database-level audit trail was not enabled for one of the accounting softwares used.
Two key customers represent 23% of the company's total revenue.
The business is highly concentrated in pain therapy and operates as a price-taker in commodity molecules.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave a clean, unmodified opinion. They included an emphasis of matter regarding the restatement of standalone accounts for the merger of Mastek Enterprise Solutions, which had no impact on the consolidated numbers. The auditor also flagged revenue recognition on fixed-price contracts and goodwill impairment as key audit matters.
reports.contingent: Contingent income-tax demands increased to ₹36.7 crore by March 2026, up from ₹5.6 crore the previous year. The company also faces ₹9.4 crore in sales tax demands and ₹7.1 crore in employment claims. Capital commitments were very low at just ₹1.1 crore.
reports.other: In FY26, the UK and Europe segment earned ₹2,411 crore in revenue and ₹476 crore in profit. This region brings in almost all the company's profit. North America revenue fell 11% to ₹829 crore, earning just ₹51 crore in profit. The AMEA segment reported ₹459 crore in revenue and ₹23 crore in profit. The company holds ₹1,333 crore in goodwill for North America, and it raised the discount rate used to test this goodwill for impairment to 15%.
flags: North America carries a massive ₹1,333 crore in goodwill on the balance sheet despite its revenue falling 11% and margins remaining weak.
The auditor specifically flagged goodwill impairment as a key audit matter because North American goodwill is 1.6 times its revenue.
Contingent income tax demands jumped sharply to ₹36.7 crore by the end of March 2026.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion with no emphasis of matter. Key audit matters focused on the impairment of investment property and the capitalisation of project costs, which included borrowing costs.
reports.relatedParties: Material related-party transactions with sister company Antara were approved in FY26. Antara receives a development-management fee of about 9 to 9.5% of the sales value on senior-living project segments. This applies to about ₹1,200 to ₹1,500 crore at Estate 360 and 15 to 20% of Estate 361.
reports.contingent: The company reported negligible contingent liabilities. These consist of ₹0.2 crore for Uttarakhand VAT and ₹0.5 crore for income tax.
reports.other: The balance sheet includes a deferred tax asset of about ₹195 crore, which stems from accumulated tax losses. The company declared no dividends.
flags: Sister company Antara takes a significant 9 to 9.5% development-management fee on senior-living sales.
The company carries a ₹195 crore deferred tax asset resulting from accumulated tax losses.

reports.auditor: The auditor, ATK & Associates, gave a clean, unmodified opinion with no key audit matters. The audit trail worked all year. Quarterly stock statements given to banks matched the company's books. They noted ₹13 crore in capital work-in-progress and a SIDBI term loan of ₹7.5 crore.
reports.relatedParties: The company bought ₹72.44 crore of materials from M/s Volts AMP, a relative of a promoter or director. This was about 30% of its total ₹241.5 crore material cost and 24% of revenue. It sold ₹5.89 crore to and bought ₹1.11 crore from M/s Ultra Energy, another relative. The company also gave a ₹23.9 lakh advance to Mukesh Gupta. All deals were stated to be at arm's length.
reports.contingent: The auditor's report noted that there are no contingent liabilities.
reports.outlook: The board report targets revenue growth of 40% to 50% for the coming year. The management discussion highlights risks from its dependence on imported cells, mainly from China, noting that holding large stocks leaves the company vulnerable if cell prices fall.
reports.other: The company reports as a single business segment. It owns 75% of a battery recycling subsidiary, Maxvolt ReEarth Pvt Ltd, with an investment of ₹37.5 lakh. The board reported issuing 9,61,822 warrants at ₹440 each to promoters Mukesh Gupta (5,61,822) and Suresh Jha (4,00,000). They paid 25% upfront, totaling ₹10.6 crore, with the remaining ₹31.7 crore due within 18 months.
flags: Purchases from a related party, M/s Volts AMP, accounted for a highly concentrated 30% of total material costs.
The related-party note in the accounts is garbled with misaligned names and categories.
The management discussion section mistakenly left in draft wording about liquidity and hedging policies.
The chairman's letter incorrectly states the profit after tax as 1,011.68 million instead of ₹1,011.68 lakh.
Consolidated profit is higher than standalone profit only because of a ₹3.6 crore deferred-tax credit, even though the subsidiary barely operated.

reports.auditor: The auditor identified the recoverability of the Gwalior polyurethane (PU) plant as a key audit matter. This plant has persistently been under-used and reported operating losses in current and previous years. Its carrying value is ₹102.7 crore, and an outside valuer assessed its fair value.
reports.relatedParties: The parent company sold ₹180.75 crore worth of goods to its wholly owned US subsidiary during the year. These sales were made at an arm's-length price using the transactional net margin method.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities totalled ₹12.8 crore, decreasing from ₹22.5 crore in the previous year. This includes disputed claims of ₹9.5 crore for GST, ₹2.1 crore for income tax, and ₹1.2 crore for customs.
reports.outlook: Management plans to set up a new R&D centre. The report cites an industry study projecting the global synthetic leather market to grow from about US$49 billion in 2025 to US$104 billion by 2035. The automotive segment is expected to be the fastest-growing application with a 13% compound annual growth rate.
reports.other: The company operates as a single reported segment and is effectively debt-free, showing a 0.01 debt-to-equity ratio and a 247x interest cover. Two wholly owned subsidiaries reported losses: the US warehouse unit lost ₹1.5 crore on ₹176.9 crore turnover, and the Lithuanian unit lost ₹1.6 crore. The company paid a dividend of ₹5 per share for FY25.
flags: The auditor highlighted the recoverability of the PU plant as a key audit matter due to its ₹102.7 crore carrying value and ongoing operating losses.
The wholly owned US subsidiary reported a net loss despite the parent company selling ₹180.75 crore of goods to it.
Operating margins fell to 22% in Q1 from 31% in Q4, missing management's guided baseline of 25-26%.
The company faces significant customer concentration risk with a few US programs, worsened by US tariffs and freight costs that have jumped fourfold.
There is key-man risk as the Chairman and Managing Director faced health issues, and his son is not involved in operations.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. There were no key audit matters or emphasis of matter paragraphs. No contingent liabilities were disclosed beyond a subsidiary guarantee.
reports.relatedParties: The company reported sales of ₹19.47 crore and service charges of ₹2.51 crore to Mani Auto Components, where Chairman Nitin Menon is a partner. This accounted for about 6.5% of revenue, with ₹4.37 crore outstanding. There were also small dealings with Flyga Resorts, Sunshine Acres, and Menon United.
reports.contingent: There were no contingent liabilities disclosed other than a ₹29 crore corporate guarantee given by the parent company to its subsidiary, Menon Alkop.
reports.other: The company reports a single "Auto Components" segment. Two wholly owned subsidiaries are operating, while a third, Menon Bearings New Ventures, has no operations. Bank term loans are secured by Kolhapur assets and a personal guarantee from Chairman Nitin Menon. Out of ₹66.5 crore in consolidated receivables, ₹14.6 crore are 6 to 12 months old. MD R.D. Dixit served until March 3, 2026, and Arun Aradhye took over on March 4, 2026.
flags: Related-party dealings with a Chairman-linked firm account for about 6.5% of revenue.
A significant portion of consolidated receivables, ₹14.6 crore out of ₹66.5 crore, is aged between 6 and 12 months.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The only key audit matter highlighted was revenue recognition at high-volume stores and discount accruals.
reports.relatedParties: In FY26, the company paid showroom rent and concessions to Chairman Rafique Malik (₹1.8 crore) and Aziza Malik (₹2.6 crore). It also paid a retail-agency commission of ₹2.5 crore to Metro Shoes. The Board noted these transactions were small and at arm's length. Additionally, the Managing Director's re-appointment from April 2027 allows for pay of up to ₹10 crore a year.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were very small at roughly ₹5 crore, related entirely to minor tax cases.
reports.outlook: The CEO's letter highlighted the opening of 147 new stores and the closure of 23 in FY26. About 40 of these new openings were value-format Walkway stores. The annual report's cash flow showed a capital expenditure of ₹139 crore for the year, driven by store fit-outs, IT upgrades, and warehousing.
reports.other: The company reports as a single business segment focused on retail footwear, bags, and accessories through company-operated stores and e-commerce. The annual report also notes ₹40 crore in goodwill related to the acquisition of the Fila brand.
flags: Growth engines like sports and Walkway are scaling slower than expected and currently dilute profit margins.
Erratic quality-certification (BIS) renewals for overseas factories are stalling the rollout of Foot Locker, MetroActiv, and Fila.
Profits are lagging behind sales growth due to higher marketing, talent, and new-store occupancy costs.
Inventory is very heavy at 273 days, posing a risk of markdowns if there is a fashion miss or a drop in demand.

reports.auditor: The auditor, S.R. Batliboi & Co., gave an unmodified opinion but included a key audit matter on revenue recognition for year-end price-variation estimates. CARO remarks flagged the parent for using ₹312 crore of short-term funds for long-term purposes. Two subsidiaries reported cash losses. Seven subsidiaries with ₹327 crore in revenue were audited by other auditors. The audit trail was not enabled at the database level.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid ₹27.8 crore in rent to the promoter company Minda Capital, up from ₹24.5 crore in FY25. It made purchases worth ₹29.9 crore from Minda Silca. The chairman's pay was ₹14.3 crore.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities jumped to about ₹105 crore from about ₹17 crore in March 2025. This mainly includes a ₹67.1 crore income-tax demand for AY2023-24 under appeal, which includes ₹17.8 crore in interest. It also includes ₹32.1 crore for GST and VAT claims.
reports.outlook: Management outlined a Vision 2030 target in the annual report, aiming for ₹17,500 crore in consolidated revenue, which implies 3.5 times growth and a 28% CAGR from FY25. The vision targets an EBITDA margin over 12.5%, a net debt-to-equity ratio of 0.3x, ROCE above 25%, and exports of ₹1,500 crore. The year's record ₹413 crore capex was the first tranche of a five-year, ₹2,000 crore organic plan through FY30.
reports.other: Geographically, India accounted for ₹5,479 crore of FY26 revenue, while outside India contributed ₹707 crore. Interest costs nearly doubled to ₹123 crore due to a debt-funded stake purchase. The annual report presents conflicting financial baselines, quoting an unexplainable FY25 ROCE of 23.1% and MD&A net debt of ~₹1,165 crore, while the capital-management note states net debt of ₹1,369 crore and a 51.5% net debt-to-capital ratio.
flags: The CARO report flagged that the parent company used ₹312 crore of short-term funds for long-term purposes.
Contingent liabilities sharply increased to about ₹105 crore, driven largely by a ₹67.1 crore disputed income-tax demand and ₹32.1 crore in GST and VAT claims.
The auditor noted that the accounting audit trail was not enabled at the database level.
Two subsidiaries, Spark Minda Green Mobility and Spark Minda-Toyodenso, incurred cash losses according to the CARO remarks.
The annual report contains unexplained inconsistencies in its metrics, citing a baseline ROCE of 23.1% and varying net debt figures across different sections.

reports.auditor: The auditor re-issued the reports with an 'Other Matter' added at the CAG's request, noting the FY26 accounts were approved without an audit committee because the company had no independent directors. An emphasis of matter stated that receivables, payables, and advances are subject to balance confirmation. Key audit matters included revenue recognition, inventory valuation, and raw-material consumption. Under CARO, the auditor noted that conveyance deeds for 275 acres of land are not yet in the company's name, and 1.5 acres are encroached.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities stood at ₹449 crore, up from ₹291 crore the previous year. This includes ₹310 crore in claims not acknowledged as debt and ₹118 crore in bank guarantees. The nature of the claims was not detailed, but the total is large compared to the annual net profit of ₹131 crore. Capital commitments were ₹58 crore, compared to ₹29 crore a year earlier.
reports.outlook: The management discussion in the annual report stated that the order book stood at ₹2,594 crore on 1 April 2026. However, in its SWOT analysis, management cautioned that gaining market share in exports will be challenging.
reports.other: The company provides no segment reporting, as it is exempted as a defence producer. The aluminium joint venture with NALCO (UADNL) was found commercially non-viable and recommended for strike-off, with no further capital at risk. Imported raw materials cost ₹255 crore in FY26. The balance sheet showed inventory of ₹1,333 crore, which is larger than a full year's revenue, and receivables of ₹554 crore. A total dividend of ₹2.10 per share was declared.
flags: The FY26 accounts were approved without an audit committee because the company lacked independent directors.
Contingent liabilities are very high at ₹449 crore, including ₹310 crore in unexplained claims not acknowledged as debt.
The auditor noted that conveyance deeds for 275 acres of company land are not yet in the company's name.
The auditor emphasised that receivables, payables, and advances lack balance confirmations or reconciliations.
Inventory is extremely high at ₹1,333 crore, which exceeds the company's entire annual revenue.

reports.auditor: The auditor flagged ₹11.0 crore of internally generated intangibles, which included salary costs and director pay, as a key audit matter. The recoverability of receivables was also made a key audit matter. The auditor included an emphasis of matter regarding an ongoing foreign-exchange compliance gap for capital remittances to a UK holding company and a Russian subsidiary, which remain "in process". Additionally, three foreign subsidiaries' accounts were unaudited.
reports.relatedParties: The listed company bought Mobavenue Media Pvt Ltd from its three promoters (Kunal Kothari, Tejas Rathod, Prachi Arora) for ₹59.68 crore, with ₹45.7 crore still outstanding at March 2026. The company also gave interest-bearing loans to promoter-linked PD Avenue Marketing (₹2.46 crore) and Quid Innovation (₹4.0 crore). Both act as customers and suppliers, with Quid owing ₹3.6 crore in receivables. A Russian subsidiary also appears in related-party sales.
reports.contingent: The file does not mention any disputed tax or legal claims or company guarantees. It only notes that all directors have provided personal guarantees for ₹8.5 crore in bank borrowings.
reports.other: For FY26, the company reported data costs of ₹131.6 crore, employee costs of ₹25.9 crore, and other expenses of ₹15.6 crore. Promoters voluntarily forgo dividends. At March 2026, ₹50 crore raised via a preferential allotment to non-promoters remained completely unutilised and was held in fixed deposits. The company carried ₹59.3 crore in trade receivables, which reached ₹87.3 crore when including unbilled contract assets.
flags: The company purchased its operating business from its own promoters for ₹59.68 crore, leaving a large ₹45.7 crore balance still owed to them at year-end.
The auditor raised a key audit matter regarding ₹11 crore in capitalised salaries and director pay, which flatters operating margins.
The company provided ₹6.46 crore in loans to two promoter-linked entities that concurrently act as its customers and suppliers.
The auditor highlighted an ongoing foreign-exchange compliance gap over capital remittances to entities in the UK and Russia.
The financial accounts for three of the company's foreign subsidiaries were left unaudited.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The report highlighted revenue recognition and the capitalisation of ₹135 crore as key audit matters. The CARO report was clean, noting that bank stock statements agreed with the company's books and that disputed tax amounts were small.
reports.relatedParties: The company made purchases from promoter-controlled firms, including ₹4.4 crore from Friends Packaging, ₹4.5 crore from Capricorn Industries, and ₹2.7 crore from Dynamic Metal. It also paid ₹1.0 crore to Sri Kanaka Durga Mini Transport. Several family members are employed as Vice Presidents, and the Chairman and Managing Director's pay was roughly ₹3.9 crore.
reports.contingent: The company reported contingent liabilities of ₹6.5 crore, which included ₹5.6 crore for income tax. It also had capital commitments of ₹22 crore at the end of March 2026.
reports.other: In FY26, EBITDA grew 20.6% and net profit grew 20.4%. Total volume rose 11.4% to 42,629 tonnes. Paint volumes grew 14.4% to 20,689 tonnes, bringing in ₹388 crore. Food and FMCG volumes rose 22.2% to 13,070 tonnes, while lubricants fell 13% to 8,015 tonnes. Pharma volumes jumped 209%, with revenue reaching ₹35 crore. Additionally, the company recorded a ₹0.8 crore gain from transferring a lease and building in Sandila.
flags: The Management Discussion and Analysis section mistakenly copied text from another company, referring to 'our journey of growth at Cosmo'.
The company relies on related-party purchases from several promoter-controlled entities.
Multiple family members of the promoters are employed as Vice Presidents.

reports.auditor: The auditor's report flagged the arm's-length pricing of related-party transactions as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: The company relies heavily on its promoters. In FY26, it bought ₹5,243 crore of goods from its jointly-controlling group and ₹216 crore from other related parties, making up about 70% of its material bill. It paid about ₹99 crore in rent and lease payments. It also paid a management fee of ₹60.9 crore to SAMIL. Shareholders were asked to approve FY27 transactions with Sumitomo, including up to ₹75 crore in royalty and ₹922 crore in purchases.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities included ₹37.5 crore for indirect-tax claims (down from ₹40.5 crore in FY25) and ₹3.3 crore for workmen claims.
reports.other: The company has no subsidiaries. FY26 revenue came from passenger cars (64%), two-wheelers (12%), commercial vehicles (10%), off-road and tractors (6%), and others (8%). Material costs rose to 67.5% of revenue in FY26, with copper making up 24 to 28% of raw-material costs. The company paid out 62% of its FY26 profit as dividends and made a 1:2 bonus issue.
flags: The auditor highlighted the arm's-length pricing of related-party transactions as a key audit matter.
The company is heavily dependent on its promoter group, sourcing about 70% of its materials from related parties.
The company pays a ₹60.9 crore management fee to SAMIL, which equals the royalty SAMIL pays to Sumitomo.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave no qualifications and included no emphasis of matter. The key audit matter was revenue recognition.
reports.relatedParties: Promoter-family executive pay for FY26 was ₹8.33 crore for Anoop Bector, ₹3.62 crore for Ishaan Bector, and ₹3.61 crore for Suvir Bector. This totalled about 11% of the profit after tax. Rajni Bector is paid by the subsidiary Bakebest.
reports.contingent: Consolidated contingent liabilities included income tax of ₹3.29 crore, stamp duty of ₹0.91 crore, and sales tax of ₹0.51 crore. A previous GST matter of ₹6.51 crore was cleared during FY26.
reports.other: FY26 capacity utilisation averaged 60% for biscuits and 75% for bakery. New plants included Dhar for biscuits, alongside Kolkata and Khopoli for bakery. The company declared an interim dividend of ₹0.60 and a final dividend of ₹0.70 per share. A CFO change to Anshul Rastogi was noted for August 2026.
flags: The consumer protection regulator fined the company ₹0.10 million in June 2026 over its '100% Atta' and '100% Whole Wheat' bread labels, which the company has appealed.
Promoter-family executive pay took up a substantial 11% of the company's profit after tax in FY26.
Exports in FY26 were negatively impacted by Dominican Republic duties, regulatory pressures, and the loss of a government duty-free export incentive.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The only key audit matter was revenue recognition, covering ₹147.4 crore in domestic sales and ₹717.9 crore in exports. The auditor also remarked that electronic backups of the books were not kept on servers in India from April to August 2025.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings were small. The managing director received ₹3.1 crore in pay. The company paid rent to K. Shalini, a relative of the promoter, and paid internet charges to Nettlinx, an entity with common key management personnel.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were just ₹2.3 crore. Margin-money deposits back ₹149.9 crore of bank guarantees and letters of credit. Capital commitments jumped to ₹160 crore at the end of March 2026, up from ₹12 crore.
reports.other: The company has four reporting sectors: clean energy (fuel cells and hydel), clean energy (civil nuclear), aerospace and defence, and products and others. It has two subsidiaries, Gee Pee Aerospace & Defence and Magnatar Aero Systems. Bloom Energy accounted for ₹633 crore of the ₹865 crore in standalone revenue. Several promoter-group members sold shares during the year. The NSE fined the company ₹5,000 for filing a related-party transaction and XBRL report one day late.
flags: A single US customer accounts for 73% of standalone revenue, posing a high concentration risk.
Electronic backups of the books were not maintained on servers in India between April and August 2025.
Several promoter-group members sold shares during the year.
Three designated persons traded without pre-clearance and executed contra trades, resulting in a ₹1.8 lakh profit being disgorged to SEBI.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an emphasis of matter because the company made no provision for interest on delayed payments to micro and small suppliers. It owed ₹4.9 crore to MSMEs out of ₹21.9 crore in total payables. Under CARO, the auditor warned that persistent losses warrant attention for medium and long-term financial sustainability. They noted a cash loss of ₹13.7 crore and concluded there was no material going-concern uncertainty only because of equity infusions and larger bank lines.
reports.relatedParties: The company sold goods worth ₹13.7 crore in FY25 and ₹1.8 crore in FY26 to a disclosed related party, Quadrant Future Tek Ltd. It also bought ₹2.6 crore from this company in FY26. The promoters, including Mohit Vohra and the Dhawan family, lent and were repaid ₹2.6 crore in FY26. Other promoter-linked counterparties are MV Mobility, Prime Electronics, and IBoard India.
reports.contingent: The company has small contingent liabilities, which include claims worth ₹3.1 crore and bank guarantees of ₹0.5 crore.
reports.other: The annual report notes the company listed after a ₹290 crore fresh-issue IPO, issuing 68.2 lakh shares at ₹425 each. It operates in two segments: rail propulsion, and rail electrification and cable products. At the end of March 2026, the company held ₹67.5 crore in inventory and had around ₹50 crore in borrowings.
flags: The auditor warned under CARO that persistent losses warrant attention regarding the company's medium and long-term financial sustainability.
The auditor stated that a material going-concern uncertainty was avoided only because of new equity infusions and larger bank lines.
The auditor issued an emphasis of matter because the company failed to provide for interest on delayed payments to MSME suppliers.
The company engaged in large related-party sales with Quadrant Future Tek Ltd, totaling ₹13.7 crore in FY25 and ₹1.8 crore in FY26.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters included revenue estimates under profit-share deals, deferred tax assets tied to past tax disputes, and the impairment of the agro plant due to its demerger. The auditors noted no overdue or over-budget projects. However, the accounting software's database-level audit trail was not enabled from 1 April to 10 July 2025, and certain tables lacked it for the rest of FY26.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small, with disputed tax amounting to about ₹3 crore. However, the financial impact of patent suits against the company's launched products cannot be estimated.
reports.outlook: The management discussion notes that the crop-health division's demerger is effective October 2026. The Kothur plant is being upgraded for the carfilzomib launch, expected to finish by the end of 2026. In Brazil, the company remains the sole source of everolimus for the fourth year and was among the first to launch apixaban.
reports.other: FY26 pharmaceutical revenue was ₹3,940 crore with a ₹1,547 crore profit, while the agro-chemicals segment reported ₹138 crore in revenue and a ₹19.8 crore loss. Geographically, the USA contributed ₹2,381 crore, India ₹691 crore, and the rest of the world ₹1,006 crore. Capital work-in-progress includes ₹84 crore that is one to two years old. The company also reported a CFO change, with Amit Parekh taking over in February 2026.
flags: A single customer accounted for 41% of FY26 revenue, but this profit stream has almost run off.
The accounting software's database-level audit trail was not enabled for the entire year.
The financial impact of patent lawsuits against launched products cannot be estimated.
The CFO left the company in February 2026.

reports.auditor: The auditor's opinion was unmodified. However, it included a key audit matter regarding the carrying value of the Dewas CDMO plant (₹314 crore) and investments in UK subsidiaries, including Manchester Organics (₹94 crore). The auditor noted that impairment testing for these assets relies on management forecasts.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were small, totaling approximately ₹7 crore for tax and excise disputes, along with some employee matters.
reports.outlook: Management noted that raw materials were 41.5% of revenue, with sulphur prices rising while fluorspar, boric acid, and chloroform prices fell. The company is incubating an Advanced Materials vertical. Ongoing capital expenditure plans mentioned in the report include a ₹75 crore debottlenecking of multi-purpose plants and a US$14 million Chemours project, of which Chemours is funding US$5 million.
reports.other: FY26 segment revenue was ₹1,615 crore for high-performance products, ₹1,152 crore for specialty chemicals, and ₹546 crore for CDMO. Exports comprised about 67% of total revenue at ₹2,225 crore, with export shares of 55% for HPP, 71% for Specialty, and 96% for CDMO. A QIP raised ₹750 crore to repay debt, dropping promoter holding from 28.4% to 27.1%.
flags: The auditor flagged the carrying value of the Dewas plant (₹314 crore) and UK investments (₹94 crore) as a key audit matter because impairment testing depends on management forecasts.
Customer concentration is high, with three customers contributing ₹545 crore, ₹391 crore, and ₹342 crore, together making up about 39% of total FY26 revenue.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an emphasis of matter regarding the Gurugram 37-D project, which has ₹469 crore in provisions, a ₹750 crore recovery suit, and 16 other cases. Further emphasis points included Faridabad land without a conveyance deed (₹132 crore), an unsold Kochi project lacking environmental clearance (₹87 crore), and unconfirmed balances or revenue irregularities at subsidiaries. Key audit matters were revenue recognition, inventory valuation, provisions, and group trade receivables of ₹5,092 crore.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings are mostly with subsidiaries and other government companies. These transactions are exempt from detailed disclosure under SEBI rules, and nothing unusual was found.
reports.contingent: Standalone contingent liabilities at March 2026 included claims not acknowledged as debt of ₹1,670 crore. The company also faces GST demands of ₹219 crore and VAT demands of ₹58 crore. A DVAT demand of ₹405 crore has been remanded and its outcome is not ascertainable, though it would be payable by the client if confirmed.
reports.other: Consolidated FY26 revenue was dominated by project management consultancy at ₹12,375 crore, or 96% of the total. EPC contributed ₹382 crore and real estate ₹100 crore. Geographic revenue included ₹116 crore from the Maldives. The company reversed an ₹80 crore inventory write-down for a Kochi project, helping boost net profit. Inventory for land and real-estate work-in-progress was ₹1,194 crore. The Government of India owns 61.75% of the company, with no shares pledged.
flags: Contingent claims not acknowledged as debt stand at ₹1,670 crore, alongside ₹219 crore in GST demands.
Group trade receivables reached ₹5,092 crore and were flagged as a key audit matter.
The auditor highlighted ₹469 crore in provisions and multiple legal disputes regarding structural cracks at the Gurugram 37-D project.
Auditors noted unconfirmed balances, manual ageing of receivables, and subcontractor irregularities at the HSCC and HSCL subsidiaries.
Stock exchanges penalized the company for non-compliance with board composition rules because independent directors had not been appointed.

reports.auditor: The auditor's report found no emphasis of matter in the extracts reviewed. However, the auditor designated the company's receivables and contract assets (₹3,336 crore and ₹9,552 crore respectively, making up 56% of standalone assets) as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: The company has related-party exposures including ₹290 crore in loans to group companies and ₹867 crore in investments. An old real-estate loan to Vizag Urban is still in the process of being recovered, and an investment in Oman was impaired by ₹21.3 crore in FY26.
reports.contingent: As of March 2026, group contingent liabilities included about ₹350 crore in tax disputes. This consisted of ₹137 crore in sales tax, ₹155 crore in GST, and ₹35 crore in service tax. The company also had ₹512 crore in disputes with the NHAI.
flags: Receivables and contract assets are extremely high, representing 56% of standalone assets, which the auditor flagged as a key audit matter.
The group faces significant contingent liabilities, including ₹512 crore in NHAI disputes and roughly ₹350 crore in tax disputes.
The company maintains high related-party exposure with ₹290 crore in loans and ₹867 crore in investments to group companies.
An investment in Oman suffered a financial impairment of ₹21.3 crore during the year.

reports.auditor: The auditor, S.R. Batliboi, gave an unmodified opinion. However, they included an emphasis of matter highlighting uncertainty from an income tax search conducted in FY24 at company premises and staff homes. The auditor also named year-end price variations as a key audit matter, as they are material and rely on judgment.
reports.relatedParties: The company relies heavily on Bharat Seats, a family-controlled associate. Sales to Bharat Seats were ₹486.6 cr in FY26, up from ₹388.4 cr in FY25, forming about 59% of total revenue. The company also leases premises from and buys capital work (₹2.8 cr) from Bharat Seats. At year-end, Bharat Seats owed the company ₹61.7 cr, and a ₹17 cr loan to the associate was repaid during the year.
reports.contingent: Total contingent liabilities stood at ₹12.3 cr, which is small compared to the net worth. This includes ₹5.5 cr in income tax demands and ₹6.8 cr in GST claims. A major GST dispute over two-wheeler seat classification involves ₹4.96 cr in tax deposited under protest, an equal penalty, and a new ₹1.55 cr notice. Capital commitments dropped to ₹5.6 cr from ₹33.5 cr.
reports.other: The company reports a single seating systems segment and operates solely in India. Customer concentration is extreme, with just two clients providing ₹729.7 cr, or 89% of revenue. The group structure includes a 28.66% stake in Bharat Seats, three 50% joint ventures, and two wholly owned subsidiaries. Year-end cash and equivalents fell sharply to ₹15.1 cr from ₹50.8 cr. Promoters hold 73.13% of shares, with no pledges disclosed.
flags: Auditors flagged an emphasis of matter regarding an income tax search at company premises and employee homes.
The business has extreme customer concentration, with just two customers generating about 89% of total revenue.
Nearly 59% of the company's revenue comes from a single related party, Bharat Seats.
The company faces unresolved GST disputes and penalties over the classification of two-wheeler seats.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an Emphasis of Matter regarding the Dahej plant fire. A ₹362.9 crore loss and a ₹348.8 crore insurance claim were booked based on a surveyor's opinion, even though the insurer's assessment is still ongoing. Key audit matters highlighted revenue recognition due to a fraud-risk presumption and the capitalisation of costs in the subsidiary Neogen Ionics' capital work-in-progress.
reports.relatedParties: The parent company gave a ₹1,223 crore corporate guarantee for borrowings by its subsidiary, Neogen Ionics. It also pledged 30% of its shares in the subsidiary to lenders. Furthermore, the parent provided inter-corporate deposits of ₹110 crore to the subsidiary at a 9.85% interest rate.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities rose to ₹117.9 crore from ₹28.7 crore the previous year. This includes ₹81.7 crore in possible customs duty and GST on fire-damaged goods sold as scrap, though the company expects its insurance to cover this amount.
reports.other: Standalone revenue for FY26 included ₹606 crore from India and ₹250 crore from overseas, which includes deemed exports. The company also disclosed using supplier finance and factoring arrangements to manage working capital, which keeps its payables high with supplier consent.
flags: The auditor flagged that a ₹348.8 crore insurance claim was booked while the insurer is still processing the assessment.
Contingent liabilities surged to ₹117.9 crore, largely due to potential tax claims on fire-damaged scrap.
The parent company has taken on significant risk with a ₹1,223 crore corporate guarantee and a share pledge for its subsidiary.
The company relies on supplier factoring arrangements, which acts as a hidden form of borrowing and flatters operating cash flow.

reports.auditor: The auditor identified revenue recognition on multi-element contracts as a key audit matter. The report did not contain any qualifications or emphasis of matter.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities consist mainly of bank guarantees totaling ₹136 crore. There is also about ₹1 crore in tax liabilities.
reports.outlook: The annual report highlights business risks tied to a heavy dependence on IndiaAI Mission spending and a select few neo-cloud customers like Yotta. It also notes that management has stopped chasing exports.
reports.other: Three customers each contributed 10% or more to FY26 revenue, up from two in FY25. Exports dropped to ₹30.5 crore (1.4% of revenue), down from ₹62 crore in FY25. Only about 30% of procurement is sourced from India. The company also changed its inventory valuation accounting from FIFO to a moving weighted average method starting April 1, 2025.
flags: Three customers each contributed 10% or more of FY26 revenue, showing very high client concentration.
The top three suppliers account for 65% to 70% of all purchases.
The business relies heavily on government IndiaAI Mission spending and a handful of neo-cloud clients.
The company changed its inventory valuation method from FIFO to moving weighted average, requiring prior periods to be restated.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. They noted one key audit matter: revenue recognition on fixed-price contracts using the percentage of completion method. This requires heavy management judgement and is relevant given the company's lumpy, milestone-driven revenue.
reports.relatedParties: The parent company provides loans and lends float to two of its unlisted subsidiaries: SSK Citizen Services and Timepay Digital Infotech.
reports.contingent: The annual report notes contingent liabilities of roughly ₹15 crore in bank guarantees. There is also a ₹4.7 crore commitment for intangibles under development.
reports.other: The financial accounts show only a single operating segment, meaning there is no audited breakdown of revenue by vertical or geography. The management discussion states FY26 total income was ₹209.4 crore with a net profit of ₹40.8 crore. Out of a ₹300 crore preferential share issue, ₹277.86 crore remained unutilised at the end of March 2026 and was parked in fixed deposits. The company paid a token dividend of ₹4.09 crore.
flags: Trade receivables more than tripled over the year to ₹103.7 crore, driving operating cash flow to a negative ₹45 crore.
The NSE and BSE each fined the company ₹50,000 for issuing preferential shares without prior in-principle approval.
The monitoring agency flagged a technical deviation because ₹3.18 crore from the fundraise was spent on rent and salaries.
The company's reported headline revenue and EBITDA are inflated by other income, largely interest earned on its unspent fundraise.
Management quietly downgraded its growth and margin targets within a single quarter while insisting that guidance had not changed.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The only key audit matter mentioned was the carrying value of goodwill resulting from the Neuland Health Sciences merger.
reports.relatedParties: The company routed about ₹14 crore in corporate social responsibility funds through the promoter-linked Neuland Foundation in FY26. It also paid ₹3.6 crore a year in rent to Mrs. D. Vijaya Rao, a relative of the promoters. The promoter and director pay figures could not be reliably read from the document.
reports.contingent: The company had capital commitments of ₹154 crore at the end of March 2026, up from ₹83 crore a year earlier. Contingent liabilities included disputed income tax of ₹7.5 crore and GST or customs disputes of ₹1.1 crore. There was also a ₹4.5 crore power surcharge and old land-title disputes at Bonthapally.
reports.other: The segment notes showed high concentration, with three customer groups each making up over 10% of revenue. Together they accounted for ₹1,088 crore, or about 53% of FY26 revenue, up from ₹504 crore in FY25. The report also confirmed a leadership change where Saharsh Davuluri became CEO and MD, and Sucheth Davuluri moved to Executive Vice Chairman.
flags: Three customer groups make up roughly 53% of the company's total revenue, representing severe client concentration.
Promoter and director pay figures could not be reliably read or verified from the provided annual report file.
The company is facing unresolved land-title disputes at its Bonthapally site.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unmodified opinion with no emphasis of matter. They noted a key audit matter regarding percentage-of-completion revenue recognition for fixed-price implementation contracts.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are very small. They consist entirely of income-tax demands totaling ₹3.1 crore.
reports.other: The company recorded ₹43.4 crore in exceptional items for FY26. This included ₹30.1 crore for Labour Codes and ₹13.4 crore for a Qatar legal claim over non-delivery of services. On management compensation, CMD Diwakar Nigam was paid 79 times the median salary, and his wife (a whole-time director) was paid 27 times. Their daughter was added to the board as a non-executive director in November 2025.
flags: A Qatar bank successfully sued the company for non-delivery of contracted deliverables, resulting in a ₹13.4 crore exceptional charge.
The CMD and his wife take very high compensation at 79 times and 27 times the median salary, respectively.

reports.auditor: The auditor highlighted key audit matters including revenue recognition, inventory valuation involving complex overhead absorption, and expected credit losses on receivables.
reports.relatedParties: MD Rahul Nachane and WTD/CFO Rajesh Lawande each drew roughly ₹1.2 crore in salary plus ₹1.62 crore in profit commission, which rose 2.6 times. VP Ahaan Nachane received ₹0.47 crore. Total promoter pay was around ₹6 crore, or 12% of net profit. The company paid rent and professional fees to promoters and promoter-linked Nupur Remedies. It also bought ₹21.4 crore in goods and paid ₹13.7 crore for processing to its subsidiary Macrotech Polychem, and earned ₹0.6 crore interest on loans to it.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were very small, consisting only of a ₹0.18 crore provident fund claim.
reports.other: The directors' report noted credit ratings of CRISIL BBB+ (with the outlook revised from negative to stable in March 2026) and ICRA BBB+ (stable). The company's wholly owned intermediates subsidiary, Macrotech Polychem, was classified as a material subsidiary in FY26.
flags: The company and promoters paid ₹54.4 lakh and ₹12.6 lakh to settle a SEBI show-cause notice for incorrect shareholding-pattern disclosures and takeover-rule lapses.
The BSE and NSE fined the company for late related-party reporting in FY24.
The company failed to inform the stock exchanges when an independent director left.
Profit commissions paid to top management jumped 2.6 times, pushing total promoter family pay to roughly 12% of the year's net profit.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The only key audit matter noted was revenue recognition, which is a standard item.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings were described as immaterial. They involved employee trusts and an entity named Vrata Tech, though specific amounts were not detailed.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were small at ₹13.6 crore, down from ₹27.5 crore previously. Capital commitments stood at ₹9.8 crore, compared to ₹83 crore last year.
reports.outlook: Management highlighted a completed ₹250 crore TDQ capacity expansion at Dahej, finished 10 to 12% under budget with trial production ongoing. A new ₹130 crore specialty rubber chemicals plant at Dahej was also approved, with trial production expected by Q2 FY28. Management noted significant risks to margins from cheap imports and free trade agreements.
reports.other: The company operates in a single segment for rubber chemicals. Total investments were ₹415 crore, including ₹240 crore in non-convertible debentures and ₹15 crore in inter-corporate deposits, with minimal borrowings of ₹8 crore. FY26 exports totaled ₹440 crore, making up 34% of turnover.
flags: Management blamed a 200 basis point margin fall on dumping from China and Southeast Asia.
The company is facing pressure from zero-duty imports entering through free trade agreements with Thailand and Korea.
Export revenue fell 10% and export volume dropped 8% due to US tariffs and cheap Chinese latex pricing.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unqualified opinion but highlighted inventory as a key audit matter. Standalone inventory of ₹271.9 crore makes up 24% of total assets, and there is an ₹81.4 crore allowance for slow-moving and obsolete stock. Work-in-progress and finished goods are valued using Excel spreadsheets across many locations.
reports.relatedParties: The company provided corporate guarantees totaling about ₹203 crore for its subsidiaries. This includes ₹112 crore for Thailand, ₹43.6 crore for Europe, and ₹47.3 crore for the USA. The company also has a USD 6 million loan to NRB Holdings and will provide debt to its Unitec joint venture.
reports.contingent: Standalone contingent liabilities include ₹49.8 crore for income tax, of which ₹12.4 crore was paid under protest, and ₹1.8 crore for sales tax and VAT. The impact of provident fund basic wages cannot be ascertained. The company also has open capital commitments of ₹21.6 crore.
reports.outlook: The company is expanding into new verticals, including aerospace with HAL orders, an industrial bearing joint venture with Italy's Unitec, and US production for GM. It is also targeting robotics, data centres, and off-highway markets. Brownfield expansion running through early 2028 will add 15% to 25% capacity across various bearing types.
reports.other: Standalone revenue rose 10% to ₹1,185.7 crore, and profit before tax and exceptional items grew 21.8% to ₹201 crore. Domestic original equipment manufacturers make up 65% to 70% of revenue, and no single customer exceeds 7%. The company declared a total dividend of ₹5.70 per share, a 39% payout.
flags: The auditor noted that ₹271.9 crore of standalone inventory is valued using Excel spreadsheets across multiple locations, requiring an ₹81.4 crore obsolescence allowance.
Standalone exports grew by a sluggish 2.7% during the year.
The Management Discussion text contradicts its own data table regarding whether economic value added (EVA) was negative or positive.
The company faces ₹49.8 crore in disputed income tax liabilities and an unascertainable risk related to provident fund basic wages.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unmodified opinion. They highlighted revenue recognition as a key audit matter, specifically regarding the percentage-of-completion method used for fixed-price contracts.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small. They consist of disputed income tax claims of ₹4.0 crore and GST claims of ₹0.6 crore. The company also has capital commitments of ₹4.7 crore.
reports.other: In FY26, product revenue was ₹740.6 crore (85% of total), while projects and services contributed ₹135.5 crore (15%). About 42% of revenue came from overseas. No single client accounted for more than 10% of revenue during the year. The company added a new Vietnam subsidiary in February 2026 and secured a US auto-finance client. The report noted that new labour codes increased staff costs.
flags: The auditor flagged revenue recognition on fixed-price contracts as a key audit matter requiring judgement.
Forward currency cover was minimal at just $2 million, despite about 42% of revenue coming from overseas currencies.
New labour codes contributed to rising staff costs during the year.

reports.auditor: The directors' and governance reports state the auditor's report is unmodified and does not contain any qualification or adverse remark. However, the exact auditor's report could not be read because the uploaded annual report file ends at page 103, omitting the financial statements.
reports.relatedParties: The annual report notice showed FY26 purchases of ₹20.8 crore from shareholder Omega Bright Steel & Components and ₹10.2 crore from Omega Bright Steel Pvt Ltd. The company also made ₹5.9 crore in sales to the latter. Shareholders were asked to approve transaction limits of ₹25 crore and ₹20 crore for FY27.
reports.other: The management discussion showed gross margins rose 284 basis points to 28.7%, while operating EBITDA was 18.1%. It listed exports to 17 countries, led by Italy at ₹13.9 crore, the USA at ₹11.2 crore, and Germany at ₹10.7 crore. Reported ratios included a 0.40 debt-to-equity ratio, 1.50 debt-service coverage, and interest cover of 8.1 to 9.7 times.
flags: The official uploaded annual report is incomplete and omits the financial statements, preventing a review of the contingent liabilities and detailed notes.
Operating cash flow was negative ₹2 crore in FY26, leading to increased borrowings and repeated equity raises to fund growth.
Related-party purchases from promoter group companies reached around 14% of revenue, raising concerns over fair pricing for key raw materials.
A recent preferential share allotment was priced at ₹601, significantly below the prevailing market price near ₹930.
Customer concentration is heavy, with the top five clients accounting for 50% to 55% of total revenue.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion but noted a key audit matter regarding revenue cut-off due to incentives or external pressures. They also flagged an audit-trail exception. The auditors could not confirm the database-level edit log for the third-party stock-records software, which is important for an inventory-heavy business.
reports.relatedParties: Promoter-family members lend money to the company and receive interest payments. The amounts involved are a few crore, which is small compared to the total debt of about ₹390 crore.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were negligible, involving just ₹0.2 crore for GST. The company had capital commitments of ₹73.0 crore at the end of March 2026, up from ₹23.6 crore a year earlier.
reports.other: In February 2026, the IPO raised ₹583 crore, including a ₹418 crore fresh issue and a ₹165 crore offer for sale by promoters. FY26 revenue by customer location included ₹263.6 crore from the USA, ₹131.6 crore from India, ₹78.6 crore from the UAE, and ₹37.5 crore from others. One customer accounted for ₹78.3 crore, or 15% of revenue. Company borrowings carry personal guarantees from directors and a relative.
flags: Auditors could not confirm the edit log for the stock-records software, raising a red flag for an inventory-heavy business.
A single customer accounted for 15% of the company's total revenue in FY26.
Company borrowings are backed by the personal guarantees of directors and a relative.

reports.auditor: The auditor reported that seven accounting software packages lack a database-level edit log, meaning they could not comment on them. Another software package keeps its edit log for only one year. Additionally, the auditor's CARO report recorded a merchant fraud incident where an app bug was exploited.
reports.contingent: The company has a disputed service-tax demand of ₹7.9 crore, plus a ₹7.9 crore penalty, relating to recharge commissions between FY15 and FY18. This is currently under appeal. There are also income-tax adjustments, but these are absorbed by the company's tax losses.
reports.outlook: The directors' report noted that shareholders approved extending the timeline and changing the objects for unused IPO proceeds on 2 July 2026. This change was done partly to capitalise the company's lending subsidiary.
reports.other: The company reports a single operating segment for payment and financial services, located entirely in India. In FY26, payments revenue was ₹857 crore and financial services was ₹262 crore. The accounts showed ₹15.8 crore of exceptional items, which included labour-code gratuity and a merchant fraud write-off, leaving an underlying loss of ₹46.3 crore. By March 2026, ₹182.2 crore of the net IPO proceeds remained unused.
flags: Merchants and users exploited an app bug to claim ₹40.4 crore, resulting in an ₹11.8 crore exceptional write-off.
Seven accounting software packages lack a database-level edit log, preventing the auditor from commenting on them.
One of the company's accounting software packages keeps its edit log for only a single year.
The company faces a disputed service-tax demand of ₹7.9 crore plus a ₹7.9 crore penalty.
Unused IPO money had to be re-purposed and its timeline extended by shareholder approval.

reports.auditor: Deloitte gave an unmodified opinion. However, the auditor noted that the audit trail (edit log) was not enabled for certain critical tables in one accounting software. Independent-director commission also awaits shareholder approval. The auditor flagged the impairment test for ₹1,976 crore of merger goodwill as a key audit matter, noting it depends on long-range forecasts exceeding five years.
reports.relatedParties: The company generated roughly ₹400 crore, or about 28% of its FY26 revenue, from Strides-group and Steriscience entities. The largest related-party customer was Strides Pharma Inc., which accounted for approximately ₹274 crore.
reports.contingent: Subsidiary Biolexis faces a $136.3 million (₹1,286 crore) claim from Prestige Biopharma at the Singapore International Arbitration Centre over a terminated vaccine deal. The company calls the claim frivolous and is seeking a $13.6 million refund. Additionally, capital commitments stood at ₹282 crore in March 2026, up from ₹58 crore a year earlier.
reports.other: The company reports a single contract development and manufacturing segment. High expenses include ₹122 crore in interest and roughly ₹280 crore in depreciation, which includes about ₹138 crore to amortise merger intangibles. The company targets a return on capital employed above 50% excluding goodwill, scheme intangibles, and capital work in progress. The company's own share pledge to lenders was released in September 2024.
flags: Subsidiary Biolexis faces a $136.3 million (₹1,286 crore) arbitration claim, representing about a fifth of the company's net worth.
The ₹1,976 crore merger goodwill could face an impairment write-down if product volumes are delayed.
Related parties accounted for roughly ₹400 crore, or about 28%, of the company's FY26 revenue.
The auditor found that the audit trail edit log was not enabled for certain critical tables in one accounting software.
Promoters have pledged 37.2% of their shareholding in the company.

reports.auditor: Auditor B S R & Co. LLP gave an unmodified opinion. Revenue recognition was highlighted as a key audit matter. The auditor also noted that the audit trail was not verified at the database level for some software.
reports.relatedParties: The company pays rent of ₹0.5 crore a year to Desai & Diwanji, an entity controlled by key management personnel.
reports.contingent: The company reported a contingent liability of $4.2 lakh (₹3.9 crore) related to a former employee's lawsuit in Cook County, Illinois.
