Profit after tax jumped 72.3%. Revenue per employee reached about ₹22 lakh, a significant increase from ₹8 to ₹9 lakh four years ago. The employee attrition rate was 14.85%.
flags: A former employee's lawsuit in Illinois created a contingent liability of $4.2 lakh (₹3.9 crore) and caused a temporary freeze of US bank balances.
The auditor noted that the audit trail was not verified at the database level for some company software.
Management judged certain tax notices as remote and chose not to disclose them as contingent liabilities.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave a qualified opinion on the consolidated accounts because three US subsidiaries with assets of ₹3.86 crore are consolidated using unaudited accounts. The standalone opinion is unmodified. The auditor also noted that the merged Dhanuka division's accounting software did not have an audit trail enabled throughout the year.
reports.relatedParties: The company bought goods worth about ₹245 crore from related party Otsuka Chemical (India) in FY26, down from ₹351 crore in FY25, and owed it ₹68.5 crore at year-end. Dhanuka family members and Dhanuka Agritech provided unsecured loans, with FY26 repayments including ₹24 crore to Shashwat Dhanuka, ₹17.5 crore to Mridul Dhanuka, and ₹10 crore to Dhanuka Agritech.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small, consisting of tax, electricity, and customs claims of a few crore. Pre-insolvency claims were extinguished by the 2020 resolution plan. Standalone corporate guarantees for subsidiary loans increased to ₹579.6 crore in March 2026 from ₹447.2 crore.
reports.other: The company operates a single Pharmaceuticals segment and does not disclose segment margins. FY26 product revenue was ₹1,210 crore, with India at ₹414.7 crore and the rest of the world at ₹795.8 crore (FY25: India ₹387.8 crore, rest of world ₹996.1 crore). The report confirms FY26 total revenue of ₹1,232.78 crore and profit of ₹9.96 crore. FY26 capex was ₹389.6 crore, pushing work-in-progress from ₹81 crore to ₹414 crore. Of a ₹394.5 crore QIP, ₹62 crore remained in fixed deposits. Operating cash flow was ₹126 crore (FY25: ₹51 crore), with free cash flow at −₹255 crore.
flags: The consolidated accounts received a qualified auditor opinion because three US subsidiaries were consolidated using unaudited financials.
The accounting software for the merged Dhanuka division lacked an active audit trail throughout the year.
The company relies heavily on related-party purchases, buying ₹245 crore in goods from Otsuka Chemical (India) during FY26.
Large unsecured loan repayments were made to promoter family members and related entities during the year, including ₹24 crore to Shashwat Dhanuka.
Standalone corporate guarantees provided for subsidiary loans are substantial, rising to ₹579.6 crore at the end of March 2026.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave a clean opinion. The only key audit matter noted was the accounting for dealer schemes and discounts.
reports.relatedParties: The company bought about ₹69 crore of tiles from its two Morbi associates in FY26, representing about 10% of revenue. This included ₹42.9 crore from Proton and ₹26.1 crore from Corial. It also paid ₹0.95 crore in rent to promoter-linked Freesia Investment.
reports.contingent: The company has about ₹16 crore in contingent liabilities. This mainly consists of old sales tax and GST disputes worth ₹7.8 crore, plus ₹7.1 crore in interest.
reports.other: Key management pay was around ₹8.4 crore in FY26, compared to a net profit of ₹12 crore. No single customer accounts for 10% of sales. Capital expenditure for FY26 was very low at ₹5.5 crore, falling well below the depreciation of ₹22 crore.
flags: Key management pay was high at about ₹8.4 crore in FY26 against a net profit of just ₹12 crore.
The company faces contingent liabilities of about ₹16 crore primarily due to old tax disputes and interest.
The company relies on related-party tile purchases from its associates for roughly 10% of its revenue.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unmodified opinion on the financial statements. Revenue recognition regarding the timing of delivery was noted as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party transactions were very small. The company had ₹0.13 crore in sales to Orient Paper. Additionally, the chairman's relative, Avani Birla, is employed as President of Strategy.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities totaled ₹108 crore. This includes GST anti-evasion demands of ₹29.25 crore plus an equal penalty in Maharashtra, MP, and AP, alongside a similar ₹2.87 crore demand in Vijayawada, alleging goods were bought high and sold low. The company has filed writs against these. The company also faces a Haryana Pollution Control Board demand over Faridabad discharges, having paid 50% under protest.
reports.outlook: Management cited an industry estimate that the consumer durables market will grow about 11% a year to reach ₹3 lakh crore by FY29. The report also noted that revised BEE star norms took effect on 1 January 2026, leading to the entire ceiling fan range being re-rated.
reports.other: The company operates two segments: Electrical Consumer Durables and Lighting & Switchgear. Manufacturing plants are located in Faridabad, Kolkata, Noida, and a new facility in Hyderabad. The merger of two Noida units resulted in an exceptional write-down of ₹1.51 crore. Trade payables included ₹139 crore of bank-paid acceptances and ₹26 crore in TReDS borrowings carrying interest of 6.1% to 6.25%.
flags: Contingent liabilities of ₹108 crore include significant GST anti-evasion demands and penalties alleging goods were bought at higher prices and sold lower.
The company faces a pollution control demand over plant discharges, which resulted in summons to its directors that were stayed by the High Court.
The working capital cycle is flattered by a dependence on supplier finance, with trade payables holding ₹139 crore of bank-paid acceptances.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unmodified opinion but remarked that the audit trail was not enabled at the SAP HANA database level. They also highlighted ₹44.98 crore in goodwill from a 2017 amalgamation as a key audit matter, noting that no impairment was booked.
reports.relatedParties: The parent company invested ₹130 crore in equity and lent ₹3.9 crore to its Mahad subsidiary, OASL. It also paid ₹0.23 crore in rent to Vaishnavi Chemicals, a promoter entity. Promoter remuneration was ₹4.74 crore for Dharmil Bodani and ₹3.79 crore for Shyamal Bodani. CEO Parag Satoskar and Chief R&D Officer Anita Satoskar each received ₹1.93 crore.
reports.contingent: The company reported contingent liabilities of ₹87.9 crore. This mainly consists of a ₹78.6 crore drawn bank guarantee for the Mahad subsidiary, out of an ₹80 crore total guarantee. It also includes about ₹9 crore in disputed tax items.
reports.outlook: In the management discussion, the company stated there will be no major new capital expenditure until plant utilisation and profits improve. It also noted the negative impact of an export slide and brief 50% US tariffs.
reports.other: The accounts show a single reportable segment. Domestic sales grew 29% to ₹685 crore, but exports fell 14% to ₹341 crore. The Mahad subsidiary was a major drag, reducing standalone profit of ₹25.3 crore to a consolidated profit of just ₹3.3 crore. Operating cash flow was positive at ₹2.4 crore. An Indonesian subsidiary was written off, wiping out a ₹9.34 crore investment and ₹0.69 crore receivable.
flags: Combined promoter remuneration of ₹8.5 crore exceeded the company's total consolidated profit of ₹3.3 crore.
The auditor warned that the mandatory audit trail was not enabled at the database level in the accounting software.
The new Mahad subsidiary is heavily loss-making, draining roughly ₹22 crore after tax from standalone profits.
Exports declined by 14% during the year, hurt by global challenges and brief 50% tariffs in the US.
The company carries ₹44.98 crore in goodwill that has not been impaired, which the auditor flagged as a key audit matter.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters were inventory valuation and revenue recognition. The audit trail was not enabled at the database level and missed some changes, though an ERP upgrade is under way. Notably, bank drawing-power statements had to be revised to match the company's books.
reports.relatedParties: The company bought ₹132 crore of goods in FY26 from Walso Solar Solution, up from ₹64.5 crore in FY25. Walso is an associate formed by merging two promoter-linked firms. The Chairman and Managing Director also lent money to the company and receives rent.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are very small. They include ₹3.8 crore for GST, ₹1.0 crore for labour claims, and ₹0.2 crore for civil matters.
reports.outlook: Management noted that solar module capacity is expanding from 570 MW to 2.1 GW. Pump capacity stood at 4,704 MT and saw utilization increase to 85% in FY26, up from 51% in FY25.
reports.other: The expected-credit-loss provision increased from ₹3.8 crore to ₹8.8 crore during the year. The company also highlighted its scale by ranking third in a major Maharashtra state installation drive.
flags: The accounting database audit trail was not enabled and failed to capture some changes.
Bank drawing-power statements had to be revised to match the accounting books.
Related-party purchases from a promoter-linked associate doubled to ₹132 crore.
The expected-credit-loss provision more than doubled to ₹8.8 crore.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion with generic key audit matters concerning doubtful debts, revenue, and impairment. Under CARO, the auditor noted that advance tax installments of ₹1.75 crore, ₹5.50 crore, and ₹0.50 crore were paid late. There were also a few delays in paying other statutory dues. Additionally, title deeds for some property remain in the name of the former partnership firm, Paramount Cable Corporation.
reports.relatedParties: The Indian subsidiary Valens Technologies was exited in November 2025 after it repaid an ₹8.9 crore loan. Three third-generation relatives (Dhruv, Tushar, and Parth Aggarwal) were paid ₹0.70 crore each in FY26, which is double their FY25 pay. The MD and CEO each received between ₹1.87 crore and ₹1.89 crore.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities totaled roughly ₹151 crore, up from ₹81 crore. This included bank guarantees of ₹66.7 crore and discounted bills worth ₹78.1 crore. There were also tax and duty demands of ₹6.5 crore, which included income tax claims of ₹5.29 crore.
reports.other: The company reported a single segment with no product-wise profit. Other income of ₹51 crore included ₹27.8 crore from key-man insurance policies, previously pledged for a 9.5% loan. It took a one-time labour-code charge of ₹2.4 to ₹2.5 crore. The UK subsidiary is in liquidation. Shareholders rejected a promoter warrant issue at ₹60, but later approved 72 lakh warrants at ₹42 (₹30.24 crore total, with 25% or ₹7.56 crore paid) alongside 2.20 crore non-promoter shares (₹92.39 crore). Overall, ₹99.95 crore was received, leaving ₹22.7 crore due.
flags: Shareholders rejected a promoter warrant issue at ₹60 in August 2025, but later approved one at a lower price of ₹42.
FY26 profits were heavily inflated by a ₹27.8 crore key-man insurance maturity, meaning the reported P/E overstates core earnings.
The company delayed paying advance tax installments and other statutory dues, signaling tight cash flow during the tariff shock.
Title deeds for some properties are still in the name of a former partnership firm.
Contingent liabilities are substantial at ₹151 crore, largely consisting of discounted bills and bank guarantees.

reports.auditor: The consolidated auditor's report includes an emphasis of matter. It highlights a material uncertainty regarding the going-concern status of four subsidiaries: Shreeanant Construction, West Kameng Energy, Digin Hydropower, and Meyong Hydropower.
reports.other: The annual report details non-core assets, which include land banks with about 400 acres remaining near Hyderabad. It also mentions the Smondo Gachibowli residential project, where the occupation certificate is still pending due to ongoing litigation.
flags: The auditor flagged a material uncertainty regarding the going-concern status of four subsidiaries: Shreeanant Construction, West Kameng Energy, Digin Hydropower, and Meyong Hydropower.
The Smondo Gachibowli residential project is pending an occupation certificate due to ongoing litigation.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unqualified opinion and reported no key audit matters. The company's subsidiaries were audited by a different firm, S B Ohara & Co.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid ₹4.64 crore in factory rent to MD Manoj Patil and director Aarti Patil. Salaries included ₹1.80 crore for the MD, ₹1.68 crore for Aarti Patil, and ₹0.90 crore for other relatives. Services from three relative-linked firms cost ₹4.54 crore in total. A ₹6 crore loan from the MD was repaid in FY26. In FY25, a daughter bought a company flat for ₹1.02 crore, and a related entity repaid a ₹13.7 crore loan.
reports.contingent: The company reported ₹1.47 crore in guarantees as its only contingent liability.
reports.other: In September 2025, the company acquired 60% stakes in Pentaco Automation for ₹3.00 crore and MII Robotics for ₹0.60 crore, creating ₹3.29 crore in goodwill. Standalone borrowings included a ₹19 crore overdraft against fixed deposits. The September 2025 IPO raised ₹69.6 crore, primarily for working capital to set up a new manufacturing facility. By March 2026, ₹18.47 crore of these IPO proceeds remained unspent.
flags: Related-party rent and salary payments to the promoter family exceed ₹8 crore, which is large relative to standalone profits.
The company relies on three relative-linked firms for over ₹4.5 crore in services.
A company flat was sold to a promoter's daughter for ₹1.02 crore in the previous year.
A significant portion of the IPO proceeds, ₹18.47 crore, remained unspent at year-end.

reports.auditor: The auditor's report contained no emphasis of matter.
reports.outlook: Management stated that the US pre-engineered buildings and structural platform is a key differentiator. They noted that this division is actively benefiting from US reshoring trends.
reports.other: The company has 14 plants, with 11 in India and 3 in the US. It acquired Agile Traders FZCO for West Asia distribution. FY26 investments included a new Raebareli plant in India, the Telco acquisition, and a US robotic welding line that reduced welding labour from 20–30 people to just 2 per product. Capital work in progress stood at ₹136 crore. A promoter committed ₹50.4 crore through convertible warrants, bringing in ₹20 crore so far.
flags: Title deeds for ₹115.9 crore of immovable property are pledged with banks.

reports.auditor: S.S. Kothari Mehta & Co gave an unmodified opinion. The main operating subsidiary, PG Technoplast, and other subsidiaries are audited by a different firm. The auditor noted that a database-level audit trail was missing at PG Technoplast until 30-Sep-25 and at PG Plastronics for the entire year.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small at about ₹17 crore. This includes ₹7.7 crore for central excise, ₹7.4 crore for an anti-dumping duty case at the Supreme Court, and ₹2 crore for third-party claims.
reports.other: The Board's report shows the company raised ₹1,500 crore via a QIP at ₹699 a share on 10-Dec-24. Most of the business sits in subsidiaries, which account for ₹3,956 crore in revenue and ₹4,977 crore in assets.
flags: Most of the business sits in subsidiaries that are audited by a different firm than the parent company.
A database-level audit trail was missing at subsidiary PG Technoplast until 30-Sep-25 and at PG Plastronics for the entire year.

reports.auditor: The statutory auditor for FY26 is Suresh Surana & Associates, who provided an unmodified opinion. Eleven subsidiaries, which brought in ₹5,040 crore or over half the group's revenue, were audited by other auditors. The auditor highlighted a key audit matter regarding the recoverability of ₹1,257 crore in goodwill and ₹301 crore in intangibles under development, which was noted as relevant after a recent ₹176 crore write-off.
reports.relatedParties: The company holds a 49% stake in an associate company, AbbVie Therapeutics India, which generated FY26 revenue of ₹526 crore and a 23% profit after tax margin. It also holds a 33% stake in Yapan Bio.
reports.contingent: The company has contingent liabilities of about ₹95 crore, which include ₹78 crore for GST and excise claims and ₹12 crore for a pollution-board dispute. It also has capital commitments of ₹583 crore as of March 2026, plus another ₹332 crore committed for Kenalog.
reports.other: The company experienced significant turnover in a key administrative role, with three different office-holders serving as company secretary between February and April 2026.
flags: A new statutory auditor was appointed for FY26, and 11 subsidiaries making up over half the group's revenue are audited by different firms.
The auditor raised a key audit matter about the recoverability of ₹1,257 crore in goodwill and ₹301 crore in developing intangibles.
The company had three different company secretaries between February and April 2026.
The company faces a ₹12 crore pollution-board dispute and ₹78 crore in disputed GST and excise claims.

reports.auditor: The standalone and consolidated auditor reports contain no key audit matters and no qualifications. There are no adverse remarks under CARO. The auditors confirmed there were no defaults, bank returns matched the company's books, and the audit trail operated properly.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings are modest. Key management personnel received about ₹9 crore in remuneration. The company also paid about ₹3.5 crore for rent and leases, largely to a promoter entity named Pitti Electrical Equipment.
reports.contingent: The company faces consolidated tax disputes for excise, GST, and income-tax appeals totaling just under ₹10 crore, which it has not acknowledged as debt. Additionally, there are capital commitments amounting to roughly ₹50 crore.
reports.other: The company reports a single segment for iron and steel engineering products, providing an end-market split instead. The directors' report shows consolidated net debt was ₹554.6 crore with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.74 at March 2026. The management discussion notes that on a standalone basis, the pre-merger parent had revenue of ₹1,590 crore and a net profit of ₹97.5 crore.
flags: Standalone net profit for the pre-merger parent fell 8.7% to ₹97.5 crore in FY26, showing that most of the year's growth relied on acquired subsidiaries.
The company has unresolved excise, GST, and income-tax disputes totaling up to ₹10 crore.

reports.auditor: The FY26 audit was clean and contained no emphasis of matter.
reports.contingent: At the end of March 2026, contingent liabilities included indirect-tax disputes of about ₹61 crore and letters of credit totalling ₹38.6 crore.
reports.other: PNC has diversified into water supply, irrigation, coal-mining, airports, railways, and a solar-plus-battery project. It has executed about 100 major projects across 16 states. The company sold 12 road assets to Vertis Infrastructure Trust at an enterprise value of ₹9,005.7 crore and an implied equity value of ₹2,902 crore. FY26 figures included ₹515.75 crore received under NHAI settlement agreements and a ₹56.39 crore early-completion bonus for the MSRDC package. Management includes CMD Pradeep Kumar Jain, MDs Chakresh and Yogesh Jain, and Director T.R. Rao.
flags: FY26 earnings quality was weak, as profits leaned heavily on ₹435.19 crore of one-off arbitration claims and early-completion bonuses.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion with no emphasis of matter or key audit matters. However, the CARO report noted that quarterly stock returns submitted to SBI did not agree with the company's books for some quarters, such as a mismatch in first-quarter inventory.
reports.relatedParties: The company made related-party purchases of roughly ₹37 crore, which is about 12% of revenue. This included raw materials from G K Founders (~₹18.5 crore) and G K Alloys (~₹6.4 crore). It also paid Jayshree Pistons for labour (~₹6.6 crore) and materials (~₹3.9 crore), and Dakshendra & Associates for professional fees (~₹1.4 crore). Shareholders were asked to approve further material transactions with Jayshree Pistons and G K Founders.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were very small, consisting only of performance guarantees worth ₹0.77 crore. However, the company had significant capital commitments of ₹82.05 crore at the end of March 2026.
reports.outlook: Management plans to expand operations primarily through its new Unit III plant, noting multiple casting processes under one roof. The Chairman's message also proposed a new Unit IV facility dedicated to magnesium components. The management discussion highlights their in-house design capabilities and notes that power accounts for about 7 to 8% of total expenses.
reports.other: Revenue was heavily domestic at ₹291.37 crore (99.16%), with exports at ₹2.48 crore and material imports at ₹35.8 crore. By segment, automobiles made up 72.58% of revenue, electric vehicle applications 9.81%, and non-automobile 17.61%. Commercial vehicles were the largest single category at 50.88%. The company had capital work-in-progress of ₹28.40 crore. It also noted delayed payments to MSME suppliers during FY26, though interest liability was judged insignificant.
flags: The published management discussion carelessly left in a drafting instruction about aligning segment disclosures.
The Directors' report claims the company fully utilized its net IPO proceeds within weeks of listing, which is not supported by the rest of the report.
Quarterly stock statements submitted to the bank did not match the company's books for some quarters.
The company relies on related-party entities for about 12% of its revenue in raw materials, labour, and professional fees.
The company delayed its payments to MSME suppliers during the financial year.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unqualified opinion. The only key audit matter reported was revenue recognition. There were no fraud or whistle-blower complaints, and the audit trail is working.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings are small and include sales to Platino, rent, and director pay. None of these transactions amount to more than 1% of revenue. The notes also record that founder Naresh Oberoi stepped down as CMD in December 2025, handing the role to his son Bharat Oberoi, and the CFO changed in July 2025.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include roughly ₹45–50 crore in disputed sales-tax, service-tax, GST, customs, and income-tax demands. The largest single disputed item is about ₹33 crore. There are also ₹68 crore in letters of credit. Capital commitments jumped to ₹934 crore from ₹157 crore at the end of the previous year.
reports.outlook: Management budgets ₹380 crore for a 52.7 MW wind project and ₹750 crore for a 100 MW GUVNL wind project. These projects will be funded 70–75% by bank debt and the rest from internal cash. This heavy capital expenditure will turn the company's net cash position back into net debt.
reports.other: The reported FY26 net profit was flattered by a ₹51 crore deferred-tax credit. This resulted from the company moving to a lower tax regime.
flags: Capital commitments jumped massively to ₹934 crore by March 2026, up from ₹157 crore.
The ₹1,130 crore wind build-out will rely 70–75% on bank debt, turning the company's net cash back into net debt.
The company faces roughly ₹45–50 crore in disputed tax demands, including a single unresolved item of about ₹33 crore.
The reported net profit for the year was artificially boosted by a ₹51 crore deferred-tax credit.

reports.auditor: The auditor, MSKA & Associates LLP, gave an unmodified opinion. They noted key audit matters regarding revenue recognition and the impairment of trade receivables. The auditor also flagged an impairment risk concerning a ₹291 crore loan given by the parent company to its subsidiary, Praj GenX, which has accumulated losses of ₹183 crore.
reports.relatedParties: The parent company has lent ₹291 crore to its subsidiary, Praj GenX. The company also provided intra-group corporate guarantees.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small. They include a demand for income-tax interest and GST on intra-group corporate guarantees.
reports.other: The annual report showed a ₹23.8 crore exceptional charge related to a labour code. Additionally, a fire at the R&D centre on 28 March 2025 required ₹12.75 crore in replacement capital expenditure. The company filed a ₹12.5 crore insurance claim for the fire and received a ₹6.5 crore advance.
flags: The auditor highlighted an impairment risk regarding the ₹291 crore parent loan to subsidiary Praj GenX, which has ₹183 crore in accumulated losses.
The company recorded a ₹23.8 crore exceptional charge related to a labour code.
A fire at the R&D centre required the company to spend ₹12.75 crore on replacement capital expenditure.

reports.auditor: The auditor, MSKA & Associates, issued key audit matters regarding overseas investments and loans. They flagged standalone investments in subsidiaries of ₹162.7 crore, of which ₹103 crore has already been provided for impairment. They also highlighted loans to subsidiaries of ₹92.6 crore, which carry an impairment provision of ₹27.5 crore.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings were small. The company made purchases from promoter-linked Cams Technology for about ₹0.7 crore and Core Power for about ₹1.4 crore. It also donated ₹0.35 crore to a promoter trust. Pay for key management personnel was ₹9.5 crore.
reports.contingent: The company faces an income-tax demand of ₹17.0 crore related to an ESOP disallowance, of which ₹3.4 crore was paid under protest. There are smaller claims for GST (₹2.0 crore), stamp duty, provident fund, and excise. Capital commitments stood at ₹50.1 crore, and a corporate guarantee for MEMCO was ₹3.2 crore.
reports.other: The company operates one reportable segment. Geographically, India revenue was ₹438 crore, while outside India fell to ₹335 crore (Europe ₹172 crore, Asia ₹42 crore). Two customers each accounted for over 10% of group revenue. Consolidated profit included a ₹10.6 crore exceptional gain and other income largely from mutual funds valued around ₹357 crore. German subsidiary MFT filed for insolvency and was deconsolidated.
flags: The auditor raised key audit matters over massive capital destruction overseas, noting a ₹103 crore impairment on subsidiary investments and a ₹27.5 crore provision on subsidiary loans.
The German subsidiary MFT filed for insolvency, forcing a ₹48.9 crore impairment hit to standalone profit.
Reported profits are of poor quality as they rely heavily on a ₹10.6 crore exceptional gain and mutual-fund treasury income rather than core operations.
The company has a disputed income-tax demand of ₹17.0 crore regarding an ESOP disallowance.
The annual report entirely fails to disclose an ongoing investigation by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

reports.auditor: Majeti & Co. gave a qualified opinion on internal financial controls due to a material weakness. Significant procurement decisions and approvals were concentrated with a single individual, causing inadequate segregation of duties and risk of management override. The report also included an emphasis of matter regarding a ₹6.1 crore insurance claim for an accident, recognized as a receivable but not yet settled.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small, consisting of disputed sales tax of ₹5.8 crore, GST of ₹1.0 crore, and income tax of ₹0.6 crore. Letters of credit and guarantees issued by banks totaled ₹76 crore.
reports.other: The management discussion showed FY26 revenue was 81% Defence & Space (₹315.4 crore) and 19% Commercial explosives (₹72.9 crore). Revenue from exports fell to ₹51.7 crore. FY26 profits were heavily supported by ₹42.1 crore of other income, which included a ₹34.2 crore one-off supplier discount settlement and a ₹5 crore contract-loss provision reversal. The company booked a ₹5.2 crore exceptional item for ex-gratia payments relating to an accident. Revenue was reported net of ₹24.8 crore in variable consideration deductions.
flags: The auditor issued a qualified opinion on internal controls, citing a material weakness and risk of management override in procurement.
A fire and explosion at the Katepally plant in April 2025 killed four people and led to a temporary closure order.
Reported profit growth relied heavily on a one-off ₹34.2 crore purchase discount settlement with a supplier for prior-year materials.
A single unnamed customer accounted for over 10% of total revenue in both FY25 and FY26.
Reported revenue was reduced by ₹24.8 crore in variable consideration, reflecting liquidated damages, deductions, and rebates.

reports.auditor: The new auditor provided an unmodified opinion for FY26. Key audit matters included revenue recognition, specifically cut-off, rebates, and price revisions, as well as disputed taxes and litigation. The previous statutory auditor, VKS Aiyer & Co, resigned in July 2025 and was replaced by Sundaram & Srinivasan.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid roughly ₹36 crore in FY26 to promoter-linked entities for services and reimbursements, down from ₹54 crore in FY25. Managing Director Vikram Mohan received ₹8.07 crore, which is 107 times the median employee salary. Chairperson Vanitha Mohan was paid 59 times the median before she stepped back.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include ₹8.6 crore for taxes and ₹35.0 crore for labour cases, which dropped from ₹48.9 crore the previous year. Letters of credit, guarantees, and EPCG commitments amount to ₹43.9 crore.
reports.other: The company operates 16 plants, including one in Indonesia, and employs over 470 engineers. It spends about 4.5% of its revenue on R&D. Additionally, inventories worth ₹425.9 crore have been pledged to lenders.
flags: The statutory auditor resigned in July 2025, and the specific reasons were not reproduced in the annual report.
Managing Director Vikram Mohan's compensation is 107 times the median employee salary, and the Chairperson's pay is 59 times the median.
Inventories totaling ₹425.9 crore are pledged to lenders.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unqualified opinion. The report included a key audit matter regarding the timing of revenue recognition across different shipment terms.
reports.relatedParties: Privi Fine Sciences, owned by the promoter family, is being merged into the company at a ratio of 1 Privi share for every 135 Privi Fine Sciences shares. The company bought ₹27.7 crore and sold ₹15.5 crore with Prasad Organics, an enterprise related to key management. It paid ₹3.3 crore in rent to promoter entities Moneymart Securities and MM Infra, and ₹1 crore for job work to Privi Fine Sciences.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were small. They included disputed income tax claims of ₹18 crore and GST or customs claims of ₹15 crore.
reports.outlook: The annual report's risk table highlighted exposure to raw material and foreign exchange volatility. It noted that over 55% of raw materials are imported and 15% to 18% of inputs are linked to crude oil.
reports.other: Sales routed through the company's US subsidiary increased to ₹409 crore in FY26, up from ₹330 crore in FY25. Additionally, the Board's report noted that CRISIL revised the company's credit rating upward from A+/Positive during the year.
flags: A related-party merger is underway to absorb Privi Fine Sciences, a company owned by the promoter family.
The company relies heavily on imports, with over 55% of raw materials coming from overseas.
Between 15% and 18% of input materials are linked to crude oil, exposing the business to commodity price swings.

reports.auditor: The auditor's report was unqualified. The key audit matter noted was revenue recognition, due to a fraud-risk presumption.
reports.contingent: The company reported contingent liabilities of ₹38.9 crore related to income-tax matters and about ₹2 crore for other claims.
reports.other: The company runs India's digital public infrastructure, including PAN issuance, pension recordkeeping, and identity services. It is widely held with no promoter, and domestic institutional investors own 21%. The company reported having 839 permanent employees in March 2026. A small subsidiary for the Account Aggregator business reported a loss of ₹1.4 crore.
flags: The auditor highlighted revenue recognition as a key audit matter due to a fraud-risk presumption.
The company experienced leadership churn during the year, including the resignation of its MD and CEO.
The company faces contingent liabilities of ₹38.9 crore related to income-tax disputes.
The Account Aggregator subsidiary is loss-making, with a reported loss of ₹1.4 crore.

reports.auditor: The FY26 audit was clean, with no emphasis of matter.
reports.contingent: At the end of March 2026, contingent liabilities included bank guarantees of ₹735.4 crore, which were down from ₹896.4 crore. The company also had tax disputes amounting to ₹16.1 crore.
reports.other: PSP is an Ahmedabad-based building-construction EPC contractor with its own precast plant. It builds industrial, institutional, government, residential, religious, and heritage buildings. Its execution record includes the Kashi Vishwanath corridor, Surat Diamond Bourse, and Vishwa Umiya Dham, which featured a record 24,000 cubic meter continuous pour. Adani Infra (India) Ltd became a co-promoter with joint control alongside founder Prahaladbhai Patel after acquiring a 34.41% stake in 2025.
flags: Governance now involves joint control between the founder family and Adani Infra (India) Ltd.
Institutional investors have largely exited the company.

reports.auditor: The auditor included an emphasis of matter regarding ongoing legal proceedings that could adversely affect the group. These involve ₹61.4 crore in deposits on disputed land, a ₹35 crore claim from minority shareholders, ₹82.7 crore of inventory under government acquisition, ₹58.2 crore of customer receivables, and ₹17.6 crore of other balances under litigation.
reports.relatedParties: Transactions are mainly with subsidiaries and primarily involve guarantees and security pledges. There were no material related-party transactions flagged outside the group.
reports.contingent: The company faces assessment orders with a potential tax impact of ₹45.1 crore following an October 2023 income tax search. Additionally, it received a Benami Property Act show-cause notice questioning its beneficial ownership of 43.5 acres of land, which has a carrying value of ₹13.2 crore.
flags: The auditor warned that ongoing legal proceedings may have an adverse effect on the functioning of the group.
The company has ₹61.4 crore tied up in deposits and advances on land plots with title disputes.
The company faces a ₹35 crore claim from minority shareholders of a subsidiary.
An income tax search resulted in assessment orders with a potential tax impact of ₹45.1 crore.
The company received a show-cause notice under the Benami Property Act regarding 43.5 acres of land.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion and no adverse CARO remarks were found in the parts read. Key audit matters included revenue recognition, recoverability of trade receivables, capital expenditure capitalisation, and inventory valuation. The report noted inventory stood at ₹107 crore at March 2026.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings were small. The company paid ₹2.25 crore in director pay and ₹0.18 crore in rent to a promoter company. Company loans carry a personal guarantee from Managing Director Bijay Kumar Agarwal and guarantees from promoter entities Anmol Monower Plastics, Yash Synthetics, and Credence Financial.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were small, consisting of ₹2.1 crore in bank guarantees, and there were no tax disputes. Capital commitments were only ₹3.7 crore at March 2026.
reports.other: The annual report called its ₹90 crore FY26 capex the largest single-year capex in company history. Operational highlights noted the sale of 3.36 lakh intermediate bulk containers in FY26. The report also cited cost advantages from backward integration, including in-house caps, closures, handles, captive solar power, and recycling.
flags: Operating cash flow turned negative at −₹41 crore in FY26, and free cash flow was negative −₹118 crore.
Borrowings more than tripled from ₹55 crore to ₹184 crore by the end of March 2026.
Working capital is stretched, with the cash cycle lengthening to 124 days in FY26 as inventory and debtor days increased.
Capacity utilisation has fallen steadily over the last three years, dropping to 68.7% in FY26 despite capacity additions.

reports.auditor: The group auditor, Kishor Gujar & Associates, relied on other auditors for three subsidiaries, including Endoks. These other auditors covered ₹749.6 crore of revenue and ₹799.8 crore of assets, representing about three-quarters of group revenue. The auditor also reported a modification on the audit trail for the holding company and one subsidiary, noting that the accounting software's edit log works at the application level only.
reports.relatedParties: The company made purchases of ₹19.9 crore from its 50:50 joint venture, Sukrut Electric. Rent was paid to promoter family members, and machinery rent of ₹19 crore was paid within the group. Additionally, an extraordinary general meeting approved pay of up to ₹5 crore a year for 25 years for a promoter relative holding an office of profit, with actual pay recorded at ₹86.4 lakh.
reports.contingent: The contingent liability note reveals bank and corporate guarantees of about ₹421 crore, a significant increase from ₹118 crore a year earlier. There is also an additional ₹51 crore listed.
reports.other: Minority shareholders take a large share of the profits. Non-controlling interests received ₹64.2 crore, which is 34.6% of the FY26 consolidated profit of ₹185.5 crore, with Endoks alone producing 51% of consolidated profit. The company holds a 50:50 joint venture, Sukrut Electric, and a wholly-owned subsidiary, S&S Transformers. Additionally, promoters waived their dividend and salary increments ahead of the fundraise.
flags: A large portion of profit leaks to outside owners, as 34.6% of FY26 consolidated profit belongs to minority shareholders.
The group auditor relied on other auditors for three subsidiaries that account for about three-quarters of group revenue and ₹799.8 crore of assets.
The auditor issued a modification regarding the audit trail edit log for the holding company and one subsidiary, as it works only at the application level.
Contingent liabilities show bank and corporate guarantees surged to about ₹421 crore from ₹118 crore the previous year.
The company approved a pay package of up to ₹5 crore a year for 25 years for a promoter relative holding an office of profit.

reports.auditor: The auditor highlighted the Novigo business combination and the impairment testing for Velotio's ₹266 crore goodwill as key audit matters.
reports.contingent: The company reported capital commitments of ₹1 crore.
reports.other: In CY25, the Americas accounted for 72.7% of revenue. The Tech, Internet, Platforms & Services vertical contributed about 39%, down from 42% in CY24. Other segments included Healthcare, Telecom, Media, Manufacturing, and BFSI. The business responsibility report revealed that voluntary attrition rose to 20.5% in CY25, up from 15.6% in CY24 and 13.7% in CY23.
flags: Voluntary attrition reached 20.5% in CY25 according to the annual report, which contradicts the 11% figure claimed by the CEO on an earnings call.
The company acquired Novigo for ₹400 crore, but Novigo's pitched revenue of about $32 million was later restated down to $21–22 million.
The auditor flagged Velotio's ₹266 crore goodwill impairment testing and the Novigo business combination as key audit matters.

reports.auditor: The auditor's report was unqualified. The only key audit matter highlighted was revenue cut-off.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party transactions were small. The Chairman and Managing Director received ₹2.72 crore in remuneration, and his wife received a retainership. His son, acting as Chief Operating Officer, received ₹0.58 crore. Additionally, the company paid ₹0.87 crore to a CSR trust and ₹0.12 crore to a pickleball company.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were negligible. The company reported ₹0.03 crore in disputed tax, some small bank guarantees, and a €1.1 million standby letter of credit for its Austrian subsidiary.
reports.other: The Management Discussion and Analysis noted standalone FY26 export sales of ₹336 crore (up 15.5%) and domestic sales growth of 18.5%. The reported standalone EBITDA of ₹126 crore and consolidated revenue of ₹512 crore both included other income. The annual report also recorded a ₹80 crore preferential issue used to prepay debt (dropping the promoter stake from 53.3% to 42.7%) and note 41 showed March 2026 borrowings at ₹236 crore with a 0.63x debt-to-equity ratio.
flags: About a third of the FY26 pre-tax profit of ₹66 crore relied on ₹21.7 crore of foreign-exchange gains, which flattered the company's earnings quality.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unqualified opinion, and the CAG had nil comments on the accounts. CARO showed only small disputed GST dues. Expected credit losses and contingent liabilities were named key audit matters. An 'Other Matter' remark flagged that having only one independent director violates the Companies Act.
reports.relatedParties: The company claims a government-related-entity exemption and transacts with Indian Railways and railway PSUs at market terms. Indian Railways accounted for ₹693cr of FY26 revenue. Year-end receivables from Indian Railways stood at ₹615cr. The report noted nothing unusual.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities reached ₹447cr, mostly from arbitration and court cases worth ₹406cr. Bank guarantees given by the company doubled to ₹1,482cr due to new project wins. Capital commitments stood at ₹345cr at the end of March 2026.
reports.outlook: Management plans a capital expenditure of approximately ₹241cr for the year ahead. This money will go toward the network, data centres, and technology upgrades. The company plans to fund these investments purely through internal accruals, with no borrowings beyond leases.
reports.other: The telecom segment generated ₹1,500.7cr in revenue with a 26.7% result margin, while the projects segment earned ₹2,776.8cr at a thin 3.9% margin. An expected credit loss charge of ₹24.4cr was booked as an exceptional item. The company declared a dividend of ₹3.25 a share.
flags: The auditor flagged non-compliance with the Companies Act due to a lack of independent directors on the board.
Trade receivables grew faster than revenue to ₹2,196cr, with ₹238cr remaining unpaid for over three years.
Unpaid dues from Indian Railways jumped 46% to ₹615cr.
Contingent liabilities are substantial at ₹447cr, mostly tied up in arbitration and court cases.
Outstanding bank guarantees doubled during the year to ₹1,482cr.

reports.auditor: The auditor's report was unmodified. The only key audit matter mentioned was revenue recognition.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid consultancy fees of ₹1.66 crore to LFC Consulting Practice LLP and rent of ₹1.49 crore to the chairman's father. It also spent ₹1.31 crore on CSR through the Rajratan Foundation. Promoter Sunil Chordia lent and was repaid ₹27 crore during the year.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are negligible. They consist of a ₹2.26 crore electricity bill dispute in the MP High Court, which is mostly reimbursable, and a ₹0.6 crore tax dispute.
reports.other: Geographic revenue included ₹636 crore from India, ₹287 crore from Thailand, ₹116 crore from the USA, and ₹117 crore from the rest of the world. Exports grew to 17% of revenue. The Chennai plant is located 45–50 km from a port and within 30 minutes to 12 hours of most southern tyre plants. Product acceptance stood at 99.82%.
flags: Three customers each account for over 10% of revenue, heavily concentrating sales as they together make up ₹390 crore or 34% of total revenue.

reports.auditor: Joint auditors S.R. Batliboi & Co. LLP and S.K. Naredi & Co. LLP gave an unmodified opinion on the standalone results. They included a key audit matter regarding the timing of revenue recognition and the recoverability of ₹867 crore in trade receivables. They also remarked that the audit-trail feature was not enabled for some software.
reports.contingent: The company has a shortfall undertaking of ₹524.8 crore for its rail-wheel joint venture against joint venture loans of ₹1,029 crore. It gave corporate guarantees of ₹642.5 crore for subsidiaries, including ₹417 crore for Casting Solutions, ₹178 crore for Mexico, and ₹47 crore for the US. It also gave a ₹37.5 crore bank guarantee for the joint venture. Other contingent liabilities include ₹6.7 crore for excise and service tax, and ₹0.8 crore for GST. Capital commitments stood at ₹183.7 crore.
reports.outlook: The management discussion targets a double-digit share of revenue from the railways segment in FY27. It notes that a contracted 80,000-wheel Railways order will be executed through the joint venture. Management also highlights risks from exposure to the US Class 8 cycle and tariffs.
reports.other: The Corporate Governance section confirmed an inventory overstatement of ₹220.5 crore at March 2025 and ₹50.2 crore at March 2024, leading to restated figures. The Directors' Report noted promoter warrants of ₹204.75 crore to Riddhi Portfolio and ₹199.9 crore to Chaitanya Jalan. The Secretarial Audit flagged a board-meeting gap of over 120 days resulting in a ₹10,000 fine, and a promoter-group entity seeking reclassification as public.
flags: An external study confirmed inventory overstatements of ₹220.5 crore for FY25 and ₹50.2 crore for FY24 due to erroneous accounting entries, requiring restatements.
The company carries large off-balance-sheet risks, including ₹642.5 crore in corporate guarantees for subsidiaries and a ₹524.8 crore shortfall undertaking for a joint venture.
The auditor noted that the mandatory audit-trail feature was not enabled for some accounting software.
The company was fined ₹10,000 by exchanges for a governance lapse where the gap between board meetings exceeded 120 days.
Management noted that margins and pricing power were negatively impacted by US Class 8 demand weakness and a 26% reciprocal tariff.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion but highlighted two key audit matters. The first is the impairment of the Light Metal Castings unit, which has a carrying value of ₹250.1 crore and nil headroom after a ₹4.1 crore goodwill impairment. The second is the recoverability of ₹62.8 crore in deferred tax assets on past losses.
reports.relatedParties: In FY26, the company paid its parent, Rane Holdings, about ₹20.8 crore for professional charges, ₹13.6 crore for information systems, ₹1.5 crore for trademark fees, and ₹19 crore for reimbursements. It also recorded purchases and professional charges with Rane Steering Systems and the ZF joint ventures.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities stood at ₹87.6 crore. This includes ₹30.1 crore for income tax, ₹55.9 crore for GST, excise, and sales tax, and ₹1.7 crore for labour claims. The company also had capital commitments of ₹74.6 crore at the end of March 2026, up from ₹31.5 crore a year earlier.
reports.other: The Board's report stated the company does not have any associate or joint venture. Standalone net profit for FY26 was ₹111.4 crore, with earnings per share of ₹40.32 and a dividend of ₹16 per share. The company sold 3.48 acres of Velachery land for ₹361.18 crore, receiving ₹145 crore by March 2026.
flags: The auditor warned that the Light Metal Castings unit has zero headroom left, meaning any adverse changes will cause further impairment on its ₹250.1 crore carrying value.
The auditor flagged the recoverability risk of ₹62.8 crore in deferred tax assets tied to past losses.
The company faces ₹87.6 crore in contingent liabilities, which primarily consist of disputed taxes.

reports.auditor: Deloitte Haskins & Sells gave an unmodified opinion. The auditor flagged business-combination accounting and goodwill impairment as key audit matters due to the Sojern acquisition.
reports.relatedParties: The standalone company provided a ₹1,291 crore financial guarantee for a subsidiary's acquisition loan.
reports.contingent: The company has an indirect-tax demand of ₹62 crore, which remains unchanged from FY25. There is also a ₹1,291 crore intra-group financial guarantee for a subsidiary loan.
reports.outlook: The business is asset-light, so capex consists mostly of capitalised software, with the exception of the large $250 million Sojern acquisition. The report notes foreign exchange risks, warning that a stronger rupee would reduce revenue since most of it is earned in dollars.
reports.other: The company reports its business as a single segment. The Sojern deal was accounted at a consideration of ₹2,222.7 crore, creating a group goodwill of ₹1,581 crore. FY26 absorbed real charges of ₹9.3 crore for team earn-outs and ₹11.6 crore for stock appreciation rights. No promoter pledges were recorded.
flags: Adjusted profit figures exclude real costs like employee earn-outs and stock appreciation rights.
Goodwill of ₹1,581 crore makes up roughly 75% of the company's net worth.
The auditor highlighted goodwill impairment and business-combination accounting as key audit matters.
The company has a contingent liability for an indirect-tax demand of ₹62 crore.
A stronger rupee poses a revenue risk because most earnings are in dollars, while debt is held as a dollar SOFR loan.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion with an emphasis of matter regarding the realty-demerger accounting. The fair value of ₹1,695 crore in investments was flagged as a key audit matter. The auditor noted that the accounting software audit trail was not operated throughout the year for the holding company, five subsidiaries, one associate, and one joint venture. There were also adverse CARO remarks regarding property and asset records at JKMPTL, JKMGAL, and Everblue Apparel.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities total about ₹95 crore, mostly stemming from legacy divested cement, steel, and denim divisions. This includes ₹29.6 crore for stamp duty (50% of which is reimbursable), ₹19 crore for GST, and ₹16 crore for sales tax. There is also a pending tenancy-rights claim in Thane.
reports.other: The governance report highlighted management churn, specifically a change in the Group CFO in December 2025 from Amit Agarwal to Rakesh Tiwary. It also noted a history of promoter-family litigation.
flags: The auditor noted the software audit trail was not operated throughout the year for the parent company and several subsidiaries.
Adverse CARO remarks were issued regarding property and asset records at JKMPTL, JKMGAL, and Everblue Apparel.
The company faces about ₹95 crore in contingent liabilities, including disputed legacy taxes and a tenancy-rights claim.
The governance report highlighted recent management churn with a Group CFO change, alongside a history of promoter-family litigation.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The report includes an emphasis of matter regarding demerger accounting. The key audit matter highlighted is the percentage-of-completion method used for revenue recognition.
reports.relatedParties: The company reported no material related-party transactions. Because of this, no AOC-2 filing was required.
reports.contingent: The company faces a disputed GST liability of about ₹19.8 crore. There is also an unquantified tenancy-rights claim over a portion of its Thane land, although revenue courts have ruled in the company's favor.
reports.other: The company recognizes revenue using the percentage-of-completion method as construction progresses. This accounting approach smooths out the reported revenue.
flags: Operating cash flow was deeply negative at -₹910 crore in FY26, and management expects the company to remain cash-negative for the next two years.
An income-tax survey was conducted at the company's offices in September 2025.
The company has a ₹19.8 crore GST contingent liability and an unquantified tenancy-rights dispute over its Thane land.
The company missed its FY26 land addition target, delivering about ₹3,000 crore of new project value against a guidance of ₹5,000 to ₹10,000 crore.
Institutional ownership dropped sharply from about 22% at listing to roughly 8.8%.

reports.auditor: The auditor, A B C D & Co. LLP, issued an unmodified opinion. It included an emphasis of matter regarding the discontinued segments and the ongoing demerger. Key audit matters highlighted contingent liabilities and the massive contract assets, specifically ₹696 crore in unbilled ash revenue where the billing unit differs from daily progress reports. The audit trail operated normally.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include ₹509 crore in corporate guarantees for subsidiaries as of March 2026 (a steep rise from ₹46 crore the prior year), primarily for wind business letters of credit, alongside ₹37.5 crore in other corporate guarantees. The Directors' report also notes a pending final order from a December 2025 Income Tax search, and a stayed SEBI penalty of ₹10 lakh against the CMD.
reports.other: The report details the discontinuation of the refrigerant gas and power trading businesses, and the demerger of the green mobility EV unit. FY26 revenue segments included ₹2,012.7 crore from ash and coal handling, ₹237.5 crore from wind, ₹10.4 crore from services, and ₹0.8 crore from solar. NTPC (28%) and IL&FS Tamil Nadu Power (12%) were major customers. Additionally, ₹45 crore of unused preferential-issue money was parked as an inter-corporate deposit at 11%, and a ₹1 per share dividend was noted.
flags: The auditor raised a key audit matter over ₹696 crore of unbilled ash revenue, noting the billing unit of measure differs from the company's daily progress reports.
Corporate guarantees provided for subsidiaries surged to ₹509 crore to support the new wind business, up from just ₹46 crore a year earlier.
An Income Tax search was conducted at company premises and executives' homes in December 2025, and the final order remains unresolved.
Unused funds of ₹45 crore from a preferential issue have been parked as an inter-corporate deposit with an outside NBFC.
There is high customer concentration, with just two clients (NTPC and IL&FS Tamil Nadu Power) accounting for 40% of the company's revenue.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unqualified opinion. They highlighted revenue rebates, discounts, and litigation provisions as key audit matters.
reports.relatedParties: Several promoter family members work as paid executives. The company paid lease rent of about ₹7.6 crore to promoter parties. The annual report also lists a property purchase of ₹17.5 crore in FY26, though the counterparty's name is not clearly legible. There were no material related-party transactions as defined by rules.
reports.contingent: The company reported contingent liabilities of ₹124.9 crore. This consists mostly of disputed taxes: ₹55.9 crore for GST and sales tax, ₹58.2 crore for income tax, and ₹18.7 crore for Haryana entry-tax interest. Capital commitments stood at ₹34.5 crore, and an unspent CSR obligation of ₹72.6 crore was shown under commitments.
reports.outlook: Management plans capital spending of ₹180 to ₹200 crore for FY27. The report notes that the unorganised sector makes up about 65% of the Indian market. The company also faces an inverted GST duty structure, with a 5% tax on output but 18% on some inputs, which blocks tax credits on services and capital goods.
reports.other: The company operates as a single business segment. It has a manufacturing plant in Bahadurgarh, Haryana. During FY26, it spent ₹139.4 crore on capital expenditures, which was internally funded. The board declared a dividend of ₹3.50 per share for FY26, representing a payout of about 49%.
flags: The related-party table shows a ₹17.5 crore property purchase where the counterparty is not clearly legible.
The company faces large contingent liabilities of ₹124.9 crore, mostly for disputed income and sales taxes.
An inverted GST duty structure is blocking tax credits on services and capital goods.

reports.auditor: The auditor, Kanu Doshi Associates LLP, named the valuation of goodwill in a subsidiary as a key audit matter.
reports.contingent: The consolidated notes show contingent liabilities of ₹7.8 crore, compared to ₹7.2 crore previously.
reports.other: The report's AOC-1 section notes Remsons Edge Tech, which handles rail brake parts and defence sub-assemblies at a new 30,000 sq ft Chakan plant.
flags: The valuation of goodwill in a subsidiary was flagged as a key audit matter by the auditor.
The company carries ₹7.8 crore in contingent liabilities.
The annual report text is not machine-readable due to custom font encoding, preventing the verification of related-party amounts.

reports.auditor: PwC resigned as the statutory auditor mid-year, effective 14 August 2026, to align with a group-wide change. BSR & Co. was appointed to fill the vacancy. The board stated no other concerns were raised. The auditor's report noted that ₹324 crore of goodwill remaining on the books is a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid a royalty of ₹35 crore to its parent in FY26, up from ₹32 crore in FY25. It also buys about ₹390 to ₹400 crore of materials a year from group companies. These transactions are approved and in the ordinary course of business, but act as a structural drain on margins.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were small at ₹29 crore as of March 2026, down from ₹36 crore a year earlier. These mostly consist of customs and tax claims. Open capital commitments fell to ₹23 crore from ₹77 crore over the same period.
reports.outlook: The management discussion notes that many long-term contracts lack adequate price escalation provisions. The industry faces overcapacity, with utilisation often at 60% to 70%, while competitors add capacity and try to fill plants at any cost. The company spent about ₹135 crore on capex in FY26 for robotics, a new hydraulic press, a tunnel kiln, and inspection systems.
reports.other: The company serves over 850 customers from 8 plants and 2 mines, with an installed capacity of 512 kilotonnes. The industrial division made up about 13% of FY26 revenue. The report shows a ₹556 crore impairment on the Dalmia investment. Parmod Sagar resigned as managing director for personal reasons effective 1 July 2026, replaced by Pankaj Malhan. CFO Azim Syed also stepped down as a whole-time director.
flags: The company took a massive ₹556 crore impairment charge on its Dalmia investment in FY26 due to structural issues like import competition and falling exports.
There is ₹324 crore of goodwill remaining on the balance sheet, which was flagged as a key audit matter.
PwC resigned as the statutory auditor mid-year, though management cited a group-wide auditor change as the reason.
The managing director resigned for personal reasons, and the CFO stepped down as a whole-time director.
Many long-term contracts lack price escalation clauses, and industry overcapacity is leading competitors to price aggressively.

reports.auditor: The auditor noted revenue recognition as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: Promoter-group firm ASN Manufacturing & Services provides raw materials, job work, services, and rent. Transactions with enterprises controlled by key management personnel totaled about ₹38 crore in FY26, up from ₹26 crore. The company also holds a loan balance of roughly ₹10 crore from them. Total managerial remuneration was ₹15.3 crore, compared to a net profit of ₹52 crore.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities totaled ₹15.4 crore at the end of March 2026. This mostly consisted of ₹12.4 crore in income tax claims. The company also had outstanding capital commitments of ₹27.3 crore.
reports.other: Borrowings included ₹147 crore from sales-bill discounting and ₹147 crore from TReDS purchase-bill discounting. The borrowings note also showed interest-free short-term loans from directors. A roughly two-acre Haridwar land plot valued at about ₹10 crore is held for sale, with payment due by December 30, 2026. The company changed its CFO to Naveen Sorot in November 2025.
flags: Managerial pay of ₹15.3 crore is high compared to the net profit of ₹52 crore.
Transactions with enterprises controlled by key management reached ₹38 crore, and the company holds a ₹10 crore loan balance with them.
Two independent directors share the promoter family's surname, but the annual report does not clarify if there is a relationship.
The company relies heavily on bill discounting, totaling ₹294 crore across its sales and purchases.
The company changed its Chief Financial Officer in November 2025.

reports.auditor: Kirtane & Pandit LLP gave an unmodified standalone opinion with no key audit matters. The consolidated report included an emphasis of matter regarding the disposal of a subsidiary. Under CARO, the auditor noted minor discrepancies between bank statements and books related to forex and late entries.
reports.relatedParties: The company bought ₹41.95 crore of silicon-carbide fabrication know-how from Sicamore Semiconductor Inc. USA, an entity linked to a director. It sold its 100% subsidiary Visicon Power Electronics to Silicon Power Corporation for ₹2.16 crore, but bought ₹27.5 crore of plant and machinery from Visicon.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities consist of only ₹0.40 crore in bank guarantees.
reports.other: The company has one reportable segment for power electronics. It received a ₹47.84 crore subsidy from Odisha, booked as deferred income. Capital work-in-progress was ₹46.9 crore, and intangible assets under development were ₹51.1 crore. A final dividend of ₹0.10 per share was declared. Promoter holding fell to 58.61%. A new MD and CEO joined in February 2026.
flags: The company purchased ₹41.95 crore of process know-how from an entity linked to a director.
The company sold its completely owned subsidiary to the chairman's original company for ₹2.16 crore.
The auditor added an emphasis of matter to the consolidated report concerning the subsidiary sale.
The auditor noted minor discrepancies between bank statements and company books.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave unmodified opinions. The report noted that six subsidiaries accounting for ₹130.1 crore of revenue were audited by other auditors, while one small subsidiary and an associate were unaudited. Additionally, the audit trail was not enabled at the database level for one accounting software.
