Current assets of about ₹140 crore are hypothecated to working-capital lenders, though there are no promoter share pledges. The company declared a dividend of ₹2 per share for FY26, and ESOP costs will continue for three more years at a smaller scale.
flags: Six subsidiaries generating ₹130.1 crore in revenue were audited by other auditors, and one small subsidiary and an associate were unaudited.
The audit trail feature was not enabled at the database level for one of the company's accounting softwares.
The company faces a ₹6.58 crore legal dispute in a Rajkot court from a customer claiming to have received faulty inverters.
The standalone accounts took a ₹0.29 crore impairment hit on investments in the Energy Solutions Labs subsidiary.

reports.auditor: The audit report included in the annual report was unmodified. However, the filed document only contained the standard Regulation 33 results report. The analyst could not find a CARO annexure or key audit matters section.
reports.relatedParties: The standalone accounts showed large sales to the company's own subsidiaries. This included about ₹106 crore to RMC Green Energy and ₹27 crore to RMC Solar Park. The company also had a receivable or advance balance of about ₹64 crore from RMC Green Energy. Trade with related parties How Sweet and Acme Metawires was small.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were small. Pending litigation, GST, and EPCG items totaled about ₹1.0 crore at March 2026.
reports.other: The accounts showed segment results of ₹96.5 crore for Electrical Products, ₹96.1 crore for Electrical EPC, and ₹209.0 crore for Solar EPC. The board's report noted a ₹10.34 crore loan to subsidiary RMC Green Energy and total subsidiary investments of ₹11.9 crore. Standalone receivables at March 2026 totaled ₹175.8 crore: ₹70.7 crore was not due, ₹84.4 crore was under 6 months, and ₹20.7 crore (about 12%) was between 6 and 12 months. The company pledged its 51% stake in Intelligent Hydel Solutions and deconsolidated it.
flags: A secretarial audit revealed a promoter violated insider-trading rules with an unreported contra trade.
Instances of sharing unpublished price-sensitive information were not recorded in the digital database, and the company secretary post was temporarily vacant.
The filed annual report lacked a CARO annexure and key audit matters section.
Standalone sales figures were inflated by large intra-group transactions to the company's own subsidiaries.
The company pledged its entire 51% stake in Intelligent Hydel Solutions for financial assistance and deconsolidated it without fully explaining the terms.

reports.auditor: The auditor, S R B C & Co, gave an unmodified opinion. They noted revenue timing as the key audit matter. This is because duty is paid on entry for consignment stock in US warehouses, but revenue is only booked when customers actually lift the goods.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings were small. The company paid about ₹7 crore in family remuneration. It also spent about ₹1 crore on subcontracting to relatives' firms, Rapid Cut and Revolve Engineering. In addition, it gave ₹0.3 crore for corporate social responsibility to the promoter's NeoRajkot Foundation.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities totaled ₹27.2 crore, increasing from ₹20.2 crore. This included ₹23.6 crore in income-tax disputes, ₹2.4 crore for GST disputes, and ₹1.3 crore for electricity claims. Capital commitments stood at only ₹2.8 crore at the end of March 2026.
reports.other: The annual report showed a ₹50.4 crore exceptional charge for a Right of Recompense, which was a lenders' claw-back from a 2013 debt restructuring. This claim was fully settled, with ₹101 crore paid on 31 March 2026.
flags: The auditor highlighted revenue timing as a key audit matter because revenue from US consignment stock is delayed until customers lift the goods.
Contingent liabilities have grown to ₹27.2 crore, driven mostly by ₹23.6 crore in unresolved income-tax disputes.

reports.auditor: Walker Chandiok & Co gave a clean, unmodified opinion. The only key audit matter was revenue recognition regarding rebates and cut-offs. The auditor noted one CARO exception, stating that the database-level audit trail for the accounting software's service provider could not be verified.
reports.relatedParties: Sons and a daughter of the promoters hold office of profit roles. Mikhail Menezes was paid ₹0.99 crore, and Yash Chari was paid ₹0.66 crore. Yashika Chari received AED 0.28 million at the Dubai subsidiary. The file notes these amounts are modest, but the practice is growing.
reports.contingent: No material contingent liabilities were disclosed in the consolidated notes. The company only reported capital commitments of ₹22.0 crore and Unitop retention pay of ₹1.6 crore.
reports.other: Total borrowings rose to ₹436 crore, including ₹94 crore in non-current term loans, ₹29 crore in current maturities, and ₹284 crore in working-capital loans. Subsidiary Unitop had revenue of ₹922 crore, and Tristar had ₹292 crore. The consumer arm is losing money: Buzil Rossari lost ₹12.7 crore and Rossari Consumer Products lost ₹9.3 crore, leaving both with negative net worth. A ₹24 crore intra-group exposure to Buzil was also listed. Domestic sales were ₹1,782.8 crore and exports were ₹613.6 crore.
flags: The sellers of subsidiary Unitop invoked a put option for their remaining 20% stake, resulting in an ongoing dispute and a carried ₹88.5 crore current liability.
Total borrowings doubled year-over-year from ₹218 crore to ₹436 crore.
The consumer subsidiaries Buzil Rossari and Rossari Consumer Products are losing more money and now operate with negative net worth.
The auditor noted a CARO exception because the accounting software's database-level audit trail could not be verified.
Promoter children are increasingly holding office of profit roles and drawing salaries from the company.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion but included an emphasis of matter. They noted that 18 months after the company's demerger, supply agreements with some customers are still in the name of the promoter's tea company, Rossell India Ltd. As a result, those supplies and revenues have been routed through the demerged entity.
reports.relatedParties: Bank loans are partly secured by mortgages on Rossell India Ltd's tea estates and hypothecation of its movable assets. However, the related-party note only lists the US subsidiary and key managers. It fails to disclose the revenue routing or the loan security provided by Rossell India as related-party transactions.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities consist only of bank guarantees amounting to ₹1.08 crore, down from ₹1.50 crore the previous year. Contracted capital commitments were very small, standing at just ₹8.1 lakh at the end of March 2026.
reports.outlook: Management targets 80% to 90% revenue growth for FY27. They expect space and semiconductor revenues to grow 300% to 400% in FY27, shifting the business mix to a 50:50 ratio. Headcount is planned to reach 2,000 by FY27. They anticipate long-run margins of 17% to 22% on current competencies. Commercial aerospace requests for proposals are expected by Q2 FY27, and strategic agreements for Boeing's T-7 trainer programme should ramp up from late FY27.
reports.other: The company reports operations as a single segment, providing no audited breakdown between defence, space, and semiconductor revenues. Standalone debt-to-equity was reported at 2.84x, up from 1.85x. Managing Director Rishab Mohan Gupta received a salary of ₹3.0 crore in FY26, equating to about 14% of net profit. Careless boilerplate text was left in the credit-risk note, falsely naming a UK tea buyer as an export customer.
flags: The auditor flagged that parts of revenue still legally flow through the promoter's tea company 18 months after the demerger.
Bank loans rely on security from the promoter's tea estates, with some transferred property title deeds still in the tea company's name.
The related-party note fails to disclose the crucial transactions of revenue routing and asset security involving Rossell India Ltd.
The managing director's pay of ₹3.0 crore consumes a high 14% of the company's net profit in FY26.
The annual report contains carelessly copied boilerplate text, inaccurately stating the company exports to a UK tea buyer.

reports.auditor: The auditor's report included emphasis-of-matter paragraphs regarding ₹135.9 crore in exceptional write-offs for vendor prepayments. This involved a ₹108.0 crore loss from a Singapore arbitration award against a subsidiary for minimum-commitment prepayments, and ₹27.9 crore tied to a vendor that ceased business. The auditor also named the ₹544.5 crore in goodwill from past acquisitions as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: The largest related-party item was sales of messaging services to fellow subsidiaries of the Proximus group. This totaled about ₹659 crore in FY26, up from ₹460 crore in FY25, making up roughly 15% of total revenue. These sales were priced at cost plus an agreed mark-up, and the report suggests they went mainly to Telesign.
reports.other: The annual report showed 174.9 billion billable transactions for FY26. It noted the company uses a meaningful amount of cash for vendor prepayments. The parent company's permanent staff was reported at 497. Additionally, the CEO of the Colombian subsidiary, Masivian, was listed in the report only 'up to June 30, 2026'.
flags: The auditor included emphasis-of-matter paragraphs for ₹135.9 crore in exceptional write-offs tied to vendor prepayments and a lost arbitration award.
The company continues to use a meaningful amount of cash on vendor prepayments, which is the same practice that caused the recent write-offs.
Auditors flagged ₹544.5 crore in goodwill from past acquisitions as a key audit matter.
A cyber incident occurred at the Masivian subsidiary, and its financial impact remains unquantified.
Related-party sales to the parent group's other subsidiaries account for a substantial 15% of total revenue.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion, noting revenue recognition as a key audit matter. However, they pointed out that the audit trail was not enabled for certain direct database changes in some software.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings were small. They included services from CEAT for ₹1.49 crore and a brand licence fee paid to RPG Enterprises for ₹1.31 crore.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are minor, consisting of ₹4.8 crore in bank guarantees and small tax claims. The company also had capital commitments of ₹14.1 crore as of March 2026.
reports.other: The Directors' Report showed domestic branded formulations at ₹483.5 crore, international formulations at ₹123.4 crore, and APIs at ₹95.1 crore. Exceptional items netted to a positive ₹3.9 crore, which included ₹24.75 crore from fire insurance, offset by an ₹11.69 crore charge for new labour codes and a ₹9.16 crore intangible write-off. The company declared a ₹24 per share dividend. No promoter pledge was shown.
flags: The auditor flagged that the audit trail was not enabled for certain direct database changes in some software.
A fire in early 2025 idled an API block for most of FY26, highlighting single-site concentration risk.
The company took exceptional charges of ₹11.69 crore for new labour codes and ₹9.16 crore to write off intangibles.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters included revenue cut-off risks, fictitious sales risks, and impairment testing for the loss-making FMEG unit. The auditor noted an audit-trail exception where one accounting software lacked database-level and some application-level edit logs. Change logs were also missing until 24 November 2025.
reports.relatedParties: The promoters gave personal guarantees for ₹369 crore of secured and ₹146 crore of unsecured bank lines. The company paid about ₹0.66 crore in rent to the promoter family. Executive directors received a commission of ₹6.6 crore, which the auditor noted was modest and at arm's length. The company also made ₹69.7 crore in sales to its Bangladesh joint venture, RR-Imperial Electricals.
reports.contingent: Contingent income-tax demands jumped to ₹105.3 crore from ₹11.5 crore in FY25. Of this, ₹103.4 crore is unpaid and covers the years 2008-09 to 2023-24. Total contingent liabilities for tax, GST, and customs export obligations stand at about ₹130 crore. Unexecuted capital commitments rose sharply to ₹256.7 crore. The company also issued a letter of comfort for up to BDT 75 crore of loans to its Bangladesh joint venture.
reports.outlook: Management outlined Project RRise, a three-year roadmap to FY28. Targets include an 18% annual volume growth for wires and cables, 25% growth for FMEG, and a 2.5 times increase in overall EBITDA. The company aims to improve wire and cable margins by 300 basis points to 10.5% by FY28. Management noted that a potential India-EU free trade agreement could remove tariffs on Indian wires and cables. The company plans to continue outsourcing about two-thirds of its FMEG manufacturing.
reports.other: Trade payables of ₹1,364 crore include ₹1,107 crore of interest-bearing letter of credit acceptances, up from ₹374 crore in FY25. Borrowings stood at ₹232 crore alongside ₹105 crore in lease liabilities. The company buys 100% of its metal back-to-back for B2B and export orders. Management saw changes, with founder Tribhuvanprasad Kabra stepping down as Executive Chairman on 31 May 2025, and the CFO changing in November 2025.
flags: Contingent income-tax demands jumped significantly to ₹105.3 crore, with ₹103.4 crore remaining unpaid.
One accounting software lacked required database-level edit logs, and change logs were missing until late 2025.
The FMEG segment is a loss-making cash-generating unit that required auditor impairment testing.
Reported working capital and net debt are flattered by a heavy reliance on ₹1,107 crore of interest-bearing letter of credit acceptances.
The company's promoters personally guarantee a total of ₹515 crore in secured and unsecured bank lines.

reports.auditor: Deloitte Haskins & Sells gave an unmodified opinion for FY26. Key audit matters included revenue cut-offs and judgement-heavy accruals for US chargebacks, rebates, and returns. Other auditors reviewed 11 subsidiaries, which accounted for ₹263 crore in revenue and ₹350 crore in assets. The CARO report showed no defaults and confirmed that IPO money was used as stated.
reports.relatedParties: In FY26, the company paid ₹5.1 crore to lease an office from Medone Pharma Labs, whose partners are relatives of the MD and CEO. The CEO received a pay of ₹5.1 crore. Additionally, the company employed three family members who received a combined pay of about ₹4.6 crore.
reports.contingent: As of March 2026, the company faced disputed tax claims under appeal. These included income tax demands of ₹18.4 crore and sales tax demands of ₹0.7 crore, up from ₹10.6 crore and ₹1.6 crore respectively in the prior year.
reports.other: The group reports a single pharmaceutical products segment. Business is almost entirely American, with the US providing ₹1,737 crore (99%) of the ₹1,754 crore FY26 revenue, while India provided just ₹6.3 crore. Customer concentration is extreme, as five large clients supplied about 72% of revenue. The management discussion also highlighted the company's five approved nasal drug-device products and claimed one of the largest single-site nasal spray capacities.
flags: Geographic concentration is highly extreme, with 99% of total revenue coming from the US market.
Customer concentration poses a significant risk, as just five clients account for roughly 72% of revenue.
The auditor noted that accounting for US chargebacks, rebates, returns, and revenue cut-offs requires heavy management judgement.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave a clean opinion. Revenue recognition, specifically concerning discounts and cut-off procedures, was highlighted as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: Rushil International, a promoter-family partnership, is a promoter shareholder with small transactions. Notably, one loan is secured against the key-man insurance policies of the directors.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small, consisting of bank guarantees worth ₹8.8 crore and letters of credit totaling ₹0.5 crore. A previous customs dispute has been closed. Capital commitments dropped sharply to ₹1.5 crore in FY26 from ₹48 crore.
reports.other: The company produces MDF boards, decorative laminates under the 'VIR' brand, and small PVC/WPC boards. It is one of India's larger MDF makers with a capacity of 3.3 lakh CBM, benefiting from a southern plant base near timber and the Vizag port. Both phases of its Jumbo laminates facility were commissioned in FY26 for roughly ₹90 crore.
flags: A company loan is secured against the key-man insurance policies of its directors.

reports.auditor: Tax positions are noted as a key audit matter. The file mentions no other auditor remarks, qualifications, or CARO points.
reports.contingent: A vendor has claimed $115.9m (₹1,094 cr) for unjust enrichment, or $53.2m for lost profits, regarding pre-acquisition commissions. The former sellers (HGS and affiliates) retained this liability and indemnify Sagility. There are also new, unprovided income-tax and transfer-pricing demands of ₹92.6 cr for FY22 and FY23.
reports.other: Sagility serves 7 of the 10 largest US payers, with nine clients above $20m. Top-5 client revenue grew 16.7% in FY26. Group goodwill stands at about ₹6,039 cr against equity of ₹9,660 cr. The promoter reduced its stake from 82.39% to 50.95% through an offer for sale of 70.3 cr shares. The Group CFO and Chief Growth Officer resigned in November 2025. ICRA withdrew its credit rating at the company's request.
flags: The top 3 clients make up 60% of revenue, which the annual report lists as a key risk if payers merge or consolidate.
New income-tax and transfer-pricing demands of ₹92.6 cr have not been provided for.
Group goodwill is very high at ₹6,039 cr against equity of ₹9,660 cr, posing a heavy impairment risk if growth slows.
A vendor has filed a legal claim for up to $115.9m (₹1,094 cr), though the company holds an indemnity from former sellers.
Two key management personnel, the Group CFO and the Chief Growth Officer, resigned in November 2025.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion and the CARO report noted no material discrepancies. However, inventory valuation was flagged as a key audit matter due to missing reconciliations and a system disruption.
reports.relatedParties: The company lent ₹6.6 crore with interest to Infopower Technologies, a merging promoter company. It recorded sales, purchases, rent, and multi-crore expense reimbursements with promoter entities Sahasra Electronics Pvt Ltd and a sole proprietorship, though exact splits are unclear due to misaligned PDF columns. Promoter guarantees and properties secure bank loans.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities consist of a ₹27.5 crore guarantee provided for the semiconductor subsidiary's bank borrowings and a minor income-tax claim of ₹0.26 crore.
reports.outlook: The Board's report highlights a pending merger to absorb three promoter-owned entities into the listed company. These include Sahasra Electronics Pvt Ltd, Infopower Technologies, and a skill development firm. The merger has an effective date of April 2026, pending approvals from the NSE, SEBI, and NCLT.
reports.other: Consolidated FY26 revenue was ₹138.8 crore, driven by EMS (66%) and memory solutions (18.9%). Exports made up 56% of revenue. Promoters hold 69.9% of the company with no disclosed pledges.
flags: The annual report states that a quantitative reconciliation of raw materials and finished goods was not prepared.
Following an SAP disruption, physical raw-material quantities did not tally with system stock records at year-end and had to be rectified later.
A PDF formatting error in the annual report makes the exact breakdown of multi-crore related-party transactions unclear.
The company plans to merge three promoter-owned private companies into the listed entity using a share-swap ratio determined by the promoters' valuer.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The key audit matter noted was revenue recognition on fixed-price contracts. This is measured by the percentage of completion and relies heavily on management judgement.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were ₹97 crore, up from ₹58 crore the previous year, consisting mostly of ₹86 crore in income-tax demands. Capital commitments stood at ₹354 crore in March 2026, rising from ₹103 crore a year earlier.
reports.other: Company EBITDA for FY26 was ₹661 crore, representing a 30.1% margin including forex. One major customer accounted for ₹267 crore of revenue in FY26, whereas two customers brought in ₹364 crore in FY25. The company ended March 2026 with net debt of ₹16 crore, shifting from a net cash position of ₹161 crore at March 2025.
flags: Four designated persons breached the insider-trading code by trading or pledging shares without pre-clearance, resulting in fines of ₹11.1 lakh.
Contingent liabilities are rising, reaching ₹97 crore mostly due to ₹86 crore in income-tax demands.

reports.auditor: The auditor highlighted the impairment testing of ₹124.6 crore in goodwill and ₹47.9 crore in intangibles on consolidation as a Key Audit Matter. The report also contained a disclosure inconsistency. It stated that the Noumed acquisition occurred on April 1, 2025, which contradicts management's stated consolidation date of November 12, 2025.
reports.relatedParties: Managing Director Anil Kumar Karusala lent the company ₹24.7 crore and was repaid ₹27.8 crore during the year. The company paid rent and security deposits to promoter family members. There were also loan flows with Revat Laboratories, where the company took ₹33.7 crore and repaid ₹35.1 crore.
reports.contingent: The promoters provided personal guarantees to secure the company's loans.
reports.other: The consolidated balance sheet recorded goodwill of ₹124.6 crore and intangibles of ₹47.9 crore. The borrowings note disclosed that the company's loans are secured by a pledge of its shares in Noumed Pharmaceuticals.
flags: The auditor's report has a date inconsistency, stating Noumed was acquired on April 1, 2025, instead of November 12, 2025.
The company's shares in its Noumed Pharmaceuticals subsidiary are pledged to lenders.
The company engaged in multi-crore related-party loan flows with its Managing Director and Revat Laboratories.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unqualified opinion with no emphasis of matter, fraud, or loan defaults reported. They highlighted two Key Audit Matters: the existence and valuation of ₹70 crore in inventory, and the capitalisation of product-development spending as intangibles (₹5.5 crore in FY26 and ₹4.1 crore in FY25). Under CARO, they noted income tax demands for AY 2020-21 that are under appeal.
reports.relatedParties: Promoter pay jumped significantly during the year to total about ₹4.4 crore, which is roughly 14% of the FY26 net profit. Sanjay Shah received ₹2.40 crore (up from ₹0.72 crore in FY25), Aarsh Shah received ₹1.80 crore (up from ₹0.60 crore), and Rita Shah received ₹0.18 crore.
reports.contingent: The company reported no contingent liabilities. However, there are disputed income tax demands of ₹2.82 crore and ₹0.09 crore for the assessment year 2020-21 currently under appeal.
reports.other: The company has only one reportable segment in its accounts and does not publish audited segment data, so the oncology and non-oncology revenue split cannot be seen in the report. The company had 435 employees at the end of March 2026. Management reported an interest coverage ratio of 9.1x and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.14x. Promoters hold a 52.5% stake with no pledges disclosed.
flags: Promoter pay jumped sharply to ₹4.4 crore, taking up roughly 14% of the company's net profit for FY26.
The auditor raised a Key Audit Matter regarding the existence and valuation of a heavy ₹70 crore inventory balance.
The auditor highlighted product-development spending capitalised as intangibles (₹5.5 crore in FY26), a practice that flatters reported profits.
The company faces income tax demands of ₹2.91 crore for AY 2020-21, but it reported no contingent liabilities for them in the notes.
The company does not publish audited segment data, meaning the fast-growing oncology numbers are not verified in the accounts.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion and found no emphasis of matter. The group auditor relied on the reports of other auditors for 15 subsidiaries, which account for ₹861 crore in revenue and about 85% of the group. Testing the impairment of ₹518 crore in goodwill was noted as a key audit matter.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were small and included ₹6.7 crore for income tax. Contingent consideration for earn-outs, which stood at ₹39.5 crore in March 2025, fell to nil by March 2026.
reports.other: Promoters hold 66.7% of the company, and no share pledges were shown. Voluntary employee attrition rose from 10.8% in FY25 to 13.4% in FY26. The company uses forward contracts, which are recorded as a derivative liability.
flags: Goodwill from serial acquisitions totals ₹518 crore, making up 48% of assets and bringing an impairment risk if acquired units stall.
The main group auditor did not audit 15 subsidiaries that make up roughly 85% of the group's revenue (₹861 crore).
Voluntary employee attrition increased to 13.4% in FY26.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Revenue recognition was the only key audit matter. The CARO report was clean, noting that bank returns agreed with the company books and there were no defaults.
reports.relatedParties: The company sold about ₹39 crore of materials to promoter-group firm Salzer Exports Ltd. It also paid a few crore each to Salzer Spinners and SRVE Industries for purchases, labour, rent, and electricity. Quebec Information Services provided services worth ₹0.85 crore.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities included EPCG export obligations of ₹42.9 crore, letters of credit of ₹15.2 crore, and bank guarantees of ₹13.9 crore. There was also a ₹0.4 crore customs appeal, disputed income-tax demands of about ₹0.9 crore, and a ₹0.55 crore penalty under appeal.
flags: The company engages in related-party transactions with a web of promoter entities, including about ₹39 crore in annual sales to Salzer Exports Ltd.
The company faces disputed income-tax demands of about ₹0.9 crore and a ₹0.55 crore penalty under appeal.

reports.auditor: S S Kothari Mehta & Co. gave a clean audit opinion, noting revenue recognition as the only key audit matter. The CARO report is also clean, stating that bank returns agree with the books, there are no defaults, and the audit trail has been preserved.
reports.relatedParties: In FY26, the company recorded sales of ₹15.5 crore to promoter-linked Sadhguru Pipes LLP, up from ₹7.5 crore in FY25. It made purchases of ₹4.5 crore from Anjaneya Minerals and paid ₹3.4 crore for job work to Ganpati Sponge Iron. Group-company corporate guarantees of ₹879 crore for Ganpati Sponge and ₹198 crore for S. Pyarelal Ispat were released. The subsidiary repaid ₹34 crore of loans.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are tiny, consisting of claims worth ₹0.19 crore and income tax of ₹2.6 crore. However, the company reported standalone capital commitments of ₹612 crore as of March 2026.
reports.other: In its MD&A SWOT analysis, the company notes it is the only Indian ERW maker at a single site that refines steel from iron ore rather than buying coil. Additionally, a note states that a 15% stake in Vajra Alloys was bought for ₹7.5 crore on April 1, 2026.
flags: The company's own MD&A SWOT analysis acknowledges a very low ERW pipe market share of only about 3%, which is cited as evidence against having a competitive moat.

reports.auditor: B S R & Co. gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters included revenue recognition and the impairment of ₹365 crore in subsidiary and joint venture investments. Eight subsidiaries were audited by other auditors. The auditor also noted a minor audit-trail reporting gap at one subsidiary and one joint venture.
reports.relatedParties: The company purchased goods worth ₹60.7 crore in FY26, up from ₹53.4 crore, from Swaran Enterprises, a firm where promoter family member Mrs. Santosh Davar is a partner. It also paid lease rentals to promoter entities Sandhar Estates, Jubin Finance, and Shorah Realty. The auditor and board stated these were at arm's length.
reports.contingent: The company provided guarantees of ₹624 crore at March 2026, up from ₹411 crore the prior year, mostly for subsidiary loans. GST disputes stood at ₹15.6 crore, compared to ₹7.8 crore previously. Standalone capital commitments were ₹22.4 crore, down from ₹40.5 crore a year ago.
reports.other: The promoter holding remained unchanged at 70.38%. Within this, Jayant Davar transferred a 4.36% stake to his son Neel Jay Davar as an intra-family move. There were no disclosed share pledges.
flags: Guarantees given by the company, mostly to support subsidiary loans, jumped to ₹624 crore from ₹411 crore.
The auditor highlighted the potential impairment of ₹365 crore in subsidiary and joint venture investments as a key audit matter.
The company maintains a recurring related-party supply line, purchasing ₹60.7 crore in goods from a promoter family firm.
Unresolved GST disputes doubled year-on-year to ₹15.6 crore.
A minor audit-trail reporting gap was reported at one subsidiary and one joint venture.

reports.auditor: Price Waterhouse & Co gave an unmodified opinion but noted audit-trail gaps. The core accounting software does not log changes by certain privileged users, and the database-level trail was not enabled. Additionally, the auditor could not comment on the payroll provider's audit trail for October to December 2025.
reports.relatedParties: The parent provides trademarks and product rights free of cost. CY25 purchases from group companies were ₹537 crore, including ₹462 crore from Sanofi-Aventis Singapore and ₹75 crore from Sanofi Healthcare India. Sales to group companies were ₹254 crore. Shareholders are asked to approve 2026 transactions of up to ₹1,385 crore with the Singapore affiliate and ₹530 crore with Sanofi Healthcare India.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include ₹318.6 crore in income-tax demands, which is a key audit matter. This includes ₹79.7 crore where the department appealed and ₹238.9 crore under the company's appeal. There are separate provisions of ₹36.7 crore for DPCO/NPPA price-overcharging demands and ₹16.2 crore retained for NPPA demands remanded in 2019. Capital commitments were just ₹6 crore at December 2025.
reports.other: CY2025 revenue from operations was ₹1,837 crore, split into ₹1,593 crore from India, ₹231 crore from the Singapore affiliate, and ₹14 crore from others. Two customers exceeded 10% of revenue: Emcure at ₹504 crore and the Singapore affiliate at ₹229 crore. The company saw management churn in 2025, including the departure of MD Rodolfo Hrosz in April and three different company secretaries.
flags: The auditor noted audit-trail gaps in the core accounting software and the payroll provider.
The company faces significant contingent liabilities, including ₹318.6 crore in disputed income-tax demands.
Operations rely heavily on related parties, with CY25 purchases from group companies totaling ₹537 crore.
Revenue is highly concentrated, with Emcure and the Singapore affiliate each exceeding 10% of total sales.
The company experienced notable management churn in 2025, including the exit of its managing director and three company secretaries.

reports.auditor: Deloitte Haskins & Sells gave an unmodified opinion but noted revenue cut-off as a key audit matter. The auditor flagged that the accounting software's audit trail feature was not enabled between 1 April 2023 and 20 May 2024. The auditors also reported two fraud instances: a former employee forged invoices to misappropriate ₹1.22 crore, and subsidiary Fitwel Tools & Forgings suffered ₹9.12 crore in fraudulent payments.
reports.relatedParties: The company made CSR contributions of ₹5.5 crore to the Sansera Foundation. Chairman and Managing Director Sekhar Vasan received ₹5.5 crore in pay. The company also invested ₹25 crore in associate MMRFIC Technology during the year and provided a comfort letter for MMRFIC's bank borrowings.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities included ₹9.3 crore for indirect taxes, ₹3.7 crore for income tax, ₹9.4 crore for customer claims, and a ₹1.2 crore pollution demand. About ₹10 crore in disputed tax dues were not deposited. The company provided a corporate guarantee and standby letter of credit up to ₹70.8 crore for Sansera Sweden. Capital commitments stood at ₹211.9 crore. The company also faced an American Axle lawsuit with only a ₹2 crore initial provision.
reports.outlook: The Management Discussion and Analysis stated that the combined peak annual revenue of new business stood at ₹1,919 crore at the end of the year.
reports.other: The Directors' report detailed the company's investments in associate MMRFIC Technology, expecting to hold a 45-50% stake after the conversion of preference shares. It also noted a 60:40 joint venture with Nichidai, Japan.
flags: Auditors reported control gaps involving a ₹1.22 crore employee invoice fraud and ₹9.12 crore in fraudulent payments at subsidiary Fitwel Tools & Forgings.
The accounting software's audit trail feature was left disabled for over a year between April 2023 and May 2024.
The company initially provided only ₹2 crore for an American Axle lawsuit, which later required a ₹16.9 crore settlement, highlighting potential disclosure quality issues.
Disputed tax dues that remain un-deposited stand at approximately ₹10 crore.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters included revenue recognition from licence fees and the company's acquisition of a stake in Bhansali Productions. The auditor also noted that the audit trail operated.

reports.auditor: The audit opinion is unmodified. Key audit matters include revenue recognition, trade receivables, and tax litigation. reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unmodified opinion but included Key Audit Matters (KAMs) regarding product-development capitalisation and revenue recognition. The report also noted that the audit trail was not enabled at the database level.

flags: The auditor noted that the audit trail was not enabled at the database level.

The company operates a web of numerous related-party transactions with promoter-linked entities and carries borrowings from relatives.

reports.auditor: Statutory auditor S K Patodia & Associates LLP issued an unmodified opinion. Key Audit Matters (KAMs) included revenue recognition (covering discounts, rebates, and export incentives) and credit-loss allowance. The auditor noted that the audit trail operated all year.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion with no emphasis of matter. They highlighted two key audit matters. Dealings with promoter-linked firms are small, totaling about ₹3 crore in sales, and there is no promoter pledge. The report also lists Emerge Solar Projects, in which a 26% stake was purchased, as an associate and an entity influenced by key management personnel.
reports.contingent: Consolidated contingent liabilities rose to ₹723 crore from ₹560 crore in FY25. This total includes indirect-tax claims of ₹138 crore, customs of ₹15 crore, VAT of ₹15 crore, and income tax of ₹5 crore. It also includes bank guarantees of ₹227 crore and discounted bills of ₹323 crore.
reports.other: The standalone company reports a single operating segment for iron and steel. The standalone entity holds alternative investment fund (AIF) investments valued at ₹654 crore as of March 2026, up from ₹215 crore a year earlier. These are classified using Level 3 valuations. Additionally, there are further AIF commitments of ₹281 crore on a standalone basis and ₹507.5 crore at the group level.
flags: The Enforcement Directorate provisionally attached ₹152.48 crore of a subsidiary's assets in an illegal mining probe, prompting an auditor Emphasis of Matter.
The auditor could not verify proper audit-trail compliance for two accounting software systems used by the company.
Consolidated contingent liabilities increased to ₹723 crore from ₹560 crore the previous year.
The company holds a growing balance of Level 3 alternative investment funds valued at ₹654 crore, alongside large pending group commitments.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unmodified opinion with an emphasis of matter on the merger accounting and a GST dispute over joint-development transactions, where ₹16.8 crore was paid under protest. Key audit matters included uncertain tax positions and the merger. A separate auditor noted the UK subsidiary generated ₹348 crore in revenue but recorded a ₹19.1 crore net loss.
reports.relatedParties: The company lent ₹121 crore to and borrowed ₹165 crore from promoter Chintalapati Holdings during FY26, owing ₹44.5 crore by the end of March. The company also provided a ₹30.7 crore advance to its associate Indrajaal. The CARO report flagged large loans made to an associate during the year.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities stood at ₹61.7 crore, which consisted almost entirely of guarantees. There is also an ongoing income-tax dispute for ₹20 crore related to the 2012-13 year, which is pending at the Madras High Court.
reports.other: Total FY26 revenue was ₹492 crore, with ₹334 crore coming from outside India. Reported net profit was driven by one-off items, including a ₹184.6 crore gain from selling land and a ₹76.9 crore gain from selling most of a Swiss associate. The company also paid ₹197 crore in net cash for the Nasmyth acquisition.
flags: FY26 net profit relied heavily on one-off gains from land and stake sales rather than core operations.
The audited UK subsidiary reported a net loss of ₹19.1 crore for the year.
The company engaged in large related-party lending and borrowing with its promoter entity.
There are pending tax disputes involving a ₹20 crore income tax claim and a ₹16.8 crore GST claim.
The secretarial audit noted the company was fined by exchanges for not having enough directors during the year.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified (clean) opinion on the financial statements and internal controls. The key audit matter was revenue recognition, specifically the cut-off risk around the year-end and credit notes issued after the financial year ended.
reports.relatedParties: Key management personnel received ₹3.1 crore in pay, while relatives (the managing director's daughter and son-in-law) were paid ₹0.6 crore. BGB Italia is also listed as part of the promoter group.
reports.contingent: The company disclosed no contingent liabilities.
reports.outlook: The management discussion expects a 25% to 30% compound annual growth rate for revenue. The company is targeting ₹1,000 crore in revenue by FY29.
reports.other: The company operates in one reported segment for wood coating products. It raised ₹75.3 crore by issuing 19.84 lakh shares to non-promoters at ₹379.50 each. The balance sheet carries ₹100.75 crore in goodwill from purchasing the Wembley and Welcome brands. A dividend of ₹2 per share was declared.
flags: The FY26 results are the company's first financial statements under Ind AS rules, meaning comparisons with earlier years need care.
The secretarial audit report notes that the company is still regularising old foreign exchange filings (FC-TRS) from FY2008-09 and FY2009-10.
The balance sheet carries ₹100.75 crore of goodwill from the Wembley acquisition, representing about 21% of equity, which is at risk if that business remains flat.

reports.auditor: The auditor, S.R. Batliboi, gave an unqualified opinion. The only key audit matters were revenue recognition and price-variation provisions. As a minor note, subsidiaries SDPL and WPI filed some forms late.
reports.contingent: Consolidated contingent income-tax liabilities were ₹25.6 crore in March 2026, up from ₹1.8 crore a year earlier. This mainly includes a ₹23.0 crore demand for AY 2024-25 regarding ESOP expenses, metro-land compensation, and a subsidiary acquisition adjustment, plus a ₹2.4 crore demand on non-compete fees. No provision was made. Additionally, unexecuted capital contracts stood at ₹45.8 crore, compared to ₹29.3 crore the previous year.
reports.other: The company reported having only one operating segment, which is aesthetics for auto and appliances. Because of this, the annual report does not provide an audited segment margin split.
flags: The Registrar of Companies issued notices to subsidiary WPI regarding a statutory auditor's report of suspected fraud, with the nature and amount remaining undisclosed.
Contingent income-tax liabilities surged to ₹25.6 crore without any provisions being made.
The tax department surveyed the Bengaluru office in January 2025 and issued reopening notices for AY 2019-20 and 2020-21.

reports.auditor: The board report states that the auditor's opinion is unqualified. However, the text detailing the key audit matters was not legible in the extracted annual report.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid ₹89 crore in royalty and trademark fees to its promoter, AB SKF, during FY26. This compares to ₹132 crore paid by the combined company in FY25 before the demerger.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities fell to ₹214 crore from ₹582 crore. This includes ₹158 crore for income tax, roughly ₹26 crore for excise and customs, ₹21 crore for GST and service tax, and ₹9 crore for other items. A new FY22 transfer-pricing addition of ₹69.4 crore is under appeal. There is an old advance-licence customs bond issue from FY1997-98. Pre-demerger tax disputes are shared with the industrial business. Open capital commitments were ₹69 crore.
reports.other: Standalone automotive revenue for FY26 was ₹2,129.6 crore, up 15.4% from the carve-out base. Profit before tax prior to exceptional items was ₹262 crore, yielding a net profit of ₹117 crore. An exceptional catch-up tax charge of ₹61.5 crore impacted profits due to a transfer-pricing settlement. The company is debt-free, holding ₹292 crore in cash and equivalents at March 2026. A final dividend of ₹40 per share was declared, totaling about ₹198 crore.
flags: The key audit matter text was not legible in the extracted annual report.
The company paid ₹89 crore in royalty and trademark fees to its promoter in FY26.
A transfer-pricing settlement covering FY13 to FY21 resulted in an unexpected ₹61.5 crore extra tax charge.
A new transfer-pricing addition of ₹69.4 crore for FY22 is currently under appeal.

reports.auditor: The auditor's report is unqualified with no key audit matters.
reports.relatedParties: For the six months since the demerger in FY26, royalty paid to AB SKF was ₹15.3 cr, trademark fees were ₹10.2 cr, and group IT services were ₹48 cr. For FY27, shareholders are asked to approve related-party transactions with AB SKF totaling ₹464.7 cr. This includes up to ₹121.5 cr for royalty, ₹100.6 cr for trademark fees, and ₹133 cr for IT services.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include ₹103.8 cr for civil court cases. Pre-demerger tax disputes remain with SKF India Ltd, but any settlement is shared, so financial exposure still exists. Open capital commitments are ₹46.7 cr. Provisions include ₹77.7 cr for dealer and industrial-market incentives and special-price claims.
reports.outlook: The annual report shows ₹650+ cr of total proposed investments. Management cites IMARC estimates that the Indian industrial bearings market was about ₹66,000 cr in 2024, growing 4.3% annually to 2033.
reports.other: Financial periods before October 2025 are management carve-outs built on assumptions. The company operates one plant in Pune and imported ₹974 cr of finished goods in foreign currency during FY26. FY26 exceptional items included ₹163.9 cr for stamp duty and transfer premium on land, plus ₹26.4 cr for demerger IT costs. The company is debt-free with cash of ₹569 cr and paid a ₹10 per share dividend totaling about ₹49 cr.
flags: Shareholders are asked to approve up to ₹222 cr in royalty and trademark fees to AB SKF for FY27, which equals about 6% of sales and has no sunset clause.
Total FY27 related-party approvals with AB SKF equal ₹464.7 cr, including a substantial ₹133 cr for IT services.
The demerger cost shareholders ₹164 cr in stamp duty and land transfer premiums, plus another ₹29 cr for IT and other demerger expenses.
The company retains exposure to pre-demerger tax disputes because settlements are shared with SKF India Ltd.
High import dependence exposes the company to foreign exchange risks, with foreign-currency spending on finished goods reaching ₹974 cr in FY26.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Revenue recognition was noted as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: The company reported sales of ₹54.7 crore to its associate VKT Pharma in FY26, up from ₹39.6 crore in FY25. It made purchases of about ₹17 crore from promoter-linked Haleos Labs, formerly SMS Lifesciences. It also purchased about ₹15 crore from other related firms, including Raghavendra Engineering, Eswar Coal Movers, and Fours Engineering. Executive director pay was ₹12.9 crore, up from ₹10.4 crore in FY25.
reports.contingent: The company faces an income-tax demand of ₹45.6 crore for assessment year 2023-24 due to GST-return turnover mismatches. This is admitted as a high-pitched assessment, an appeal is pending, and no provision has been made. Additionally, capital commitments stood at ₹44 crore in March 2026, up from ₹10 crore a year earlier.
reports.outlook: The management discussion outlines a ₹280.78 crore capital expenditure project. This will expand ibuprofen capacity from 500 to 800 tonnes per month and include backward integration of ibuprofen intermediates. It also adds a multi-API block for four to five new high-margin APIs. Management notes their automated Vizag plant provides a leading share in ibuprofen for Europe. International markets generate 85% of revenue, with 88% coming from regulated markets.
reports.other: The company holds a 34.83% stake in an associate formulation company, VKT Pharma, and a new 99.99% subsidiary, SMS Peptides. Promoters converted 90 lakh warrants issued at ₹127 each, increasing their shareholding from 64.67% to 68.07%. Assets of about ₹1,168 crore are pledged as security for loans under a normal bank charge.
flags: The company faces an unprovided income-tax demand of ₹45.6 crore, which is about 6% of its net worth.
Executive director pay of ₹12.9 crore is elevated, representing roughly 13% of the company's FY26 net profit.
The company relies on related-party revenue, reporting ₹54.7 crore in sales to its own associate VKT Pharma.

reports.auditor: The auditor raised an emphasis of matter regarding an income tax search and demands of ₹ 67.2 crore for AY2015-16 to AY2023-24. The Enforcement Directorate case regarding land advances to Technobuild is a key audit matter. The auditor also issued a CARO reporting remark because they could not confirm if the audit-trail feature was enabled all year for a third-party-hosted software.
reports.relatedParties: The group does business with promoter-linked Technobuild through land advances under a memorandum of understanding. Nearly all other related-party transactions are with subsidiaries. No AOC-2 transactions were reported, meaning there were no material deals that were not at arm's length.
reports.contingent: Standalone contingent liabilities totaled about ₹ 394 crore in March 2026. This includes a ₹ 201.6 crore land attachment by the Enforcement Directorate and ₹ 122.9 crore in indirect taxes. There is also an unquantified criminal complaint by a unit holder, alongside land-acquisition, forest, and pollution-board cases.
reports.other: The company reported gross segment revenue of ₹ 4,420 crore for real estate and ₹ 1,028 crore for contractual and manufacturing. Segment results were ₹ 383 crore for real estate and ₹ 115 crore for contractual and manufacturing. Main costs for the real estate segment included land at ₹ 2,023 crore, project materials at ₹ 1,157 crore, and subcontractors at ₹ 1,153 crore.
flags: The Enforcement Directorate provisionally attached land worth ₹ 201.6 crore held by Technobuild Developers, impacting Sobha's land advances.
Income tax search demands of ₹ 67.2 crore for AY2015-16 to AY2023-24 are currently under appeal.
Auditors issued a reporting remark because they could not verify if a third-party software's audit trail was enabled all year.
The company faces an unquantified criminal complaint from a unit holder, plus land-acquisition and environmental cases.

reports.auditor: The auditor's report highlighted a key audit matter regarding the ₹364.9 crore goodwill associated with the Human API business, noting that impairment testing relies heavily on management forecasts.
reports.relatedParties: The company recorded ₹329 crore in sales to promoter-group company Strides Pharma Science in FY26, up from ₹215 crore in FY25, representing roughly a quarter of its total revenue. The company also received loans from promoter entities Tenshi Pharmaceuticals and Chayadeep Properties.
reports.contingent: Solara faces a disputed income-tax demand of ₹161.9 crore for AY 2019-20, currently under appeal, relating to disallowed deductions for R&D, goodwill, and product-portfolio depreciation. Additionally, ₹342 crore of carried-forward losses were restricted for AY 2024-25, alongside similar tax disallowances spanning multiple other assessment years.
reports.other: The directors' report noted a CRISIL BBB/Stable credit rating, which is the lowest in its peer group. The company recorded an exceptional charge of ₹5.9 crore for a labour-code item in FY26. It also experienced severe leadership churn, replacing its MD & CEO, CFO, and Company Secretary in 2025, while an executive director changed in January 2026 and a non-executive director resigned in November 2025.
flags: A disputed ₹161.9 crore income-tax demand represents roughly 13% of the company's net worth.
The ₹364.9 crore goodwill balance was flagged as a key audit matter because its valuation relies on management forecasts.
Roughly a quarter of total revenue is concentrated with a single related party, Strides Pharma Science.
The company suffered extreme leadership turnover, losing its MD & CEO, CFO, and Company Secretary all within 2025.
Tax authorities restricted ₹342 crore in carried-forward losses and issued similar disallowances across multiple assessment years.

reports.auditor: Singhi & Co. issued a clean opinion, noting receivables and inventory valuation as key audit matters. However, they flagged a control gap: the audit trail (edit log) was not enabled at the database level for certain SAP tables and another software.
reports.relatedParties: The standalone company purchases heavily from group joint ventures and subsidiaries, including roughly ₹235 crore from Sudha Somany and ₹112 crore from Vintage Tiles. It also provided inter-corporate deposits, including ₹36.5 crore to loss-making subsidiary Somany Max and ₹5 crore each to three others. Promoter pay was ₹6.6 crore for Abhishek Somany and ₹5.2 crore for Shreekant Somany (together ~12% of standalone PAT), with three family members in paid roles.
reports.contingent: Consolidated contingent liabilities total about ₹38 crore. This includes ₹22.3 crore for GST, excise, and service tax, ₹8.1 crore for income tax, ₹5.6 crore in claims, and a ₹0.56 crore pollution penalty from the GPCB. There are also undetermined labour disputes.
reports.outlook: The management discussion and analysis highlights that gas constitutes 25 to 30% of production costs, remaining a significant operational risk. Standalone performance for FY26 reached ₹2,640 crore in revenue with a 7.0% EBITDA margin and ₹99 crore in net profit.
reports.other: The company reports only one segment (building products) and does not disclose segment margins. A buyback is on hold until the amalgamation of three wholly-owned subsidiaries clears. In July 2025, the company bought a 51% stake in Dura Build Care for ₹10.3 crore; it reported a ₹0.4 crore loss in FY26. Furthermore, the ~85% owned subsidiary Somany Max lost ₹21 crore in FY26.
flags: The auditor identified a control gap because the audit trail was not enabled at the database level for certain SAP tables.
The standalone business relies heavily on related-party purchases and extended a ₹36.5 crore deposit to its loss-making subsidiary, Somany Max.
Promoter compensation is relatively high, consuming roughly 12% of the standalone net profit.
The company faces approximately ₹38 crore in contingent liabilities, which includes disputed taxes and a pollution penalty.
Subsidiary performance remains a drag, highlighted by a ₹21 crore loss at Somany Max in FY26.

reports.auditor: Walker Chandiok gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters included the accounting for the railway business combination and the impairment of intangibles. The auditor also remarked that the audit trail was not enabled at the database level for the whole year.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small. They include a ₹28 crore GST writ regarding an export refund and about ₹11 crore for income tax and transfer pricing. Service tax liabilities were negligible.
reports.other: The annual report outlines four verticals: driveline, motors, sensors and software, and railway. The MD and Group CEO's total pay rose to ₹15.0 crore in FY26 from ₹3.4 crore in FY25. This included a 15% raise, a ₹6.0 crore share-plan perquisite, and a new ₹5.5 crore commission set at 1% of consolidated profit and capped at 5% of net profit. A new 15 lakh-share performance plan was approved in December 2025.
flags: The auditor noted that the accounting software's audit trail was not enabled at the database level for the whole year.
The late chairman's mother has alleged fraud over the family trusts that control the 28% promoter stake, leading to High Court litigation.
The MD and Group CEO's total pay increased more than fourfold to ₹15.0 crore in FY26.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters highlighted in the report were fixed-price revenue recognition and goodwill impairment, with goodwill standing at ₹1,268 crore in March 2026.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include parent guarantees up to $40 million to domestic subsidiary suppliers, and $77.5 million ($42.5 million plus $35 million) to banks for the North America subsidiary's loans. The company also has disputed income-tax demands of about ₹365 crore and service tax disputes of ₹25 crore.
reports.other: Notes for the domestic subsidiary show that one customer accounted for over 10% of its revenue, contributing ₹990 crore in FY26. In FY25, there were two such large customers contributing ₹1,778 crore.
flags: The company faces contingent liabilities of about ₹390 crore from disputed tax demands, representing approximately 19% of its net worth.
Revenue from the domestic subsidiary's largest accounts fell sharply, with sales from customers exceeding the 10% revenue threshold dropping from ₹1,778 crore in FY25 to ₹990 crore in FY26.

reports.auditor: The auditor noted a limitation in the audit scope for the standalone accounts. These accounts include three joint operations with ₹89.4 crore of revenue whose financial information is unaudited and was merely furnished by management.
reports.contingent: The company reported capital commitments of ₹55 crore for its battery energy storage (BESS) operations at the end of March 2026. This is a reduction from ₹173 crore a year earlier.
reports.other: The report highlighted a major NTPC battery energy storage order worth ₹1,128 crore, which includes 15-year operations and maintenance with technical support from Energy Vault. It also showed FY26 capital work in progress of ₹64 crore for the battery plant, and noted that a 104.4 kWh battery pack cleared international safety testing.
flags: The standalone accounts include three joint operations with ₹89.4 crore of revenue whose financials are completely unaudited and rely solely on management figures.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion with no emphasis of matter. They included a key audit matter regarding revenue recognition on the percentage-of-completion method.
reports.relatedParties: The company has borrowings of ₹ 75 crore owed to the promoter, Anand Pandit. It paid about ₹ 0.96 crore in office rent to promoter-linked entities. There are many promoter-family entities involved, including film production LLPs like Aish Motion Pictures and Bombay Masti Films, though management claims there are no material related-party transactions.
reports.contingent: The company faces a ₹ 10 crore GST show-cause notice for FY21, FY22, and FY24 under Section 74, which relates to fraud or suppression, received after the year-end. There are also outstanding bank guarantees of ₹ 15.7 crore.
reports.other: The annual report notes that revenue is recognised using the percentage-of-completion method, meaning revenue tracks construction progress rather than handovers. It also records that ₹ 170.6 crore of promoter loans were repaid in FY25. There are no pledged shares.
flags: The company received a ₹ 10 crore GST show-cause notice for fraud or suppression after the financial year closed.
Profit is booked well before cash comes in due to percentage-of-completion accounting, creating a significant cash conversion risk.
The presence of numerous promoter-family entities, including unrelated film production LLPs, is a corporate governance point of concern.

reports.auditor: Mittal & Associates gave a clean opinion with no key audit matters. The CARO report found no defaults, no fraud, and no deviation in the use of rights-issue funds. The internal auditor was changed in April 2025.
reports.relatedParties: In FY26, the managing director received ₹4.98 crore in pay, up from ₹2.61 crore in FY25. Total pay for key management and directors was about ₹8.2 crore. The company also paid ₹1.2 crore in rent to the managing director. A ₹2.43 crore interest-free director loan was repaid.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include income-tax disputes of ₹1.19 crore, up from ₹0.56 crore, which contains an assessment year 2015-16 demand of ₹0.70 crore. There are also bank guarantees to customs of ₹0.62 crore. These are secured by the managing director's personal fixed deposit.
reports.outlook: The company processes and distributes over 40 gases to more than 200 customers across 15 industries. Management says it continues to optimise plant utilisation. It has signed an agreement with Rajasthan for a new HFO manufacturing plant, with plant and machinery costs estimated at ₹200 crore.
reports.other: The company reports a single business segment for the sale of gases, with revenue from operations at ₹430.7 crore. It held ₹276.7 crore in unspent rights-issue cash meant for plant and machinery. IPO funds spent on working capital reached ₹102.7 crore. A ₹1.65 crore provision write-back was booked.
flags: Total pay for key management and directors was about ₹8.2 crore, which took up roughly 19% of the annual profit.
Rights issue expenses were very high at ₹36 crore, consuming about 10% of the gross ₹363.9 crore raised.
IPO spending on working capital reached ₹102.7 crore, overshooting the original ₹95 crore target.
The company does not disclose any sales breakdown by product, customer, or exports, grouping everything into a single segment.
The headline revenue and profit figures are boosted by other income, including a ₹1.65 crore provision write-back.

reports.auditor: MSK A & Associates LLP gave an unmodified opinion. The key audit matter identified in their report was revenue recognition.
reports.relatedParties: The company deals with several promoter-family firms. It buys from Asahi Glass Plant Inc., Reliability Engineering Industry, ATR Asahi Process Systems, and Schematic Engineering. It sells to Standard Equipment Leasing Services and Schematic. It pays rent to S2 Engineering Services/Equipment and a director, and receives services from Stylosoft LLP. Purchases from these firms rose sharply in FY26, with several entries of ₹10–15 crore each compared to ₹1–2 crore in FY25. The note's layout prevents calculating exact totals. Remuneration to key managers and relatives was ₹2.8 crore.
reports.contingent: Standalone contingent liabilities at March 2026 include an income-tax reassessment of ₹1.65 crore for AY2020-21 from a search on Hetero Group entities. There are also bank guarantees of ₹7.8 crore and letters of credit of ₹16.6 crore. Corporate guarantees for subsidiary loans rose to ₹57 crore, up from ₹25 crore the prior year. Promoters have personally guaranteed group loan lines of ₹110–270 crore. The standalone notes also show capital commitments of ₹6.5 crore.
reports.outlook: The Directors' report notes that subsidiaries Scigenics and C2C are targeting about ₹60 crore each in FY27 revenue.
reports.other: The standalone accounts reported only one operating segment for glass-lined reactors and related equipment. The Directors' report lists several subsidiaries, including 100%-owned S2 Engineering and Standard Engineering Inc. USA. Out of ₹232 crore in IPO proceeds, ₹185.6 crore was used by March 2026, including ₹130 crore to repay debt. Unused funds include ₹19 crore for S2 Engineering capital expenditure and ₹25 crore for general purposes. Hetero Infrastructure appears in board profiles in the corporate governance section.
flags: Purchases from related-party promoter-family firms rose sharply in FY26, with several entries jumping to ₹10–15 crore each.
The layout of the related-party note prevents readers from calculating exact transaction totals.
Contingent liabilities include a ₹1.65 crore income-tax reassessment linked to a search on Hetero Group entities.
The exact relationship with Hetero Infrastructure is unclear despite it appearing in board and director profiles in the annual report.
Corporate guarantees for subsidiary loans more than doubled to ₹57 crore from ₹25 crore a year earlier.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unqualified opinion and listed no key audit matters for the standalone accounts. The CARO report noted a ₹100 crore term loan from HDFC that was taken to buy AMW.
reports.relatedParties: The company gave a ₹133.15 crore loan to its subsidiary AMW, and has ₹8.3 crore of interest receivable from it. Key management personnel pay was ₹15.7 crore, with the managing director earning 268 times the median employee's pay. Promoter-group entities like SAB Industries and Steel Strips Infrastructure are listed as related parties.
reports.contingent: The company had capital commitments of ₹155.1 crore at the end of March 2026. This was an increase from ₹99.1 crore the year before.
reports.other: The annual report showed that the Chief Financial Officer changed in November 2025. The analyst also searched the annual report and found no disclosure of the ₹400 to ₹500 crore in factoring limits the company uses.
flags: The company uses ₹400 to ₹500 crore of factoring that is kept off the balance sheet and hidden from the annual report.
Management regularly provides conflicting figures for capacity, utilisation, and profit margins.
The managing director's compensation is exceptionally high at 268 times the median employee's pay.
The company experienced management turnover with a change in the Chief Financial Officer in November 2025.
Upcoming capital expenditures of roughly ₹600 crore are significantly higher than recent operating cash flows, which will push debt higher.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an emphasis of matter on the standalone accounts regarding a ₹3,654.75 crore exposure to a wholly owned subsidiary, warning it may hurt company functioning. They also highlighted wrongfully invoked bank guarantees of ₹441.33 crore and ₹106.98 crore, plus ₹24.86 crore of remediation costs. These are carried as recoverable without provisions. Auditor Kalyaniwalla & Mistry will leave at the 2026 AGM, while Deloitte will continue.
reports.relatedParties: As of March 2026, major shareholders are Reliance New Energy at 32.49%, Shapoorji Pallonji & Co at 6.94%, and Kainaz Daruvala at 5.57%. The former promoters, the SP Group and the Daruvala family, have agreed to indemnify the company for net claims above ₹300 crore.
reports.contingent: The annual report discloses about ₹3,800 crore in counter-claims. A US subcontractor arbitration resulted in a dismissed ₹485.64 crore recovery claim. Instead, the subcontractor was awarded ₹57.85 crore, ₹36.61 crore in interest, and ₹30.84 crore in costs. This created a ₹610.94 crore total charge that is not indemnified.
reports.outlook: The company is executing an EPC portfolio of 27.3 GWp across 20 countries, with over 10 GW under execution in India. The company works with repeat clients across public sector units and conglomerates. To support this scale, headcount was increased from 2,500 to 3,459 employees, which included hiring about 100 graduate engineer trainees.
reports.other: The company recorded a standalone FY26 loss of ₹2,510 crore. This was driven by ₹2,802 crore in exceptional items due to the impairment of investments in and loans to a wholly owned subsidiary. Consolidated FY26 accounts included exceptional items of ₹610.94 crore. Additionally, the CEO's remuneration exceeded the Schedule V limit due to company losses, requiring shareholder approval.
flags: The auditor warned that a ₹3,654.75 crore exposure to a subsidiary could adversely affect the company's functioning.
Wrongfully invoked bank guarantees of ₹441.33 crore and ₹106.98 crore are being carried as recoverable without any provision.
A failed US arbitration led to a non-indemnified charge of ₹610.94 crore.
The annual report discloses roughly ₹3,800 crore in counter-claims.
The CEO's remuneration exceeded legal limits because of the company's financial losses.

reports.auditor: Walker Chandiok & Co (Grant Thornton) gave an unqualified opinion. They included a key audit matter regarding revenue recognition, specifically concerning discounts and variable consideration.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid ₹1.3 crore in rent to Sterling Technologies, a promoter entity. It also donated ₹1.1 crore for corporate social responsibility to the promoter family foundation. Small legal fees were paid to Swarup & Company, the firm of independent director Shailendra Swarup.
reports.contingent: Capital commitments stood at ₹8.2 crore at the end of March 2026. Contingent liabilities included ₹1.1 crore for service tax plus ₹0.9 crore in interest, and about ₹6 crore for income tax appeals across four years. There was also ₹7.9 crore for deferred customs duty on imported machines.
reports.other: The standalone profit included an exceptional gain of ₹9.5 crore from DMRC land compensation. Key management compensation was ₹18.3 crore, including ₹5.8 crore in share-based pay. Director Jaideep Wadhwa received ₹7.6 crore. The company experienced management turnover, with a new CFO and two company secretaries during the year.
flags: Key management compensation of ₹18.3 crore was very high compared to the consolidated net profit of ₹29.3 crore.
The company experienced management churn during the year, including the departure of its CFO in December 2025 and having two company secretaries.

reports.auditor: Auditor PwC included an emphasis of matter regarding a $101.25 million (about ₹900 crore) unprovided judgment against the US subsidiary. The CARO report confirmed no debt defaults and noted guarantees of ₹45 crore and ₹347 crore. CARO also reported slight delays in depositing taxes and provident-fund dues.
reports.relatedParties: In FY26, group purchases were ₹295 crore, including about ₹265 crore from Vedanta Ltd. Group sales were ₹350 crore, comprising ₹176 crore to Vedanta Ltd, ₹57 crore to Hindustan Zinc, and ₹56 crore to STL Networks. The non-STL-Networks part of ₹294 crore roughly matched STL Digital's revenue. The company gave a ₹347 crore guarantee for STL Networks and had ₹3,434 crore in pass-through banking and collections pending separation.
reports.contingent: The company has not provided for a $101.25 million (about ₹900 crore) trade-secrets judgment against its US subsidiary, which is currently on appeal with a $41.53 million bond posted. It has also issued guarantees of ₹45 crore and a ₹347 crore guarantee specifically for STL Networks.
reports.other: In FY26, the optical segment generated ₹4,486 crore in revenue and ₹606 crore in EBITDA, representing a 13.5% margin. The STL Digital IT-services arm reported ₹284 crore in revenue and ₹3 crore in EBITDA. No promoter shares were declared as pledged in FY26. Managerial pay exceeded legal limits by ₹11 crore, which required shareholder approval at the AGM.
flags: The auditor included an emphasis of matter regarding a $101.25 million (about ₹900 crore) unprovided judgment against the US subsidiary.
Managerial pay exceeded legal limits by ₹11 crore and required shareholder approval.
The auditor noted slight delays in depositing statutory tax and provident-fund dues.
The company has ₹3,434 crore in pass-through banking and collections pending separation with related party STL Networks.

reports.auditor: The auditor included an emphasis of matter regarding a November 2023 Income Tax search, noting assessment orders demanding ₹2.45 crore in extra tax, which are under appeal. A CARO remark stated that stock statements reported to banks did not match the books; receivables reported to lenders were higher by ₹19 to ₹35 crore each quarter, while inventory was lower by ₹16 to ₹27 crore. The auditor also flagged an audit trail gap where one accounting software failed to log direct database changes.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings were limited to pay for key management personnel, which included ₹1.58 crore for the managing director, and small balances with entities linked to the promoters.
reports.contingent: The company reported small contingent liabilities totaling ₹18 crore. This included ₹14.7 crore for indirect tax, ₹2.2 crore for direct tax, and ₹0.65 crore for provident fund disputes, plus an additional ₹7.1 crore in interest. Capital commitments of ₹52.9 crore remained to be executed as of March 2026.
reports.outlook: The management discussion highlighted that the company's heavily backward-integrated manufacturing plants are designed to support up to ₹3,000 crore in revenue. After five years of capital spending and retail store roll-outs, management's primary focus for the future is to achieve operating leverage on this fixed asset base.
reports.other: The company operates in a single reported segment, 'Kitchen and Home appliances,' and does not disclose segment margins. True net debt stood at ₹171 crore, which included a ₹76 crore sale-and-leaseback liability for a plant that was accounted for as a loan. High depreciation of ₹80 crore and interest of ₹30 crore consumed most of the operating profit.
flags: An income tax search resulted in a ₹2.45 crore tax demand that is currently being appealed.
Receivables and inventory reported to lending banks did not match the company's books in any quarter of the financial year.
An accounting software used by the company lacked a proper audit trail because it did not log direct database changes.
True net debt included a ₹76 crore sale-and-leaseback liability for a plant, which was accounted for as a loan.

reports.auditor: The auditor provided an unmodified opinion. The report highlighted key audit matters concerning the impairment of goodwill and intangible assets, which involve non-current assets worth ₹3,314 crore. The auditor also flagged US gross-to-net accruals, including chargebacks, rebates, and Medicaid, as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: The company spun out OneSource, formerly known as Stelis, which is a promoter-linked biologics and CDMO unit. Strides retained a stake of roughly ₹320 crore in OneSource, and related-party trading continues between them.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small. They consist mainly of tax disputes for approximately ₹83 to ₹85 crore, along with another dispute for ₹35 crore.
reports.other: The company is still booking exceptional items for legacy recall and settlement costs related to ranitidine (NDMA) and losartan (azide). For FY26, these net exceptional items amounted to ₹32 crore.
flags: Legacy recall and settlement costs for ranitidine and losartan are still impacting the company, resulting in a ₹32 crore net exceptional charge in FY26.
Strides continues to engage in related-party trading with its spun-out, promoter-linked business, OneSource.

reports.auditor: The auditor, Rajan Chhabra & Co., issued a clean opinion with no qualifications or emphasis of matter. The only key audit matters were revenue cut-off and inventory valuation, which included a ₹0.22 crore provision and a ₹0.14 crore reversal. The CARO report confirmed that the company's disputed statutory dues match its listed contingent liabilities.
reports.relatedParties: Promoter family pay included ₹2.80 crore for Madhu Bhushan Khurana, ₹2.73 crore for Sidhartha Khurana, and ₹1.49 crore for Shilpa Arora, alongside other family salaries. The company made ₹4.7 crore in sales to its US subsidiary, Bikerz US, leaving a ₹3.2 crore receivable. Bikerz US was purchased from a promoter-linked entity for ₹2.56 crore in 2024. The company made no loans to promoters.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were small and totaled ₹3.7 crore. This amount consisted of ₹2.1 crore in bank guarantees and a series of disputed statutory dues. The disputed taxes included ₹0.32 crore for service tax, ₹0.59 crore for GST, and ₹0.42 crore for income tax.
reports.outlook: Management expects the Indian helmet market to grow by 6.1% a year, expanding from 26 million units in 2024 to 35 million by 2029. A proposed rule requiring two certified helmets with every new two-wheeler will widen this market. The unorganized sector's market share is expected to drop from 20-30% to 10-15% within three years. To support this growth, a ₹160 crore expansion at Facility V will increase annual capacity from 9.5 million to 12.5 million units.
reports.other: The company listed in November 2025 through an IPO that was entirely an offer for sale, meaning it received no new funds. It operates as a single reportable segment for helmets and accessories, so it does not disclose separate segment margins. Export revenue jumped 32.3% to ₹128.6 crore, rising from 16.75% to 20% of total sales. However, the company's inventory turnover fell by 26.6% during the year.
flags: Inventory turnover dropped sharply by 26.6% during the year, prompting the auditor to highlight inventory valuation as a key audit matter.
The US subsidiary, Bikerz US, was purchased from a promoter-linked entity for ₹2.56 crore.

reports.auditor: Mittal Goel & Associates (Chandigarh) gave an unmodified opinion. Revenue recognition was highlighted as a key audit matter. The report confirmed the audit trail operated all year with no tampering found.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings were small. They included sales to Gourmet House, which is linked to key management, and reimbursements with Aica Vstyle in Malaysia. The managing director's remuneration was about ₹3.1 crore.
reports.contingent: The company has disputed income tax of about ₹15 crore, primarily ₹12.4 crore for AY2018-19, and disputed GST of about ₹0.2 crore. Unfinished capital contracts stood at roughly ₹116 crore. Large export obligations under advance licences of about ₹1,064 crore carry penalty risks if unmet.
reports.outlook: The annual report notes macroeconomic risks, stating that the war in West Asia has raised freight costs as well as prices for phenol and melamine.
reports.other: The company reports one segment for laminates and allied products, with no customer exceeding 10% of revenue. Capital work-in-progress rose to ₹221 crore. Year-end receivables were ₹208 crore and inventory was ₹218 crore. Total cash and bank balances of ₹23.6 crore were offset by short-term borrowings of ₹29.1 crore. Several family relatives and two whole-time directors resigned in February 2026.
flags: The company faces pending disputed income tax claims of about ₹15 crore and GST of ₹0.2 crore.
Export obligations under advance licences are massive at roughly ₹1,064 crore, posing a penalty risk if export targets fall short.
Two whole-time directors and several family relatives abruptly resigned in February 2026.
Despite being branded as debt-free, liquidity is thin with year-end cash and bank balances lower than short-term borrowings.
Forex hedging is very thin for an export-led business, resulting in a ₹3.4 crore mark-to-market loss during the year.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters included tax litigation, a ₹2.78 crore exceptional labour-code charge, and bargain-purchase accounting for the Thailand plant acquisition, which recorded a gain of ₹367.6 crore. The CARO report noted no defaults or fraud.
reports.relatedParties: In FY26, the company paid a royalty of ₹2.62 crore to the promoter company, Shiva Performance Materials, up from ₹1.77 crore in FY25. It sold goods worth ₹24.75 crore to the promoter and made purchases of ₹5.48 crore. It also paid ₹5.80 crore for services from promoter-linked SES Engineering and paid a ₹43.91 crore dividend to the promoter.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities at March 2026 were ₹49.7 crore, including ₹34.0 crore for income tax disputes and ₹10.6 crore for excise and service tax. Capital commitments stood at ₹104 crore. The company also gave parent guarantees of approximately ₹222 crore and ₹166 crore to back its Thailand acquisition loans.
reports.outlook: Management expects Indian ABS demand to grow 7 to 8% annually until FY30, and polystyrene demand to grow 5 to 6%. The company put further polystyrene expansion on hold because its extra GPPS capacity is under-used due to weak demand and imports. A separate HIPS plant is still being studied.
reports.other: The company reports only one segment, Engineering Polymers, and does not disclose product volume splits. Standalone India volumes grew 5% to 195 KT in FY26, generating revenue of ₹2,640 crore and a PAT of ₹234.3 crore. March 2026 borrowings were ₹309 crore, largely for the Thailand acquisition. Promoter holding fell significantly from 62.73% to 46.24% during the period.
flags: The company pays royalty fees to a promoter entity, Shiva Performance Materials, which increased to ₹2.62 crore in FY26.
Promoter holding in the company fell sharply from 62.73% in March 2024 to 46.24% by June 2024.
The extra polystyrene production capacity is currently under-used due to cheap imports and weak demand, forcing the company to pause its expansion plans.
The company operates solely in one reportable segment and refuses to disclose product-wise volume splits, limiting visibility into specific business lines.
The Thailand operations are burdened with bank debt repayable up to 2030, which the parent company has had to back with financial guarantees.
