reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. They included a key audit matter regarding ₹31.1 crore of internal development costs for project-linked know-how and payroll that were capitalized as intangible assets under development, noting this required judgement on future viability.
reports.relatedParties: Sales to related parties, primarily Maruti Suzuki, accounted for a massive 82% of total sales in FY26, slightly down from 85% in FY25. Shareholders approved transactions with Maruti Suzuki for up to ₹3,048 crore for the year.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities rose to ₹79.5 crore, up from ₹47.8 crore the previous year. This consisted of disputed customs claims of ₹37.6 crore, GST issues of ₹20.2 crore, income tax claims of ₹11.1 crore, and workmen claims of ₹6.9 crore.
reports.other: The company recorded royalty expenses of ₹54.6 crore in FY26, up from ₹50.8 crore the prior year, representing technology payments to its collaborator.
flags: Customer concentration is exceptionally high, with 82% of sales relying on related parties like Maruti Suzuki.
Contingent liabilities surged to ₹79.5 crore due to rising customs and GST disputes.
The auditor raised a key audit matter over ₹31.1 crore of capitalized internal development costs, which rely on management's judgement of future viability.

reports.auditor: The group auditor (S R B C & Co, EY) gave an unmodified opinion. They did not audit 57 subsidiaries holding ₹7,060 crore of assets and ₹7,127 crore of revenue, which is roughly 73% of group revenue. Key audit matters included revenue timing, hedge accounting, purchase-price allocation, and tax contingencies at Sudarshan Colorants India.
reports.relatedParties: The CMD received ₹16.1 crore in pay for FY26, which represented about 39% of the consolidated net profit of ₹41 crore. Additionally, promoter holding fell from 35.8% to 8.2% after the P.R. Rathi family was reclassified as public following his resignation as Chairman.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are rising, including ₹189 crore in GST and VAT disputes, ₹36 crore for Maharashtra electricity duty, and ₹20 crore for excise. Provisions of ₹353 crore were made for inherited contingent liabilities, heavily driven by a ₹264 crore decommissioning liability. Disputed invoices of ₹18.5 crore from the Heubach administrator were not booked.
reports.other: For FY26, the pigments segment reported ₹9,525 crore in revenue with ₹582 crore in EBITDA, while the RIECO equipment segment posted ₹263 crore in revenue and ₹9 crore in EBITDA. Total capex was ₹270 crore. The distressed Heubach purchase resulted in a ₹1,196 crore bargain-purchase gain booked directly to capital reserve. A ₹32 crore exceptional charge was recorded for labour codes.
flags: The principal auditor did not audit 57 subsidiaries that account for approximately 73% of the group's total revenue.
The CMD's pay of ₹16.1 crore consumed about 39% of the company's total consolidated net profit in FY26.
Contingent tax liabilities are increasing, with ₹189 crore tied up in GST and VAT disputes.
An inherited decommissioning liability will cause a future cash drain of an undiscounted ₹388 crore over about 8 years.
The company has not booked ₹18.5 crore in disputed invoices from the Heubach administrator's group company.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unqualified opinion. Key audit matters included subsidiary investment impairment and revenue recognition. The auditor specifically highlighted a reversal of a previous ₹41.3 crore impairment for the UK subsidiary, of which ₹28.8 crore was reversed as a gain this year.
reports.relatedParties: The company sold goods worth ₹114.6 crore to its 46.79% promoter, TVS Sundram Fasteners Pvt Ltd. This increased from ₹110.6 crore in FY25. At the end of the year, ₹25.8 crore was receivable from the promoter, down from ₹50.1 crore last year. These transactions are disclosed as arm's length.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small and dropped to ₹28.7 crore from ₹36.7 crore the previous year. The total includes ₹18.2 crore for indirect taxes, ₹4.8 crore for sales tax, and ₹4.7 crore for income tax.
reports.other: Promoter pay consumed about 3.3% of standalone profit. MD Arathi Krishna was paid ₹9.99 crore and Joint MD Arundathi Krishna ₹9.32 crore, representing 129 and 121 times the median pay. Exceptional items flattered the yearly profit by a net ₹17.8 crore, driven by a ₹28.8 crore impairment reversal minus an ₹11.0 crore gratuity charge. Financial support for subsidiaries included ₹289.9 crore in investments, ₹15.5 crore in loans, and ₹8.2 crore in guarantees.
flags: The company makes material, recurring related-party sales to its promoter holding company, which totalled ₹114.6 crore this year.
Promoter compensation is exceptionally high, with the two managing directors earning 129 and 121 times the median employee pay.
Profits for the year were flattered by a net ₹17.8 crore from exceptional items.
The company continues to support weaker subsidiaries, carrying ₹289.9 crore in investments alongside loans and outstanding guarantees.

reports.auditor: The auditor drew attention to a ₹14.0 crore receivable from a former partnership firm. This amount is in dispute and challenged in the Bombay High Court, and the firm's accounts are unavailable. The auditor also raised questions about the recoverability of a ₹17.3 crore investment in the Piramal Sunteck Realty joint venture.
reports.contingent: The group's share of claims not acknowledged as debts is about ₹0.8 crore in the joint venture note, with no large items reported.
reports.other: Revenue is recognised mainly at the time of possession. The percentage-of-completion method is used for some projects.
flags: The auditor highlighted a disputed ₹14.0 crore receivable from a former partnership firm whose accounts are unavailable.
The auditor questioned the recoverability of a ₹17.3 crore investment in the Piramal Sunteck Realty joint venture.

reports.auditor: Goodwill impairment testing for Wescon and Luxlite, valued at ₹158.0 cr, was highlighted as a key audit matter. Under an Other Matter paragraph, the auditor noted that 15 subsidiaries are audited by other firms. These subsidiaries account for ₹2,368.6 cr in revenue (about 62% of the group total) and ₹1,927.6 cr in assets, meaning the consolidated opinion relies heavily on other auditors.
reports.relatedParties: The company gave comfort letters to its loss-making subsidiaries, Luxlite and Suprajit USA. It also provided corporate guarantees of ₹553.7 cr ($58.5m) for bank loans taken by Suprajit USA. Additionally, the company has a 50:50 joint venture with Chuo Spring (Japan) to make transmission cables in India.
reports.contingent: The company faces two GST show-cause notices for July 2017 to March 2023 regarding product classifications, demanding ₹137.4 cr. The Karnataka High Court granted an interim stay, so the company expects no liability and made no provision. There are also outstanding corporate guarantees of ₹553.7 cr ($58.5m) for Suprajit USA's bank loans.
reports.other: Revenue by customer location for FY26 included ₹1,668.5 cr from India (44%), ₹896.2 cr from the USA (23%), ₹38.2 cr from Morocco, and ₹1,221.9 cr from the rest of the world. The company's investment in its loss-making Luxlite subsidiary was written down by ₹79.2 cr. Promoter holding stands at 45.26%, and the annual report discloses no pledged shares.
flags: The company received GST show-cause notices demanding ₹137.4 cr, for which no provision has been made.
The company has issued ₹553.7 cr in corporate guarantees for a subsidiary's bank loans.
The investment in the loss-making Luxlite subsidiary had to be written down by ₹79.2 cr.
Goodwill has risen to ₹158.0 cr, with impairment testing flagged as a key audit matter.
Other audit firms audit 15 subsidiaries representing 62% of the group's revenue, rather than the main group auditor.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unqualified opinion. They included key audit matters regarding inventory valuation, because raw material prices swing, and the capitalization of the new ABS plant.
reports.relatedParties: The company sold goods worth ₹129 crore to its promoter, Supreme Industries. These sales were made at market rates.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were very small. They consisted of ₹17 crore for disputed income tax and ₹3 crore for indirect tax claims.
reports.outlook: Management expects compounding volumes to grow by 30% in FY27. They aim to operate the ABS plant at 75% to 80% of its curtailed capacity. Capital expenditure of roughly ₹250 crore is planned for FY27. Management warned that China is now self-sufficient in polystyrene, forcing Asian exporters to redirect material to India. They also noted that zero import duties on polymers would hurt local producers.
reports.other: The company operates as a single styrenics segment and does not disclose product-wise revenue. During the year, it acquired an 80% stake in a subsidiary, Xmold Polymers, for ₹31 crore. The remaining 20% is due by March 2027 to complete a total purchase price of ₹39 crore.
flags: The newly commissioned ABS plant suffered a critical equipment failure, curtailing its effective capacity to just 65%.
The company operates under a single reporting segment and obscures exact product performance by not disclosing product-wise revenues or ABS volumes.
Asian polystyrene exporters are redirecting their surplus into India because China is now self-sufficient.
Management warned that domestic producers will be hurt by the government's zero import duty policy on polymers.
Auditors highlighted inventory valuation as a key audit matter because raw material prices are highly volatile.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters included revenue recognition (cut-off, price-variation claims, liquidated damages) and the valuation and existence of inventories. The accounts use Indian GAAP, not Ind AS. Under CARO, there were no defaults or disputed statutory dues. However, quarterly stock and debtor statements submitted to banks differed from the company's books by 4% to 5% on debtors every quarter, which was explained as being based on provisional books.
reports.relatedParties: Supreme holds 90% of Danya Electric Company, while its managing director Vee Rajmohan holds 7.5% and director K V Pradeep holds 2.5%. In FY26, Supreme made purchases of ₹25.6 crore and sales of ₹24.6 crore with Danya. The company sought approval for up to ₹125 crore of related-party dealings, including loans and guarantees up to ₹25 crore, which equals 299% of Danya's turnover. Danya is also listed as a source of customer orders.
reports.contingent: The only contingent liability recorded is a ₹14.7 crore corporate guarantee given to IndusInd Bank for Danya Electric Company's loans. There are no tax demands. Notably, no capital commitments were recorded at March 2026, even though a tank factory project has been announced.
reports.outlook: The management discussion notes that combined capacity increased from 2,500 MVA to about 9,000 MVA after the ₹100 crore Kannur plant was capitalised in FY26. Management states that the real barrier to entry in the industry is "not capital but qualification." The report names several concentration risks, including reliance on southern states, a few large EPC clients, and a 30% exposure to government customers, who are described as slow payers.
reports.other: The company operates in one reportable segment. According to the ratio table in the annual report, the debt-to-equity ratio increased from 0.20 to 0.42. Meanwhile, the debt-service coverage ratio fell sharply from 8.6x to 2.5x, which the report explains is due to loan repayments rising by about 287%.
flags: The promoters personally own 10% of a subsidiary, Danya Electric Company, which trades heavily with the listed company and relies on it for bank guarantees.
The company is seeking approval for up to ₹125 crore in dealings with Danya, with loans and guarantees making up 299% of Danya's turnover.
Quarterly debtor statements submitted to banks differed from the company's internal books by 4% to 5% every quarter.
Despite announcing a new tank factory project, the company recorded zero capital commitments at the end of March 2026.
The debt-service coverage ratio deteriorated significantly from 8.6x to 2.5x due to a 287% increase in loan repayments.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave no qualification or adverse remark. Revenue recognition was noted as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid about ₹5.1 crore in CSR funds to the promoter's Satish Wagh Foundation. It paid lease rent to promoter-linked Vaibhav Chemicals and engaged in job-work with Samaira Pharmaceuticals. Key-management remuneration appears to be about ₹27.5 crore (up from ₹26.7 crore in FY25), which is high relative to the ₹209 crore net profit.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small, consisting of ₹0.8 crore for tax and ₹8 crore in bank guarantees.
reports.other: The company recorded an exceptional item of ₹0.46 crore for a labour-code gratuity.
flags: Key-management remuneration appears high at approximately ₹27.5 crore relative to the ₹209 crore net profit.
The company directed about ₹5.1 crore of its corporate social responsibility funds to the promoter's Satish Wagh Foundation.
The company engages in related-party transactions for lease rent and job-work with promoter-linked entities.

reports.auditor: BSR & Co gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters included the impairment of Australian goodwill and the timing of revenue recognition. The previous year's figures were restated because ₹21.6 crore of currency-translation losses were incorrectly booked directly to equity instead of other comprehensive income. Additionally, the secretarial audit noted a ₹5,000 fine from the NSE for a late related-party disclosure, which was later waived.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party transactions were minimal and clean. The company paid only ₹0.15 crore to a design firm linked to a director, in addition to the standard pay for key management personnel.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities increased to ₹25.9 crore from ₹9.7 crore the prior year. This was mainly driven by a central excise tax demand of ₹22.0 crore, up from ₹0.9 crore. Open capital commitments stood at just ₹5.4 crore at the end of March 2026.
reports.outlook: Management expects the ₹5,000 crore primary residential cooler market to double over the next five to seven years. New energy-rating norms and manufacturing rules are expected to help branded players by hurting unorganised metal-body makers. The company plans no manufacturing capex, choosing instead to run growth spending through the income statement for marketing and launch costs of direct-to-consumer sales and new products like water heaters.
reports.other: The company has one reported segment for air cooling and appliances. In FY26, India revenue fell to ₹684 crore with a ₹154 crore profit before exceptionals, while international revenue was ₹447 crore with an ₹11 crore profit before a massive ₹215 crore exceptional charge. Direct-to-consumer sales reached scale parity with its two largest e-commerce platforms combined. The board approved selling the Australian and Mexican subsidiaries in 2025 but reversed this decision in early 2026.
flags: Group CEO Amit Kumar resigned in March 2026, and the annual report names no replacement.
The board flip-flopped on capital allocation, approving the sale of its Australian and Mexican units in 2025 before abruptly reversing the decision in 2026.
The previous year's financials had to be restated because ₹21.6 crore of currency losses were incorrectly accounted for.
The management discussion report appears to contain careless copy-paste errors, bizarrely claiming a small subsidiary had $413 million in washing machine sales.
The auditor flagged the timing of when the company recognizes its revenue as a key audit matter.

reports.auditor: Auditor Walker Chandiok & Co gave an unmodified opinion. The standalone report includes an emphasis of matter regarding the amalgamation of SGS Tekniks and SGS Infosystems. The auditor noted an audit-trail exception because the edit log was not enabled at the database level for the holding company's accounting software. Key audit matters include ₹454.7 crore in goodwill (with ₹203.9 crore for Johari MedTech) and the accounting for the Elcome purchase and liability to buy its remaining 40% stake.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party transactions were modest. These included about ₹0.9 crore in sales to promoter-linked Infinx, travel expenses from Jetways, and rent or services from Tandon Holdings. Director Jayesh Doshi received an ESOP perquisite of ₹14.0 crore in FY26. Previously, a ₹47 crore upfront lease payment was made in FY25 to promoter-linked Ebony Electronics for a site.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small, consisting of tax and GST demands totalling roughly ₹5 crore. Capital commitments stood at ₹158 crore at the end of March 2026.
reports.outlook: The company operates 17 domestic plants plus one in Germany, employing over 10,000 people to serve about 350 customers. It highlights plans for a ₹1,600 crore greenfield facility for copper-clad laminates and PCBs. Management lists several risks, including Middle East and Red Sea disruptions, specialty-chemical shortages, and component lead times. It also notes that the electronics PLI scheme ended in March 2026.
reports.other: The annual report shows dependence on the largest customer fell sharply, dropping from ₹976 crore (26% of revenue) in FY25 to ₹618 crore (13%) in FY26. The 60% buyout of Elcome for ₹235 crore added ₹50.8 crore to FY26 operating EBITDA. The remaining 40% of Elcome will be bought in phases over about three years under an earn-out arrangement.
flags: The auditor noted that the edit log was not enabled at the database level for the holding company's accounting software.
Management highlighted supply chain risks including Middle East and Red Sea disruptions, specialty-chemical shortages, and component lead times.
The electronics PLI scheme, which contributed to other income, ended in March 2026.
Goodwill of ₹454.7 crore and the liability to buy the remaining 40% of Elcome were flagged as key audit matters.

reports.auditor: The audit was conducted by Maharishi & Co., a small firm in Jamnagar, which issued an unmodified opinion. The report included key audit matters regarding consolidation and the capitalisation of product-development costs, noting product intangibles of ₹4.8 crore at the end of March 2026.
reports.relatedParties: The CEO's relative, Shivani Arora, received ESOP shares with a fair value ₹7.1 crore higher than the exercise price in FY26. Additionally, the CEO waived ₹1.5 crore of approved pay while taking a company loan.
reports.other: The company is asset-light but capitalises development costs, spending ₹4.4 crore on intangibles and ₹6.2 crore on subsidiaries in FY26. Part of the staff cost is also capitalised to intangibles. At the end of March 2026, cash and bank balances were ₹22.9 crore, equity was ₹83 crore, and borrowings were about ₹1 crore. The company also lent a ₹5 crore inter-corporate deposit to Goenka Business & Finance Ltd at 12% interest, with ₹4.7 crore outstanding.
flags: A secretarial audit found that loans were made to the CEO and a director in violation of the Companies Act, although they were repaid by year-end.
Related-party transactions were executed without omnibus approval and exceeded approved limits, and the transaction figures reported to the exchange did not match the audited figures.
Governance lapses included unapproved payments to independent directors, missed audit-committee meetings, insider-trading control failures, and exchange fines for late board intimations.
Cash conversion is weak, generating only ₹9.5 crore in operating cash flow against a net profit of ₹26.4 crore in FY26.
Trade receivables increased by ₹10.6 crore, pushing debtor days to 145, which is unusually high for a SaaS model and contradicts management claims about collections.

reports.auditor: The auditor noted a key audit matter regarding the valuation of unquoted, fair-valued investments in group companies due to high estimation uncertainty. The standalone books recorded investments of ₹247 crore in joint venture stakes that are fair-valued.
reports.relatedParties: The annual report's AGM notice asked shareholders to approve related-party transactions up to ₹125 crore for FY27 with QH Talbros Pvt Ltd, including royalty and dividend receipts. In FY26, the company made sales of ₹75.4 crore to this associate firm, which is a promoter-family business where Umesh Talwar is a promoter director and Talbros holds a 5.83% stake.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were small at ₹4.5 crore, which included ₹2.55 crore for Faridabad development charges. Additionally, standalone capital commitments were only ₹4.1 crore as of March 2026.
reports.outlook: The annual report outlines the formation of a new 49:51 joint venture called Lohum Talbros CarbonTech, partnered with Lohum Cleantech. This venture focuses on recovered carbon black and devulcanised rubber, involving a total investment of approximately ₹70 crore over two years.
reports.other: The annual report provided descriptions of the company's four main business segments. These include gaskets and heat shields, hot forgings, a 50:50 joint venture with Marelli Suspension Systems Italy (MTCS), and a 50:50 joint venture with Marugo Rubber Japan (TMR).
flags: The auditor highlighted high estimation uncertainty in valuing the company's unquoted, fair-valued investments in group companies.
The company engages in substantial related-party sales with a promoter-family associate firm, QH Talbros Pvt Ltd.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion and reported no key audit matters.
reports.relatedParties: The company made ₹13.2 crore in sales to its promoter, Anupam Rasayan, in FY26, down from ₹17.6 crore in FY25. As of March 2026, it had a ₹13.2 crore receivable due from Anupam Rasayan.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small, consisting of GST claims of ₹1.3 crore, service tax and VAT of ₹0.1 crore, and an old sales-tax dispute of ₹0.5 crore. The company also holds bank guarantees and letters of credit totaling ₹51.8 crore.
reports.outlook: Management expects exports to grow to about 50% of the mix once the new R-32 plant is running. They project domestic solar-grade DHF demand will reach 150-210 KT by FY29-FY31 as India's solar cell capacity expands heavily.
reports.other: FY26 operating EBITDA was ₹112 crore with a PAT of ₹70.1 crore. Capacity utilisation was 101% for sulphuric acid, 95% for hydrofluoric acid, and 41% for specialty fluorides. Short-term borrowings were ₹93 crore against ₹21 crore in cash and ₹17 crore in current investments. Capital commitments stood at ₹257.7 crore.
flags: The company lost about ₹70 crore of hydrofluoric acid output in FY26 due to unplanned maintenance on its old plant.
The annual report's key managerial personnel table is garbled, making exact executive roles before January 2026 difficult to confirm.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters focused on goodwill impairment and revenue recognition, specifically high-volume IT billing, unbilled revenue, and credit notes. Additionally, the secretarial auditor noted that designated persons broke insider-trading rules through contra trades and pledging, which was reported to the exchanges.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities grew to ₹63.6 crore from ₹16.8 crore a year ago. This was largely driven by a ₹46.9 crore income-tax demand for not withholding tax on the 2018–19 Karix acquisition payment, though the seller has indemnified Tanla. The company also has ₹189 crore in bank guarantees and a ₹200 crore parent guarantee for a subsidiary.
reports.other: The company holds 8 granted patents and has 19 patent applications.
flags: Contingent liabilities increased sharply to ₹63.6 crore, mainly due to a ₹46.9 crore income tax demand.
The secretarial auditor reported that designated persons violated insider-trading rules through contra trades and pledging.
The company has a large ₹200 crore parent guarantee active for a subsidiary.

reports.auditor: The auditor noted key audit matters regarding the valuation of the company's US assets. Specifically, ₹9,072 crore of US mining rights remain on the books without being written down. Additionally, ₹426 crore for silica and nutraceutical plants are currently under impairment review.
reports.relatedParties: The company sells salt to Tata Consumer Products under a long-term arrangement that was approved by the board. Overall, the reported related-party balances are small.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities total roughly ₹2,000 crore. This includes ₹833 crore for income-tax disputes and ₹150 crore for indirect tax issues. There is also an ₹891 crore Kenyan land-rates demand; the company won at the Court of Appeal, but the county has appealed to the Supreme Court. Other claims account for about ₹100 crore.
reports.outlook: Management warns of oversupply risks from China. Global demand is expected to grow by only 0.2% in FY27, compared to approximately 3.8 million tonnes of new capacity. Furthermore, China's new 2 million tonnes per annum natural soda ash capacity in Inner Mongolia is flattening the company's low-cost advantage.
reports.other: The standalone Indian business is the main profit engine, reporting FY26 revenue of ₹4,831 crore and EBITDA of ₹954 crore. The farm segment, via Rallis India, has an extensive network of 7,200 dealers and 95,000 retailers. Fixed assets are heavy at ₹20,602 crore due to acquired mining rights and goodwill.
flags: The auditor highlighted ₹9,072 crore of un-impaired US mining rights and ₹426 crore of silica and nutraceutical plants as key audit matters.
The company faces roughly ₹2,000 crore in contingent liabilities, driven heavily by tax disputes and a Kenyan land-rates demand.
Management noted that massive Chinese capacity expansions are threatening to eliminate the cost advantage of the company's natural soda ash.

reports.auditor: The auditor's opinion was clean, with no emphasis of matter found. The auditor flagged two key audit matters: the percentage-of-completion revenue on fixed-price contracts due to estimate risks, and the purchase-price allocation and contingent consideration for the ES-Tec acquisition.
reports.relatedParties: The company has significant related-party dependence on its promoter group. In FY26, JLR billed ₹1,337 crore (about 24% of group revenue) and Tata Motors (CV) added ₹342 crore. For FY27, the company sought AGM approval for related-party transactions with JLR up to ₹1,750 crore, plus other approvals of ₹1,541 crore and ₹652.5 crore. Pricing is certified at arm's length.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small, totaling about ₹41 crore. These relate to bonus, income tax, GST, and service tax.
reports.outlook: The management discussion and analysis in the annual report explicitly lists top-5 client concentration as a key risk for the business.
reports.other: The Services segment earned ₹4,256 crore (77% of FY26 revenue), while Technology Solutions earned ₹1,249 crore (23%). By geography, India led with ₹2,227 crore, followed by the UK at ₹1,480 crore and North America at ₹1,277 crore. The ES-Tec acquisition created ₹365 crore in customer intangibles and ₹407 crore in goodwill, funded partly by a ₹569 crore unsecured bank term loan.
flags: JLR, a related party, accounts for a highly concentrated 24% of group revenue.
The management discussion and analysis cites top-5 client concentration as a key risk.
The auditor highlighted percentage-of-completion revenue on fixed-price contracts as a key audit matter due to growing estimate risks.
The ES-Tec acquisition added ₹407 crore of goodwill, which carries risk as it depends heavily on Volkswagen amid German automotive restructuring.

reports.auditor: NDJ & Co., a small Vadodara firm, gave an unqualified opinion. They highlighted four key audit matters: revenue cut-off, capitalisation of capex, inventory valuation, and recoverability of MAT credit. The audit trail operated throughout the year.
reports.relatedParties: Dealings are clean and limited to pay and dividends. The three executive promoters received about ₹1.7 crore each. Total benefits for key management personnel were ₹5.97 crore. Promoters hold 72.0% of the company, with no pledges reported.
reports.contingent: Total contingent liabilities are ₹14.0 crore. This includes ₹2.3 crore for indirect tax, featuring a ₹1.1 crore IGST refund dispute currently at the Supreme Court. It also includes ₹0.4 crore for direct tax, ₹3.8 crore in bank guarantees, and ₹7.6 crore in letters of credit.
reports.outlook: The Management Discussion states the Dahej facility can reach a peak revenue of ₹850 to ₹900 crore after debottlenecking, needing ₹10 to ₹12 crore in annual capex. Dahej land is nearly saturated, so growth beyond ₹800 to ₹850 crore requires the new Jolva site. The report also notes the current ratio fell from 2.76 to 1.63.
reports.other: The accounts show one reportable segment with no segment margins disclosed. Exports made up 76% of revenue at ₹381.8 crore, with subsidiaries in the US and Netherlands. About 36% of raw material purchases (₹99 crore out of ₹275 crore) were imported. The company carries a MAT credit of ₹41.1 crore as a deferred-tax asset. Cash tax is low at ₹7 crore because of SEZ benefits.
flags: A single customer accounts for 35% of total revenue and 43% of receivables.
The second-largest customer makes up 19% of revenue, showing high overall customer concentration.
The current ratio fell significantly from 2.76 to 1.63.
The company relies on imported raw materials, which made up 36% of purchases at ₹99 crore.
The auditor flagged the recoverability of a ₹41.1 crore MAT credit deferred-tax asset as a key audit matter.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unmodified opinion. Inventory valuation across the company's plants was highlighted as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: The company bought ₹53 crore of raw materials from TCPL Halma and ₹4.3 crore of services from Accura Reprotech, which are both promoter-influenced entities. Remuneration for key managerial personnel was ₹17.8 crore.
reports.contingent: The company has an outstanding EPCG export obligation of ₹201 crore, meaning duty-free machine imports must be matched by future exports. Other contingent liabilities include ₹11.3 crore for income tax, ₹13.8 crore for bank guarantees and letters of credit, ₹2.7 crore for GST, and ₹0.8 crore for excise.
reports.other: Packaging is the only reported segment. FY26 revenue growth was only 2.3% because exports were hit by Gulf shipping disruptions. The notes show a ₹13.5 crore exceptional charge related to labour codes. Executive Chairman K.K. Kanoria resigned in February 2026. The subsidiary Creative Offset Printers lost ₹4.4 crore on ₹54 crore turnover, and Accura Technik posted a small loss.
flags: The subsidiary Creative Offset Printers reported a loss of ₹4.4 crore on ₹54 crore in turnover.
The company carries a large ₹201 crore export obligation to match duty-free machine imports.
A ₹13.5 crore exceptional charge related to labour codes negatively impacted profits.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unmodified opinion on the financial statements. The auditor's report noted only one key audit matter, which was the revenue recognition on custom products.
reports.relatedParties: Managing Director Nikhil Kumar was paid about ₹5.1 crore in FY26. This included a ₹4.1 crore commission, up from a ₹3.3 crore commission in FY25. The company paid professional fees to Trilegal, where independent director Rahul Matthan is a founding partner. It also paid for vehicle servicing from Trident Automobiles, a business linked to the promoters.
reports.contingent: The company reported contingent liabilities of ₹122 crore for performance guarantees. It faces a disputed transfer-pricing tax demand of ₹19.9 crore for assessment year 2017-18, though recovery has been stayed by the Karnataka High Court. It also had capital commitments of ₹40 crore at the end of March 2026.
reports.outlook: The annual report identifies risks around heavy customer concentration and a strong dependence on the US gas and data-centre build-out. Management warns that if an original equipment manufacturer decides to re-source its supply or if data-centre projects pause, it would quickly hurt the business.
reports.other: The company makes generators for steam (up to 250 MW), gas turbines (up to 250 MVA), engines (up to 25 MVA), and hydro (up to 45 MW). Gas-engine generators were the top revenue contributor. Standalone and deemed exports formed 66% of sales, while top 10 customers provided 84% of revenue. It has a UK office for 40–200 MW designs and appointed its first CEO, Deepak Kumar Sinha, in April 2026. A ₹3 crore impairment on subsidiary DF Power Systems fully wrote off the ₹20.4 crore investment.
flags: The top 10 customers contributed a massive 84% of consolidated revenue, showing severe customer concentration.
The company relies heavily on US data-centre construction, creating a risk if projects pause or customers change suppliers.
The business wrote down its entire ₹20.4 crore investment in loss-making Indian subsidiary DF Power Systems after a final ₹3 crore impairment.
The company faces a disputed ₹19.9 crore transfer-pricing tax demand for assessment year 2017-18.

reports.auditor: Walker Chandiok & Co LLP gave an unmodified opinion. They noted a Key Audit Matter regarding goodwill impairment, specifically including ₹73 crore in older Australian goodwill. They also made audit-trail remarks for some entities. Additionally, eight subsidiaries with assets of ₹888 crore and revenue of ₹671 crore were audited by other auditors.
reports.relatedParties: The report notes that the former holding company, Nihal Fiscal Services, ceased to be the parent entity on November 28, 2025. No promoter pledges were reported.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small, consisting of disputed income tax of ₹8.4 crore, GST of ₹0.6 crore, sales tax of ₹0.4 crore, and service tax of ₹0.1 crore. Capital commitments were ₹178 crore at March 2026, mostly for the Chile plant, up from ₹2.7 crore the prior year.
reports.outlook: Management notes the global mill-liner market could reach US$4.59 billion by 2034. They expect blended gold and copper demand to grow about 3% a year until FY30. They also highlight that copper demand is projected to grow 40% by 2040, which will require roughly US$250 billion in investments and about 80 new mines.
reports.other: In segment results, consumables recorded FY26 revenue of ₹1,434 crore with a result of ₹197 crore, which was hit by acquisition costs. Equipment revenue was ₹269 crore with a result of ₹34 crore. The cash flow statement showed investing outflows of ₹991 crore and financing inflows of ₹1,690 crore reflecting deal funding.
flags: The auditor highlighted a Key Audit Matter concerning goodwill impairment, including ₹73 crore of older Australian goodwill.
The auditor's report contained audit-trail remarks for some entities.
Eight subsidiaries, representing ₹888 crore in assets and ₹671 crore in revenue, were audited by other accounting firms rather than the principal auditor.

reports.auditor: Walker Chandiok gave an unmodified opinion. The only exception noted was that the accounting software's audit trail was not enabled at the database level for the parent company and two subsidiaries.
reports.relatedParties: The company sold ₹6.6 crore in goods to joint venture PT Tempsens Asia Jaya and ₹4.8 crore to Tempsens GmbH. It bought ₹4.1 crore in goods from Pyrotech Electronics. Promoters Virendra and Vinay Rathi received ₹2.6 crore in pay. Aryan Rathi received ₹1.1 crore and Sonal Rathi received ₹0.6 crore. The company also repaid ₹4.9 crore in loans to the promoter family.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small. They include a ₹1.09 crore indirect tax claim and a ₹0.65 crore land claim from the Udaipur Collector regarding ex-Marathon land. Contracted capital commitments stood at just ₹1.3 crore.
reports.other: The company paid a small interim dividend with a 4% payout. It also granted 3.47 lakh employee stock options between September and October 2025, mostly priced at ₹123.
flags: The auditor noted that the accounting software's audit trail was not enabled at the database level for the parent company and two subsidiaries.
The company granted employee stock options mostly at ₹123, a steep discount to the ₹300 IPO price.

reports.auditor: Deloitte Haskins & Sells LLP gave an unmodified opinion with no key audit matters and no adverse CARO remarks. The only auditor remark was that the accounting software's audit trail was not enabled at the database level.
reports.relatedParties: The company pays a royalty of 2.5% of net sales to the parent group. Approximately 70% of exports go to group companies at transfer prices. The group withdrew its advance-pricing application for royalty and management-support charges, and transfer-pricing tax disputes for FY20, FY21, and FY23 are currently pending.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities reached ₹131.8 crore, up from ₹116.5 crore last year. This includes ₹88.7 crore for income tax, ₹19.7 crore for Maharashtra stamp duty on a 2019-20 demerger, ₹13.7 crore for customs, and ₹6.8 crore for GST disputes. Additionally, outstanding capital commitments stood at ₹157 crore.
reports.outlook: The management discussion notes that the company is extending its new damper technology to smaller A/B-segment cars. It also acknowledges that the company's absence from Maruti in the clean air segment cost it growth during the recent small-car boom.
reports.other: Value-added revenue for FY26 was ₹4,918 crore, nearly split between Clean Air (₹2,430 crore) and Advanced Ride Technologies (₹2,489 crore). All subsidiaries are profitable, with the material subsidiary holding the ride technologies business earning a ₹244 crore net profit. The company booked a ₹27.2 crore exceptional charge for a labour-code gratuity provision and paid massive pre-IPO dividends of ₹1,036.6 crore.
flags: Three customers account for roughly 50% of the company's total revenue.
Contingent liabilities stand at ₹131.8 crore, representing about 11% of net worth.
About 70% of exports are routed to related group companies, and the group has withdrawn its advance-pricing application for royalties.
Transfer-pricing tax matters for three prior fiscal years remain unresolved and pending appeal.
The statutory auditor flagged that the required audit trail was not enabled at the database level.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave a qualified opinion for both the standalone and consolidated financial statements. They flagged that the company created a ₹700 crore provision for contingencies by directly charging free reserves (₹494 crore from the general reserve and ₹206 crore from retained earnings) instead of the profit and loss account. This provision is recorded as a current liability. The auditor also highlighted ₹178.5 crore in tax litigation as a key audit matter.
reports.contingent: The auditor's report notes ₹178.5 crore in tax litigation as a key audit matter. The annual report also outlines a ₹700 crore provision for contingencies, which was created from free reserves to cover worst-case risks regarding geopolitics, supply chains, costs, and currency fluctuations.
reports.outlook: The annual report does not detail specific financial targets or capex plans for the year ahead. However, the board notes that business risks related to geopolitics, supply chains, costs, and currency are broad and not tied to any specific year or identifiable contract.
reports.other: The annual report lists four segments: Freight Car Division, Infra-Rail & Green Energy, Infra-Electrical, and a new Real Estate unit. In FY26 standalone results, the Freight Car segment made ₹285 crore in profit on ₹3,413 crore in revenue. The Infra-Rail & Green segment posted a ₹27 crore loss on ₹348 crore in revenue, while Infra-Electrical made a ₹66 crore profit on ₹610 crore in revenue. Customer advances jumped from ₹52 crore to ₹213 crore. The board recommended a dividend of ₹0.75 per share.
flags: The auditor issued a qualified opinion because a ₹700 crore contingency provision was charged directly to free reserves rather than the profit and loss account.
Any future losses absorbed by this ₹700 crore provision would bypass reported profit, making earnings quality harder to trust.
The auditor identified ₹178.5 crore in ongoing tax litigation as a key audit matter.
The Infra-Rail & Green Energy business is losing money, reporting a standalone loss of ₹27 crore in FY26.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The timing of revenue recognition and contract assets was named as a key audit matter. Under CARO, the auditor noted that a ₹38.6 crore land parcel is still titled in the old company name (Anveshan Heavy Engineering) pending with the revenue department.
reports.relatedParties: Dealings with Arvind group companies were small, consisting mainly of a licence purchase for about ₹1 crore and some services.
reports.contingent: Outstanding bank guarantees were ₹284 crore, down from ₹460 crore the year before. There are tax disputes of about ₹2.4 crore. An unquantified charter of demands from contract workers is pending at the labour court.
reports.other: Receivables stood at ₹416 crore, which included ₹197 crore in unbilled revenue. The company recorded a ₹1.5 crore net exceptional charge for new labour codes. The report notes the 100% purchase of Mabel Engineers in Chennai for ₹33 crore. A dividend of ₹12 per share was also declared.
flags: Receivables grew to ₹416 crore, including ₹197 crore of unbilled revenue, stretching debtor days to 185.
The auditor highlighted the timing of revenue recognition and contract assets as a key audit matter.
A ₹38.6 crore land parcel is still titled in the old company name.
An unquantified charter of demands from contract workers is pending at the labour court.

reports.auditor: Auditor B S R & Co. flagged ₹1,183 crore of goodwill as a key audit matter. 47 subsidiaries with ₹2,003 crore in assets were entirely unaudited, while 7 were audited by others. The consolidation software lacked a database-level audit trail until May 19, 2025, and Sterling's software trail was unverifiable. CARO adverse remarks highlighted statutory dues issues and property title deeds not held in the company's name, including the Kodai Valley View and Puri resorts carrying a combined ₹303.5 crore.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities stood at roughly ₹382 crore at March 2026, or about 15% of net worth. This included tax matters of ₹209.5 crore, luxury-tax appeals of ₹93.0 crore, disputed claims of ₹67.6 crore, an ED/FEMA penalty of ₹6.2 crore, and stamp duty of ₹4.9 crore. The company also reported capital commitments of ₹40.9 crore.
reports.outlook: The board approved a demerger of the resort business into a new listed entity, Sterling Holiday Resorts Ltd, with completion expected by Q1 FY28. The company is also co-developing a travel AI platform through a joint venture with Atirath Technologies.
reports.other: The board approved a generous payout to management, granting an ex-gratia payment of ₹17.1 crore to retiring executive chairman Madhavan Menon in May 2025. Following the Sterling demerger, shareholders will receive 0.81 Sterling shares per TCIL share, and TCIL shares will undergo a 4-for-1 consolidation reducing the face value to ₹3.
flags: 47 subsidiaries generating ₹938 crore in revenue and holding ₹2,003 crore in assets were not audited by anyone.
The consolidation software lacked a database-level audit trail until May 2025, and Sterling's third-party software audit trail could not be verified.
The auditor made adverse remarks regarding statutory dues and property title deeds not being in the company's name for resorts carrying over ₹303 crore.
Contingent liabilities amount to about 15% of net worth, including large disputed tax demands and an ED/FEMA penalty.
The company made a substantial ex-gratia payment of ₹17.1 crore to its retiring executive chairman.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unqualified opinion. The only key audit matter was the timing of capitalising ₹742 crore of additions and ₹100.7 crore of capital work-in-progress. The auditor confirmed compliance with the audit trail rule. The CARO report noted ₹7.4 crore in unpaid disputed dues.
reports.relatedParties: In FY26, the company bought goods worth ₹479 crore from Timken Wuxi, ₹359 crore from The Timken Corporation, and ₹60 crore from parent The Timken Company. It sold ₹298 crore to Timken Corporation and ₹201 crore to the parent. The company paid an ₹84 crore royalty. Timken GGB was bought from Timken Europe B.V. for ₹128.8 crore. For FY27, approved purchases from Timken Corporation rise to ₹708 crore and sales to ₹617 crore. The board states all deals are at arm's length.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities total about ₹182 crore. This includes a ₹103.6 crore provident-fund damages order related to closing the company's trust, which is under appeal in the Jharkhand High Court. It also includes ₹63.3 crore in transfer-pricing tax claims and ₹15.3 crore in GST claims. No provisions were made for these amounts. Open capital expenditure commitments stood at ₹83 crore at the end of March 2026, net of ₹46 crore in advances.
reports.outlook: The report estimates the Indian bearing market at 2.9 billion US dollars, growing over 9.4% a year. The company plans to start commercial production of GGB plain bearings at Bharuch in the second quarter of FY27. A new robotic line for rail components at Jamshedpur is slated for completion in the third quarter of FY27 to serve Indian, African, and North American markets.
reports.other: Revenue from India was ₹2,740 crore. Overseas sales were ₹679 crore, with US sales falling 15% to ₹268 crore and other exports rising 57% to ₹411 crore. One unnamed customer group accounted for ₹625 crore, or 18% of revenue. Cash and mutual funds fell to ₹268 crore due to capital spending, the GGB acquisition, and dividend payments. Inventory rose by ₹134 crore and receivables by ₹98 crore.
flags: Contingent liabilities are high at roughly ₹182 crore, including a ₹103.6 crore provident-fund damages order and ₹63.3 crore in transfer-pricing tax claims.
Related-party reliance is growing, with approved FY27 purchases from Timken Corporation expected to nearly double to ₹708 crore.
Exports to the US fell 15% to ₹268 crore in FY26, which contradicts management's commentary about strong North American demand.
The CARO report listed ₹7.4 crore of unpaid disputed dues.

reports.auditor: Auditors S.S. Kothari Mehta & Co. LLP gave unqualified standalone and consolidated opinions. They noted no key audit matters. Two of the foreign subsidiaries and the joint venture were audited by other auditors.
reports.relatedParties: The company sold goods worth about ₹18 crore to promoter-linked Fratelli Vineyards in FY26. It bought shipping services from B.G.K. Shipping LLP for about ₹5.4 crore and paid professional fees to a relative. The chairman provided loans, with ₹3 crore taken and ₹5.6 crore repaid during the year. The company also holds shares in promoter-linked BGK Infratech, which bought back some shares and had the remaining balance revalued to ₹19.4 crore.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include ₹0.43 crore in claims, roughly ₹0.5 crore in disputed taxes, and bank guarantees of about ₹9.9 crore. There is a land dispute with HSIIDC demanding ₹3.73 crore. An advance-licence export obligation of ₹32.9 crore is outstanding. Capital commitments stand at ₹19.7 crore. SBI term loans are backed by personal guarantees from B.K. and Gaurav Sekhri, a corporate guarantee, and a mortgage on a promoter company's farm-house property.
reports.outlook: The Management Discussion and Analysis highlights competition, noting over 500 tyre recyclers are registered on the regulatory portal. By March 2026, these recyclers processed 12.23 lakh tonnes and generated 11.69 lakh tonnes of recycling certificates. The supply of these certificates is ample, and they trade at the floor price. The Directors' Report notes that FY26 capex was funded through term loans, internal accruals, and an equity raise.
reports.other: Unsold recycling credits of ₹19.1 crore were booked on the balance sheet as realizable at March 2026, based on accrual accounting. Customer concentration rose, with one customer buying ₹54.4 crore (over 10% of standalone revenue) in FY26. The company consolidates several foreign entities and an associate. A management change saw CFO Ravindra Chhabra leave in March 2026, replaced by Abhay Kumar.
flags: Unsold recycling credits are booked as revenue on accrual before actual sale, creating risk since the supply of these certificates is ample.
Customer concentration increased, with a single customer accounting for over 10% of standalone revenue (₹54.4 crore) in FY26.
The company engaged in notable related-party dealings, including ₹18 crore in sales to a promoter-linked company and borrowing from the chairman.
A related-party valuation gain was recorded for shares held in promoter-linked BGK Infratech.
The annual report had to be reissued via a corrigendum to fix errors regarding the financial year footer and share counts of investee companies.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Revenue recognition was noted as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: The company buys content from Tips Films, a related party where promoters Kumar and Ramesh Taurani each own about 20%. In FY26, it bought ₹17.3 crore of audio-video rights and paid a ₹15.5 crore advance. Shareholders are asked to approve up to ₹60 crore in deals for FY27.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are tiny at ₹1.9 crore.
reports.other: Music is the company's only reported business segment. The board approved an open-market buyback of up to ₹44.5 crore at a price up to ₹750 per share. CEO Hari Nair left the business on April 30, 2026.
flags: Shareholders are being asked to approve up to ₹60 crore in related-party content purchases from a promoter-group company for FY27.
Pricing for related-party deals is only checked by a valuer after the project is already completed.
The CEO left on April 30, 2026, and no replacement has been found yet.

reports.auditor: The financial statements are unqualified, but the auditor gave a qualified internal-controls opinion. They found material weaknesses in reviewing the impairment of investments in an associate and a joint venture, a loss allowance on a joint venture loan, and a provision for collateral given for an associate's loan. An emphasis of matter was added regarding the restatement of FY25 results due to the Firema associate's audited losses.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include a financial undertaking to fund cash shortfalls for a wheel joint venture's loans, with Titagarh's share at ₹504 crore at year-end, up from ₹170 crore a year earlier. The company also faces ₹187.5 crore in disputed tax and legal claims, which were flat year-on-year, alongside a Gwalior municipal tax demand of ₹7.2 crore.
reports.other: FY26 total revenue was ₹3,186 crore. Freight earned ₹2,604 crore (profit ₹318 crore, 12.2%), passenger earned ₹539 crore (profit ₹77 crore, 14.3%), and shipbuilding earned ₹42 crore (loss ₹21 crore). Shipbuilding moved to a wholly owned subsidiary on January 1, 2026, for ₹114.88 crore. Wagon dispatches were 7,019 (59% capacity). Consolidated borrowings were ₹522 crore, cash ₹162 crore, and net debt ₹360 crore (net debt/equity 0.15, down from 0.22). Promoters hold 21.1 lakh warrants at ₹947 (₹200 crore, 25% paid). A ₹0.50 per share dividend was paid for FY25.
flags: The auditor qualified the internal-controls opinion due to material weaknesses in reviewing impairments and provisions for a joint venture and an associate.

An emphasis of matter highlighted that FY25 was restated, dropping reported profit from ₹317 crore to ₹90.6 crore after the Firema associate's actual audited loss was €104.7 million (₹948 crore) instead of €16.9 million.
Titagarh took a ₹112.7 crore investment impairment and a ₹157.5 crore collateral provision (total exceptional ₹270 crore) for FY25, plus a ₹64.8 crore loss allowance in FY26.
The company had pledged 3 million Firema shares for a bank loan, but Firema's business was taken over by another group with nothing paid to shareholders.
Standalone working capital deteriorated, with debtor days lengthening from 59 to 75 and inventory days worsening from 66 to 84.

reports.auditor: The auditor named standalone receivables of ₹1,057.71 crore, which make up 42.3% of total assets, as a key audit matter. Contingent liabilities were also flagged as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: The related-party list includes promoter-controlled vendors Benchmark HR Solutions LLP, Skytrek Tours & Travels, and Harsha Engineers International. The company also provides guarantees for its subsidiaries' bank loans.
reports.contingent: The company has about ₹19 crore in pending litigation. Tax and customs matters are listed separately. Unfinished capital contracts rose to about ₹183 crore from ₹58 crore.
reports.other: A director pledged 4.32 crore shares (about 14% of total shares) for cash-credit limits and a bank loan, backed by personal guarantees. Quarterly bank stock statements for inventory, debtors, and creditors do not match the books due to goods in transit and pending entries. The company saw high management churn, with the CEO and CFO both leaving during the year, and a promoter's son taking over as MD and CEO.
flags: Standalone receivables of ₹1,057.71 crore and contingent liabilities were flagged as key audit matters.
A director pledged 4.32 crore shares, roughly 22% of the promoter stake, to secure company bank loans.
Quarterly bank stock statements for inventory, debtors, and creditors do not match the company's financial books.
The company experienced high management churn, losing both its CEO and CFO during the year.
Unfinished capital contracts sharply increased from ₹58 crore to about ₹183 crore.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unmodified opinion. The only key audit matter identified was revenue from contracts.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party transactions are routine. The chairman and vice chairman also manage the group company, Triveni Engineering.
reports.contingent: Consolidated contingent liabilities are small at ₹17.2 crore. These consist mostly of income tax items.
reports.outlook: The company announced no large capacity expansions. Capital expenditure is focused on research and development, digital tools, the Pretoria unit, and the Houston refurbishment workshop.
reports.other: In FY26, exports formed 57.7% of revenue at ₹1,258 crore (up 30.1%), with domestic sales making up 42.3%. Products accounted for 73% of sales and the aftermarket for 27%. The company has over 6,000 installations across more than 80 countries. It operates manufacturing plants in Bengaluru and service workshops in Houston and Pretoria.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion but included an emphasis of matter. It stated that componentisation of the three dual-feed plants is incomplete, so the fixed-asset register is not updated. Key audit matters were inventory valuation and revenue recognition. Under CARO, it noted a whistle-blower complaint was received and withdrawn.
reports.relatedParties: The company bought ₹879cr of raw materials from promoter-owned Nirani Sugars and owed it ₹175cr at March. TruAlt bought a 51% stake in TruAlt Gas from its shareholder for ₹8.42cr. Later, Sumitomo bought the remaining 49% from promoter Nirani Holdings for about ₹35cr. TruAlt guarantees this subsidiary's NABARD loan and pledged 15.11% of its stake.
reports.contingent: No contingent liabilities were reported. Capital commitments stood at ₹164cr at March 2026, down from ₹222cr a year earlier.
reports.outlook: The management discussion notes that India's installed ethanol capacity of about 1,995 crore litres far exceeds oil marketing company procurement of about 1,200 crore litres. The planned ₹2,000cr to ₹2,250cr sustainable aviation fuel project in Andhra Pradesh remains subject to feasibility studies, and the related memorandum of understanding is non-binding.
reports.other: Segment revenue included ₹1,705cr from ethanol and other products, and ₹22.5cr from compressed biogas. All revenue is from India. Operating cash flow was a negative ₹296cr, and standalone interest cover was 1.61x. Out of IPO funds, ₹140.1cr was used by March for Unit 4's dual-feed conversion. About 2.23 crore promoter shares, representing 26% of the company, were pledged to SBI and IREDA as collateral for term loans.
flags: Operating cash flow was a negative ₹296cr in FY26.
The auditor flagged that the fixed-asset register was not updated for three plants due to incomplete componentisation.
Promoters have pledged 26% of the company's shares to SBI and IREDA as collateral for term loans.
TruAlt guarantees a subsidiary's loan, but the promoter sold a 49% stake in that subsidiary to Sumitomo for about ₹35cr.
The management flagged that national installed ethanol capacity far exceeds the amount oil companies procure.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion and noted no emphasis of matter. Revenue recognition and subsidiary impairment were listed as key audit matters. The audit trail was enabled throughout the year.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid promoter firm TT Krishnamachari & Co a logo licence fee of ₹14.2 crore and C&F charges of ₹3.2 crore, bringing total expenses to promoter-controlled entities to ₹17.6 crore. It also lent ₹11 crore in inter-corporate deposits to its loss-making 51% subsidiary Ultrafresh and invested ₹5 crore in GramyaHaat.
reports.contingent: Standalone contingent liabilities include ₹52.7 crore in guarantees, of which ₹50.3 crore supports the UK subsidiary's £4 million bank facility. Tax claims include indirect tax (₹35.0 crore), customs (₹2.5 crore), and direct tax (₹1.9 crore). Capital commitments stood at ₹46.7 crore. CARO noted ₹36.3 crore in disputed, unpaid dues, primarily a ₹23.2 crore GST dispute and ₹8.0 crore for service tax.
reports.outlook: Management aims to grow faster than the market, gain share, and return EBITDA margins to 13-14% once its investment phase ends. FY27 capex is estimated at ₹100 crore for normal capacity, logistics, and augmentation. This is part of a larger ₹500 crore three-year plan covering automation, digitisation, factory upgrades, and business excellence.
reports.other: Domestic sales contributed ₹2,704 crore, while exports were just ₹68.3 crore. Traditional channels grew 11.6%, but rural microfinance and military canteen sales dragged. The UK subsidiary Horwood posted an EBITDA loss of £0.9 million, and domestic subsidiary Ultrafresh lost ₹7.6 crore. The company declared a dividend of ₹7.50 per share for FY26.
flags: The company pays a ₹14.2 crore logo licence fee to a promoter-controlled entity.
CARO highlights ₹36.3 crore in disputed, unpaid tax dues, notably a ₹23.2 crore GST dispute.
The UK subsidiary Horwood is still loss-making, and its latest impairment test avoided a charge only by raising terminal and sales growth assumptions despite falling sales.
The ₹30 crore carrying value of the loss-making Ultrafresh subsidiary has a very slim headroom of ₹3.19 crore, risking a future write-down.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unqualified opinion. The only key audit matter raised was about IT controls, specifically noting that a database-level audit trail only began on 7 September 2024.
reports.relatedParties: The Managing Director and CEO, Dhirendra Mahyavanshi, sold the broking subsidiary TIB to the listed company in May 2024 in a related-party deal. The related-party list names family members without stating their relationship, but none hold shares.
reports.contingent: The company faces a confirmed DGGI GST penalty of ₹51.2cr for allegedly raising invoices without actual supply of services between FY2017 and FY2023. This is under appeal and not provided for. There are also contested income-tax disallowances of ₹6.2cr.
reports.outlook: In the founders' letter, management stated they will not chase growth that lacks a credible path to sustainable economics. The company remains asset-light with nil contracts on the capital account.
reports.other: The CEO and COO each received a pay of ₹1.5cr for the year. Technical and support services brought in just ₹10.7cr of the ₹1,098cr total revenue. About half of the renewal premium comes from health and life insurance. Partner attrition drops to 2-3% a year after the first 24 months.
flags: GST penalties of ₹51.2cr have been confirmed for invoices allegedly raised without actual services, which the company has not provided for.
The company faces contested income-tax disallowances of ₹6.2cr.
Database-level audit trails were only implemented on 7 September 2024, which the auditor flagged as a key audit matter.
The FY26 results include a ₹52.5cr non-cash exceptional charge from a change in the preference-share conversion ratio.
Six junior staff members breached the insider trading code by trading in a closed window.

reports.auditor: S.R. Batliboi & Associates, Chennai gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters included revenue recognition judgements and ₹659 crore in goodwill impairment. The auditor issued an adverse CARO remark at the holding company because a ₹5.63 crore loan to Thai subsidiary TVS Logistics Siam was renewed to settle overdue dues. Five subsidiaries were audited by other firms. The auditor also noted an audit-trail gap at the database level for one consolidation software.
reports.relatedParties: The company gave ₹96.2 crore in repayable-on-demand loans to wholly owned subsidiaries. It also borrowed ₹40 crore from its subsidiaries. Transactions with the promoter group are small.
reports.contingent: The company faces a ₹17.2 crore provident fund demand from 2011 to 2015, of which ₹7.7 crore is deposited while pending at the EPF Tribunal. Tax and guarantee items are each under ₹40 crore. Disputed statutory dues that remain unpaid include ₹9.5 crore for income tax and about ₹20 crore for GST across states. Capital commitments are small at around ₹10 crore.
reports.other: The annual report shows the Integrated Supply Chain Solutions segment had FY26 revenue of ₹8,239 crore and a segment result of ₹734 crore. The Global Forwarding segment posted revenue of ₹2,764 crore and a result of ₹61 crore. By geography, India contributed ₹3,037 crore to FY26 revenue, while the rest of the world brought in ₹7,966 crore. The balance sheet carries ₹659 crore in goodwill.
flags: The auditor issued an adverse CARO remark because a ₹5.63 crore loan to a Thai subsidiary was renewed simply to settle overdue dues.
The auditor noted an audit-trail gap at the database level for one of the consolidation software systems.
The company has unpaid, disputed statutory dues including ₹9.5 crore for income tax and about ₹20 crore for GST.
It faces a pending provident fund demand of ₹17.2 crore dating back to 2011.
The company has ₹96.2 crore tied up in repayable-on-demand loans given to its wholly owned subsidiaries.

reports.auditor: Price Waterhouse Chartered Accountants LLP gave an unmodified opinion. They highlighted goodwill impairment testing of discounted cash flow assumptions as a key audit matter, because goodwill from Shipway stood at ₹117.2 crore, making up 43% of total assets.
reports.relatedParties: Select staff were moved to the parent company, AceVector, under a shared-services deal, which caused subcontracting charges to jump 303% to ₹11.6 crore in FY26. The company also paid AceVector for rent and recruitment. Auditor fees for the parent's IPO were billed to AceVector.
reports.contingent: The company has no pending litigation and no contingent liabilities. There were also no capital commitments as of March 2026.
reports.other: The promoter group, AceVector, holds 36.0% of the company, while the public holds 61.6% and foreign institutions hold 0.02%. The company saw governance changes after the financial year ended, with Chairman Manoj Kohli resigning on July 4, 2026, to be replaced by Ullas Kamath. The compliance officer was also changed on August 13, 2026.
flags: Subcontracting charges jumped 303% to ₹11.6 crore in FY26 following a shared-services deal with the parent company.
Goodwill from the Shipway acquisition makes up a large 43% of total assets at ₹117.2 crore.
Both the chairman and the compliance officer were replaced shortly after the financial year ended.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The key audit matter was the timing of revenue recognition. The CARO report was clean regarding loans, noting regular repayments. The CARO report also noted outstanding standalone guarantees of ₹115 crore for a subsidiary and outstanding loans of ₹52.3 crore at the end of March 2026.
reports.relatedParties: Dheya Engineering is a related party because Unimech's Chairman and Managing Director, Anil Kumar Puttan, and Whole-Time Director, Rajanikanth Balaraman, sit on its board. Unimech raised its stake in Dheya from about 16% to roughly 30% during FY26.
reports.contingent: The company reported no contingent liabilities at the end of March 2026, as a previous ₹3.8 crore GST demand was closed. It had capital commitments of ₹11.5 crore.
reports.outlook: Management noted a record standalone order book of ₹214 crore at the end of March 2026, consisting mainly of aero-tooling and precision components. Their plans include a joint venture in Saudi Arabia with a planned investment of $30 million over three years. They also highlighted a new five-year contract with FACC worth an initial $7.5 million.
reports.other: The company reports its operations as a single segment. A subsequent events note detailed the ₹450 crore acquisition of Hobel Bellows in April 2026. The board reported that IPO funds were redirected, leaving ₹94.5 crore unutilized at year-end. The books hold a Minimum Alternate Tax credit of ₹26.2 crore, and the company has a tax holiday until FY35.
flags: Customer concentration was high, with the top customer accounting for 44.5% of FY26 revenue and the top three making up 72.4%.
The business is heavily reliant on a single geography, with the US driving 76% of total revenue in FY26.
The company changed its IPO spending objectives within a year of listing, reallocating ₹61.3 crore to acquisitions, joint ventures, and greenfield projects.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters included inventory valuation, revenue timing, receivables, and significant related-party transactions. These transactions involved cross-border dealings with subsidiaries, royalty payments, and management service charges.
reports.relatedParties: Dealings with promoter-controlled entities were very small, comprising ₹0.16 crore in rent paid to Soni Holdings. The bulk of related-party transactions consisted of ₹330 crore in intra-group sales to US and German subsidiaries, along with ₹84 crore in dividends received from subsidiaries.
reports.contingent: The company issued a corporate guarantee to banks for a subsidiary, which increased to ₹21.9 crore from ₹1.8 crore. Standalone capital commitments were ₹21.9 crore at the end of March 2026. Contingent tax and GST claims were small at about ₹9 crore.
reports.other: The annual report notes recorded a fire at the Ludhiana finishing shop, which left a ₹22.1 crore insurance claim receivable at March 2026. It also documented a management change, with CFO Rohit Maheshwari leaving on 12 March 2026 and Sandeep Taneja taking over on 16 March 2026.
flags: The auditor highlighted significant cross-border related-party transactions involving royalties and management service charges as a key audit matter.
Corporate guarantees provided to banks for a subsidiary rose sharply to ₹21.9 crore.
The company suffered a fire at a Ludhiana facility, resulting in a pending ₹22.1 crore insurance claim receivable.
The Chief Financial Officer resigned just before the financial year ended in March 2026.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The report stated there were no key audit matters.
reports.relatedParties: The company sold ₹6.8 crore (about 10% of revenue) in FY25 and ₹0.6 crore in FY26 to promoter-group Uniheat Research and Solutions. A ₹0.27 crore receivable from promoter entity Uni-Spec Foods has remained unchanged for two years. Promoter family members are paid as employees. Loans from the family were repaid in FY26.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities include a provident fund demand for ₹1.7 crore. There are also bank guarantees and letters of credit ranging from ₹6.6 crore to ₹9 crore.
reports.other: The company secretary changed in November 2025.
flags: Sales to a promoter-group entity were ₹6.8 crore in FY25, which was about 10% of revenue.
A ₹0.27 crore receivable from a promoter entity has sat unchanged for two years.
The company faces a contingent liability for a provident fund demand of ₹1.7 crore.
The company secretary was changed during the year in November 2025.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The only key audit matter was revenue recognition concerning trade discounts and volume rebates. The statutory audit trail operated throughout the year.
reports.relatedParties: The company invested an additional ₹25 crore in its 30.35% associate Gegadyne in FY26. It also provided Gegadyne with a ₹6.6 crore secured loan and up to ₹4 crore as an interim loan, all fully repaid by March 2026.
reports.contingent: Standalone contingent liabilities totalled ₹83.4 crore, up from ₹69.1 crore the prior year. This consisted of ₹65.3 crore in direct tax claims and ₹17.5 crore in indirect tax claims.
reports.outlook: Management noted FY26 capital expenditure was ₹173.7 crore, focused on in-house manufacturing, capacity, new product development, and IT. The Hyderabad battery plant expansion started in May 2025. A new fans factory in Hyderabad is scheduled for commercial production in FY27. A new Innovation Campus also opened in Kochi in January 2026.
reports.other: During FY26, Electricals revenue was ₹2,461 crore (+13.4%), Electronics was ₹1,640 crore (+8.6%), Consumer Durables was ₹1,616 crore, and Sunflame was ₹250 crore. Around 65% of revenue came from in-house products across multiple state plants. Average factory utilisation was 59%, meaning volume can grow without big new plants. The Sunflame merger was approved in principle in July 2025 but remains pending.
flags: The recently acquired Sunflame business is operating at a low 5.3% margin, and its formal merger into V-Guard is not yet completed.

reports.auditor: The auditor, S R B C & Co LLP, issued a qualified opinion for FY26. They could not verify ₹20.99 crore of income recognised from the former China JV, which is disputed by TYC Parties. The report also contains two emphasis of matter paragraphs. One flags an unprovided US$66.41 million (roughly ₹550 crore) arbitration claim by OPmobility. The second highlights appealed GST orders with a demand cut to ₹28.4 crore.
reports.relatedParties: The company reported sales of ₹36.9 crore to Endurance Technologies, a Jain-family company, and purchases of ₹11.5 crore from them. It also recorded a royalty of ₹21.0 crore from Varroc TYC, which is the disputed income.
reports.contingent: Group contingent liabilities stood at ₹98.1 crore at the end of March 2026, down from ₹156.4 crore a year earlier. The company also has EPCG export obligations of ₹164.5 crore. Additionally, OPmobility has an arbitration claim of US$66.41 million plus costs, and there is a GST demand of ₹28.4 crore under appeal.
reports.outlook: The managing director's letter acknowledges that overseas targets were missed for three consecutive years. However, management states that achieving EBITDA breakeven for overseas operations by Q4 FY27 is a firm commitment they should be held accountable for. The report also notes that ₹1,040 crore of capital was deployed in FY26.
reports.other: During FY26, the company spent ₹33.3 crore on voluntary retirement compensation. The corporate governance section notes that promoters hold a 75% stake in the company with no shares pledged.
flags: The auditor issued a qualified opinion regarding ₹20.99 crore of disputed income from the former China JV.
OPmobility has started arbitration claiming US$66.41 million (roughly ₹550 crore) plus costs, for which no provision has been made.
The company faces GST demand orders of ₹28.4 crore which are still being appealed for interest and penalties.
Management admitted in the annual report to missing their overseas performance targets for three straight years.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unqualified opinion on the financial statements. However, the auditor listed related-party transactions as the key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: In FY26, sales to related parties were ₹1,243 crore, which is about a third of total revenue. This included ₹753 crore in sales to the holding company, VHPL. The company also made ₹460 crore in purchases from related parties.
reports.contingent: The company reported about ₹32.5 crore in contingent liabilities. This includes ₹15.5 crore for excise, ₹5.8 crore for income tax, ₹2.9 crore for electricity, and ₹2.2 crore for GST.
reports.other: The poultry segment had FY26 revenue of ₹1,897 crore and a ₹65.5 crore result, down from ₹99.5 crore in FY25. Oilseed posted ₹1,554 crore in revenue and a ₹54.4 crore result, up from ₹19.1 crore. Animal health products brought in ₹392 crore in revenue and a ₹99.0 crore result, becoming the largest profit contributor. The animal health segment margin reached about 25%. Additionally, the Managing Director draws remuneration from the holding company, VHPL, instead of Venky's.
flags: Sales to related parties made up about a third of total revenue at ₹1,243 crore.
The auditor highlighted related-party transactions as the key audit matter.
The Managing Director is paid by the unlisted holding company, VHPL, instead of Venky's.

reports.auditor: The auditor's report stated that no key audit matters were reported.
reports.relatedParties: The company purchased ₹34.8 crore in goods from Atlas Transformers India Ltd, which is 98.7% owned by managing director Nilesh Patel, and sold ₹5.5 crore to them, leaving ₹17.0 crore payable. Sales to management-influenced Tushar Transequipment were ₹11.8 crore, with a ₹6.6 crore receivable. A ₹4.2 crore land advance was paid to related party SMT Packaging. Managing director remuneration was ₹4.2 crore.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were minor at ₹0.64 crore, consisting of income tax, GST, CESTAT refunds, and legal claims. The company also had capital commitments of ₹30.0 crore at the end of March 2026.
reports.other: The company operates in a single reportable segment. It had ₹33.9 crore in unhedged advances to suppliers for imports at year-end. Corporate social responsibility spending fell short, with ₹71.4 lakh unspent and moved to a separate account in April 2026. Key management saw turnover, as the chief financial officer changed twice during the year and the company secretary resigned.
flags: The company bought ₹34.8 crore in goods from a related business largely owned by the managing director.
The managing director's pay of ₹4.2 crore consumed roughly 10.6% of the company's net profit.
The company experienced executive turnover, with the chief financial officer changing twice during the year and the company secretary resigning.
The company holds ₹33.9 crore in unhedged advances to suppliers for imports, exposing it to currency and delivery risks.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unqualified opinion and noted no key audit matters.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are negligible, consisting of income-tax demands totalling approximately ₹0.16 crore.
reports.other: During FY26, a preferential allotment of 2.0 crore shares increased share capital from ₹126 crore to ₹146 crore, and reserves from ₹177 crore to ₹424 crore. Additionally, the upcoming AGM seeks approval to issue 42 lakh convertible warrants to promoters at ₹164 each, totalling about ₹69 crore.
flags: Promoters have pledged 26.0% of their shares.
Promoter ownership dropped from 47.6% in March 2024 to 34.65% in June 2026 due to repeated preferential issues to non-promoters.
The company is seeking to ratify a change in the use of ₹12.05 crore of preferential-issue proceeds, redirecting it from subsidiary capex to buying land.
The document labelled as the FY26 annual report on Screener is actually the previous year's FY25 report.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion on the company's financial results.
reports.relatedParties: Shareholders were asked to approve large transactions with two associates until the next AGM. This includes up to ₹400 crore with Nexus Advanced Technologies Pvt Ltd (26% associate) and ₹150 crore with United Vinyas Technologies Inc. (49% associate). These deals equal 78% and 29% of FY26 turnover, priced at arm's length with no external valuation.
reports.contingent: As of March 2026, contingent liabilities included a new GST demand of ₹3.7 crore, a labour charter-of-demands litigation of ₹6.5 crore, and income tax claims of ₹0.2 crore. Bank guarantees stood at ₹35.7 crore, up from ₹19.4 crore the prior year.
reports.outlook: The management discussion reported a preferential issue of convertible warrants totaling ₹150 crore. The company received ₹61.25 crore by March 2026, utilized ₹53.25 crore, and expects the balance by March 2027. Additionally, shareholders approved raising the company's borrowing limits to ₹600 crore.
reports.other: The company added new associate structures: Nexus Advanced Technologies Pvt Ltd (26%) and United Vinyas Technologies Inc. (49%). It also incorporated a wholly-owned US subsidiary, Vinyas Innovative Technologies Inc., in February 2026. This US unit was not operating, and its FEMA ODI filing remained incomplete by the end of March 2026.
flags: The company proposed enormous related-party transactions totaling ₹550 crore with two part-owned associates without an external valuation.
Contingent liabilities feature a significant ₹6.5 crore labour litigation and a new ₹3.7 crore GST demand.
The newly formed wholly-owned US subsidiary failed to complete its FEMA ODI filing by the end of the financial year.
Shareholders were asked to approve raising the borrowing limit to ₹600 crore, suggesting a heavy reliance on future debt.

reports.auditor: The auditor, SKVM & Co., gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters included revenue recognition and inventory valuation. Comparatives were restated because this was the company's first year using Ind AS.
reports.relatedParties: An ₹8.61 crore advance for capital goods paid in FY25 to Mrs. Nikitha Shravan Poddatur, a close relative of key management, was still outstanding at the end of FY26. She also receives remuneration and received ₹36 lakh in rent in FY26. The company paid raw material advances of ₹0.35 crore in FY25 and ₹0.07 crore in FY26 to Techmark International FZE, a promoter-influenced entity in the UAE. It also pays rent to Sukrit Bharati HUF.
