reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small. They include EPCG customs of ₹6.2 crore and a GST demand of ₹4.8 crore that is under appeal.
reports.other: The company reported ₹68 crore in lease liabilities. It reports only a single segment in its financial statements, which means the specific segment margins quoted by management on calls cannot be verified.
flags: An ₹8.61 crore capital goods advance paid to a close relative of management in FY25 remained outstanding at the end of FY26.
The company pays raw material advances to a promoter-influenced entity located in the UAE.
The financial statements disclose only a single business segment, making it impossible to check the individual segment margins claimed by management.

reports.auditor: Jampani & Associates gave an unmodified opinion. Revenue recognition was noted as a key audit matter. The firm finished its second five-year term. M. Anandam & Co was appointed as the new auditor from the August 2026 AGM. This was a mandatory rotation, not a resignation. Other auditors checked the subsidiary companies.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid ₹46.1 crore in FY26 for transport, customs handling, and hire charges to promoter-linked businesses, specifically Vasantha Transport and Vasantha Shipping & Logistics. This was an increase from ₹42.9 crore in FY25. At the end of the year, the company still owed ₹11.7 crore to these related concerns.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were small, totalling about ₹9 crore. This included ₹3.7 crore for a GST transitional credit, ₹1.8 crore for sales tax, and ₹3.2 crore in guarantees. The company also had ₹43.3 crore in capital commitments at the end of FY26, a large increase from ₹8.5 crore in FY25.
reports.other: The company reported its results under one single reportable segment. The accounts show the company operates seven manufacturing units and owns a 74% stake in the Ruighoek chrome mine in South Africa through Batlhako Mining. This ownership reflects a 26% stake dilution to a local partner in February 2026. The mine was acquired via Bonmerci Investments in November 2025.
flags: The company paid ₹46.1 crore for logistics to promoter-linked entities, which is notable in a business where freight is a major cost.
Capital commitments jumped significantly to ₹43.3 crore at the end of FY26 from just ₹8.5 crore in the prior year.

reports.auditor: YRKDAJ & Associates gave a clean opinion. However, the CARO report noted slight delays in depositing TDS and profession tax.
reports.relatedParties: The board approved an annual limit of ₹15.5 crore per related party. Dealings included ₹6.85 crore of sales to and ₹3.97 crore of purchases from Vivid Green Energy, which owed ₹2.88 crore in March. The company bought ₹1.64 crore from and sold ₹0.62 crore to Mechtech, a promoter firm. The MD's parents draw a salary. A ₹30 lakh advance to a director's brother and ₹59 lakh of director loans were repaid in FY26.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities total about ₹14.8 crore. This consists mostly of ₹13.3 crore in bank guarantees, ₹1.3 crore in letters of credit, a ₹19 lakh VAT claim, and a ₹31 lakh cheque-bounce notice.
reports.outlook: The management discussion states the execution cycle takes 8 to 10 weeks. It notes the order book stood at ₹210 crore at the end of June. Management also states the new Ambernath plant is already commissioned, though the analyst notes this is incorrect.
reports.other: In FY26, the company paid ₹99 lakh to buy 99% of Mechtech Infrasolutions, a Siemens licensee. This was a partnership owned equally by the two promoters, with a turnover of about ₹2 crore in FY26. The management discussion also notes that the top five customers accounted for close to three-fifths of sales in FY26.
flags: The management discussion incorrectly claims the new Ambernath plant is already commissioned.
The CARO report notes slight delays in paying TDS and profession tax.
Customer concentration is high, with the top five buyers making up nearly 60% of FY26 sales.
The company engages in related-party dealings, including buying a firm that was owned by its promoters.

reports.auditor: The audit opinion is unmodified. The auditor noted only one key audit matter, which relates to litigation, provisions, and contingent liabilities.
reports.relatedParties: Key managerial pay was ₹21.0 crore in FY26, which is about 7% of net profit. Out of this, the two managing directors received ₹6.7 crore and ₹8.2 crore. The company also made small corporate social responsibility (CSR) contributions to trusts where management members serve as trustees or directors.
reports.contingent: The company reported outstanding bank guarantees of ₹398 crore. There are contingent tax demands of about ₹8.5 crore related to excise, income tax, and GST. Unfinished capital contracts stood at ₹85 crore.
reports.outlook: Management expects margins to normalize going forward due to rising industry capacity and aggressive pricing trends from competitors. The company will pursue only profitable growth to maintain a healthy balance sheet. A new power-transformer plant was targeted for completion by June 2026 and operations by July 2026. A new dry-type transformer plant is also planned at Karjan for ₹90 crore, plus ₹25 crore for land.
reports.other: FY26 sales volumes reached 16,514 MVA, with capacity utilization above 100% for the second year running. Exports made up 3.24% of turnover. The order book stood at ₹1,510 crore. The board declared a dividend of ₹100 per share, totaling ₹101.17 crore. Q4 FY26 other income turned negative due to mark-to-market losses on the investment book.
flags: Management warned that margins are expected to normalize as industry capacity rises and competitors adopt aggressive pricing.
Key managerial pay is high at ₹21.0 crore, taking up about 7% of total net profit.
The large investment book creates profit volatility, as seen when mark-to-market losses turned Q4 FY26 other income negative.
The order book reported in the annual report was thin at just ₹1,510 crore.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unqualified opinion. They included an emphasis of matter regarding ₹433 crore in Qatar bank guarantees. Key audit matters involved testing percentage-of-completion revenue on ₹3,845 crore of project contracts, and impairment testing for the ₹935 crore investment in Voltbek and ₹337 crore in Voltas Netherlands.
reports.relatedParties: The Tata group holds a 30.30% promoter stake. Voltas holds a 49% stake in the Voltbek joint venture with Arçelik/Beko. The company added ₹98 crore to this investment during the year, bringing the total to ₹935 crore. Joint venture losses reduced Voltas' profit before tax by ₹131 crore. Voltas also provided guarantees for its subsidiaries and joint ventures, with total limits falling to ₹759 crore from ₹3,010 crore, of which ₹209 crore was utilized.
reports.contingent: The company reported ₹433 crore in Qatar bank guarantees as a contingent liability, though courts have since ordered these returned to the consortium. Other claims not acknowledged as debt totaled ₹328 crore at the end of March 2026. This included ₹93 crore for GST, ₹99 crore for sales tax, and ₹87 crore in contractual claims.
reports.outlook: Management noted in the discussion and analysis that the Voltbek joint venture continues to operate at sub-scale profitability. The report highlighted that a cool summer heavily impacted performance as a risk factor, cutting unitary cooling profits by 66%. Management also highlighted the company's cost position, noting that overall import content is now below 30%.
reports.other: Segment revenue included ₹9,501 crore from unitary cooling, ₹4,053 crore from projects, and ₹599 crore from engineering products. Cooling profit fell by two-thirds to ₹305 crore, dropping the margin to 3.2%. The board declared a dividend of ₹4 per share, totaling a ₹132 crore payout. The company also recorded a ₹26 crore exceptional charge for the labour code and ₹55 crore in forex and treasury mark-to-market losses.
flags: The Voltbek joint venture remains loss-making, continuing to operate at sub-scale profitability and cutting profit before tax by ₹131 crore.
Cooling segment profit margin dropped sharply to 3.2% from 8.4% the previous year due to a cool summer.
Claims against the company not acknowledged as debts increased to ₹328 crore, including large GST and sales tax claims.
The company recorded a ₹26 crore exceptional charge related to the labour code.
Voltas suffered ₹55 crore in forex and treasury mark-to-market losses during the second half of the year.

reports.auditor: B S R & Co. LLP provided an unmodified opinion and named revenue recognition as a key audit matter. The auditor flagged audit-trail exceptions because the revenue software had no edit log enabled. They also could not confirm database-level logging for the third-party general-ledger software.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small, consisting of ₹6.4 crore in GST disputes over input-credit claims. The company also had ₹4.7 crore in capital commitments at the end of March 2026.
reports.other: The company has one reported segment, which is Home Furnishing. Polyol and TDI account for roughly 60% to 65% of mattress raw-material costs. The directors' report outlines the use of the ₹377 crore in fresh IPO funds, which includes ₹161.5 crore for store rent, ₹108.4 crore for marketing, ₹30.8 crore for new stores, and ₹15.4 crore for machinery.
flags: The company saw significant CFO turnover, with three people holding the role recently and one leaving just two weeks after the listing.
The auditor noted audit-trail exceptions due to missing edit logs in the revenue software and unconfirmed database logging for the general-ledger software.
A large portion of the IPO money was earmarked to fund standard operating expenses, including ₹161.5 crore for store rent and ₹108.4 crore for marketing.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unqualified opinion with no key audit matters. However, they noted disputed taxes of ₹47.0 crore, an increase from ₹19.7 crore the previous year, which have not been provided for in the accounts.
reports.relatedParties: The company bought shares in Axles India worth ₹22.68 crore from the promoter entity TSF, raising its stake from 9.5% to 12.5%. It also buys goods and services from group companies like Brakes India and Sundaram Business Services. The Managing Director's pay was ₹6.05 crore.
reports.contingent: The company reported capital commitments of ₹73.8 crore as of March 2026. There are also disputed taxes amounting to ₹47.0 crore that are not provided for in the financial statements.
reports.other: Standalone FY26 revenue was ₹5,124.4 crore, with an EBITDA of ₹403.7 crore and a net profit of ₹138.6 crore. The automotive segment reported ₹4,526 crore in revenue and ₹287.6 crore in EBIT. The industrial segment saw ₹938.5 crore in revenue and ₹41.3 crore in EBIT. The company netted ₹603.8 crore of composite services in its revenue. Chairman S. Ram stepped down on 30 March 2026.
flags: The company has hidden debt, with ₹469 crore of bill discounting and ₹23.1 crore in buyers' credit sitting inside trade payables rather than borrowings.
Promoters were allotted new equity at ₹1,461 a share, about 30% less than institutions paid and well below the market price.
Operating margins remain thin at around 8%, with the industrial segment EBIT margin at just 3-4%.
Disputed taxes of ₹47.0 crore have not been provided for in the financials.
Management admitted that demand visibility is limited to about one month due to the West Asia crisis and cyclical demand.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unqualified opinion. However, they highlighted contingent liabilities of ₹216.8 crore relating to tax and legal disputes as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: The company paid its parent ₹70.2 crore as a brand royalty and ₹29.4 crore as a technical fee in FY26. This relates to a new 30-year licence signed in October 2025. It also sold about ₹237 crore of services to Whirlpool Corporation. These service sales are priced on a cost-plus basis and contracted until March 2029, after which they are entirely at the parent company's discretion.
reports.contingent: The company has ₹216.8 crore in contingent liabilities for tax and legal disputes. A major ₹1,036 crore transfer-pricing exposure for advertising is not disclosed as contingent because a Supreme Court win makes the risk remote. Additionally, a ₹139 crore provision sits on the books for disputed e-waste expenses pending an industry challenge.
reports.outlook: The management discussion in the annual report identifies a transition risk involving its IT systems, which still run on transition service agreements with the parent company.
reports.other: The company reports its financial results as a single segment. Profit before tax and exceptional items fell 12% in FY26 to ₹425.6 crore. This was impacted by a one-time exceptional provision of ₹38.8 crore for labour-code wages. Its subsidiary Elica posted 12% revenue growth and a 16.0% profit before tax margin in FY26. The balance sheet is effectively debt-free, with listed borrowings consisting only of lease liabilities. An investing cash outflow of ₹2,029 crore simply represented cash moving into longer-term bank deposits.
flags: A ₹139 crore provision for e-waste expenses pending an industry challenge could remain a permanent cost if not resolved.
Service sales to the parent company, which brought in about ₹237 crore in FY26, are only contracted until March 2029 and are completely at the parent's discretion after that.
IT systems still run on transition service agreements with the parent company, which management explicitly states is a transition risk.
The auditor flagged ₹216.8 crore in contingent liabilities for tax and legal disputes as a key audit matter.
The company booked a one-time ₹38.8 crore exceptional provision for labour-code wages in FY26.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion and listed revenue recognition as a key audit matter. However, they noted that an audit trail at the database level of the company's SaaS software was not available.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings were small. The company paid rent of about ₹0.16 crore to each promoter, and promoter salaries ranged between ₹1.6 crore and ₹2.4 crore.
reports.contingent: The company disclosed no contingent liabilities.
reports.other: The wholly owned subsidiary in the USA, Windlas Inc., is being dissolved. The company's credit rating of ICRA A+/Stable, A1 was reaffirmed. Under the 2025 ESOP plan, 5,70,500 RSUs were granted at a ₹5 face value. CEO and CFO Komal Gupta received 3,15,000 of these (55%), valued at roughly ₹35 crore at the current price. Additionally, her FY26 salary increased to ₹2.66 crore from ₹0.90 crore.
flags: The auditor noted that an audit trail was not available at the database level for the company's SaaS software.
There is significant ESOP concentration, with 55% of the 5,70,500 RSUs granted going to the CEO and CFO.
The CEO and CFO's salary saw a sharp increase from ₹0.90 crore to ₹2.66 crore in FY26.

reports.auditor: The auditor noted lower capacity utilisation at some plants. They raised key audit matters regarding the recoverability of ₹1,707 crore in intangible assets under development for new chemical entities. They also flagged ₹312 crore in property, plant and equipment and ₹395 crore in capital work-in-progress affected by deferred projects.
reports.relatedParties: The promoter family runs the unlisted Wockhardt Hospitals. Zahabiya Khorakiwala, the managing director of Wockhardt Hospitals, now leads the company's Zaynich business in the United States.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities stand at approximately ₹675 crore. This includes ₹345 crore for income tax, ₹136 crore for NPPA overcharging, ₹117 crore for sales tax and GST, and ₹45 crore for excise. A $36 million Texas Medicaid settlement has been fully paid.
reports.other: Long-term borrowings rose by ₹313 crore during the year to ₹1,365 crore, and short-term borrowings were ₹380 crore. The company redeployed ₹162 crore of unused funds from a November 2024 share placement toward capital expenditure and research. The annual general meeting notice included a resolution to raise up to ₹3,000 crore. Pledged promoter shares rose to 1.50 crore, which is 23% of the promoter holding.
flags: The auditor raised concerns over ₹1,707 crore in capitalised research and development, which could face write-offs if drug trials fail.
The auditor flagged ₹707 crore in idle or deferred plant assets and work-in-progress due to low capacity utilisation.
The company carries about ₹675 crore in contingent liabilities for disputed taxes and pricing claims.
The promoter trust has pledged 1.50 crore shares, representing 23% of the total promoter holding.
A proposal to raise up to ₹3,000 crore poses a substantial equity dilution risk for current investors.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unqualified opinion but did not audit subsidiaries accounting for ₹1,146 crore in revenue (about 62% of the group total) and ₹1,707 crore in assets, relying instead on foreign component auditors. The auditor also accepted a joint venture's ₹6.3 crore profit based on unreviewed, board-certified accounts. Key audit matters included estimating project costs and valuing property, plant, and equipment.
reports.relatedParties: The company reported ₹46.5 crore in sales to its Thai joint venture, up from ₹21.1 crore in the previous year. It also engaged in rent dealings with promoter group firms like Bengal Steel and HSM. Unpaid bills owed to the standalone Indian business by related parties rose to ₹59 crore from ₹19 crore.
reports.contingent: Consolidated contingent liabilities totaled ₹285 crore, down from ₹321 crore the previous year. This consisted of ₹271 crore in bank guarantees and ₹12.5 crore in excise and service-tax disputes.
reports.other: The standalone Indian business had ₹781 crore in gross receivables, which is more than its entire annual revenue of ₹763 crore, plus ₹234 crore in unbilled contract assets. Receivables overdue by more than one year tripled to about ₹289 crore from roughly ₹99 crore, yet the loss allowance was only ₹10.6 crore. During the year, the company also changed its method for adjusting customer receipts, which altered its aging classification.
flags: The principal auditor relied on other auditors for subsidiaries making up 62% of group revenue and accepted unreviewed accounts for a joint venture's profit.
Standalone gross receivables of ₹781 crore exceed the entire annual standalone revenue of ₹763 crore.
Receivables overdue for more than a year tripled to about ₹289 crore, but the company kept a very thin loss allowance of just ₹10.6 crore.
The company changed its accounting basis for adjusting customer receipts, which altered the aging classification of unpaid bills.
Standalone unpaid bills owed by related parties jumped to ₹59 crore from ₹19 crore last year.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion but included an emphasis of matter. They drew attention to the company not booking ₹2.69 crore in interest owed to MSME suppliers for late payments. The company stated it will only book this once it recovers a ₹25.8 crore MSME interest claim it filed against one of its own debtors.

There are also advances to promoter-directors in the balances. Additionally, the company has given loans of roughly ₹16 crore to its subsidiaries.

reports.other: The standalone company had 243 permanent and 368 contractual employees at March 2026. Standalone inventory grew to ₹77.7 crore. Revenue was almost entirely domestic, with government and PSU clients making up roughly 47% of FY26 revenue. The group includes subsidiaries like Xtranet BPO and Xtratrust Digisign, plus a Dubai associate that made a ₹0.25 crore profit in FY26.
flags: The auditor highlighted that the company did not book ₹2.69 crore of interest owed to MSME suppliers.
Standalone receivables include ₹33.6 crore outstanding for over three years with almost no provision, representing a significant write-off risk.
The secretarial audit report flagged years of missed consolidated financial filings, resulting in penalties for the company and its directors.
The company faced penalties for using private-placement money before filing the allotment return and was flagged for Section 185 compliance issues.
Two major customers accounted for 22% of FY26 revenue, indicating client concentration.

reports.auditor: The auditor added an emphasis of matter, rather than a qualification, regarding a ₹2.10 crore loss to a cyber fraud, which is also reported under CARO clause xi. A second emphasis of matter noted it was the first year using Ind AS, meaning comparative numbers were restated.
reports.relatedParties: Managing Director Keyur Shah received ₹2.89 crore in pay and perks, ₹0.42 crore for office and car lease rent, and ₹0.44 crore in commission for personally guaranteeing company loans. Director Twinkle Shah received ₹0.30 crore in rent and ₹0.22 crore in consultancy fees.
reports.contingent: The company had tax disputes of about ₹0.8 crore for CST, sales tax, and GST between 2015 and 2022. It also faced ₹2.2 crore in FY26 GST litigation, with ₹0.31 crore paid under protest. Capital commitments stood at ₹35.3 crore as of March 2026.
reports.outlook: The company is expanding total capacity to about 15,000 units, bringing a revenue potential of about ₹700 crore. It plans to use preferential issue funds for 550 kV RIP manufacturing, an OIP brownfield expansion to clear a bottleneck, and to repay ₹28 to ₹30 crore of working-capital debt. The order book reached over ₹400 crore.
reports.other: The company has a single reportable segment, with FY26 India sales of ₹217.0 crore and exports of ₹17.2 crore. One customer bought ₹44.2 crore, making up 19% of sales. Profits included a ₹2.10 crore exceptional loss from fraud. The group includes wholly owned subsidiaries in Texas and India, plus a 50% joint venture.
flags: The company suffered a control lapse and lost ₹2.10 crore to a cyber fraud involving a fake email, resulting in an exceptional loss and an auditor's emphasis of matter.
The managing director was paid ₹0.44 crore in commission for personally guaranteeing the company's loans.
Customer concentration is high, with a single buyer accounting for about 19% of total sales in FY26.

reports.auditor: Gokhale & Sathe issued an unmodified opinion. The auditor highlighted inventory valuation and the accounting for an MNC customer advance, specifically evaluating it as a contract liability versus financing, as key audit matters. There were no CARO qualifications aside from the reported list of disputed dues.
reports.relatedParties: The company operates two sales subsidiaries: Yasho Industries Europe B.V. and Yasho Inc. in the US. Receivables from these entities rose to ₹33.0 crore, up from ₹18.5 crore the previous year. Additionally, some promoter-group relatives were reclassified as public shareholders in January 2026.
reports.contingent: The company has ₹38.5 crore in pending GST disputes, which is net of ₹4.0 crore paid under protest. This includes ₹33.7 crore for export-refund denials between FY18 and FY21, and ₹8.2 crore relating to a pre-import condition from FY18 to FY20. It also faces customs penalties of ₹1.75 crore pending at CESTAT.
reports.other: The company completed a ₹125 crore preferential equity issue in FY25 at approximately ₹1,900 per share. This issuance diluted total promoter holding from 71.9% to 68.0%. The company maintained a dividend payout of around 2%.
flags: The company is fighting ₹38.5 crore in GST disputes and ₹1.75 crore in customs penalties, which together equal about 9% of its ₹444 crore net worth.
Certain promoter-group relatives were reclassified as public shareholders in January 2026.

reports.auditor: Auditor MSKA & Associates included an emphasis of matter regarding ₹339.1 crore in IPO proceeds used as deposits and advances to airlines and hotels, which SEBI queried. The auditor also noted the reallocation of ₹52.7 crore in goodwill to air and hotel units as a key audit matter.
reports.relatedParties: The annual report notes state that the company's promoter is the Nasdaq-listed Yatra Online Inc. The promoter holds a 62.66% stake in the Indian company through THCL Travel Holding Cyprus.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities stood at ₹131 crore at the end of March 2026. This includes income-tax demands of ₹83.6 crore, which contains new notices of ₹30.8 crore on subsidiaries and a ₹52.8 crore demand from FY22 under appeal. It also includes GST notices on input credit for ₹10.9 crore, customer claims of ₹13.2 crore, and bank guarantees of ₹22.5 crore.
flags: The auditor issued an emphasis of matter due to ongoing SEBI and NSE queries about ₹339.1 crore of IPO proceeds used as deposits and advances to airlines and hotels.
Contingent liabilities are notably high at ₹131 crore, which amounts to roughly 16% of the company's net worth, largely driven by disputed tax demands.

reports.auditor: MSKA & Associates gave an unmodified opinion with no emphasis of matter. The only key audit matter was revenue recognition regarding gross Propel voucher accounting. The audit trail operated successfully all year.
reports.relatedParties: Related-party dealings were small. They included ₹0.3 crore in professional fees to KMP-linked Prismberry and eYantra, ₹0.1 crore for the chairman's daughter's salary, and a ₹4.2 crore loan to subsidiary TaxSpanner.
reports.contingent: Total contingent liabilities were ₹14.1 crore, which included ₹2.5 crore for service tax and ₹3.5 crore for GST. Income-tax contingent liabilities jumped to ₹8.1 crore from ₹1.5 crore. The company also had ₹67.9 crore in capital commitments for Dice.
reports.other: Intangible assets and those under development rose to ₹190 crore. Trade receivables increased to ₹361 crore, while other current assets rose to ₹292 crore. Promoters held a steady 44.3% stake with no pledged shares. Of the ₹594.8 crore raised in a QIP, only ₹121.5 crore was spent on acquisitions and ₹10.7 crore for general purposes by March 2026. The CFO departed the company during the year.
flags: Heavy capitalisation of software development costs flattered reported margins for the year.
The company has reported negative free cash flow for four consecutive years despite showing net profits.
Income-tax contingent liabilities jumped to ₹8.1 crore, and a recent tax appeal against an assessment was dismissed.
The chief financial officer departed, and a permanent replacement was not yet named.
The company faces acquisition risks after completing five deals in two years.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The key audit matter was the timing of revenue recognition. An 'Other Matter' paragraph noted that 11 subsidiaries, an associate, and a joint venture were audited by other auditors. The CARO report contained one qualification for the subsidiary Anawave regarding the title deeds of its property.

Promoter commissions were ₹5.9 crore for Ashok and ₹4.2 crore for Kishore. Several Atluri family members are employed in roles like vice president and recruitment head. The company also gave ₹1.46 crore in CSR funds to the Veer Sammaan Foundation, where it is a founder trustee.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are small and unchanged from the previous year. They consist of ₹10.1 crore for direct taxes and ₹8.2 crore for central excise. reports.outlook: In the management discussion, the company highlighted the government's push for indigenous procurement under the draft DAP 2026. Management stated it lobbied against equating licensed foreign technology with genuinely indigenous design. The report also detailed its main Hardware Park plant in Hyderabad, which has 421 employees.
reports.other: The company reports a single Defense and Homeland segment. Three customers made up 56.94% of group revenue, while exports dropped sharply to ₹78.7 crore from ₹363.5 crore last year. Customer advances fell from ₹410 crore to ₹224 crore. Minority interests are now material, taking roughly ₹24.5 crore of the ₹217.9 crore reported net profit. The CFO and a whole-time director left the company during the year.
flags: Three customers accounted for 57% of group revenue, showing high concentration risk.
Export revenue dropped sharply to ₹78.7 crore from ₹363.5 crore the previous year.
The auditor issued a CARO qualification for the Anawave subsidiary regarding property title deeds.
The company gave ₹17.2 crore in supplier advances to related-party associates.
The CFO and a whole-time director both left the company during the year.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unmodified opinion. The only key audit matter noted was revenue recognition, which specifically focused on fixed-price estimates and time-and-material approvals.
reports.relatedParties: Shareholders were asked to approve ₹750 crore of transactions for FY27. These involve intra-group, arm's-length dealings with the company's step-down subsidiary in South Africa.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities were small, totaling about ₹36 crore at the end of March 2026. These mostly consisted of indirect-tax disputes, bank guarantees, and minor claims.
reports.other: Capital commitments stood at ₹12 crore in March 2026, up from ₹4 crore a year earlier. The company proposed a total dividend of ₹15 for FY26, which included a ₹12.60 final dividend. No share pledges were found in the report.

reports.auditor: The auditor gave an unqualified opinion and highlighted one key audit matter regarding revenue cut-off. They also made a common, minor remark that the audit trail was not enabled at the database level for direct data changes.
reports.relatedParties: Sales to ZF CV Systems Global were ₹781 crore for goods, ₹324 crore for software, ₹60 crore for R&D, and ₹74 crore for business support. The company paid royalties of ₹101 crore to group companies and ₹45.3 crore to ZF AG for IT support. Purchases from ZF AG doubled to ₹70.8 crore. The parent lent ₹10 crore to its subsidiary. Pinnacle Mobility Solutions became a related party with ₹2.7 crore in sales and a ₹2.0 crore receivable.

reports.outlook: The management discussion stated that the company does not foresee a need to borrow or raise capital.

flags: Royalties and IT support charges paid to the parent group are rising faster than sales.
Roughly 30% of revenue comes from ZF group entities at transfer prices set by the parent.
Purchases from ZF AG more than doubled to ₹70.8 crore during the year.
A new disputed GST claim of ₹57.0 crore appeared in the financial year.
The managing director left the company in June 2025.

reports.auditor: The auditor issued an unmodified opinion. US legal proceedings were flagged as a key audit matter, notably multi-district price-fixing litigation where Zydus is a defendant in five bellwether cases facing trials between 2026 and 2028. The CARO report also noted that the audit trail in the Takeda joint venture was not enabled for certain changes by users with privileged access.
reports.contingent: Contingent liabilities are relatively small. They include general claims of ₹39 crore, drug price control demands of ₹272 crore, indirect tax of ₹266 crore, and income tax of ₹220 crore.

flags: The auditor highlighted US price-fixing litigation as a key audit matter, with the company facing bellwether trials from 2026 to 2028.
The CARO report flagged that the audit trail in the Takeda joint venture was not enabled for some changes by privileged users.
The newly acquired MedTech segment dragged on profitability with a reported loss of ₹178 crore.

reports.auditor: The auditor flagged impairment testing as a key audit matter because it depends on long-term growth and discount-rate assumptions. This was noted as goodwill and indefinite-life brands make up nearly the entire net worth.
reports.contingent: The standalone company has given ₹3,290 crore in corporate guarantees as of March 2026. These are mainly for the acquisition debt of its subsidiaries.
reports.other: Promoter holding is steady at 69.63% with no reported pledges, and the company has an S&P Global ESG score of 84.
